entries.question: What is the Operations Console and where do I find it?
entries.answer:
The Operations Console is the platform owner's live view of everything happening across RackTrack. Open it at /dashboard, or click "Console" in the left sidebar (the link only appears for the platform owner). The sidebar shows on a desktop or laptop browser and on an iPad in either portrait or landscape; on a phone there is no sidebar, so go to /dashboard directly. If you have an old /logs bookmark, it now redirects here — logs became a tab inside this console.

It has two tabs:
• Operations — "Everything happening across RackTrack — who's scanning, what's working, what's failing." You get headline tiles (Scans today, Active users today, Total scans, Success rate, Accuracy (feedback), Users, Organizations, Failures (all)), a Live activity feed, Recent errors, Top scanners, Scans by organization, What users are doing, Authentication, All users and All organizations.
• Logs — "Live application log — email delivery, errors, and requests as the server records them."

At the top right are two controls: a Live / Paused button (auto-refresh on or off, refreshing every 5 seconds while Live) and a Refresh button for an immediate reload.
entries.rootCause: DashboardPage renders a title 'Operations Console' with two tabs (ops, logs) and shared Live/Refresh controls; DesktopShell adds the '/dashboard' sidebar link only when user.role === 'owner'.

evidence.snippet:
Operations Console

... {live ? 'Live' : 'Paused'}

// Operations Console (live ops + server logs) — owner-only.
...(isOwner ? [{ to: '/dashboard', label: 'Console', icon: <DashboardIcon />, end: false }] : []),

entries.short: The Operations Console is the platform owner's live view of everything happening across RackTrack. Open it at /dashboard, or click "Console" in the left sidebar (the link only appears for the platform owner).

entries.question: My bookmark for /logs stopped working — it jumps to the dashboard.
entries.answer: That is intentional. The logs are no longer a separate page; they are the "Logs" tab inside the Operations Console. The old /logs address now redirects to /dashboard, and you land on the Operations tab — click "Logs" to get the log viewer. Update your bookmark to /dashboard.
symptoms: Bookmark goes to the dashboard instead of the logs
entries.rootCause: App.jsx replaced the /logs route with a redirect to /dashboard when LogsView was folded into DashboardPage as a tab.
entries.short: That is intentional. The logs are no longer a separate page; they are the "Logs" tab inside the Operations Console. The old /logs address now redirects to /dashboard, and you land on the Operations tab — click "Logs" to get the log viewer. Update your bookmark to /dashboard.

entries.question: What do the "Live" and "Paused" buttons do, and how often does the console update itself?
entries.answer:
The button in the top-right toggles auto-refresh. When it reads "Live", the console reloads on its own; when you click it, it reads "Paused" and stops reloading until you press "Refresh" or switch it back to Live.

While Live is on, the Operations tab reloads every 5 seconds and the Logs tab every 4 seconds. Separately, the "x ago" timestamps tick over once a second, so ages stay accurate even between reloads. "Refresh" forces an immediate reload of whichever tab you are on, whether or not Live is on.

Pause it when you are reading a specific row and don't want it to move under you.
symptoms: Rows keep moving while I read them
How often does the console refresh
entries.rootCause: DashboardPage owns `live` and `refreshTick` and passes them to both views; OperationsView polls /api/admin/dashboard on a 5000ms interval and LogsView polls /api/logs on a 4000ms interval, each gated on the live flag, with an independent 1s tick for relative time rendering.
entries.short: The button in the top-right toggles auto-refresh. When it reads "Live", the console reloads on its own; when you click it, it reads "Paused" and stops reloading until you press "Refresh" or switch it back to Live. While Live is on, the Operations tab reloads every 5 seconds and the Logs tab every 4 seconds.

entries.question: In the Live activity feed some rows say "not signed in" or show no username. Is that a bug?
entries.answer:
No. The feed records things that happen before anyone is signed in — sign-in attempts, sign-ups, password resets. Those events have no logged-in session, so RackTrack shows the identifier the person typed (the email or username they entered) and tags the row "not signed in". If no identifier was captured with the event, the name column simply reads "guest" — it is never left blank.

Other things you will see in a feed row: a green "ok" or red "fail" pill, the plain-English action (for example "Scanned a rack", "Located a port", "Signed in", "Approved an org", "Gave feedback", "Ran console command"), the organization, and how long ago it happened. Failed rows also show the error text underneath.

If an action shows as a dotted machine name (like `logs.clear`) rather than a phrase, that simply means no friendly label has been written for it yet — the event itself is recorded correctly.
symptoms: not signed in in the activity feed
Action shows as a dotted name like scan.create
entries.rootCause: The /api/admin/dashboard `recent` query falls back to json_extract(payload,'$.ident') when audit_log.username is empty and sets a guest flag; the client labels those 'not signed in'. Action text is mapped through ACTION_LABELS with a raw-key fallback.

evidence.snippet: {e.username || 'guest'} {e.actor_id ? {e.actor_id} : e.guest ? not signed in : null}

entries.short: No. The feed records things that happen before anyone is signed in — sign-in attempts, sign-ups, password resets. Those events have no logged-in session, so RackTrack shows the identifier the person typed (the email or username they entered) and tags the row "not signed in".

entries.question: What exactly does the Logs tab show, and how do I filter it?
entries.answer:
The Logs tab is a live view (it refreshes itself every 4 seconds) of what the RackTrack server has been recording — email delivery, errors, and web requests.

At the top are four counters: Total kept, Info, Warn and Error (Error also includes any fatal entries). Below them:
• Four filter buttons — All, Info+, Warn+, Errors. These are "this level and above", so Warn+ also shows errors and fatals.
• A search box: "Search messages, URLs, errors…". Press Enter to apply it; once applied, a ✕ clears it. It matches anywhere in the stored entry — the message, URL, event name, error text, and the rest of the raw log line — so it will also find things like a request id or a user id buried in the entry.

Each row shows the clock time and age, a level badge, the message, and for web requests the method, address, status code and how long it took. Click any row to expand it and see the full raw entry plus its request id (useful for following one request through several lines).

Under the filters, a line tells you exactly what you are looking at, for example "Showing 300 of 1,240 entries · kept 7 days" (300 is the most rows loaded at once; 7 days is the default retention). Next to that line is a "Clear log" button, which deletes every stored entry after a confirmation — it cannot be undone.
symptoms: What is in the Logs tab
How do I search the log
What does the request id mean
entries.rootCause: LogsView renders stat tiles, level tabs (All/Info+/Warn+/Errors), a search form and a table of rows from /api/logs; expanding a row lazily fetches /api/logs/:id for the full JSON line including request_id.

evidence.snippet:
<StatTile label="Total kept" value={stats?.total} />
        <StatTile label="Info"  value={byLevel.info}  tone="info" />
        <StatTile label="Warn"  value={byLevel.warn}  tone="warn" />
        <StatTile label="Error" value={(byLevel.error || 0) + (byLevel.fatal || 0)} tone="error" />
...
            placeholder="Search messages, URLs, errors…"
where.push(`(msg LIKE @q ${E} OR url LIKE @q ${E} OR event LIKE @q ${E} OR err LIKE @q ${E} OR meta LIKE @q ${E})`);

entries.short: The Logs tab is a live view (it refreshes itself every 4 seconds) of what the RackTrack server has been recording — email delivery, errors, and web requests. At the top are four counters: Total kept, Info, Warn and Error (Error also includes any fatal entries).

entries.question: What does "Clear log" do? Can I get the entries back afterwards?
entries.answer:
"Clear log" (bottom-right of the count line on the Logs tab) permanently deletes every stored log entry so you can start fresh. It is not undoable.

Before anything happens you get a confirmation box: "Delete all N stored log entries and start fresh? This cannot be undone." Click Cancel if you are unsure. While it runs the button reads "Clearing…".

What it does and does not touch:
• Deletes: every row in the server's stored application log, including entries the level filter or search box is currently hiding — not just the ones on screen. The database file is compacted afterwards.
• Does NOT touch: the Operations tab. The activity feed, error list, user and organization figures come from a separate audit record in a different database file and survive a clear.
• The clear itself is recorded — an audit entry and a fresh log line naming who cleared it and how many entries were removed are written immediately, so the empty log will already have one line in it.

If the button is greyed out: it is disabled whenever the current view has no rows, so clear the level filter and the search box (back to "All") and it will become clickable again.

There is no restore. If you might need the entries, note or copy what you need first.
symptoms: How do I start the log fresh
entries.rootCause: The Clear log button POSTs /api/logs/clear, which calls logStore.clearAll() — an unconditional DELETE FROM app_logs followed by VACUUM, with no backup written. It then writes an audit entry (action 'logs.clear') and one new log line. The audit_log table backing the Operations tab is a different database and is untouched.

evidence.snippet:
const DATA_DIR = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'data');
const DB_PATH = process.env.LOG_DB_PATH || path.join(DATA_DIR, 'logs.db');

entries.short: "Clear log" (bottom-right of the count line on the Logs tab) permanently deletes every stored log entry so you can start fresh. It is not undoable. Before anything happens you get a confirmation box: "Delete all N stored log entries and start fresh? This cannot be undone." Click Cancel if you are unsure.

entries.question: The "Clear log" button is greyed out and I can't click it.
entries.answer:
The button is switched off in two situations:

• There are no rows in the list right now. The list is filtered on the server, so this happens either because your level filter or search matched nothing, or because the log is genuinely empty (nothing logged yet, or you already cleared it). Set the level tab back to "All" and clear the search box using the ✕ beside it. The button turns on again as soon as at least one entry is listed — if the log is truly empty it stays off until new activity is logged, which usually takes a few seconds since the console refreshes every 4 seconds while Live is on.

• A clear is already running. The button reads "Clearing…" and stays disabled until the server confirms the wipe finished.

Important: Clear log always deletes every stored log entry, not just the rows currently shown. Filtering to "Errors" and then clearing will still remove your info and warn entries as well. You will be asked to confirm first, and it cannot be undone.

If you can see the Logs tab at all but the button never enables, check you are on the Logs tab of the Operations Console rather than the audit feed. Access is limited to the platform owner and any accounts your deployment lists as log admins; other users see "Admin access required to view logs." instead of the table.
entries.rootCause: The button's disabled prop is `clearing || !logs.length`, so an empty filtered result set (not just an empty store) disables it.

evidence.snippet:
<button
          type="button"
          className={styles.clearLogsBtn}
          disabled={clearing || !logs.length}
          onClick={clearLogs}
          title="Delete every stored log entry and start fresh"
        >
          {clearing ? 'Clearing…' : 'Clear log'}
        </button>

entries.short: The button is switched off in two situations: • There are no rows in the list right now. The list is filtered on the server, so this happens either because your level filter or search matched nothing, or because the log is genuinely empty (nothing logged yet, or you already cleared it).

entries.question: Old log entries have vanished on their own — I didn't clear anything.
entries.answer:
That is normal housekeeping, not data loss. The log keeps entries for 7 days by default, and also caps the total at 200,000 entries — whichever limit is reached first wins, and the oldest entries are dropped. The line under the filters tells you the current retention, e.g. "· kept 7 days".

The tidy-up runs automatically as new entries arrive, and once again each time the server starts.

If you need a longer history, ask whoever runs the server: the retention window and the row cap are set by the LOG_RETENTION_DAYS and LOG_MAX_ROWS settings.
symptoms: Log only goes back a week
entries.rootCause: log-store prune() deletes rows older than RETENTION_DAYS (default 7) and trims the oldest rows above MAX_ROWS (default 200000); it runs every PRUNE_EVERY (1000) inserts and once at init().

evidence.snippet: prune(); // clear anything stale left from a previous run

entries.short: That is normal housekeeping, not data loss. The log keeps entries for 7 days by default, and also caps the total at 200,000 entries — whichever limit is reached first wins, and the oldest entries are dropped. The line under the filters tells you the current retention, e.g. "· kept 7 days".

entries.question: The log used to be full of "GET /api/logs/stats 200" and now I don't see the console's own requests at all. Which is right?
entries.answer:
The current behaviour is correct. The Operations Console refreshes itself constantly (the Logs tab every 4 seconds, the Operations tab every 5), and each of those refreshes used to be written into the log — so opening the Logs tab filled the log with nothing but itself and buried the real activity.

Those self-monitoring addresses are now deliberately left out of the log, along with the health-check and version addresses and static files. They are still measured for performance metrics; they are just not written as log lines.

So: not seeing your own log-viewer traffic is expected, and everything else is unaffected.
symptoms: Console requests missing from the log
Log floods when I open the Logs tab
entries.rootCause: The pino-http autoLogging.ignore predicate excludes /metrics, /healthz, /api/health, /api/version, /api/logs*, /api/admin/dashboard*, /uploads/, /outputs/ and /assets/ from request logging while the metrics middleware still records them.
entries.short: The current behaviour is correct. The Operations Console refreshes itself constantly (the Logs tab every 4 seconds, the Operations tab every 5), and each of those refreshes used to be written into the log — so opening the Logs tab filled the log with nothing but itself and buried the real activity.

entries.question: Why can't I find debug or trace lines in the Logs tab, even though they appear in the server's terminal output?
entries.answer:
Only info-level entries and above are stored for the Logs tab — info, warn, error and fatal. The SQLite log mirror is attached at `{ level: 'info' }`, so debug and trace lines are never handed to it, and the dashboard table isn't drowned in development noise.

Where the debug detail actually goes depends on how the server is running:

- On a development server (NODE_ENV is not "production"), the logger level defaults to `debug`, so debug lines do appear in the server's console/stdout even though they are absent from the Logs tab. This is the usual cause of "the terminal shows more than the Logs tab".
- On a production server, the logger level defaults to `info`, so debug lines are not emitted at all — not to the Logs tab and not to the console. To capture them you must restart the server with `LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
- Trace lines are never emitted under either default; they require `LOG_LEVEL=trace`.

So if you need debug detail for an investigation, read it from the server's own console/stdout rather than the Logs tab — and on a production host, set LOG_LEVEL first, or there will be nothing to read.
symptoms: Debug lines missing from the Logs tab
Trace not shown in the log viewer
Logs tab shows less than the terminal
entries.rootCause: observability.js pushes the log-store stream into pino.multistream at { level: 'info' }, so sub-info levels are never handed to the SQLite mirror.
entries.short: Only info-level entries and above are stored for the Logs tab — info, warn, error and fatal. The SQLite log mirror is attached at `{ level: 'info' }`, so debug and trace lines are never handed to it, and the dashboard table isn't drowned in development noise.

entries.question: The Logs tab is completely empty and stays empty even though the server is clearly busy.
entries.answer:
Check the server's own console output at startup for either of these lines:
• "[o11y] log-store unavailable, dashboard persistence off: …"
• "[log-store] init failed, log dashboard disabled: …"

If you see one, the log database could not be opened (a missing or unwritable server/data directory, a permissions problem, or a corrupt logs.db). RackTrack deliberately keeps running with logging-to-console only rather than failing — but the Logs tab will have nothing to show until the underlying problem is fixed and the server is restarted.

If you do not see either line, check in this order:
1. The level filter is not set to "Errors" (the tabs filter that level and above) and the search box is empty — clear it with the ✕.
2. Someone may have pressed "Clear log" on the Logs tab, which empties the stored rows; new lines appear as traffic arrives.
3. Only info-level and above is mirrored to the database — debug/trace lines stay console-only by design, so a server logging solely at debug will show an empty table.
entries.rootCause: log-store.init() catches any failure opening/creating logs.db, logs the message and sets db = null, after which writeLine/queryLogs are no-ops returning zero rows; observability.js separately catches a require failure of the module.
entries.short:
Check the server's own console output at startup for either of these lines: • "[o11y] log-store unavailable, dashboard persistence off: …" • "[log-store] init failed, log dashboard disabled: …"
1. The level filter is not set to "Errors" (the tabs filter that level and above) and the search box is empty — clear it with the ✕.

entries.question: What is the Lab page and who can use it?
entries.answer:
Lab is the platform owner's view of the virtual EVE-NG test switches. Open it at /lab, or click "Lab" in the desktop sidebar — the link only appears for the platform owner. The page header reads "Lab · Owner-only · EVE-NG switches".

It shows each registered lab switch as a card with its name, its host (IP address or hostname) and a status badge, plus a one-line fleet summary such as "2 switches · 1 live · 1 offline". Selecting a card automatically runs the same full switch audit the live-switch Ports screen runs — identity, ports, PoE, VLANs, LLDP neighbours and the MAC table — and you can re-run it from the detail panel.

Anyone who is not the platform owner sees only "Restricted to platform owners." That is not a fault and cannot be granted to an Organization Admin.
symptoms: Lab link missing from the sidebar
entries.rootCause: LabPage returns the refusal text unless user.role === 'owner'; every /api/lab/* route is behind auth.requireRole('owner'), which returns 403 'Insufficient permissions' for any other role. The sidebar link is rendered only when isOwner.

evidence.snippet:
Lab

Owner-only · EVE-NG switches
const ownerOnly = auth.requireRole('owner');

// EVE-NG lab switches — owner-only while the Cisco path is shaken out.
    ...(isOwner ? [{ to: '/lab', label: 'Lab', icon: <DashboardIcon />, end: false }] : []),

entries.short: Lab is the platform owner's view of the virtual EVE-NG test switches. Open it at /lab, or click "Lab" in the desktop sidebar — the link only appears for the platform owner. The page header reads "Lab · Owner-only · EVE-NG switches".

entries.question: How do I pick a switch in Lab and run an audit? Do I have to press a button?
entries.answer:
No button needed in the normal case. Click a switch card and the audit starts on its own — the first card is selected for you when the page opens, so a report usually just appears.

While it runs, the card badge and the button both read "Connecting…". If there is no earlier result the page shows "Auditing <IP address> over SSH — identity, ports, PoE, VLANs, LLDP and the MAC table…"; if you are refreshing an existing result the timestamp line reads "Refreshing…" instead.

Two cases do not audit automatically: a switch with polling disabled, and one the background poller currently cannot reach (shown as Offline). Those display the reason instead, and you press the button to force an attempt.

Otherwise an audit runs automatically only once per switch. After that the result is remembered, so clicking back and forth between switches shows what you last saw, stamped "Audit as of 3m ago · live SSH pass, not polled". For a fresh reading press "Refresh audit" (the button reads "Run full audit" if there is no result yet).

This is deliberate: these switches accept only one SSH session at a time, and re-auditing on every click would fight the background poller for it. Only one audit runs at a time across the whole page.
symptoms: How do I run a Lab audit
Audit doesn't re-run when I click back
Run full audit vs Refresh audit
entries.rootCause: A useEffect auto-calls runAudit once per selected device, skipping when busy or when auditsRef already holds an entry; results are cached in a ref keyed by device id and the explicit re-run is the Refresh audit button.

evidence.snippet:
<button className={`${styles.btn} ${styles.btnPrimary}`}
                        disabled={busy || !selected.enabled}
                        title={!selected.enabled ? 'Polling is disabled for this device' : undefined}
                        onClick={() => runAudit(selectedId)}>
                  {busy ? 'Connecting…' : audit ? 'Refresh audit' : 'Run full audit'}
{busy ? 'Refreshing…' : `Audit as of ${fmtAgo(entry.at)}`} · live SSH pass, not polled
Auditing {selected.host} over SSH — identity, ports, PoE, VLANs, LLDP and the MAC table…

entries.short: No button needed in the normal case. Click a switch card and the audit starts on its own — the first card is selected for you when the page opens, so a report usually just appears. While it runs, the card badge and the button both read "Connecting…".

entries.question: What do the Lab status badges — Live, Offline, No data, Disabled, Connecting… — actually mean?
entries.answer:
The badges describe the background poller's last result for that switch, not the audit you just ran. They are evaluated in strict order, so the first one that applies wins:

• Connecting… — an audit is running against that switch right now (this overrides every other state while it runs).
• Disabled — polling was turned off for this switch with the "Disable polling" button in the detail panel.
• Offline — the last poll failed. Select the switch to see the detail panel, which explains the failure in plain English, shows how many attempts have failed in a row, and prints the raw SSH error. The card itself only shows the badge.
• No data — polling is on and nothing has failed, but no successful reading has ever been recorded. This happens when the poller gives up before it ever tries SSH, which it does without recording a failure: most commonly because no SSH credentials are stored for that switch, and also if the switch's vendor has no polling recipe.
• Live — the last poll succeeded and data came back. This is the healthy state.

The fleet line at the top counts only the last two states: "N live" (enabled, no error, has been read successfully) and "N offline" (enabled, last poll errored). Disabled and No-data switches appear in neither count, so the two numbers will not always add up to the total switch count.
symptoms: What do the Lab status colours mean
entries.rootCause: statusMeta() derives the badge in order: connecting → !enabled → last_error → !last_seen → Live. last_seen is stamped only on a successful metadata write, and the poller early-returns without recordPollFailure when credentials are missing, so a credential-less device shows 'No data' with zero failures.

evidence.snippet:
const liveN = devices.filter((d) => d.enabled && !d.last_error && d.last_seen).length;
  const offN  = devices.filter((d) => d.enabled && d.last_error).length;

entries.short: The badges describe the background poller's last result for that switch, not the audit you just ran. They are evaluated in strict order, so the first one that applies wins: • Connecting… — an audit is running against that switch right now (this overrides every other state while it runs).

entries.question: A Lab switch says "Poller can't reach it" with an SSH error. How do I read that message?
entries.answer:
That message appears on the Lab page, which is available only to RackTrack platform staff (owners). If you're an organization admin you'll see a refusal instead of the device list, so this is a screen you may not be able to reach.

When it does show, it means RackTrack's background monitor tried to reach the switch over SSH and couldn't connect. Any "connection refused" style error triggers it, not just one exact wording, so read it as "the switch didn't answer" rather than a specific fault. The raw SSH error is shown after the message for more detail.
symptoms: The switch isn’t answering on SSH at all.
The switch is up, but nothing is listening on SSH.
No network route to the switch.
Reached the switch, but the login was rejected.
Timed out while waiting for handshake
entries.rootCause: explainSshError() pattern-matches the poller's stored last_error string (handshake/timed out/ETIMEDOUT, ECONNREFUSED, EHOSTUNREACH/ENETUNREACH/no route, authentication/password) and returns a plain-language cause plus an EVE-NG-specific remediation hint; unmatched shapes fall through to the raw string.

evidence.snippet:
{selected.last_error && (
Poller can’t reach it {selected.consecutive_failures ? ` — ${selected.consecutive_failures} failed attempt${selected.consecutive_failures === 1 ? '' : 's'}` : ''}. ...
SSH error: {selected.last_error}

entries.short: The owner-only Lab shows this when the background monitor can't reach the switch over SSH; any 'refused' error triggers it.

entries.question: I selected an offline Lab switch and no audit ran at all — it just shows the error banner.
entries.answer:
That is deliberate. When the background poller already knows it can't reach a switch (the device has a recorded error), RackTrack skips the automatic audit: the SSH attempt would just hang for the full timeout every time you selected that card. Showing you the offline diagnosis immediately is more useful.

The same applies to a switch whose polling you have disabled.

You can still force an attempt by hand with the audit button in the detail panel — it reads "Run full audit" before the first audit and "Refresh audit" once a result has been cached. The exception is a disabled switch, where the button is greyed out with the tooltip "Polling is disabled for this device"; use "Enable polling" first.
symptoms: Audit doesn't start for an offline switch
No audit runs when I select a device
Run full audit button greyed out
Polling is disabled for this device
entries.rootCause: The auto-audit effect returns early when the device is not enabled or has a last_error; the audit button is additionally disabled while busy or when !selected.enabled.

evidence.snippet:
disabled={busy || !selected.enabled}
                        title={!selected.enabled ? 'Polling is disabled for this device' : undefined}

entries.short: That is deliberate. When the background poller already knows it can't reach a switch (the device has a recorded error), RackTrack skips the automatic audit: the SSH attempt would just hang for the full timeout every time you selected that card. Showing you the offline diagnosis immediately is more useful.

entries.question: What is in a Lab audit result, and why are Speed, Duplex and PoE all showing "—"?
entries.answer:
An audit is a live SSH reading taken at that moment (the page labels it "live SSH pass, not polled"). It is split into five tabs — Identity, Ports, VLANs, LLDP and MAC. The four collection tabs carry a count badge; Identity does not, because it is a fixed set of fields rather than a list.

• Identity — Name, Model, Serial, MAC, Firmware, Hardware, Host, Vendor.
• Ports — a coloured grid (up / down / unknown) plus a table with Port, Link, Admin, Speed, Duplex, Type, PoE (W), Description and Neighbour, and a PoE budget line if the switch reports one.
• VLANs — VLAN, Name, Status, Ports.
• LLDP — Local port, System, Chassis, Remote port.
• MAC — Port, MAC, VLAN.

A dash means "the switch did not report a value", not "RackTrack failed to read it". On the lab switches this is expected and correct: they are virtual Cisco IOL devices, which never negotiate a real link and have no PoE hardware, so Speed, Duplex and PoE legitimately read "—". A real switch, such as the bench TP-Link, fills those columns in. Empty VLAN and LLDP tabs can also be normal on the lab images — the page explains why in each case (CoreSW runs a routed L3 image with no switchports; the IOL l2-ipbase image may not support LLDP, since Cisco defaults to CDP).
symptoms: Speed and duplex are empty in Lab
Dashes in the Lab ports table
entries.rootCause: parseIfStatusFor() maps Cisco rows with speed_mbps == null to null; IOL is a virtual image that neither negotiates a link nor has PoE hardware, and the UI's dash() renders null/undefined/'' as an em dash.

evidence.snippet: const dash = (v) => (v === null || v === undefined || v === '' ? '—' : v);

entries.short: An audit is a live SSH reading taken at that moment (the page labels it "live SSH pass, not polled"). It is split into five tabs — Identity, Ports, VLANs, LLDP and MAC. The four collection tabs carry a count badge; Identity does not, because it is a fixed set of fields rather than a list.

entries.question: The Lab VLANs tab and LLDP tab both say "None". Is the audit broken?
entries.answer:
No — the audit is working. Both tabs print a short note explaining why they're empty, and on the lab switches both are expected.

• VLANs → "None. Expected on CoreSW — it runs the L3 IOL image, where interfaces are routed and there are no switchports to put in a VLAN." This wording is the fixed text shown whenever no VLANs come back, so it names CoreSW even if you selected a different lab device. Read it as the general explanation, not as a claim about which device you're looking at.
• LLDP → "None. IOS needs `lldp run` globally, and the IOL l2-ipbase image may not support LLDP at all — Cisco defaults to CDP." To get neighbours on a Cisco lab switch, enable `lldp run` on it — but the image may not support LLDP regardless.

The MAC tab, when empty, says "No MAC entries returned"; the Ports tab says "No ports returned". The audit tabs are Identity, Ports, VLANs, LLDP and MAC.

Scope: the Lab view is for platform owners only; organization admins can't open it and will see "Restricted to platform owners."
entries.rootCause: LabPage renders section-specific explanatory notes when audit.vlans is empty (L3 IOL image has no switchports) or the neighbors map is empty (LLDP is off by default on IOS and may be unsupported on the IOL l2-ipbase image; Cisco defaults to CDP).

evidence.snippet: None. Expected on CoreSW — it runs the L3 IOL image, where interfaces are routed and there are no switchports to put in a VLAN.
None. IOS needs lldp run globally, and the IOL l2-ipbase image may not support LLDP at all — Cisco defaults to CDP.
No MAC entries returned.

entries.short: The audit is fine — VLANs and LLDP show 'None' with a note explaining it's expected on the lab switches.

entries.question: Lab says "Last audit failed" but there is still a table of results below. Which one am I looking at?
entries.answer:
You are looking at the previous, older result. A failed audit never erases what RackTrack last read — it annotates it, and the banner says "Last audit failed. <reason> — showing the previous result below."

Check the "Audit as of …" line just under the tabs to see how old that data is before you act on it, then press "Refresh audit" to try again.

If the switch is also marked Offline, the "Poller can't reach it" banner above already explains the cause and the failed-audit line is not repeated.
symptoms: Audit failed but data still shown
entries.rootCause: runAudit's catch branch writes { data: prev?.data, at: prev?.at, error } back into the cache, preserving the previous payload and timestamp; the banner renders only when there is cached data to annotate or when no poller-offline banner is already explaining the failure.
entries.short: You are looking at the previous, older result. A failed audit never erases what RackTrack last read — it annotates it, and the banner says "Last audit failed. <reason> — showing the previous result below." Check the "Audit as of …" line just under the tabs to see how old that data is before you act on it, then press "Refresh audit" to try again.

entries.question: A Lab audit failed with a message about no SSH credentials. What does that mean?
entries.answer:
It means RackTrack has the switch registered but has no stored login for it, so it never even attempted to connect. The audit fails immediately, and the message names the exact fix — for example, that a login still needs to be stored for that vendor (such as cisco-ios).

Credentials are held encrypted on the server, per vendor and optionally per host, with a per-host entry taking precedence over the vendor default (a host entry missing an enable password still inherits the vendor's). Whoever administers the server needs to set this up there; it can't be entered from the browser, and the Lab view itself is owner-only.

Missing credentials will also leave a device on the "No data" badge indefinitely: the background monitor skips it, recording only that it tried. Note that "No data" is not proof of missing credentials — it means the switch has never been read successfully, so an unreachable host, a wrong password, or another session already holding the switch's single SSH slot will all look the same. Check the server log to confirm credentials are the cause before re-entering them.
symptoms: no SSH credentials stored for vendor
entries.rootCause: The lab audit route resolves credentials from lib/ssh-creds (per-host merged over per-vendor) and returns HTTP 409 with the encrypt-creds remediation string when no username is found; the poller takes the equivalent early return and only stamps last_polled_at.
entries.short: It means RackTrack has the switch but no stored login, so it never connected; a login must be set up on the server.

entries.question: How often does RackTrack poll a switch in the background, and why was it changed from every minute?
entries.answer:
Once an hour by default. It used to be every 60 seconds, and that was actively harmful: these switches (TP-Link JetStream, Cisco IOL) accept only ONE SSH session, and they don't release it when the connection drops — only on an idle timeout. Polling every minute meant the monitor held that single session most of the time, so a technician's manual probe or a Lab audit had to fight it for access, and a burst of retries could saturate the switch until it was rebooted.

Hourly is enough because the Ports page reads stored snapshots and shows the last known state either way; only drift detection and the Lab view care about how fresh the poll is.

When the monitor does run, 4 switches are polled at once by default, each command has a 15-second timeout, and a poll runs immediately at server startup so the first reading doesn't wait an hour. Startup also clears any stale per-device backoff so a previously wedged switch gets a clean attempt.

Admin note: the interval is configurable on the server. If a deployment was set up to poll every 60 seconds, it will still show the session-contention problem — whoever runs the server should raise it to hourly. Check the running deployment's setting rather than assuming, since some installs already use the hourly value.
entries.rootCause: DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS is 3_600_000 (1h) in port_poller.js and app.js starts the poller with Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) || 3_600_000; server/.env.example line 46 still sets 60000, which would override the hourly default.

evidence.snippet: PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60000

entries.short: RackTrack polls once an hour by default; every-minute polling starved the switches' single SSH session, so it was slowed down.

entries.question: A Lab switch has been offline for a while and doesn't seem to be retried every hour. Is polling stuck?
entries.answer:
Polling is not stuck. After a failed poll the monitor backs the switch off on purpose: it records how many times in a row the switch has failed and waits before retrying, and the wait doubles with each consecutive failure — 60 seconds for the first failure, then 2 min, 4 min, and so on, capped at 30 minutes. Devices inside their backoff window are simply skipped for that cycle.

Important: the monitor now runs hourly, and the maximum backoff is 30 minutes — shorter than the hourly cycle. So backoff on its own will almost never cause a switch to miss an hourly attempt. If a Lab switch genuinely hasn't been retried, check these first:
• Polling disabled for that device — the Lab page shows a "Polling disabled" banner and the monitor skips it entirely.
• No SSH credentials for that host/vendor — the monitor notes that it tried and returns without entering the backoff ladder at all.

The failure count is visible in the Lab page banner: "Poller can't reach it — 3 failed attempts.", followed by the raw SSH error.

Two things clear a backoff:
• Restarting the server — every boot clears all backoff, so each device gets a clean immediate attempt. This is what recovers a switch wedged by the server being killed mid-SSH-session.
• An operator force-reset — clears the backoff and kicks off an immediate poll cycle without restarting the server or rebooting the switch. It can target a single device or all of them.
symptoms: Polling seems stuck on a dead switch
entries.rootCause: recordPollFailure computes an exponential backoff window (BASE_BACKOFF_MS 60s doubling per failure, capped at MAX_BACKOFF_MS 30min) and dueDevices() filters on backoff_until; port_poller.start() calls clearAllBackoff() at boot, and forceReset() clears it on demand.
entries.short: Polling isn't stuck — failed switches are backed off briefly, but the 30-min cap is shorter than the hourly cycle.

entries.question: What do "Disable polling" and "Enable polling" do on a Lab switch?
entries.answer:
Note: the Lab is owner-only (platform staff). The page shows a refusal for anyone else, so organization admins can't use this control.

"Disable polling" tells RackTrack to leave that switch alone entirely. The detail panel then shows: "Polling disabled. The poller skips this device entirely, so its data goes stale and no drift is recorded. Enable it to resume."

While it's disabled the switch shows the "Disabled" badge (which takes precedence over "Offline"), no background readings are taken, no port-change history is recorded for it, and the audit button is greyed out with the tooltip "Polling is disabled for this device". Click "Enable polling" to resume; the button toggles between the two labels.

Use it when a lab node is intentionally down and you don't want it counted as offline or retried.

If the toggle fails, the message appears near the top of the device list as "Device list stale — Could not disable <name>: …" or "Device list stale — Could not enable <name>: …".
symptoms: Drift not recorded for a device
entries.rootCause: The toggle PATCHes /api/lab/devices/:id with { enabled }, which calls portsDb.setEnabled; dueDevices only returns enabled rows, so a disabled device is skipped by pollAll and records no snapshots or drift events.
entries.short: On the owner-only Lab, Disable polling makes RackTrack skip a switch entirely; Enable polling resumes it.

entries.question: Lab says "No lab devices registered." — how do I add a switch?
entries.answer:
That message means nothing has been registered in RackTrack's monitored-switch list yet. Lab is a view of that list; it doesn't discover switches by itself.

Switches are added by the platform owner — there's no add form on the Lab page, and it can't be done from the browser. When adding one, the owner supplies: host (required), SSH port (optional, defaults to 22), vendor (optional, defaults to tplink) and an optional label.

Rules that are enforced, in order:
• Host must be a bare IP address or plain hostname — no scheme, credentials, port, or characters beyond letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, and it must start and end alphanumerically. Otherwise: "host must be a bare IP or hostname".
• SSH port must be a whole number from 1 to 65535, else "ssh_port must be 1-65535".
• Vendor must be one that has a polling recipe — currently tplink and cisco-ios. Otherwise: "vendor must be one of: tplink, cisco-ios". Unknown vendors are rejected up front rather than accepted and then silently skipped.
• Host must be unique — a repeat returns "device already exists for host <ip>".

On success the new device is created and appears in the list. SSH credentials aren't part of adding a device — they're configured separately and stored encrypted on the server.
symptoms: How do I add a lab switch
host must be a bare IP or hostname
entries.rootCause: LabPage renders the empty-state note when /api/lab/devices returns no rows; POST /api/lab/devices validates host against HOST_RE, ssh_port range, vendor against Object.keys(poller.VENDOR_RECIPES) (tplink, cisco-ios) and host uniqueness.

{!devices.length && !loadErr &&

No lab devices registered.

}

entries.short: There's no add form — the platform owner registers switches; the message just means none are registered yet.

entries.question: I pressed "Poll now" repeatedly and got an error about a rate limit or a poll already in progress.
entries.answer:
There are three things that can make manual polling fail or appear to do nothing. Two return an error, one is silent.

• Rate limit (HTTP 429) — a maximum of 5 manual polls per 60-second sliding window, counted per person per switch (keyed on your user ID, or your IP if unauthenticated). The 6th attempt within the window returns "rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute". Wait a minute and try again; other users are unaffected by your limit.

• Overlap (HTTP 409) — if a poll for that switch is already running you get "poll already in progress for this device". Wait for it to finish; there is nothing to fix.

• Poll now returns success but nothing updates (HTTP 200, no error) — this is the case with no error message. If someone is probing that same switch by hand, the poller yields the host for 60 seconds and the manual poll is skipped silently while still reporting success. Two things start that 60-second yield window: opening the live-switch ports view, and running a Lab audit (owner-only) against that device. Note that pressing "Poll now" itself does NOT start a yield window. Wait a minute after the live view or Lab audit finishes, then poll again.

All three guards exist because these switches (TP-Link JetStream and similar small managed switches) accept only one SSH session at a time — a background poll landing mid-probe makes the switch drop both sessions.
symptoms: rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute
poll already in progress for this device
entries.rootCause: POST /api/ports/:deviceId/poll applies a 60s sliding window of max 5 hits keyed by (userId or IP):deviceId returning 429, and returns 409 when poller.isBusy(id); noteManualProbe() marks the host for a 60s poller-yield window, which the lab audit route also invokes.
entries.short: There are three things that can make manual polling fail or appear to do nothing. Two return an error, one is silent. • Rate limit (HTTP 429) — a maximum of 5 manual polls per 60-second sliding window, counted per person per switch (keyed on your user ID, or your IP if unauthenticated).

entries.question: The Lab page shows "Device stale — …" at the top. What happened?
entries.answer:
The Lab page refreshes its switch list every 15 seconds. If one of those refreshes fails, the page keeps the list it already had and shows "Device list stale — <reason>" rather than emptying the page on a momentary blip.

The status badges and the "Last polled" age you're looking at may therefore be a little out of date. It usually clears on the next refresh; if it persists, the server or your connection to it is the problem.

Note that the relative-time labels — "audit N ago" on each switch card, and "Last polled" in the panel for the selected device — re-age on screen every 10 seconds without re-fetching anything, so an ageing timestamp on its own does not mean something is wrong.
symptoms: Lab error line at top of page
entries.rootCause: The device-list effect polls /api/lab/devices every 15s; on failure it sets loadErr but deliberately does not clear the devices state, and a separate 10s timer only re-renders relative ages.

evidence.snippet:
// Re-render on a timer so the "as of" ages visibly without refetching.
  useEffect(() => { const t = setInterval(bump, 10_000); return () => clearInterval(t); }, []);

{loadErr &&

Device list stale — {loadErr}

}

entries.short: The Lab page refreshes its switch list every 15 seconds. If one of those refreshes fails, the page keeps the list it already had and shows "Device list stale — <reason>" rather than emptying the page on a momentary blip.

entries.question: Is the "Success rate" tile on the Operations tab the scan success rate?
entries.answer:
No — and this is worth knowing before quoting it. "Success rate" is computed across every audited event of any kind (sign-ins, member changes, scans, console commands and so on), as 100% minus the share of all audit-log events that failed. It is a whole-platform health figure, not a scanning figure. It shows "—" when nothing has been audited yet.

For scanning specifically, use the "Total scans" tile, which shows the count of successful rack scans, with a "N failed" subtitle when there have been failures. One caveat if you are quoting both numbers together: the success count covers scan creation only, while the failure subtitle covers any scan-related failure, so the two are not a clean numerator and denominator — do not present them as a scan success percentage.

The Success rate tile turns amber below 90%. Separately, "Accuracy (feedback)" is the right/wrong ratio from technicians' "wrong?" corrections and turns amber below 80%.
symptoms: Success rate doesn't match scan numbers
entries.rootCause: successRate is Math.round((1 - totalFails / totalEvents) * 100) over the whole audit_log table, not over scan.* rows; scan outcomes are reported separately as scansOk/scansFail.

evidence.snippet:
const totalEvents = one("SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM audit_log").n;
    const totalFails  = one("SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM audit_log WHERE status='fail'").n;

<StatCard label="Total scans"      value={t.scansOk ?? 0} sub={t.scansFail ? `${t.scansFail} failed` : null} />
        <StatCard label="Success rate"     value={t.successRate != null ? `${t.successRate}%` : '—'}
                  tone={t.successRate != null && t.successRate < 90 ? 'warn' : 'good'} />

entries.short: No — and this is worth knowing before quoting it. "Success rate" is computed across every audited event of any kind (sign-ins, member changes, scans, console commands and so on), as 100% minus the share of all audit-log events that failed. It is a whole-platform health figure, not a scanning figure.

entries.question: How do I create a RackTrack account?
entries.answer:
Tap "Create an organization" on the sign-in screen. You enter your Email, a Username (3–32 characters, letters, digits and . _ -), your Organization name (at least 2 characters), and a password, which you type twice. The password needs all five of: at least 8 characters, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character — the screen shows which one is still missing as you type. RackTrack emails you a 6-digit code — type it into the "Almost there" screen and tap Verify.

Important: signing up this way always creates a BRAND NEW organization, and it makes you that organization's Org Admin. It does not add you to a team that already exists — to join an existing team you need an invite link from your organization admin. The code expires after 1 minute; if it lapses, tap Resend on the code screen for a fresh one.

After you verify, your new organization is not usable yet — it goes to the RackTrack platform owner for approval, and you land on the "Waiting for approval" screen until they approve it.
symptoms: We sent a 6-digit code to your email.
entries.rootCause: POST /api/auth/signup stages a pending_signups row with a 6-digit code (60s TTL); POST /api/auth/verify creates an Organization (status 'pending'), a 'Main Site' tenant, and the user with role 'org_admin'.

evidence.snippet:
if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{3,32}$/.test(username))            { setError('Username 3–32 chars (letters, digits, . _ -).'); return; }
    if (!company.trim() || company.trim().length < 2)        { setError('Organization name is required.'); return; }

entries.short: Tap "Create an organization" on the sign-in screen. You enter your Email, a Username (3–32 characters, letters, digits and . _ -), your Organization name (at least 2 characters), and a password, which you type twice.

entries.question: I want to join my company's existing RackTrack team, but signing up made a new organization instead. How do I join the real one?
entries.answer:
You cannot join an existing organization by signing up — self sign-up always creates a brand-new organization (which then has to wait for RackTrack approval, which is why you may be stuck on the "waiting for approval" screen). Joining an existing team always comes from someone already inside it.

Important first step: your sign-up already claimed your work email address, and RackTrack will not let an invite be created or accepted for an email that already has an account. So before anything else, ask your organization admin — or the RackTrack platform owner if the stray organization needs deleting too — to remove the account you just created. Until that is done, your admin will see "Someone with that email already has an account" when they try to invite you.

Once your stray account is gone, there are exactly two ways in:

1. Ask your organization admin (or your site manager) to send you an invite link for the right Site. It looks like .../invite/<code>. The invite is tied to your email address and is single-use, expiring after 7 days. Opening it shows which organization and Site you are joining; you choose your own username and password, tap Join, and you land straight in the app on the correct Site. (A site manager can only invite you as a Member; an org admin can also make you a Site Manager.)
2. Ask your admin to create your account directly and hand you the username and password. You then sign in normally.

For reference, the sign-in screen spells this out under "How to get access": "Joining an existing team? Ask your organization admin for an invite link, or a username & password — new sign-ups can't join an existing organization on their own."
symptoms: I signed up but I don't see my team's racks
My colleagues aren't in my organization
new sign-ups can't join an existing organization on their own
entries.rootCause: /api/auth/verify unconditionally calls createOrganization() — there is no path for a self-signup to attach to an existing organization_id. Joining requires an invite row or an admin-created user.

evidence.snippet:
Setting up your own team? Tap Create an organization above.
Joining an existing team? Ask your organization admin for an invite link, or a username & password — new sign-ups can’t join an existing organization on their own.

entries.short:
You cannot join an existing organization by signing up — self sign-up always creates a brand-new organization (which then has to wait for RackTrack approval, which is why you may be stuck on the "waiting for approval" screen).
1. Ask your organization admin (or your site manager) to send you an invite link for the right Site.
2. Ask your admin to create your account directly and hand you the username and password.

entries.question: I'm stuck on "Waiting for approval" — how long does it take and what do I do?
entries.answer:
That screen means your organization was created but the RackTrack platform owner has not approved it yet. Until they do, you cannot scan or use any other part of the app — the block is enforced on the server, not just in the app, so there is no way around it.

The page rechecks by itself every 12 seconds, and you can tap "Check now" to force an immediate check. The moment your organization is approved you are taken straight into the app — you do not need to sign in again.

There is no fixed approval time; it depends entirely on when the platform owner acts. RackTrack does not email them when you sign up, so if you have been waiting, contact the platform owner directly and ask them to approve your organization. There is nothing you can change on your side to speed it up.

(If the screen instead says "Request not approved" or "Organization deactivated", the situation is different — your organization was rejected or switched off, and you need to contact the platform owner about that specifically.)
symptoms: Your request to create <org> has been sent to the platform owner.
This page checks automatically every few seconds.
Every page bounces me back to /pending
entries.rootCause: Self-signup sets organizations.status='pending'. orgNotActive() in App.jsx pins the user on PendingRoute, and requireAuth returns 403 'Your organization is awaiting approval' for every non-/api/auth route.

evidence.snippet: title: 'Waiting for approval', body: <>Your request to create {orgName} has been sent to the platform owner. You’ll be let in as soon as they approve it — this usually doesn’t take long., sub: 'This page checks automatically every few seconds.',

entries.short: That screen means your organization was created but the RackTrack platform owner has not approved it yet. Until they do, you cannot scan or use any other part of the app — the block is enforced by RackTrack itself, not just in the app, so there is no way around it.

entries.question: I see "Request not approved" or "Organization deactivated" — what happened?
entries.answer:
Both messages mean the RackTrack platform owner has acted on your organization, and the app is blocked for everyone in it.

• "Request not approved" — your request to create the organization was rejected. The screen says: "If you think this is a mistake, please contact them." There is no re-apply button; you have to contact the platform owner directly.
• "Organization deactivated" — your organization was switched off. The screen says it "will come back automatically if they reactivate it."

On both screens the only button is "Sign out". In both cases the page keeps re-checking your status in the background every few seconds, so if the platform owner reactivates (or approves) the organization while you're sitting on the screen, you're taken straight into the app without signing out and back in.

Nobody inside the organization — including your own org admin — can undo either state. Only the RackTrack platform owner can.
symptoms: has been deactivated by the platform owner, so the app is paused for now
entries.rootCause: organizations.status set to 'rejected' (POST /api/orgs/:orgId/reject) or 'inactive' (PATCH /api/orgs/:orgId). Both are non-'active' so orgNotActive()/orgBlocked() gate the user client- and server-side.
entries.short: Both messages mean the RackTrack platform owner has acted on your organization, and the app is blocked for everyone in it. "Request not approved" means your request to create the organization was rejected; the screen adds "If you think this is a mistake, please contact them." There is no re-apply button, so you have to contact the platform owner directly.

entries.question: My invite link says "Invite unavailable", "This invite has expired" or "This invite has already been used".
entries.answer:
Invite links are single-use and expire 7 days after they are created.

• "This invite has expired" — more than 7 days passed. Ask the person who sent it (your owner, org admin or site manager) to create a new invite link for you.
• "This invite has already been used" — someone (probably you, earlier) already completed it. If you already have an account, use the "Go to sign in" link on the page and sign in normally; if not, ask for a fresh link.
• "Invite not found" — the link doesn't match any invite. This is almost always a broken link rather than an expiry: the code was cut short by an email or chat client wrapping the URL, or it was retyped by hand. Copy the full link again from the original message and paste it into the address bar before asking for a new one.
• "Could not load this invite." — the app couldn't reach the server at all. Check your connection and reload the page; the invite itself is probably fine.
• "An account already exists for this email" / "That username is taken" — the email on the invite is already registered, or the username you chose is in use. Sign in with the account you already have, or pick a different username. Usernames must be 3–32 characters using letters, numbers, and . _ - only.

When the invite is valid you'll see "You're invited" and "Join <Organization> · <Site> as Member" (or "as Site Manager"). Your email is filled in and locked by the invite; you only choose a username and password, then press Join.

Two things worth knowing: RackTrack refuses to issue an invite to an email that already has an account, so your admin usually hits that before you do; and accepting a valid invite signs you in immediately and drops you on the Scan screen — you do not need approval from the platform owner.
symptoms: This invite has already been used
An account already exists for this email
My colleague sent me an invite link but it says the invite has expired / has already been used.
entries.rootCause: invites rows carry expires_at = created + 7 days and accepted_at; GET /api/invites/:code returns 410 for used or expired codes.

evidence.snippet:
const code = crypto.randomBytes(18).toString('base64url');
    const expiresAt = Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 7 days

Invite unavailable

{err || 'This invite is invalid or has expired.'}
Send this link to {f.email}. It works once and expires in 7 days.

entries.short: Invite links are single-use and expire 7 days after they are created. • "This invite has expired" — more than 7 days passed. Ask the person who sent it (your owner, org admin or site manager) to create a new invite link for you.

entries.question: I forgot my password. How do I reset it?
entries.answer:
On the sign-in screen tap "Forgot password?".

1. Enter your email and tap "Send reset code". RackTrack emails you a 6-digit code.
2. The code expires in 1 minute, so have your inbox open before you request it. Type the code and tap "Verify code". If nothing arrived, use the "Resend" link under "Didn't get a code?" to get a fresh one.
3. You'll land on a "Code verified" screen with two options: "Yes, change password" to set a new one, or "No, take me to the app" to sign in straight away without changing it. Either way you end up signed in.
4. If you chose to change it, enter the new password twice (there's a confirm field) and tap "Reset password".

Your new password must be at least 8 characters and include one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, a digit and a special character.

If no email arrives: for security RackTrack always says the request went through, even when that address has no account. Double-check you typed the address you actually registered with, and check your spam folder.

Messages you might see: "Reset code has expired — request a new one" means you took longer than a minute — start again. "Incorrect reset code" means the digits don't match. "No pending reset for that email — request a new code" means the code was already used or cleared — request a fresh one.
symptoms: No pending reset for that email — request a new code
Reset code has expired — request a new one
no email arrives after requesting a reset
entries.rootCause: POST /api/auth/forgot-password writes a password_resets row with a 1-minute code and always returns 200 to prevent email enumeration; /reset-password and /login-with-code consume it.
entries.short:
On the sign-in screen tap "Forgot password?".
1. Enter your email and tap "Send reset code". RackTrack emails you a 6-digit code.
2. The code expires in 1 minute, so have your inbox open before you request it.
3. You'll land on a "Code verified" screen with two options: "Yes, change password" to set a new one, or "No, take me to the app" to sign in straight away without changing it.

entries.question: My verification / reset code says it expired almost immediately.
entries.answer:
That is expected — both the signup verification code and the password-reset code are valid for only 1 minute from the moment they are sent. Email delivery can eat most of that.

What to do:
• Signup: on the "Almost there" screen tap "Resend" next to "Didn't get it?" — that issues a brand-new code with a fresh 1-minute window. If you see "Verification code has expired — sign up again", start the sign-up form over.
• Password reset: on the code screen tap "Resend" for a fresh 1-minute code. If you see "Reset code has expired — request a new one" or "No pending reset for that email — request a new code", go back to "Forgot password?" and request one again.

Tip: open your email app first, then request the code, and type it as soon as it lands.
symptoms: Verification code has expired — sign up again
Reset code has expired — request a new one
entries.rootCause: code_expires_at is set to Date.now() + 60 * 1000 for both pending_signups and password_resets; resend-code issues a new code with the same 60s window.

evidence.snippet:
Enter this code in the app to finish creating your account.
It expires in 1 minute.

entries.question: My password keeps getting rejected. What are the rules?
entries.answer:
A RackTrack password must satisfy all five of these:
• at least 8 characters
• at least one uppercase letter
• at least one lowercase letter
• at least one digit
• at least one special character (anything that isn't a letter or a digit)

On the sign-up screen and the reset-password screen, a strength meter tells you exactly which one is missing — e.g. "Need a digit" or "Need a special char" — and turns into "✓ Strong password" when all five pass. If you submit before all five pass, you'll see "Password is too weak."

The server enforces the same five rules everywhere: sign-up, invite acceptance, password reset, and when an administrator creates your account or sets a new password for you.
symptoms: Password must be at least 8 characters
Password must contain an uppercase letter
Password must contain a special character
entries.rootCause: validatePassword() in server/auth.js enforces length≥8 plus upper/lower/digit/special; SignupPage mirrors the same five checks client-side.

  { id: 'spec',  label: 'a special char', test: pw => /[^A-Za-z0-9]/.test(pw) },

entries.question: How do I change my password while I'm already signed in?
entries.answer:
RackTrack has no "change password" option inside the app — the Profile screen only lets you change your profile picture. Two ways to change it:

1. Use the "Forgot password?" link on the sign-in screen and reset it with the 6-digit code emailed to you (the code expires after 1 minute). You don't have to sign out first — you can go straight to the /forgot-password screen — but the link itself lives on the sign-in page. This is the fastest self-service route.
2. Ask someone who can set it for you. Your organization admin can set a new password for any member of their org; a site manager can do it for plain members of their own Site (that is the only thing, besides deactivating them, a site manager can change). If you are yourself an organization admin, only the RackTrack platform owner can reset your password. In the org console they open your account and fill in "New password (leave blank to keep)".

If an admin sets your password, they must tell you what it is — RackTrack does not email it.

entries.rootCause: No authenticated change-password endpoint or UI exists; ProfilePage exposes only the avatar picker (POST /api/auth/avatar). Password changes go through /api/auth/reset-password or PATCH /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId.

entries.question: What can I actually change on my Profile page?
entries.answer:
The Profile screen shows your picture, username, email, your Site name and the month you joined ("Since Mar 2026"), plus your Recent Scans — the 5 most recent, with a "Show all N scans" button if you have more.

The only thing you can edit yourself is your profile picture: tap the avatar (it has a small blue pencil badge), then pick one from the "Choose your picture" sheet — it saves as soon as you tap it.

You cannot change your own username, email, role or Site from the app. Ask your organization admin to change any of those. Admins and owners also see two extra sections on this page: "Administration" (Owner Dashboard for the platform owner, Organization Dashboard for an org admin) and "Data Sources" — both are hidden for regular members and site managers.

To sign out, tap the logout icon in the top-right of the Profile header, then confirm on the "Sign out?" prompt.

entries.question: Why don't I have the Marketplace? / "Marketplace" isn't in my menu.
entries.answer:
There are two reasons "Marketplace" may not be in your menu.

1. Your role. The Marketplace (buying and selling surplus gear, listings, orders, alerts, partner accounts) is restricted to organization admins and the RackTrack platform owner. If you are a member or a site manager, the Marketplace link is hidden and opening the address directly returns you to the home screen. Ask your organization admin to list or buy the gear on your behalf.

2. The device you are on. The Marketplace link only appears in the sidebar, which RackTrack shows on a desktop or laptop browser and on an iPad in landscape. On a phone the bottom bar is HOME / SCAN / PROFILE only, so there is no Marketplace link there even if you are an organization admin. If you are an admin, open RackTrack on a computer or a landscape iPad and Marketplace will be in the left sidebar, under Data Sources.

If you are an organization admin on a computer and still do not see it, or you see an "Insufficient permissions" message, contact your platform owner to confirm your role and that your organization is approved and active.

entries.question: I opened the dashboard and it says "Owner access required to view this dashboard."
entries.answer:
The Operations Console at /dashboard (live activity, audit feed and server logs) is reserved for RackTrack platform staff. Organization admins can open the page, but the data behind it is refused, which is why you see "Owner access required to view this dashboard." Members and site managers are redirected home before they get there, and /logs now redirects to /dashboard since logs became a tab inside the console.

What you probably want instead:
• Your own scan history → Profile.
• Your organization's Sites, members and scan activity → the "Organization Dashboard" row on Profile, which opens the Organizations console (org admins only).

You cannot grant yourself access from inside the app. Access is limited to the platform owner account, plus any username RackTrack has explicitly added to the server-side operations allow-list. If you genuinely need it, contact RackTrack.

On the Logs tab the equivalent message is "Admin access required to view logs."

entries.question: Why can't I see the scans my colleagues did? My Recent Scans list only has mine.
entries.answer:
That is how RackTrack is designed. What you see depends on your role:

• Member or site manager — you see only the scans you personally ran, and only within your own Site.
• Organization admin — sees every scan from every Site in the organization, whoever ran it.
• RackTrack platform owner — sees everything on the platform.

So two technicians on the same Site each see their own history. If you need a colleague's scan, ask them to share the result (Share / report link on the results screen), or ask your organization admin, who can see all of them in the Organizations console.

entries.question: Sign-in fails: "Invalid username or password" or "Invalid organization or credentials". What's the Organization box for?
entries.answer:
The "Organization (optional)" box on the sign-in screen can be left blank. Blank means RackTrack looks you up by username or email alone — that works for almost everyone. Fill it in only if you have been told to, or if the same username exists in more than one organization.

The two error messages mean different things:
• "Invalid username or password" — you left Organization blank and the username/email + password combination didn't match. Check for typos and try your email address instead of your username.
• "Invalid organization or credentials" — you typed something in the Organization box. Either that organization doesn't exist, or your account isn't in it, or the password is wrong. Try clearing the Organization box and signing in with just your username/email and password.

In that box you can type your organization's name or your Site's name, or the short name (slug) either one was given — matching is not case-sensitive.

If you are certain the password is right and still can't get in, note that a deactivated account shows a different message — "This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator." — so keep looking for typos only while you are seeing one of the two messages above.
symptoms: I don't know what to put in the Organization field
entries.rootCause: POST /api/auth/login resolves the optional tenant field against organizations then tenants; an unresolvable value or a scoped lookup miss returns 'Invalid organization or credentials', while an unscoped miss returns 'Invalid username or password'.
entries.short: The "Organization (optional)" box on the sign-in screen can be left blank. Blank means RackTrack looks you up by username or email alone — that works for almost everyone. Fill it in only if you have been told to, or if the same username exists in more than one organization.

entries.question: "This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator."
entries.answer:
Your account has been switched off. Your scan history is kept — nothing is deleted — but you cannot sign in until someone reactivates you.

Contact your organization admin. In the Organizations console they open your name, choose the ⋮ menu and pick "Reactivate". You can then sign in with the same username and password as before — reactivating does not change your credentials.

(The RackTrack platform owner can also do this. Site managers cannot: although the server allows them to change a member's status, the Organizations console member list is only available to owners and organization admins, so a site manager has no screen to do it from — go to your organization admin.)

If your whole team is locked out instead, you will see an "Organization deactivated" screen rather than this message; only the RackTrack platform owner can undo that one.

Nothing you do on the phone will change this: resetting your password, reinstalling the app or trying another device all produce the same message.

entries.question: How long does a sign-in last, and why was I suddenly signed out?
entries.answer:
A RackTrack sign-in lasts 30 days. After that you are asked to sign in again. Your session is stored on the device you signed in on, so signing in on your phone does not sign you in on a laptop.

Before the 30 days are up, you'll be signed out if:
• an administrator deleted your account ("User no longer exists"), or
• your organization is no longer active — if the platform owner deactivates or rejects your organization, your session stops working, or
• the server rejects your session for any other reason — RackTrack notices this on the next request and returns you to the sign-in screen rather than leaving you on a half-broken page.

Note that being deactivated as a user stops you signing in again, but does not end a session you are already in — that one runs until it expires.

If the server is simply unreachable (no signal in the datacenter), RackTrack deliberately keeps your session so you are not stranded on a login page that also cannot reach the server — just try again once you have connectivity.
symptoms: I got bounced back to the sign-in screen
Signed out on my phone but still signed in on the laptop
entries.rootCause: JWTs are signed with a 30d TTL (TOKEN_TTL='30d') and stored per-device in localStorage under rt_authToken; a 401 from any authFetch dispatches 'rt:auth-expired', which clears AuthContext state.

const TOKEN_TTL  = '30d';

const TOKEN_KEY = 'rt_authToken';
const USER_KEY  = 'rt_authUser';

entries.question: What are the four roles and what can each one actually do? (admin reference)
entries.answer:
RackTrack has four roles in a hierarchy: Platform Owner → Org Admin → Site Manager → Member.

• Owner (RackTrack staff, member IDs start OWN-) — belongs to no organization and is never blocked by organization status. Creates organizations and their first org admin, approves/rejects/deactivates/deletes organizations, sees every organization's Sites, members and scans, and is the only role that can use the Lab and the Operations Console data. (An org admin can navigate to the dashboard, but the console's data is owner-only, so they see a refusal message instead of the console.) Owner accounts can't be edited or removed by anyone.
• Org Admin (ADM-) — manages exactly one organization. Creates Sites, adds members, mints invites, changes member roles between Member and Site Manager, moves members between Sites, sets passwords, deactivates and removes members, and configures the organization's data-source connections. Also gets the Marketplace. Sees every scan in every Site of the organization.
• Site Manager (ADM-) — manages one Site. Can add and invite people, but only as plain Members — never other site managers or admins. On existing accounts they may change only the active/inactive status and the password, and only for plain members of their own Site; they can't change someone's username, email, role or Site. Their own scan visibility is the same as a member's: their own scans only.
• Member (USR-) — the field technician. Full access to scanning, results, ports, cables, topology, network view, drift, switch info, firmware, specifications, SFP advisor, CMDB registration, sharing, feedback and their own profile/history. No Connections, Marketplace, Operations Console or Lab.

Cross-cutting: any non-owner whose organization isn't active is held on the pending screen and is blocked from the app until an owner approves. The sign-in and authentication path stays open so the pending screen can notice the moment an owner approves.
symptoms: What's the difference between org admin and site manager
Can a site manager create another site manager
entries.rootCause: Role semantics defined in the users.role migration comment and enforced by requireRole / canManageOrg / canManageSite plus the client's AdminRoute.
entries.short: The four roles are Platform Owner, Org Admin, Site Manager and Member, each with progressively narrower access.

entries.question: As an admin, how do I add someone to my organization? (admin)
entries.answer:
Open Profile → "Organization Dashboard" (owners see "Owner Dashboard"), which opens the Organizations console. Owners first pick the organization; org admins go straight into their own.

Under Sites, each Site row has two buttons:
• "Invite" — enter their email and pick a Role (Member or Site Manager), then "Create invite link". You get a link to send them: "Send this link to <email>. It works once and expires in 7 days." They open it and set their own username and password.
• "+ Add member" — you set their username, email and password yourself and hand the credentials over.

Either way the person lands in that specific Site. If you are a Site Manager you can only create plain Members, not other Site Managers.

Both are blocked while the organization is still awaiting approval — the server replies "Your organization is awaiting owner approval." If the email already has a RackTrack account, an invite is refused with "Someone with that email already has an account", and "+ Add member" with "That email is already registered".

To change someone later, find them in the People section and click the ⋮ button on their card (clicking their name just filters the scan list): Edit (username, email, role, Site, new password), Deactivate/Reactivate, or Remove. The ⋮ menu is not shown for the platform owner, and org admins can only be edited by the owner. Removing deletes the account but keeps their past scans (they show as "—").

entries.question: As an admin I get "Cannot edit an owner account", "Only the owner can edit an organization admin", or "You cannot remove your own account". (admin)
entries.answer:
These are the guard rails on member management:

• "Cannot edit an owner account" / "Cannot remove an owner account" — RackTrack platform owner accounts are untouchable from the org console, by anyone.
• "Only the owner can edit an organization admin" / "Only the owner can remove an organization admin" — an org admin cannot edit or delete a fellow org admin. Ask RackTrack (the platform owner) to make that change.
• "You cannot remove your own account" — you cannot delete yourself; have another admin do it.
• "Not your organization" — you tried to act on an organization you don't administer.
• "Not a member of your site" — as a site manager you tried to change someone who is not a plain member of your own Site.
• "Role must be member or site_manager" — those are the only two roles assignable from the console; you cannot promote anyone to org admin or owner here. Note this message only appears for owners and org admins: a site manager's edit silently ignores username, email, role and site changes entirely (they can only toggle active status or set a password), so a site manager never sees this error.

Also note the console hides these controls: a member row only shows the ⋮ menu when the target is not an owner and not an org admin you lack rights over.
