entries.question: INTERNAL: what account and credential facts must never be given to customers?
entries.answer:
INTERNAL ONLY — do not surface any of this to end users or customers.

1. Seeded platform-owner credentials are hard-coded in the seed scripts: server/scripts/seed-orgs.js:26 and server/scripts/seed-racktrack.js:27 both define OWNER = { username: 'owner', email: 'racktrackteam@sprintpark.com', password: '[redacted]' }. Seeded org-admin passwords are [redacted — see the seed script] (username 'sprintpark-admin' or 'racktrack-admin' depending on the script), and seed-racktrack.js prints them to the console on completion. Never repeat these; treat any deployment still using them as an incident and rotate.

2. Deactivation does not revoke live sessions. users.active is checked only in POST /api/auth/login (server/auth.js:832); requireAuth (auth.js:463-499) loads the user row but never inspects `active`. A user deactivated mid-session keeps working with their existing JWT until it expires — TOKEN_TTL is '30d' (auth.js:39). When support tells an admin "deactivate the account", that is NOT an immediate cut-off. To actually lock out a compromised account, escalate for JWT_SECRET rotation and a server restart (which invalidates every token estate-wide).

3. Password reset does not invalidate existing tokens either. /api/auth/reset-password only updates password_hash; there is no jti and no password-changed-at check in requireAuth, so old sessions survive a password change.

4. POST /api/auth/login-with-code (auth.js:925) lets anyone holding a valid 6-digit reset code sign in without changing the password. The code is single-use and expires in 60 seconds, but within that window inbox access is full account access.

5. Verification AND reset codes are written to the server log in plaintext. sendVerificationEmail logs `[auth] verification code for <email>: <code>` (auth.js:385) before any send attempt, and the forgot-password route reuses that same function — so reset codes appear under the "verification code" label. With no SMTP configured the log is the only place the code exists. These info-level lines are mirrored to lib/log-store.js and served by /api/logs to the owner Operations Console; pino redaction does not cover them because the code is inside the message string. Treat the Logs tab as credential-bearing.

6. The org-status gate IS enforced server-side today: requireAuth returns 403 'Your organization is awaiting approval' when orgBlocked(user) (auth.js:479-490). The in-code comment describes a historical hole — before that gate, isOrgActive() had only three call sites and client-side routing was the only thing holding pending users back — which is now fixed. /api/auth/* remains exempt by design so PendingApprovalPage can poll /api/auth/me for approval. Do not describe the gate as bypassable.

7. The avatar endpoint accepts index 0-23 (auth.js:1027-1029) but client/src/utils/avatars.js ships only 8 presets (indices 0-7), so 8-23 store successfully and render out of range. Cosmetic, but don't promise 24 avatars.

entries.rootCause: Hard-coded seed credentials; stateless JWT auth with no revocation list; active flag checked only at login; codes logged via logger.info.

evidence.snippet: const OWNER = { username: 'owner', email: 'racktrackteam@sprintpark.com', password: 'Owner@12345' };

entries.short: INTERNAL ONLY — do not surface any of this to end users or customers. Three facts to keep inside the team: seeded platform-owner and org-admin credentials are hard-coded in the seed scripts, so any deployment still running them is an incident and needs rotating; deactivating a user does not revoke their live session; and a password reset does not invalidate existing tokens either.

entries.question: How is my company's data kept separate from other companies? (organization / Site separation)
entries.answer:
RackTrack is organised as Platform → Organization → Site → Users. "Site" is what you'd think of as a datacenter or location.

• Scans and racks belong to a Site. You can only open racks your own Site has scanned; anything else comes back as "Rack not found", with no hint that it exists elsewhere.
• Your organization admin can see across every Site in your organization, but never into another organization.
• The corrections you submit with the "wrong?" control are shared across your whole Organization (that's what improves recognition for your colleagues), not with other companies.
• Data-source connections (ServiceNow, NetBox, etc.) can be set up org-wide by your organization admin — configured once and used by everyone in the organization — and individual users can also hold their own personal connection profiles. Either way the stored credentials are encrypted and never shown again, not even to the admin who entered them.

A quirk worth knowing: if two different companies photograph the same rack, the rack gets the same internal ID because the ID is derived from the image itself — but ownership is still recorded per Site, so neither company can see the other's scan.
symptoms: Is my data visible to other customers
Can another organization see our racks
entries.rootCause: tenants table = Sites, each with organization_id; rack_owners is keyed (tenant_id, rack_id) and requireRackOwnership gates by req.user.tenant_id. Org connection secrets are AES-256-GCM and never returned.

evidence.snippet:
// 404 not 403 — don't reveal that the rack exists elsewhere
    return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Rack not found' });

entries.short: RackTrack is organised as Platform → Organization → Site → Users. "Site" is what you'd think of as a datacenter or location. • Scans and racks belong to a Site. You can only open racks your own Site has scanned; anything else comes back as "Rack not found", with no hint that it exists elsewhere.

entries.question: Every page in the app suddenly returns "Your organization is awaiting approval" even though I could use it yesterday.
entries.answer:
Your organization's status changed away from active — to pending, rejected or deactivated. RackTrack blocks the whole app for everyone in that organization the moment that happens: the server rejects every request with "Your organization is awaiting approval", and the app moves you to the waiting screen, which tells you which of the three states you are in.

Only the RackTrack platform owner can set it back to active. Nobody inside your organization — including your org admin — can override it, so contact the platform owner directly.

Leave the app open on the waiting screen. It rechecks your account roughly every 12 seconds and lets you back in automatically once the organization is active again. Sign-in and account endpoints are the only ones still permitted while you are blocked, which is exactly what makes that automatic recheck possible.
entries.rootCause: requireAuth calls orgBlocked(user) for every route except /api/auth/*, returning 403 with org_status when organizations.status !== 'active' for a non-owner.
entries.short: Your organization's status changed away from active — to pending, rejected or deactivated.

entries.question: How long do I have to reopen the app before a lost scan can't be recovered automatically?
entries.answer: About fifteen minutes, counted from when you started the scan. RackTrack leaves a marker on your phone when a scan begins, and that marker expires 15 minutes later; the server keeps its matching record of the in-flight scan for 15 minutes too. Reopen RackTrack (signed in) within that window and it recovers the scan automatically and takes you to its results. After that the automatic recovery stops — but the scan itself is not lost. It finished on the server and appears in your scan list on the Profile screen; open it from there.
symptoms: Reopened the app much later and no 'Bringing your scan back…' appeared
Landed on the Scan screen with no results
Scan is missing right after the scan but present in Profile
entries.rootCause: TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000 in both client pendingScan.js and server lib/scan-jobs.js. Expired job ids return { status: 'missing' }, which clears the marker and falls back to the current screen. Scan artifacts on disk under outputs/<rackId>/ are unaffected.

evidence.snippet: const TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;   // keep a finished job claimable for 15 min
if (Date.now() - (p.startedAt || 0) > TTL_MS) { clearPendingScan(); return null; }

entries.short: About fifteen minutes, counted from when you started the scan. RackTrack leaves a marker on your phone when a scan begins, and that marker expires 15 minutes later; RackTrack keeps its matching record of the in-flight scan for 15 minutes too.

entries.question: I re-scanned the same rack but no new scan appeared in my history — where did it go?
entries.answer:
Nothing went wrong — RackTrack recognised the scan as one it had already done.

RackTrack identifies a scan by the photo itself, not by when you took it. It fingerprints the image file you upload, so if you send the exact same file again it returns the result it already has instead of analysing it a second time. That is why it comes back almost instantly. You get the same rack ID (RK-…), and your scan list shows one entry, not two. The entry's time is updated to "now", so it moves back to the top of Recent Scans — the original scan time is kept internally.

Two things to know if you want a genuinely new scan:

- If you have never confirmed this rack's layout, taking a fresh photo is enough. A new shot is a different file, so it is analysed from scratch as a new scan.
- If you have already confirmed this rack's layout, a fresh photo of the same rack will also come back instantly. Once a rack is confirmed, RackTrack recognises re-shots of it and deliberately serves the confirmed result rather than re-detecting — the idea being "show what has already been confirmed." This is expected behaviour, not a fault.

Also note that a cached result is not simply frozen: any corrections you or your team submitted via "wrong?" since the first scan are re-applied before the result is shown, so the device names may not be identical to what you saw last time.

If you need RackTrack to re-analyse a confirmed rack from scratch — for example because the rack has physically changed — contact your administrator, as forcing a fresh analysis is a support-side option rather than a button in the app.
symptoms: Only one entry in Recent Scans after scanning twice
Results look identical, including old device names
entries.rootCause: computeRackId hashes the uploaded file bytes (sha256, first 8 hex chars) to form RK-XXXXXXXX. If outputs/<rackId>/device_unit_map.json exists, /api/analyze short-circuits to the cached result, re-applies active-learning corrections and refreshes meta.timestamp (preserving first_scanned_at). No second folder is created.
entries.short: Nothing went wrong — RackTrack recognised the scan as one it had already done. RackTrack identifies a scan by the photo itself, not by when you took it. It fingerprints the image file you upload, so if you send the exact same file again it returns the result it already has instead of analysing it a second time.

entries.question: I opened a link to a scan and it threw me onto the Scan screen instead. What happened?
entries.answer: That link points at a rack the server no longer has on disk — the scan folder was deleted, lost in a server rebuild or data reset, or cleaned up automatically, or the rack ID in the link is wrong. When you open a rack link, RackTrack asks the server for that scan; if the server says it doesn't exist, the app quietly removes it from your local Scan history and sends you to the Scan screen so you aren't stuck on a broken page. (If you'd simply been signed out you'd land on the login screen instead, and a link from a different Site or teammate is not the cause — those still open.) Check your Profile scan list for the rack; if it isn't there either, the scan is gone and you'll need to re-photograph the rack.
symptoms: Redirected to the Scan screen after tapping a results link
Rack disappeared from the local history list at the same time
Deep link to /results/RK-… does not open
entries.rootCause: ResultsPage cold-fetches /api/scan/:rackId on deep link. A 404 dispatches rt:rack-id-changed with an empty id, filters that scanId out of rackTrackHistory in localStorage, and navigates to /scan with replace:true.
entries.short: That link points at a rack RackTrack no longer has on disk — the scan folder was deleted, lost in a system rebuild or data reset, or cleaned up automatically, or the rack ID in the link is wrong.

entries.question: I pressed the refresh (Poll now) button several times and now it stops working.
entries.answer: You've hit the limit of 5 manual refreshes per minute for that switch (the limit is counted per person, per switch, so it isn't affected by other users). The limit exists because each refresh opens a real login session to the switch, and most switches only allow one session at a time - repeated refreshes compete with the automatic hourly poll and can lock everyone out. Note that the Poll now button does not display an error when this happens: it simply appears to do nothing, which is the normal sign that you have hit the limit. The same silent no-op occurs if a poll for that switch is already running. Wait up to a minute and press it again; the allowance frees up gradually as your earlier presses age past the 60-second mark. If it still appears to do nothing after a couple of minutes, the switch itself is likely unreachable rather than rate limited.
symptoms: rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute
poll already in progress for this device
Refresh button appears to do nothing
entries.rootCause: POST /api/ports/:deviceId/poll enforces a per-(user|IP, device) sliding window of 5 hits / 60 s → HTTP 429, and returns HTTP 409 when poller.isBusy(id) is true.
entries.short: You've hit the limit of 5 manual refreshes per minute for that switch (the limit is counted per person, per switch, so it isn't affected by other users).

entries.question: The drift screen says 'Waiting for first poll…' and never changes.
entries.answer:
'Waiting for first poll…' means RackTrack has no switch set up for monitoring — the drift screen has no monitored device to show you. It is not a loading spinner, so waiting longer won't help. Ask your administrator to add a switch for monitoring and save its credentials.

If you instead see the switch's name and status but the message 'No port data yet.', the switch is configured but RackTrack hasn't managed a successful reading yet — usually it isn't reachable on the network. In that case RackTrack backs off after each failed attempt, doubling the gap from 1 minute up to a maximum of 30 minutes between retries. Restarting the RackTrack server clears that back-off and retries every switch immediately.

You can force an immediate reading with "Poll now". That is limited to 5 manual polls per minute for each person on each switch (counted per user and per switch); going over returns "rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute".
symptoms: Drift screen shows no switch name or ports
"rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute"
"poll already in progress for this device"
The drift / port history page says "Waiting for first poll…" and never changes.
entries.rootCause: PortHistoryPage renders 'Waiting for first poll…' when overview.device is absent — i.e. no monitored_devices row or no snapshot. Failed SSH passes enter an exponential back-off starting at BASE_BACKOFF_MS = 60_000 and capped at MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 30 * 60_000; poller.start() calls portsDb.clearAllBackoff() on boot.

evidence.snippet:
{!device ? (
Waiting for first poll…

const BASE_BACKOFF_MS = Math.max(1000, Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_BACKOFF_BASE_MS) || 60_000);
const MAX_BACKOFF_MS  = Math.max(BASE_BACKOFF_MS, Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS) || 30 * 60_000);

const BASE_BACKOFF_MS = Math.max(1000, Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_BACKOFF_BASE_MS) || 60_000);
const MAX_BACKOFF_MS  = Math.max(BASE_BACKOFF_MS, Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS) || 30 * 60_000);
const MANUAL_PROBE_YIELD_MS = 60_000;

const POLL_RATE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000;
const POLL_RATE_MAX       = 5;
Waiting for first poll…

entries.short: 'Waiting for first poll…' means RackTrack has no switch set up for monitoring — the drift screen has no monitored device to show you. It is not a loading spinner, so waiting longer won't help. Ask your administrator to add a switch for monitoring and save its credentials.

entries.question: The Ports page says 'The poller runs once per minute' but drift data only updates every hour. Which is right?
entries.answer: Hourly is right on a default install; the on-screen text is stale. Commit 8de0faf changed the poller's DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS from 60,000 ms to 3,600,000 ms (server/lib/port_poller.js:40) so the background pass stops holding the switch's single SSH session, but the empty-state copy on the Interface inventory panel (client/src/pages/PortHistoryPage.jsx:393-396) was not updated. Ignore the "once per minute" wording. Caveat before quoting a wait time: the interval is env-overridable — server/app.js:8574 uses PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS if set, and server/.env.example still ships that value as 60000, so check the deployment's server/.env. With the default, expect the first snapshot within an hour of the switch becoming reachable, or press "Poll now" to force one immediately (manual polls are capped at 5 per minute).
symptoms: 'No port data yet. The poller runs once per minute — first snapshot lands shortly after the switch becomes reachable.'
Waited a minute and no data arrived
entries.rootCause: Stale UI copy in PortHistoryPage.jsx not updated by commit 8de0faf, which changed DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS from 60_000 to 3_600_000.

evidence.snippet: No port data yet. The poller runs once per minute — first snapshot lands shortly after the switch becomes reachable.
const DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS    = 3_600_000;

entries.short: Hourly is right on a default install; the on-screen text is stale. The poller's default interval was changed from 60,000 ms to 3,600,000 ms so the background pass stops holding the switch's single SSH session, but the empty-state copy on the Interface inventory panel was never updated — ignore the "once per minute" wording. Before quoting a wait time, check the deployment's server/.env: PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS overrides the default and server/.env.example still ships 60000.

entries.question: Admin: why is the switch still being polled every minute after the hourly change?
entries.answer:
The switch is still being polled every minute because a polling-interval setting in your server configuration is overriding the built-in hourly default. Any positive number you set for PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS wins over the 1-hour default. (A value of 0, blank, or a non-numeric value is ignored and falls back to hourly, so only a real number causes this.)

Check your server's environment configuration first. If it already sets PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=3600000, that's correct — ignore any stale comment sitting above it that still says the default is 60s. The common exposure is a deployment that was seeded by copying the example configuration, which ships PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60000, so it polls every 60 seconds. That is exactly the behaviour the hourly change was meant to stop, and it holds the switch's single SSH session most of the time — which is what surfaces as "Lost the SSH session" on manual probes and Lab audits.

Fix: in that deployment's environment configuration, either set PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=3600000 or remove the line entirely to inherit the 1-hour default, then restart the server. Also update your example configuration to 3600000 (or comment the line out) so new deployments stop inheriting 60000.
symptoms: Manual probes and Lab audits fail with 'Lost the SSH session'
Switch stops accepting SSH until rebooted
Log shows port_poller running far more often than hourly
entries.rootCause: server/app.js reads Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) || 3_600_000, so any set value overrides the default. server/.env.example line 46 still ships PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60000.

evidence.snippet: const intervalMs = Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) || 3_600_000; // 1h — see port_poller DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS
PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60000
PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=3600000

entries.short: Switch polls every minute because PORT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS is set to 60000 (often copied from the example); set it to 3600000 and restart.

entries.question: The Network view says 'Network view is being prepared' and never loads.
entries.answer: That banner means RackTrack could not reach the network discovery server (Netdisco) behind the Network view. It is shown instead of raw technical errors, but it does not mean data is on its way — if no discovery server is set up, or it's switched off, this banner stays forever. There's also a status pill on the page reading 'Network View online' or 'Network View offline'. If it says offline, ask your administrator whether the Netdisco data source is configured and running. Requests to it give up after 15 seconds.
symptoms: This updates automatically from your scan — check back in a moment.
Network tab spins then shows nothing
entries.rootCause: NetdiscoPage sets match = { netdisco_reachable: false } on fetch failure or non-JSON body and renders the 'being prepared' warn block; raw ECONNREFUSED/traceback text is suppressed by looksLikeNetdiscoNoise. netdisco_proxy uses AbortSignal.timeout(TIMEOUT_MS) with TIMEOUT_MS = 15000.

evidence.snippet: {ok ? 'Network View online' : 'Network View offline'}
const TIMEOUT_MS    = 15000;

entries.short: That banner means RackTrack could not reach the network discovery server (Netdisco) behind the Network view. It is shown instead of raw technical errors, but it does not mean data is on its way — if no discovery server is set up, or it's switched off, this banner stays forever.

entries.question: I lost signal — will RackTrack sign me out?
entries.answer: No. If the app can't reach the server it deliberately keeps you signed in, because bouncing you to the sign-in screen would be useless when that screen can't reach the server either. You can keep using the parts of the app that don't need the server, and your session is re-checked the next time you open or reload the app with the server reachable (and on any request that comes back rejected). You are only signed out if the server actively rejects your session — most commonly because the session has expired. Sessions last 30 days from when you signed in, so a long stretch offline in the field is fine. Note that if an administrator deactivates your account, you are not kicked out of an active session — the block takes effect the next time you try to sign in.
symptoms: Stayed signed in with no connectivity
Suddenly bounced to the sign-in screen after reconnecting
Session ended after a long time away
entries.rootCause: AuthContext validates the stored token against /api/auth/me on mount; it clears state only on 401/403 and explicitly swallows network errors to preserve the cached token. A 401 on any authFetch dispatches 'rt:auth-expired' which clears the session. server/auth.js TOKEN_TTL = '30d'.

evidence.snippet: const TOKEN_TTL  = '30d';

entries.short: No. If the app can't reach RackTrack it deliberately keeps you signed in, because bouncing you to the sign-in screen would be useless when that screen can't reach RackTrack either.

entries.question: Everything in the phone app fails to load even though my phone has good signal. Nothing works at all.
entries.answer: This usually means the app is pointed at a server address that no longer exists, rather than your phone being offline. Test builds of the RackTrack app (the TestFlight IPA and the shared APK) have the server's public web address compiled in at build time. On the standard Windows test setup the server is published through a temporary Cloudflare tunnel, which generates a brand-new random address every time the server is restarted — so an app built against yesterday's address keeps calling a host that is gone, and every screen fails. Quick check: if the web version works in a phone browser but the installed app doesn't, this is the cause. Ask your administrator for the current address (on the server it is written to current-url.txt each time deploy/legacy-windows/start.ps1 runs) and for a rebuilt app pointed at it — they run deploy/legacy-windows/update-apk-url.ps1 to update the address and rebuild the web bundle, then produce the new APK in Android Studio. Note this applies to tunnel-based test deployments; if your server is reached over a fixed LAN or public address instead, there is no current-url.txt and the cause is something else.
symptoms: Every screen fails on the phone app but the browser version works
Sign-in fails with no obvious error
App worked yesterday, broken today after a server restart
entries.rootCause: VITE_API_BASE is compiled into the client bundle. deploy/legacy-windows/start.ps1 launches a Cloudflare quick tunnel and writes the generated https://<random>.trycloudflare.com to current-url.txt; deploy/legacy-windows/update-apk-url.ps1 rewrites client/.env.production and rebuilds. A restarted tunnel yields a new hostname, orphaning previously-built APKs/IPAs.

evidence.snippet:
$content = $content -replace "VITE_API_BASE=.*", "VITE_API_BASE=$url"
    $content | Set-Content $envFile
}

# Rebuild client
Set-Location "$ProjectRoot\client"
npm run build
npx cap sync android

entries.short: This usually means the app is pointed at a server address that no longer exists, rather than your phone being offline. Test builds of the RackTrack app (the TestFlight IPA and the shared APK) have the server's public web address compiled in at build time.

entries.question: The rack shortcuts (Overview / Ports / Topology) disappeared from the sidebar after I refreshed the page.
entries.answer:
That's expected. On a wide screen (the sidebar layout, 1024px and up) the RACK section — Overview, Ports, Topology, Network, Switches and Drift — only appears once you're actually looking at a rack in that browser session. RackTrack keeps the rack in memory only; it is never saved to the browser, so an old rack from a previous visit can't linger in your navigation.

What clears it:
- Refreshing the page while you're somewhere other than the rack itself (Home, Profile, Scan, and so on).
- Opening the Scan page to start a new scan.
- Signing out or signing back in.
- A brand-new tab, which starts with nothing remembered.

Note that refreshing while you are on the rack's own page (a /results/... or /switch-info/... address) does not lose the shortcuts — the rack is read straight back out of the address bar. To get them back after they've gone, open the rack again from your scan history on Profile, or open a /results link directly.
symptoms: RACK section missing from the desktop sidebar
Shortcuts never appear in a fresh tab
entries.rootCause: DesktopShell derives the rack context from the URL or the in-memory rt:rack-id-changed event; the rackId is deliberately module-level memory so a refresh wipes it.

evidence.snippet:
// Tell the desktop sidebar which rack we're on. Pure in-memory
    // event — no sessionStorage / localStorage.

entries.short: That's expected. On a wide screen (the sidebar layout, 1024px and up) the RACK section — Overview, Ports, Topology, Network, Switches and Drift — only appears once you're actually looking at a rack in that browser session.

entries.question: Admin: I activated a data source connection and the 'pulling fresh data' banner never goes away.
entries.answer: Activating a **ServiceNow** connection kicks off a background re-poll of the incident inbox and CMDB records (other connection types — NetBox, SolarWinds, Spectrum, own SQL/REST — do not trigger this pull, so the banner should not appear for them). The app waits 1.5 seconds, then checks progress every 3 seconds, and stops waiting after 6 minutes, showing 'Stopped waiting after 6 minutes — check the server log for poll progress.' The server itself kills the poll after 5 minutes and reports a failure naming the instance: 'Poll timed out after 300s talking to <instance>.service-now.com. Open <instance>.service-now.com in a browser, sign in to confirm it's awake, then try again.' The usual cause is a sleeping ServiceNow developer instance. Wake it in a browser, then activate the connection again. You can navigate away while it runs — the job continues server-side.
symptoms: Stopped waiting after 6 minutes — check the server log for poll progress.
Poll timed out after 300s talking to <instance>.service-now.com
entries.rootCause: ConnectionsContext.waitForRefresh polls /api/incidents/refresh/status every 3000 ms after a 1500 ms head start, with MAX_WAIT_MS = 360_000. Server-side the refresh child process is SIGKILLed at TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000 and _refreshState is set to 'failed'.

evidence.snippet:
const start = Date.now();
    const MAX_WAIT_MS = 360_000;   // 6 min — gives the server's 5-min cap room

entries.short: Activating a **ServiceNow** connection kicks off a background re-poll of the incident inbox and CMDB records; the other connection types do not trigger this pull, so the banner should not appear for them. The app stops waiting after 6 minutes and the server kills the poll after 5. The usual cause is a sleeping ServiceNow developer instance — wake it in a browser, then activate the connection again.

entries.question: Owner: how far back do the Operations Console logs go, and does 'Clear log' delete anything else?
entries.answer: Logs are kept for 7 days, and no more than 200,000 lines total — whichever limit is reached first wins, so on a busy day you may have less than 7 days of history. (A server administrator can change both via the LOG_RETENTION_DAYS and LOG_MAX_ROWS settings.) Pruning runs automatically once per 1,000 new log lines, and once when the server starts. 'Clear log' in the Operations Console wipes every stored log line through the live database connection and then compacts the file to reclaim disk space; it does not touch scans, users, or drift history. The action is audited, and a line is written immediately afterwards so the fresh log records who cleared it and when. While the console's Live toggle is on, the dashboard refreshes every 5 seconds and the Logs tab every 4 seconds; those self-monitoring requests are excluded from the log so they no longer drown out real activity.
symptoms: Logs tab showed almost nothing but 'GET /api/logs/stats 200'
entries.rootCause: log-store.js: RETENTION_DAYS = 7 (LOG_RETENTION_DAYS), MAX_ROWS = 200000 (LOG_MAX_ROWS), PRUNE_EVERY = 1000 inserts; clearAll() runs DELETE FROM app_logs through the live handle. DashboardPage polls at 5000 ms, LogsPage at 4000 ms; commit 4bb69e5 excluded those endpoints from request logging.

evidence.snippet: db.prepare('DELETE FROM app_logs').run();
const id = setInterval(() => { if (liveRef.current) load(); }, 4000);
const id = setInterval(() => { if (liveRef.current) load(); }, 5000);

entries.short: Logs are kept for 7 days, and no more than 200,000 lines total — whichever limit is reached first wins, so on a busy day you may have less than 7 days of history. ) Pruning runs automatically once per 1,000 new log lines, and once when the server starts.

entries.question: Owner: the Lab page shows a switch audit that's clearly old — why doesn't it refresh itself?
entries.answer: By design. An audit is a live SSH session, and these lab switches allow only one session at a time — which the background poller also uses. So the Lab runs an audit once, the first time you select a device, and then shows that cached result with an 'audit <time> ago' stamp on the card (and 'Audit as of <time>' above the report) rather than re-running it every time you click back to the device. To force a fresh pass, use the button in the device header: it reads 'Refresh audit' when a result is already on screen, and 'Run full audit' when there isn't one. If a device is disabled, or already known to be unreachable (shown as 'Offline'), the automatic audit is skipped entirely so it doesn't hang waiting on a timeout — the offline explanation appears immediately and 'Run full audit' still lets you retry by hand. The device list itself refreshes every 15 seconds, and the 'as of' ages tick every 10 seconds without refetching. Note the cache lives in the page only: reloading the Lab clears it, so the next device you select is audited fresh.
symptoms: Audit data doesn't change when switching between devices
Device shows 'Offline' and no audit runs
entries.rootCause: LabPage caches per-device audits in auditsRef and auto-runs runAudit only once per device, skipping devices where !d.enabled or d.last_error. Device list interval 15_000 ms; 'as of' re-render bump interval 10_000 ms.

evidence.snippet: if (d.last_error)  return { label: 'Offline',     cls: styles.stOff };

entries.short: By design. An audit is a live SSH session, and these lab switches allow only one session at a time — which the background poller also uses.

entries.question: Is there any risk of losing a scan if the server is restarted while I'm scanning?
entries.answer:
A scan that finished analysing is safe: the result is written to disk under the rack's folder before the response goes back, so it survives a server restart. RackTrack also writes down a record of your in-flight scan, which is how the app finds its way back to a scan it lost while the phone was locked or the app was backgrounded — that claim ticket stays valid for 15 minutes.

What can be lost is a scan that was still being analysed at the moment the server went down. That analysis does not resume, and the job is never marked as failed either — so the app may simply sit on the progress screen until the 15-minute window expires instead of showing an error. If that happens, don't wait it out: just scan again. If the same photo had in fact already been fully analysed, RackTrack recognises the identical image and returns the stored result immediately rather than re-running the analysis.
symptoms: Scan works on retry with no changes
entries.rootCause: scan-jobs.js keeps an in-memory map as the source of truth and persists it to server/data/scan-jobs.json so the resume window survives a restart. Analysis itself runs in Python workers with a per-request wall-clock cap (RACKTRACK_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS, default 120000 ms) and no restart-resume; only completed scans have outputs/<rackId>/device_unit_map.json on disk.
entries.short: A scan that finished analysing is safe: the result is written to disk under the rack's folder before the response goes back, so it survives a server restart.

entries.question: Admin: how long is drift and port history kept before it's deleted?
entries.answer: Port change events are kept for 30 days and port state snapshots for 90 days by default. Snapshot clean-up only removes superseded rows, so the most recent snapshot for every port is always preserved regardless of age; event clean-up has no such protection and deletes everything past the cutoff. A clean-up sweep runs once when the port poller starts (i.e. at server startup) and then every hour. Both windows are configurable through the PORT_DRIFT_EVENT_DAYS and PORT_DRIFT_SNAPSHOT_DAYS settings in your server configuration; values are clamped to a minimum of 1 day, and a value of 0 or a non-numeric value silently falls back to the default rather than disabling retention. If you need drift evidence retained longer for an audit, raise those values before the window expires — the sweep is a hard delete with no undo and no archive.
symptoms: Drift timeline empty beyond a month
Historical port states unavailable for an old incident
port_poller retention: pruned N event(s), N snapshot(s) in the log
entries.rootCause: port_poller DEFAULT_EVENT_DAYS = 30, DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_DAYS = 90, DEFAULT_RETENTION_MS = 60 * 60_000; _retentionTick() calls portsDb.pruneOldEvents/pruneOldSnapshots at startup and on that interval.

evidence.snippet:
// A retention sweep runs alongside polling (default every hour) to keep
// the SQLite file from growing unbounded.

entries.short: Port change events are kept 30 days, snapshots 90 days by default; both are configurable, clamped to a 1-day minimum, and deletion is permanent.

entries.question: The drift screen updates on its own — how often, and does that hammer the switch?
entries.answer:
No — the drift screen never touches the switch. It only re-reads what RackTrack has already saved. The port grid refreshes about every 15 seconds; when you open a single port, its details and change list refresh every 15 seconds and the timeline chart every 20 seconds. All of that is reading stored data, so it costs the switch nothing.

The switch itself is contacted only on the background pass, which runs once an hour, or when you trigger a poll by hand using the refresh icon next to the switch name (manual polls are capped at 5 per minute). So a screen that refreshes often is not the same as data that is fresh — check the "Last poll" timestamp on the switch panel, not how often the page redraws.

One thing that trips people up: if the port grid is empty, the screen currently shows a message saying "The poller runs once per minute." That text is out of date — the real interval is one hour. Trust the "Last poll" timestamp, and if you need current state right now, trigger a manual poll.
symptoms: Numbers on screen change but port state doesn't
Page looks live but drift events are old
Confusion about whether the switch is being contacted
entries.rootCause: PortHistoryPage sets OVERVIEW_REFRESH_MS = 15_000, HISTORY_REFRESH_MS = 15_000, TIMELINE_REFRESH_MS = 20_000, all against stored /api/ports/* endpoints. Live SSH happens only in port_poller's hourly tick or POST /api/ports/:deviceId/poll.

evidence.snippet:
// Hourly, NOT every 60s. The Ports page reads stored snapshots, so it does not
// need a live SSH pass to render — it shows the last known state either way.

entries.short: No — the drift screen never touches the switch. It only re-reads what RackTrack has already saved. The port grid refreshes about every 15 seconds; when you open a single port, its details and change list refresh every 15 seconds and the timeline chart every 20 seconds.

entries.question: My correction ('wrong?' feedback) didn't save — I got 'Could not save'.
entries.answer: Corrections are sent to the server the moment you tap Yes or Submit. There is no offline queue or local buffer for them, so if the connection drops at that point the correction is not stored anywhere. You'll see an error under the prompt — usually 'Could not save', though it may instead show the specific network or server message (for example 'Failed to fetch' or 'Load failed'). The control stays on screen and retryable: if you tapped Yes it returns to the Yes/No prompt, and if you were submitting a correction it returns to the dropdown with your choice still selected. Nothing is queued for later, so don't leave the results screen expecting it to sync — re-submit the correction once you're back online.
symptoms: Correction reverts after leaving the screen
'wrong?' feedback not reflected on a later scan
entries.rootCause: StandardFeedback posts directly and on failure just sets an error string and returns the form to its prior phase — there is no retry queue, no localStorage buffer, and no background flush.

evidence.snippet: catch (e) { setErr(e?.message || 'Could not save'); setPhase('idle'); }
catch (e) { setErr(e?.message || 'Could not save'); setPhase('pick'); }

entries.short: Corrections are saved to RackTrack the moment you tap Yes or Submit. There is no offline queue or local buffer for them, so if the connection drops at that point the correction is not stored anywhere.

entries.question: How do I install RackTrack on my iPhone? I can't find it in the App Store.
entries.answer:
RackTrack is not in the App Store yet — it is a beta, so it arrives through Apple's testing app, TestFlight. It takes about five minutes.

Before you start: RackTrack runs on iOS 13 and later. TestFlight itself needs a newer iOS than that, so if the App Store won't let you install TestFlight, that is the reason. You will also need the Apple ID email your invitation was sent to.

1. On your iPhone, open the App Store, search for TestFlight, and install it. It is free and made by Apple. Do this FIRST — tapping the invite before TestFlight is installed just opens a web page telling you to go install TestFlight.
2. Find the invitation email from Apple (subject along the lines of "You're invited to test RackTrack"). Check spam and the Promotions tab — it lands there more often than not. It must be opened on the iPhone itself; clicking it on a laptop does nothing useful. If it only lives on your desktop, forward it to yourself and open it on the phone.
3. Tap "View in TestFlight". If that button does nothing, open TestFlight yourself, tap "Redeem" in the top corner, and type the redeem code from the email by hand.
4. Accept, then tap the blue "Install" button. RackTrack lands on your home screen with a small orange dot beside the name marking it as a beta.
5. Open RackTrack from the home screen (you don't need to go back through TestFlight) and sign in. On first run it asks for camera permission — say yes, or scanning won't work.

Important if TestFlight says it can't find your invitation: TestFlight matches the invite against the Apple ID signed into the phone. If your iPhone is signed into a personal Apple ID but the invite went to your work address, TestFlight won't find it, and the error it shows won't tell you that is the problem. Contact your RackTrack administrator with the address you want to use and the invite can be re-issued.

Finally, turn on automatic updates once: open TestFlight, tap RackTrack, and switch on "Automatic Updates". Beta apps do not update themselves through the App Store, so new RackTrack builds arrive through TestFlight instead. With this on, they install on their own.
symptoms: RackTrack is not in the App Store
orange dot next to the app name
entries.rootCause: iOS distribution is TestFlight-only. The IPA is exported with method app-store-connect and uploaded via altool/Transporter; there is no public App Store listing.

xcrun altool --upload-app -t ios -f "$IPA" --apiKey "$KEY_ID" --apiIssuer "$ISSUER_ID"

2. Find the invitation email from Apple (subject along the lines of "You're invited to test RackTrack").
3. Tap "View in TestFlight".

entries.question: RackTrack suddenly won't open at all and TestFlight says the build has expired.
entries.answer:
TestFlight builds expire 90 days after they are uploaded. That is Apple's rule, not RackTrack's. When a build lapses the app stops opening — with no warning beforehand.

Nothing is broken and you have lost nothing. Open TestFlight and install the current build of RackTrack. If TestFlight has no build to offer, email racktrackteam@sprintpark.com and a fresh one will be shipped — even if nothing has changed in the app, a new build resets the 90 days.

If instead you see "This beta isn't accepting new testers", that can mean either an expired build or that the tester group is full — email the same address and it will be sorted from our side.
symptoms: app closes immediately after tapping the icon
This beta isn't accepting new testers
entries.rootCause: Apple expires TestFlight builds 90 days after upload; the installed binary refuses to launch and the only remedy is a newer uploaded build.

Each build has a "What to Test" note on the RackTrack page in TestFlight saying what changed — worth ten seconds before you dive in.

entries.question: Is my iPhone or iPad new enough to run RackTrack?
entries.answer:
RackTrack itself runs on iOS 13 and later, on 64-bit iPhones and iPads (any iPhone from the last several years qualifies). It works in portrait and landscape on iPhone, and in all four orientations on iPad.

The practical limit is usually TestFlight, not RackTrack: Apple's TestFlight app requires a newer iOS than 13. If the App Store will not let you install TestFlight on your device, that is the reason, and there is no way around it other than updating iOS or using a newer device.

this app requires a newer version of iOS

entries.question: I got an APK file for Android. How do I install it, and will my phone let me?
entries.answer:
The Android version of RackTrack is not on the Play Store — it is a single file (about 11 MB) you install directly. You need Android 7.0 or newer.

How it reaches you: builds are pushed through Firebase App Distribution. You get an email and a push notification in Firebase's "App Tester" app, and you install and update straight from there — no file passing around. Always install the newest build rather than reusing a file you saved earlier: each build has the server address compiled into it, so an old file can point at an address that no longer works.

If you were handed the .apk file itself instead, tap it in your Downloads. Android will ask permission to install apps from this source — grant it for whichever app you tapped the file from (usually your browser or Files app), then tap Install again. The exact wording and location vary by Android version and phone maker; it is usually under Settings → Apps → Special access → Install unknown apps, and searching Settings for "unknown apps" will find it. You may also see a Play Protect warning that the app is from an unknown developer; choose the option to install anyway. That warning is expected for a file that has not gone through the Play Store, not a sign that anything is wrong.
symptoms: for your security your phone is not allowed to install unknown apps
entries.rootCause: Android distribution is sideload/Firebase App Distribution of an unsigned-for-store debug APK, so Android's unknown-sources gate and Play Protect scanning both trigger. minSdkVersion 24 = Android 7.0.

evidence.snippet: minSdkVersion = 24
APK built (~11 MB)ID com.racktrack.appAndroid 7+ Delivery sideload

# Build the Android APK and push it to every tester via Firebase App Distribution.
# Replaces hand-sharing the file in WhatsApp: testers get an email + a push in the
# "App Tester" app, and can update straight from there.

firebase appdistribution:distribute "$APK" \
  --app "$APP_ID" \
  --groups "$GROUP" \
  --release-notes "$NOTES"

entries.short: The Android version of RackTrack is not on the Play Store — it is a single file (about 11 MB) you install directly. 0 or newer. How it reaches you: builds are pushed through Firebase App Distribution.

entries.question: Android says "App not installed" when I try to install the new RackTrack APK over the old one.
entries.answer:
This almost always means the new build was signed with a different key than the copy already on your phone, so Android will not treat it as an upgrade. (Installing an older build over a newer one produces the same message.)

Fix — remove the old copy first:
1. Uninstall the RackTrack that is on the phone: long-press the RackTrack icon and choose Uninstall, or go to Settings → Apps → RackTrack → Uninstall.
2. Install the new build again:
   - If you get RackTrack through the App Tester app (you receive an email and a push notification when a new build is ready), open App Tester, pick the latest RackTrack release and tap Download / Install.
   - If someone sent you the APK file directly, open it from your Downloads and tap Install. You may need to allow "Install unknown apps" for the browser or file manager you are installing from.
3. Sign in again. Nothing else is lost — your scans, racks and history are stored on the RackTrack server, not on the phone.

If it still refuses: check you have enough free storage, and re-download the file — a download that was cut off partway gives the same "App not installed" message.

If it keeps failing after a clean uninstall and a fresh download, contact your RackTrack administrator with the phone model and Android version.
symptoms: App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package
entries.rootCause: The APK is a debug build (gradlew assembleDebug); a debug keystore differing from the one used for the installed copy makes Android reject the upgrade. versionCode is currently 17 — installing an older-versionCode APK over a newer one is also refused.

evidence.snippet:
# 3. Compile the APK.
( cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-daemon )

APK="android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/racktrack.apk"

versionCode 17
versionName "1.0"
Installed Android Studio and produced a working APK file (~11 MB) with the tunnel address baked in.

This almost always means the new build was signed with a different key than the copy already on your phone, so Android will not treat it as an upgrade.
1. Uninstall the RackTrack that is on the phone: long-press the RackTrack icon and choose Uninstall, or go to Settings → Apps → RackTrack → Uninstall.
2. Install the new build again:
3. Sign in again.

entries.question: The app opened fine but every screen is blank or shows an error. Is my phone broken?
entries.answer:
No — this is almost never the phone. The RackTrack app on your phone is only the screen; all the real work (the AI that reads your rack photos, and the live switch reading) happens on a server on our side. If that server is off, or the app was built pointing at an address that has since changed, every screen fails at once even though the app itself launches normally. You may see "Load failed" on each screen.

What to do: report it to racktrackteam@sprintpark.com rather than reinstalling. Mention that the app opens but all screens fail — that tells us to check the server and the address baked into your build. A reinstall of the same build will not help, because the server address is fixed when the app is built; only a new build pointed at the current address will fix it.

One related case worth knowing: if photo scanning works but only the live switch screens (Ports, Cables, Trace, Network) are empty, that is also on our side, not your phone — but it is usually a different cause. Those screens read the switch directly, so they also need switch credentials configured, the switch reachable on the network, and (for Network) a Netdisco server set up. Messages like "The switch didn't respond" or "Lost the SSH session" point at that rather than at the app being broken.
symptoms: app opens but every screen fails
scanning works but Ports and Network are empty
entries.rootCause: The backend base URL (VITE_API_BASE) is compiled into the JS bundle at build time. A stopped server, or a rotated tunnel URL, makes every API call fail while the shell still launches.

evidence.snippet: App opens, screens are blank or error Not your phone. RackTrack talks to a server on our side — tell us and we'll check it.
App installs, then every screen fails Backend unreachable — not a TestFlight problem Check the Windows server and the tunnel URL baked into the build
**The Windows box must be on with `deploy/legacy-windows/start.ps1` running, or none of this works.**

entries.short: No — this is almost never the phone. The RackTrack app on your phone is only the screen; all the real work (the AI that reads your rack photos, and the live switch reading) happens on a server on our side.

entries.question: The app was working last week and now nothing loads. Nobody changed anything on my phone.
entries.answer:
This is almost always a server-side problem, not a phone problem — you're right that nothing changed on your device.

RackTrack's app talks to a backend server reached over a Cloudflare tunnel, and there are two things that can break that link:

1. The server or tunnel is simply down. The app only works while the host machine, the RackTrack server and the tunnel are all running. This is the most common cause, and it's fixed by the RackTrack team restarting the server — no new app build needed. Once it's back up, your existing app works again.

2. The server's address changed. The current deployment uses a temporary Cloudflare quick-tunnel, which is issued a brand-new random https://<random>.trycloudflare.com address every time it restarts. That address is compiled into the app you installed, so if the tunnel restarted, every installed copy stops reaching the server until a new build is issued.

Either way, there is nothing to do on the phone — reinstalling the same build will not help, and neither will clearing data. Report it to racktrackteam@sprintpark.com and mention roughly when it stopped working. If it's case 1 you'll be back up as soon as the server is restarted; if it's case 2 a rebuilt app has to be pushed out (a new TestFlight build on iPhone, a new APK on Android).
symptoms: no data on any screen after a period of working
entries.rootCause: deploy/legacy-windows/start.ps1 opens a `cloudflared tunnel --url` quick tunnel whose https://<random>.trycloudflare.com hostname changes on every restart, and that hostname is baked into the shipped bundle. The mobile build guard explicitly warns about this.

evidence.snippet:
Start-Process "$ProjectRoot\cloudflared.exe" -ArgumentList "tunnel --url http://localhost:3001" ...
if ($content -match "https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com") { ... $url | Set-Content "$ProjectRoot\current-url.txt" }

The APK has a web address baked in that points, through a Cloudflare tunnel, to the Mac's server. ... The address is random and changes if the Mac restarts — then the APK can't reach the server and we'd have to rebuild.

entries.short: This is almost always a server-side problem, not a phone problem — you're right that nothing changed on your device. RackTrack's app talks to a backend server over a Cloudflare tunnel, and either that server and tunnel are down, or the tunnel restarted and came back on a brand-new address the installed app does not know about.

entries.question: The camera doesn't start when I try to scan — I just get "Camera access denied".
entries.answer:
RackTrack shows "Camera access denied. Allow camera permission or use Upload." when it cannot open the camera. The most common cause is that the phone has not granted camera access — the permission prompt appears on first use and is easy to decline by accident.

Fix the permission:
- iPhone/iPad: Settings → RackTrack → turn Camera on. Then reopen RackTrack and try Scan again.
- Android: Settings → Apps → RackTrack → Permissions → Camera → Allow.

If the permission is already on and you still see the message, the camera is usually busy or unavailable rather than blocked. Close any other app or browser tab using the camera (video call, camera app), then reopen RackTrack. If you opened RackTrack from a plain http:// link rather than the installed app or an https:// address, the camera will not start at all — use the installed app.

Either way you can still scan without the camera: on the Scan screen use the Upload tab (it is the tab RackTrack opens on) and pick a photo you have already taken.

Note: a preview that stays black, or "Starting camera…" that never finishes, is a different problem — the camera did open but the preview did not start. Leave the Scan screen and come back, or switch between the Camera and Upload tabs to restart it.
symptoms: Camera access denied. Allow camera permission or use Upload.
entries.rootCause: navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia rejects when the OS-level camera permission is denied; ScanPage catches this and sets the fixed error string. iOS declares NSCameraUsageDescription so the prompt appears once on first use.

evidence.snippet:
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>RackTrack uses your camera to scan and photograph your equipment racks.</string>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
Camera does nothing Settings → RackTrack → turn Camera on. Easy to decline on first launch.

entries.short: RackTrack shows "Camera access denied. Allow camera permission or use Upload." when it cannot open the camera. The most common cause is that the phone has not granted camera access — the permission prompt appears on first use and is easy to decline by accident. On an iPhone or iPad, fix it under Settings → RackTrack → turn Camera on.

entries.question: What permissions does RackTrack ask for on my phone, and do I have to say yes?
entries.answer:
RackTrack asks for these, each with a plain reason shown in the prompt:

- Camera — "RackTrack uses your camera to scan and photograph your equipment racks." Required for the Camera tab on the Scan screen. Say yes, or scanning from the camera will not work (you can still use Upload).
- Photos — "RackTrack reads photos you select for offline rack analysis." Only needed when you pick an existing photo via Upload.
- Saving to Photos — "RackTrack saves annotated rack scans to your photo library when you choose to." Only when you deliberately save a result.
- Microphone — "RackTrack needs microphone access to record video scans of your rack." In practice the in-app video scan records picture only, so you should not normally see this prompt.

On Android the app additionally declares Internet and Camera. Everything else — no location, no contacts, no background tracking.
symptoms: what permissions does the app need
why does it want my photos
entries.rootCause: Permission strings are declared in the iOS Info.plist and the Android manifest. The in-app camera stream is opened with audio:false, so the microphone is not actually engaged by the video scan path.
