<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>RackTrack uses your camera to scan and photograph your equipment racks.</string>
<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>RackTrack needs microphone access to record video scans of your rack.</string>
<key>NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription</key>
<string>RackTrack saves annotated rack scans to your photo library when you choose to.</string>
<key>NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription</key>
<string>RackTrack reads photos you select for offline rack analysis.</string>

<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.camera" android:required="false" />

entries.short:
RackTrack asks for these, each with a plain reason shown in the prompt:
- Camera — "RackTrack uses your camera to scan and photograph your equipment racks." Required for the Camera tab on the Scan screen. Say yes, or scanning from the camera will not work (you can still use Upload).
- Photos — "RackTrack reads photos you select for offline rack analysis." Only needed when you pick an existing photo via Upload.

entries.question: I tried to record a video scan and got "Video recording is not supported in this browser".
entries.answer:
Your device or browser cannot record video from inside the app. On the Scan screen's Camera tab, switching to Video and tapping the shutter shows either "Video recording is not supported in this browser. Use Upload instead." or "Could not start video recording on this device."

Fix: record the video with your phone's normal Camera app, then in RackTrack go to the Scan screen, choose the Upload tab, select the VIDEO mode button, and pick the file.

Keep the clip between 1 and 120 seconds and under 340 MB. Anything over 340 MB is rejected by the server outright. If the clip is too short or too long, RackTrack warns you and offers Retake or "Proceed anyway" — but proceeding with an out-of-range clip usually gives poor results, so re-record instead.

Note: the VIDEO button under the Upload tab is a file picker, not a recorder — it has no record button. Only the Camera tab records.
symptoms: Video recording is not supported in this browser. Use Upload instead.
Could not start video recording on this device.
record button does nothing in VIDEO mode
entries.rootCause: The in-app recorder uses the browser MediaRecorder API; where MediaRecorder is absent or refuses every candidate mime type (video/mp4, video/webm variants), recording cannot start.

evidence.snippet:
const candidates = ['video/mp4','video/webm;codecs=vp9','video/webm;codecs=vp8','video/webm'];
for (const t of candidates) { if (typeof MediaRecorder !== 'undefined' && MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported(t)) return t; }

const MIN_DURATION = 1.0;
const MAX_DURATION = 120;
limits: { fileSize: 340 * 1024 * 1024 },

entries.short: Your device or browser cannot record video from inside the app. On the Scan screen's Camera tab, switching to Video and tapping the shutter shows either "Video recording is not supported in this browser. Use Upload instead." or "Could not start video recording on this device."

entries.question: My upload was rejected — it says the file is too large or an invalid file type.
entries.answer:
There are two hard limits on a rack scan upload:

- Size: 340 MB per file. A long 4K video will exceed this — record a shorter clip or drop the recording quality.
- Type: the file must be a recognised photo or video. Accepted extensions are jpg, jpeg, jfif, png, gif, webp, tif, tiff, avif, bmp, heic, heif for photos, and mp4, mov, webm, m4v, avi for video. Anything else is refused with "Invalid file type" (in the app you may see "Unsupported file type. Upload an image or video."). For video, stick to mp4, mov or webm — these are the formats the frame extractor handles.

iPhone HEIC photos are fine — RackTrack converts them to JPEG on the server and applies EXIF rotation.

Note: marketplace listing photos are a separate, stricter upload — 8 MB maximum, and only jpg, png, webp or heic. That one fails with "Only jpg / png / webp / heic images are accepted".
symptoms: Unsupported file type. Upload an image or video.
entries.rootCause: multer enforces a 340 MB fileSize limit and a whitelist-based fileFilter on the original filename extension; the client mirrors this with its own type check in validateMedia.

evidence.snippet:
// HEIC/HEIF (iPhone default): most browsers can't decode in JS.
// Skip client-side checks and let the server normalize + validate.

entries.short: There are two hard limits on a rack scan upload: - Size: 340 MB per file. A long 4K video will exceed this — record a shorter clip or drop the recording quality. - Type: the file must be a recognised photo or video.

entries.question: I got "Too many uploads — retry in 30s" while scanning a row of racks.
entries.answer:
RackTrack accepts up to 20 scan uploads per minute. Scanning a whole row back to back can hit that ceiling.

What to do: the message tells you how long to wait — wait that many seconds and scan again. The allowance refills continuously, so it is usually only a few seconds before you can shoot the next rack, not a full minute.

The scan you were trying to send was not accepted, so re-take or re-submit that one. Everything you scanned before it is safe and already saved — nothing you have already captured is lost.

One thing to know: for scan uploads this allowance is shared by everyone connecting from the same network, not tracked per person. If several technicians on the same site network are scanning at once, you can hit the limit sooner than you expect. Switching to a different phone on the same network will not give you a fresh allowance; pausing for a few seconds will.
symptoms: Too many uploads — retry in Ns
entries.rootCause: lib/rate_limit.js token bucket keyed by user id, default RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_MIN = 20, returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

evidence.snippet:
const DEFAULT_RATE = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_MIN) || 20;
const DEFAULT_BURST = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_BURST) || DEFAULT_RATE;

entries.short: RackTrack accepts up to 20 scan uploads per minute. Scanning a whole row back to back can hit that ceiling. What to do: the message tells you how long to wait — wait that many seconds and scan again.

entries.question: On Android, pressing Back closes RackTrack instead of going to the previous screen.
entries.answer:
That only happens on the two root screens. RackTrack maps the Android hardware Back button to in-app navigation: on any normal screen it takes you back one step. On the Home screen ("/") or the Login screen, Back exits the app — that is deliberate, so you are not trapped in the app.

If Back is closing the app from somewhere else, you are almost certainly on Home without realising it. Use the on-screen back arrow at the top of the page instead.

This applies to Android only; iPhone has no hardware back button.
symptoms: back kicks me to the home screen of the phone
entries.rootCause: AndroidBackHandler registers a Capacitor backButton listener that calls navigate(-1) except on '/' and '/login', where it calls CapApp.exitApp().
entries.short: That only happens on the two root screens. RackTrack maps the Android hardware Back button to in-app navigation: on any normal screen it takes you back one step. On the Home screen ("/") or the Login screen, Back exits the app — that is deliberate, so you are not trapped in the app.

entries.question: iOS asked me to trust an "Untrusted Developer" / asked about a profile. Should I?
entries.answer:
You should not see that on a genuine RackTrack install. RackTrack is delivered to iPhone and iPad through TestFlight, which uses Apple's own App Store signing — TestFlight apps never ask you to trust a developer profile in Settings.

If you are seeing an "Untrusted Enterprise Developer" prompt, or being asked to install a configuration profile, you have a copy of the app that did not come from TestFlight. Do not trust it. Delete it, and install RackTrack from your TestFlight invitation instead. If you are unsure where the copy came from, contact racktrackteam@sprintpark.com before opening it.
symptoms: asked to trust a developer in Settings → General → VPN & Device Management
asked to install a configuration profile
entries.rootCause: The shipped iOS build is exported with method app-store-connect and uploaded to TestFlight, so it carries App Store distribution signing and never triggers the enterprise/ad-hoc trust prompt. Any build that does trigger it was signed and distributed outside the sanctioned pipeline.

evidence.snippet:
<key>method</key>
<string>app-store-connect</string>
<key>signingStyle</key>
<string>automatic</string>

# 3. Archive  (-allowProvisioningUpdates lets Xcode create the distribution
#    cert + App Store profile automatically for this team)
xcodebuild -workspace ios/App/App.xcworkspace -scheme App -configuration Release ... CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic -allowProvisioningUpdates clean archive
RackTrack isn't in the App Store yet — it's a beta, so it arrives through Apple's testing app, TestFlight.

entries.short: You should not see that on a genuine RackTrack install. RackTrack is delivered to iPhone and iPad through TestFlight, which uses Apple's own App Store signing — TestFlight apps never ask you to trust a developer profile in Settings.

entries.question: I had to reinstall the app and now it wants me to sign in again. Did I lose my scans?
entries.answer:
No, your scans are safe. Everything — scans, results, port history — lives on the server, not on your phone. Sign back in and your full scan history is on your Profile page exactly as before.

All the app keeps on the phone is your sign-in token, the flag remembering you have seen the first-run walkthrough, and a couple of small view preferences. Deleting and reinstalling the app clears that, so you sign in again and the four-step first-run walkthrough may reappear once. Installing a normal update over the top (TestFlight Update, or a new APK over the old one) does not sign you out.

You will also be asked to sign in again if you have not used the app for a long time — a sign-in lasts 30 days.
entries.rootCause: The auth token is persisted in WebView localStorage under 'rt_authToken' and the tour completion flag likewise; an uninstall clears the WebView data store. Server-side JWTs are issued with a 30-day TTL.

evidence.snippet: const TOKEN_KEY = 'rt_authToken';
const TOKEN_TTL  = '30d';
| How long you stay signed in | 30 days |

entries.short: No, your scans are safe. Everything — scans, results, port history — lives in RackTrack, not on your phone. Sign back in and your full scan history is on your Profile page exactly as before.

entries.question: Testers report the app installs but scan result images render broken or blank.
entries.answer:
Admin/internal. This is the ngrok interstitial issue. A free ngrok tunnel serves a ~2.8 KB HTML warning page (with HTTP 200) instead of the real bytes to any client whose user-agent looks like a browser — and a Capacitor WebView does.

Two separate fixes are required and both must be present in the shipped build:

1. A fetch interceptor adds the ngrok-skip-browser-warning: true header. This fixes API calls only.
2. A user-agent override fixes images. Image tags cannot send custom headers, so no JavaScript can rescue them — without the override every scan result image, overlay and rack photo renders broken.

Both are currently present in the app. If a build regresses, verify on a phone: the result image rendering is the check that catches it.
symptoms: blank rack photo in the app
entries.rootCause: Free ngrok serves an HTML browser-warning interstitial at HTTP 200 to browser-like user-agents. The header skip fixes fetch; only the Capacitor user-agent override fixes loads.

evidence.snippet: Free ngrok serves a **2.8 KB HTML warning page** instead of the real response to any client whose user-agent looks like a browser — and a Capacitor WebView does. It returns **HTTP 200** ... The **user-agent override** (1a) is what fixes **images** — `` tags *cannot send custom headers*

import { installFetchInterceptor } from './utils/api.js';

installFetchInterceptor();

entries.short: Broken scan images come from the free ngrok warning page; the build needs both the skip-warning header (API) and the user-agent override (images).

entries.question: How do I ship a new build to testers, and what stops a build from being accepted?
entries.answer:
Admin/internal.

iOS (Mac only — Xcode does not run on Windows):
1. Bump the build number (there are exactly two occurrences to update). TestFlight rejects a duplicate build number outright. Leave the marketing version (1.0) alone; read the current build value out before you bump it, since older setup notes may be stale.
2. Sync the web assets into the iOS project.
3. Build the IPA, passing your Team ID and the backend API URL. The API URL argument is optional: if omitted, the build falls back to the current tunnel URL, and only fails when neither is available. Whatever URL it ends up with is checked first — the build hard-fails on an empty, localhost, or non-HTTPS value, and warns (but does not fail) on a temporary quick-tunnel URL because that changes on every restart.
4. Ship the IPA with release notes — release notes are mandatory (it stops and shows usage without them). It uploads to App Store Connect and then sets the TestFlight "What to Test" text. Apple processing is usually 5–30 minutes; nobody can install until it clears.

Android:
Ship the APK with release notes. It builds the web bundle with the backend URL baked in (falling back to a default backend if that isn't set), then builds and pushes the APK to the Firebase App Distribution "testers" group (which you can override). You'll need to be logged in to Firebase and have a Firebase Android App ID configured. Testers get an email plus a push in the App Tester app. Android can also be built on Windows; iOS cannot.

Common blockers: a duplicate build number; an empty, localhost, or non-HTTPS backend URL (iOS path); a missing App Store Connect API key; the Firebase CLI missing or not logged in; or no Firebase App ID.
entries.rootCause: Release tooling enforces preconditions: check-api-base.mjs guards the API base, TestFlight rejects duplicate CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION, ship-ipa.sh requires the App Store Connect .p8 key, ship-apk.sh requires the Firebase CLI and App ID.

evidence.snippet: TestFlight **rejects a duplicate build number outright.** You are on **1.0 (4)**, so the next one is **1.0 (5)**. In `client/ios/App/App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`, change **both** occurrences: CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 4;   →   CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 5;

[ -f "$IPA" ] || { echo "✗ $IPA not found — run ./make-ipa.sh first."; exit 1; }
BUILD_NUM="$(grep -m1 -oE 'CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = [0-9]+' "$PBXPROJ" | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"
...
echo "✗ $KEY_FILE not found (looked in $KEY_DIR and the repo root)."

command -v firebase >/dev/null || { echo "✖ firebase CLI missing:  npm i -g firebase-tools"; exit 1; }
firebase login:list 2>/dev/null | grep -q '@' || { echo "✖ Not logged in.  Run:  firebase login"; exit 1; }
Usually 5–30 minutes. You get an email when it clears. Until then it shows as processing and no one can install it.
> **Important:** the Windows box replaces the **backend server** only. **Building the iOS app still requires the Mac** (Xcode only runs on macOS). Android APKs can be built on Windows.

entries.short: How to ship iOS (Mac-only) and Android tester builds, plus what blocks one: duplicate build number, bad backend URL, missing key/App ID, or Firebase login.

entries.question: Which live features will never work for a remote tester, no matter what we fix in the app?
entries.answer:
Internal. The phone never touches the switch — the server does. Every live feature depends on the backend host being able to reach the equipment's private LAN; no client-side change affects this.

Works on any internet connection (assuming a hosted HTTPS backend exists): sign in/sign up, scan (photo, multi-image stitch, video), AI detection, results/overview, port location from the photo, specifications, firmware lookup, SFP advisor, reports, share, marketplace, profile/history.

Will NOT work for a remote tester on a cloud backend: Live switch Ports tab, Cables view, Trace tab, Drift polling, switch console — all need server→switch SSH on the private LAN (e.g. 192.168.1.x) — and the Netdisco Network view, which needs the backend to reach the Netdisco discovery server on that same LAN (HTTP, not SSH).

Do not triage these as app or install problems. The tell is: photo scanning works fine but only the live screens are empty. Beta workaround is a backend on a machine with LAN/VPN access to the switch, exposed via an HTTPS tunnel; the production answer is an on-prem collector.
symptoms: Ports tab empty for a remote tester
Drift stuck on Waiting for first poll…
live screens empty while scanning works
entries.rootCause: Live-switch features require server→switch SSH reachability on a private network (e.g. 192.168.1.x). A cloud-hosted or tunnel-only backend outside that network cannot reach it; no client-side change affects this.

evidence.snippet: Live Network Switch (Ports tab) Won't work — All of these need the server to SSH into a switch on a private LAN (192.168.1.x). A cloud-hosted backend cannot reach it. ... Cables view / Trace tab / Drift / Switch console / Network view (Netdisco) Won't work

RackTrack's photo scanning works anywhere you have internet. The live switch screens — ports, cables, trace — read your actual equipment through a server on our network. If those screens are empty while scanning works fine, it's our server, not your phone.

Phone app  ──HTTPS──>  api.racktrack.ai  ──port-forward──>  Windows PC (always on, GPU)
 ... └── SSH ──> switch 192.168.1.33
- Windows PC is **always on**, has a **GPU** (faster AI), and is on the **same office network as the switch**.

entries.short: Internal. The phone never touches the switch — the server does. Every live feature depends on the backend host being able to reach the equipment's private LAN; no client-side change affects this.

entries.question: The sign-in screen just says "rate_limited" — what does that mean and how long do I wait?
entries.answer:
You tried to sign in too many times in a short burst, so RackTrack temporarily throttled attempts for your account.

What's happening: the server allows 20 attempts back-to-back, then refills at 10 attempts per minute — roughly one attempt every 6 seconds. The error message may say "Too many uploads — retry in 6s"; ignore the word "uploads", the same throttle code is reused for sign-in.

Steps to fix:
1. Wait about 10 seconds and try once more. Extra taps while you're throttled are simply rejected — they don't make the wait longer — but they won't get you in either, so just wait.
2. If you're not sure of your password, stop guessing and use "Forgot password?" instead.
3. This is per-account, not per-device. Your colleagues can still sign in normally, and switching to another phone or Wi-Fi will not clear it — only waiting does.

Good news: your account is NOT locked. RackTrack has no lockout requiring an administrator to unlock you. The throttle clears on its own.
symptoms: Sign in stops responding after many rapid attempts
entries.rootCause: app.js mounts authLimit (token bucket, rate 10/min, burst 20, keyed by the lowercased username/email in the request body) in front of /api/auth/login, /signup, /forgot-password, /reset-password and /login-with-code. The 429 body is {error:'rate_limited', message:'Too many uploads — retry in Ns'}; AuthContext.callApi throws data.error, so the raw token 'rate_limited' is what the login form renders.

evidence.snippet:
app.use(['/api/auth/login', '/api/auth/signup', '/api/auth/forgot-password',
  '/api/auth/reset-password', '/api/auth/login-with-code'], authLimit);

entries.short:
You tried to sign in too many times in a short burst, so RackTrack temporarily throttled attempts for your account.
1. Wait about 10 seconds and try once more.
2. If you're not sure of your password, stop guessing and use "Forgot password?" instead.
3. This is per-account, not per-device.

entries.question: I signed in successfully but I'm stuck on a "Waiting for approval" screen and can't reach anything.
entries.answer:
Your sign-in worked. What's blocking you is that your organization has not been approved yet.

When you create an organization by signing up, RackTrack files it as a request. A RackTrack platform owner has to approve it before anyone in it can scan racks or use the rest of the app.

What you'll see: a screen titled "Waiting for approval" with the text "Your request to create <your organization> has been sent to the platform owner." The page re-checks by itself every few seconds, and there's a "Check now" button if you're impatient.

Steps to fix:
1. Contact the RackTrack platform owner directly (by phone/email/chat). They are NOT emailed automatically when you sign up — if nobody tells them, nobody approves you.
2. Leave the app open, or come back later; the moment they approve, the screen moves you straight into the Scan page. You do not need to sign in again.
3. If you were meant to join a team that already exists, you signed up the wrong way — see the entry about invite links.

Two related screens use the same page:
- "Request not approved" — the owner rejected the request.
- "Organization deactivated" — the owner switched your whole organization off. It comes back automatically if they reactivate it.
symptoms: This page checks automatically every few seconds.
entries.rootCause: Self-signup sets organizations.status = 'pending' at the verify step. Client-side orgNotActive() in App.jsx redirects any non-owner whose organization.status !== 'active' to /pending, and server-side requireAuth returns 403 'Your organization is awaiting approval' for every route outside /api/auth/*.

evidence.snippet: timer.current = setInterval(check, 12000); ... title: 'Waiting for approval', body: <>Your request to create {orgName} has been sent to the platform owner.

entries.short:
Your sign-in worked. What's blocking you is that your organization has not been approved yet.
1. Contact the RackTrack platform owner directly (by phone/email/chat).
2. Leave the app open, or come back later; the moment they approve, the screen moves you straight into the Scan page.
3. If you were meant to join a team that already exists, you signed up the wrong way — see the entry about invite links.

entries.question: How long does my sign-in last? Why was I suddenly asked to sign in again?
entries.answer:
A RackTrack sign-in lasts 30 days. After that the app signs you out and shows the Sign in screen again. That's normal and expected — just sign in again.

RackTrack does not silently renew your session in the background: there is no refresh step. The 30 days start when you sign in and don't get extended by using the app, so even a technician who scans racks daily will be asked to sign in roughly once a month.

You will ALSO be signed out immediately (before the 30 days) if:
- An administrator deleted your account. The app sees "User no longer exists".
- The RackTrack server was reinstalled or its signing key was replaced (ask your admin).
- You cleared your browser's site data, used a private/incognito window, or cleared the app's storage on the phone.

What you will NOT be signed out by:
- Closing the app, switching to another app, or restarting your phone.
- Losing signal. Going offline keeps you signed in on purpose.
- Changing your own password (existing sessions keep working).
symptoms: Bounced to the Sign in screen without warning
Session ends about a month after signing in
entries.rootCause: TOKEN_TTL = '30d' passed to jwt.sign as expiresIn. requireAuth calls jwt.verify with no clockTolerance and no refresh path; any failure returns 401. api.js authFetch dispatches 'rt:auth-expired' on any 401, and AuthContext clears token+user in response.

evidence.snippet:
const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || loadOrCreateSecret();
const TOKEN_TTL  = '30d';

const onExpired = () => setState({ token: null, user: null });
    window.addEventListener('rt:auth-expired', onExpired);

entries.short: A RackTrack sign-in lasts 30 days. After that the app signs you out and shows the Sign in screen again. That's normal and expected — just sign in again. RackTrack does not silently renew your session in the background: there is no refresh step.

entries.question: The Sign in screen shows something like "Load failed" or "Failed to fetch" instead of an error about my password.
entries.answer:
That is not a password problem. Your device could not reach the RackTrack server at all, so it never got as far as checking your credentials.

How to tell the two apart:
- "Invalid username or password" — or "Invalid organization or credentials" if you filled in the optional Organization field — means the server answered and rejected you. Fix your credentials (and check the Organization name, since a wrong org name produces the same message as a wrong password).
- "This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator." also means the server answered — that is an account state, not a network fault.
- "Load failed", "Failed to fetch", "NetworkError", or "Request failed (502/503/504)" = the server did not answer. Your credentials were never tested.

Steps to fix:
1. Check you actually have signal or Wi-Fi. Open any website in your phone browser to confirm.
2. If you're in a datacenter, you may be on a restricted network. Switch to mobile data and try again — this is by far the most common cause in the field.
3. If you're on a corporate VPN or guest Wi-Fi that blocks unknown sites, get off it or ask your network team to allow the RackTrack address.
4. If everyone at your site is affected at the same time, the RackTrack server or its public address is down — contact your administrator rather than retrying.

While you're offline you cannot sign in for the first time — RackTrack has no offline sign-in. If you were already signed in, the app deliberately keeps you signed in when the server is unreachable, so you won't be thrown out to the login screen while out of coverage. You are only signed out if the server explicitly rejects your session.
symptoms: Error text on Sign in that doesn't mention the password
Spinner then a red bar with a browser-style message
entries.rootCause: AuthContext.callApi does a bare fetch; a transport failure rejects with the browser's own TypeError (WebKit: 'Load failed', Chromium: 'Failed to fetch') and LoginPage renders err.message verbatim in the error box. Non-JSON/gateway responses fall through to `Request failed (${res.status})`. There is no offline credential store — login always requires a live round-trip.
entries.short:
That is not a password problem. Your device could not reach RackTrack at all, so it never got as far as checking your credentials.
1. Check you actually have signal or Wi-Fi. Open any website in your phone browser to confirm.
2. If you're in a datacenter, you may be on a restricted network.

entries.question: The verification code from my signup email says it's expired, and now "Resend" says there's no pending signup.
entries.answer:
The 6-digit code you get when creating an account is only valid for 1 minute. The email says so: "It expires in 1 minute."

There's a trap worth knowing: if you tap "Verify" AFTER the minute has passed, RackTrack throws away your half-finished signup entirely. You'll see "Verification code has expired — sign up again", and if you then press "Resend" you get "No pending signup for that email" — because there's nothing left to resend to.

What to do:

- If it just expired: tap the back arrow at the top left to return to the signup form. Your details are still filled in — just press the signup button again to get a fresh code. No account was created, so nothing conflicts and you can reuse the same email.
- If you're still waiting on the email and haven't submitted a code yet: press "Resend" (under "Didn't get it?"). That works and gives you a fresh minute.
- Check your spam/junk folder first — the mail comes from your organization's RackTrack sending address.

To avoid it next time: open your email app first, then start the signup, so the code is waiting for you. The code boxes support your phone's one-time-code autofill, so if your keyboard offers the code as a suggestion, tap it instead of switching apps. If the code doesn't appear that way, just read it and type it — you have a full minute from when the email is sent.
symptoms: Verification code has expired — sign up again
No pending signup for that email
Code arrives but is already too late
entries.rootCause: pending_signups.code_expires_at = Date.now() + 60_000. POST /api/auth/verify DELETEs the pending_signups row when the code has expired, so the subsequent POST /api/auth/resend-code finds no row and 404s.

evidence.snippet:
const pending = db.prepare('SELECT * FROM pending_signups WHERE email = ?').get(emailNorm);
    if (!pending) { ... return res.status(404).json({ error: 'No pending signup for that email' }); }

Enter this code in the app to finish creating your account.
It expires in 1 minute.

entries.short: The 6-digit code you get when creating an account is only valid for 1 minute. The email says so: "It expires in 1 minute." If it has just expired, tap the back arrow at the top left to return to the signup form — your details are still filled in, so pressing the signup button again gets you a fresh code.

entries.question: I used "Forgot password?" but the reset code never arrived.
entries.answer:
The Forgot password screen always shows the same message — "If an account exists for that email, a 6-digit code is on its way." — whether or not the email is registered. That's deliberate privacy protection, but it means a missing code has several possible causes:

1. That email address has no RackTrack account. Very common if you signed up with a work address but typed your personal one, or if your admin created your account under a different address. Ask your admin which email is on your account.
2. The code went to spam/junk.
3. The RackTrack server's outgoing email isn't working. Unlike signup, the Forgot password screen does NOT warn you when the email fails to send — it reports success either way.

Steps to fix:
1. Check spam/junk, and search your mail for "RackTrack verification code".
2. Try again with any other email address you might have used.
3. Remember the code only lasts 1 minute — if it arrives slowly, tap "Resend" on the code screen and use the newest one.
4. If nothing arrives on any address, contact your organization admin. They can set a new password for you directly from the Members list, which bypasses email completely.
symptoms: If an account exists for that email, a 6-digit code is on its way.
Sent a fresh code. (but still nothing received)
No pending reset for that email — request a new code
entries.rootCause: POST /api/auth/forgot-password always responds 200 with the same shape, whether the user exists or not, and does not surface SMTP failure (it only records status 'partial' in the audit log). Signup/resend by contrast return 502 when the send fails.

evidence.snippet:
const code = genCode();
      const expiresAt = Date.now() + 60 * 1000; // 1 minute

entries.short: The Forgot password screen always shows the same message — "If an account exists for that email, a 6-digit code is on its way." — whether or not the email is registered. So a missing code can mean that address has no RackTrack account, that the code went to spam or junk, or that RackTrack's outgoing email is not working.

entries.question: What exactly does the password reset flow do, and can I get in without changing my password?
entries.answer:
Yes. The reset flow has four steps and you can stop after step three:

1. "Forgot password" — enter your email, tap "Send reset code".
2. "Enter code" — type the 6-digit code. It expires in 1 minute; there's a "Resend" link. Checking the code here does NOT use it up.
3. "Code verified" — RackTrack asks "Change your password? You're signed in either way."
   - Tap "No, take me to the app" and you're signed in with your existing password unchanged.
   - Tap "Yes, change password" to continue.
4. "New password" — type it twice. The strength bar must be full.

Either way you end up signed in immediately (a 30-day session) — no second trip to the Sign in screen.

Your new password must have at least 8 characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character. If any are missing the screen tells you which one (for example "Password must contain a special character") or shows "Password is too weak."

One caution: the code is single-use once you finish — BOTH finishing paths use it up, including "No, take me to the app". If you back out of the screen after step 3 without tapping either button, request a fresh code.

entries.question: Is there Single Sign-On, Microsoft/Google login, or two-factor authentication?
entries.answer:
No. RackTrack has exactly two ways to sign in:

1. Username or email + password on the Sign in screen. (The screen also has an "Organization" field — it is optional. Leave it blank unless your admin told you otherwise; it only matters when the same username exists in more than one organization.)
2. A one-time 6-digit code emailed to you via "Forgot password?" — after you enter the code you're asked "Want to change your password?", and choosing "No, take me to the app" signs you in without changing it.

There is no "Sign in with Microsoft", no "Sign in with Google", no SAML/SSO, and no authenticator-app or SMS two-factor step. If someone told you to look for an SSO button, they're thinking of a different system.

Two things that look like SSO but aren't:
- The 6-digit codes at signup and password reset are email verification, not two-factor. They never appear on a normal sign-in.
- On the Firmware and Switch screens, RackTrack links out to switch vendors' own login pages (Cisco, Juniper, etc.). Those are the vendors' logins, not RackTrack's.

So if you've lost your password, the email reset code is the only self-service route back in. Otherwise your organization admin can set a new password for you — and if you're a regular member, your site manager can do it too.
symptoms: Looking for an SSO or 'Sign in with…' button that doesn't exist
Expecting an authenticator-app prompt after entering the password
entries.rootCause: The auth surface exposed by AuthContext is login / signup / verifyCode / resendCode / forgotPassword / verifyResetCode / resetPassword / loginWithCode. No OIDC/SAML/TOTP dependency or route exists; the only OAuth in the codebase is eBay/Amazon marketplace seller linking, and the only SSO URLs are outbound vendor links.

entries.question: I want to join my company's existing RackTrack team, but signing up created a brand-new organization stuck waiting for approval.
entries.answer:
That's the expected behaviour, and it's the single most common first-time setup mistake. "Create an organization" on the Sign in screen is for setting up a NEW team. New sign-ups can never join an existing organization on their own — once you enter the emailed verification code, signup always creates a fresh organization (named after the company name you typed) plus a "Main Site", makes you its admin, and files it as pending for platform-owner approval.

The Sign in screen actually spells this out under "How to get access":
- "Setting up your own team? Tap Create an organization above."
- "Joining an existing team? Ask your organization admin for an invite link, or a username & password — new sign-ups can't join an existing organization on their own."

Steps to fix:
1. Ask your organization admin (or site manager) for either an invite link or a username and password they create for you.
2. If you already went through signup by mistake, don't wait on the approval screen — that organization is a dead end for you. Let your admin or the RackTrack platform owner know so they can reject or delete it; it won't disappear on its own.
3. Open the invite link, confirm the pre-filled email, choose a username and create a password, and you're straight into your team's site.

There is no code path in signup that attaches to an existing organization; joining requires an invite or admin-created member.

entries.question: Signup fails at the first step — it won't accept my email, username, company or password.
entries.answer:
The "Create an organization" form checks each field and tells you exactly which one it doesn't like. The rules are:

- Email — must look like name@company.com. Error: "Enter a valid email." or "Valid email required".
- Username — 3 to 32 characters, only letters, digits and the symbols . _ - (no spaces, no @). Error: "Username 3–32 chars (letters, digits, . _ -)."
- Organization name — at least 2 characters, required. Error: "Organization name is required."
- Password — at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character. The strength bar tells you which rule is still missing ("Need …"), and turns into "✓ Strong password" when all five are met. Errors: "Password is too weak." or "Passwords do not match."

Already-taken values give:
- "An account with that email already exists" — go to Sign in and use "Forgot password?".
- "That username is taken" — usernames are unique across the whole of RackTrack, not just your company, so common ones like "admin" or "tech" are often gone. Try adding your surname.

entries.question: Signup says "Could not send verification email — try again in a minute" and I never get a code.
entries.answer:
This message means RackTrack itself could not hand your verification email to a mail server. It is a server-side problem, not something wrong with your address or your phone. You will see it on both the signup step and when you tap "Resend".

What NOT to do: retrying repeatedly won't help if the mail account is misconfigured — RackTrack already tries every configured mail provider (including the backup one, if your administrator set one up) before showing you this error. After about 20 rapid signup attempts you'll also hit the sign-up throttle.

Steps to fix:
1. Wait a minute and try once — brief mail-provider hiccups do clear.
2. If it persists, this needs your RackTrack administrator: the server's outgoing mail settings (SMTP) are broken, the mail password has expired, or no mail server is configured at all.
3. In the meantime, ask your organization admin to create your account directly from the Organizations console, or send you an invite link — both paths mark your email as verified automatically and skip the code entirely, so you can start working today.
symptoms: Could not send verification email — try again in a minute
No signup code arrives on any address
entries.rootCause: sendVerificationEmail() iterates the configured nodemailer providers (SMTP_* primary, SMTP_FALLBACK_* optional) and returns false when all fail or when neither is configured; /api/auth/signup and /api/auth/resend-code then return 502. Invite acceptance and admin-created members never call it.
entries.short:
This message means RackTrack itself could not hand your verification email to a mail system.
1. Wait a minute and try once — brief mail-provider hiccups do clear.
2. If it persists, this needs your RackTrack administrator: RackTrack's outgoing mail settings (SMTP) are broken, the mail password has expired, or no mail system is configured at all.

entries.question: I was signed in, and now everything I tap throws me back to the Sign in screen.
entries.answer:
RackTrack signs you out the moment the server tells it your session is no longer valid. The usual causes, in order of likelihood:

1. Your 30-day session ran out. Just sign in again.
2. Your account was deleted by an administrator. Signing in again will show "Invalid username or password". Contact your admin.
3. The RackTrack server's security key was regenerated — this happens if the server was rebuilt without keeping its existing data folder, or an administrator changed the signing secret. It invalidates every existing session for everyone at once. If your colleagues were all kicked out at the same moment, this is it — just sign in again. (A routine server restart, or moving the server while keeping its data, does NOT do this.)
4. You cleared your browser data / used a private window / cleared the app's storage on your phone. Your saved session lives in the browser's local storage; wiping it wipes the session.

Steps to fix: sign in again on the Sign in screen.
- If it says "Invalid username or password", your account may have been deleted — try "Forgot password?", and if that also fails, ask your organization admin whether your account still exists.
- If it says "This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator.", your account was switched off by an admin. "Forgot password?" will not help — only your admin can reactivate you. (Note that deactivation doesn't kick you out mid-shift; you'll only discover it the next time you sign in.)
- If you land on a "waiting for approval" screen instead of the app, that's your organization's status, not your session — no need to sign in again.

What does NOT sign you out: going offline, poor signal, closing the app, restarting the phone, or your phone's clock being wrong. If the server is simply unreachable, RackTrack deliberately keeps you signed in. Session expiry is judged by the server's clock, not your device's.
symptoms: Whole team logged out at the same time
entries.rootCause: Any 401 from an authFetch call fires the 'rt:auth-expired' event, which clears token and user in AuthContext, so ProtectedRoute redirects to /login. 401 sources: expired 30-day JWT, deleted user row, and a changed/regenerated JWT signing secret (JWT_SECRET env or server/data/jwt.secret). Session state lives only in localStorage keys rt_authToken / rt_authUser.

entries.question: Two of us share a tablet and signing in as one person signs the other out. Can we both stay signed in?
entries.answer:
No. RackTrack stores exactly one session per browser or per app install. When a second person signs in, their session replaces the first person's — the first person is silently signed out and will need to sign in again.

This is also why the app deliberately forgets "the last rack you were looking at" on every sign-in: so the next technician doesn't open the previous technician's scan by mistake.

Options if you share a device:
- Tap the sign-out icon in the top-right of the Profile screen (it asks "Sign out?" to confirm) before handing the device over. This is the tidy way, and it makes sure scans are attributed to the right person.
- Use separate browser profiles, or one browser window plus one private window, if you're on a desktop or tablet browser.
- On phones, each person should use their own device — the installed app has one session slot.

Remember scans are recorded against whoever is signed in, so sharing a session makes the audit trail and scan history wrong.
symptoms: Signed out when a colleague signs in on the shared tablet
Scans attributed to the wrong technician
entries.rootCause: AuthContext persists a single {rt_authToken, rt_authUser} pair to localStorage and overwrites it on every successful login; there is no multi-account store. login() also broadcasts rt:rack-id-changed with null to drop the previous session's remembered rack.

entries.question: The installed phone app can't sign in at all — every attempt fails instantly — but the same login works in a web browser.
entries.answer:
The installed app has the RackTrack server address baked in at build time. If that address has changed since your copy of the app was built, the app is calling a server that no longer exists and can never sign in, no matter how correct your password is.

This happens in RackTrack's pre-production setup whenever the server's public address changes — most often when the server is reached through a temporary Cloudflare quick-tunnel, which mints a brand-new address every time the server is restarted, but also after any move to a different tunnel or host.

How you can recognise it:
- Sign-in fails immediately with a network-style message ("Load failed" / "Failed to fetch"), never "Invalid username or password".
- The same account signs in fine in a normal browser pointed at the current address.
- Everyone using that app build fails; nobody using the browser does.

Steps to fix:
1. Ask your administrator for the current RackTrack address, and open it in your phone's browser as a temporary workaround.
2. The real fix is a new app build: your administrator rebuilds and redistributes the app with the current address (Android testers receive it as a Firebase App Distribution update; iOS testers via TestFlight).
3. Don't uninstall and reinstall the old build — it will have the same dead address.

Ask your administrator to move to a stable, named address rather than a quick tunnel if the app is being distributed to a team; that stops the problem recurring on every restart.
symptoms: App-only sign-in failure while browser works
Load failed immediately on tapping Sign in
Whole tester group cannot sign in after a server restart
App worked yesterday, broken today with no change to the account

Quick Cloudflare tunnels mint a new https://<random>.trycloudflare.com on each deploy/legacy-windows/start.ps1 run and write it to current-url.txt; the packaged app keeps pointing at the previous one until rebuilt. check-api-base.mjs explicitly warns about this at build time.

entries.question: [Admin] Nobody can sign in from the web app after we moved to production — the login page shows network errors, not credential errors.
entries.answer:
Check CORS and the API base before you look at accounts. Three misconfigurations produce this symptom, and all leave the browser reporting a network failure rather than a 401:

1. CORS allow-list. In production, an origin that isn't listed in your CORS allow-list is answered without CORS headers, so the browser blocks the login response before your app code can read it — you see a CORS error, not a credential error. Fix: set the CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS setting to the exact scheme+host+port your users load, comma-separated (e.g. https://app.example.com). The setting name is CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. Older docs said CORS_ORIGINS, which the app doesn't use and does nothing.

2. A NODE_ENV value that isn't literally "production". The environment-file loader is a minimal parser: it skips lines that start with #, but it does not strip inline comments — it takes everything after the first "=" verbatim (only trimming surrounding whitespace). So NODE_ENV=production   # must be production becomes the string "production   # must be production", which fails the "production" comparison and leaves the server in dev mode. Put comments on their own line. Consequences of dev mode: raw error details are no longer hidden, and the dev-only mock-route branch activates. Note the precise CORS behaviour — dev mode reflects *any* origin only when the CORS allow-list is empty. If you set the allow-list correctly but botched NODE_ENV, the list is non-empty so origins are still enforced, and CORS will not be your login symptom; look at cause 3 instead.

3. A stale localhost API base in the web build. If the bundle was built with an API base of http://localhost:3001 and is then served over an https tunnel, every call is blocked as mixed content. The client self-heals this specific case: it falls back to same-origin when the API base points at localhost or 127.0.0.1 but the serving host is neither. That guard is anchored to localhost/127.0.0.1 only — an API base pointing at a wrong *non-localhost* host is not self-healed and must be rebuilt.

Verify with the app's version check (unauthenticated — it returns the running commit and server start time) to confirm which build is live, and the health check for liveness. Both stay reachable even when the rest of the app is degraded.
symptoms: Load failed / Failed to fetch on the login page in production
CORS policy errors in the browser console for /api/auth/login
Works from localhost, fails from the public URL
entries.rootCause: app.js builds the CORS allow-list from CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and only reflects arbitrary origins when the list is empty AND NODE_ENV !== 'production'; a non-allow-listed origin gets cb(null,false). Separately, api.js only rewrites an API_BASE that matches http(s)://localhost|127.0.0.1.

... # The variable is CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS — app.js:260 reads that name, not CORS_ORIGINS, which this file used to document.

entries.short: Post-production login network errors are usually the CORS allow-list, a NODE_ENV that isn't exactly "production", or a stale localhost API base.

entries.question: [Internal] Does changing or resetting a password kick existing sessions out?
entries.answer:
No. RackTrack's sessions are stateless JWTs with no server-side session table, no token version/generation column on users, and no denylist. Consequences when handling a support case:

- After a password reset (self-service or admin-set), any token already issued for that user id keeps working until its 30-day expiry. A stolen or shared device is NOT logged out by changing the password. (The reset endpoint only rewrites password_hash, then mints an additional fresh token.)
- Deactivating the account (users.active = 0) also does NOT invalidate existing tokens — requireAuth only checks that the user row exists, not that it is active. The active flag is enforced solely at /api/auth/login. Deleting the user is the only immediate per-user revocation (requireAuth then 401s with 'User no longer exists').
- Changing an organization's status away from 'active' (pending/rejected/inactive) DOES take effect immediately for existing tokens: requireAuth's orgBlocked() gate 403s every authenticated route except /api/auth/* — BUT orgBlocked() exempts two cases, so this is not a general containment lever: users with role 'owner' are never gated (owners have no organization), and any user row with a null organization_id is never gated. Suspending an org will not restrict an owner account.
- The only global revocation lever is rotating JWT_SECRET / deleting server/data/jwt.secret, which signs everyone out at once.

So for a lost-device or compromised-account report, the correct action is: delete the user (or, for an owner account or a broad compromise, rotate the secret) — not merely reset the password, deactivate the user, or suspend the organization.

Deactivated user's existing app session keeps working
Support asks how to force-logout a device
entries.rootCause: makeToken embeds only sub/username/tenantId/organizationId/role with a 30d expiry; requireAuth re-reads the user row for existence and the org gate but never checks users.active or any token-version field, and no revocation store exists.

Consequences when handling a support case: - After a password reset (self-service or admin-set), any token already issued for that user id keeps working until its 30-day expiry.

entries.question: I'm signed in fine but the Operations Console / Lab / Integrations / Marketplace tells me I'm not allowed. Is my login broken?
entries.answer:
No — your sign-in is working. Those screens are limited by role, and RackTrack keeps you signed in rather than sending you back to the Sign in screen.

Who can reach what:
- Operations Console (/dashboard): organization admins and the platform owner can open the page; everyone else is redirected to the home screen. If you are an org admin the page loads but says "Owner access required to view this dashboard." — the data behind it is platform-owner only.
- Lab (/lab): any signed-in user can open the page, but it shows "Restricted to platform owners." unless you are the platform owner. No lab data is ever sent to other roles.
- Integrations (/connections) and everything under Marketplace: organization admins and the platform owner only. Other roles are quietly redirected to the home screen instead of seeing the page.
- Everything else — scanning, results, ports, cables, topology, firmware, specifications, profile and history — is open to every signed-in member.

Steps to fix: if you genuinely need one of those screens, ask your organization admin to change your role (they can promote a member to site manager; only the platform owner can create organization admins, and only RackTrack staff hold the owner role). Signing out and back in isn't necessary and won't change anything, though it does refresh your role if it was just changed.

(Note for support: "Insufficient permissions" is the raw 403 response from the API — customers do not see that wording on screen.)

Dashboard or Lab page shows a refusal message
entries.rootCause: requireRole(...) runs requireAuth then 403s with 'Insufficient permissions' when req.user.role isn't in the allow-list; on the client, AdminRoute redirects any role other than org_admin/owner to '/' rather than to /login.

entries.question: My phone's date and time are wrong / I travelled across time zones. Will that stop me signing in?
entries.answer:
Almost certainly not. Every deadline in RackTrack's sign-in is measured by the server's clock, not your device's:

- Your 30-day session is checked on the server when it validates your sign-in.
- The 1-minute verification and reset codes are timed on the server.
- The 7-day invite links are timed on the server.

So a phone whose date is off by hours — or that has crossed time zones — will still sign in normally. If you're failing to sign in, look at the actual message on screen instead — see the entries on wrong credentials, expired codes and network failures.

Two things to be aware of:

- If your device's date is wrong by months or years, the secure connection to RackTrack itself can fail before sign-in is even attempted. You'll see a connection or network error rather than a password or code error. Setting your date and time back to automatic fixes it.
- Because codes are timed server-side, a code can look like it "expired instantly" if the email took more than a minute to reach you. That's slow mail delivery, not a clock problem — tap "Resend" and use the newest code immediately.

Verification code appears to expire immediately after arriving
Travel across time zones followed by a login problem

entries.question: After signing in I land on the Organizations console instead of the Scan screen (or the other way round). Did I sign in as the wrong person?
entries.answer:
No — RackTrack routes you by your role automatically, and there is no role picker on the Sign in screen.

- If you're a platform owner or an organization admin, signing in takes you straight to the Organizations console.
- Everyone else (site managers and members) goes to the Scan screen, or back to whatever page you were trying to open when you were asked to sign in.
- If your organization hasn't been approved yet (or was rejected or deactivated), you land on the "Waiting for approval" screen instead — whatever your role. Only the platform owner is never held there.

So landing somewhere unexpected usually means the account you signed in with has a different role than you assumed — for example, you signed up and created your own organization, which makes you its admin.

Steps to check: open Profile. It shows your username, email and your Site, and — if you're an owner or an organization admin — an "Administration" section with a link to the Owner Dashboard or Organization Dashboard. If that Administration section is there, you're an admin or the owner; if it isn't, you're a site manager or member. (Profile doesn't print your role as a label.) If the role is wrong, ask your organization admin to change it — only the platform owner can create or edit organization admins.

entries.question: I tapped Sign in and nothing happens — the button just spins.
entries.answer:
A spinning Sign in button means the request went out and RackTrack is still waiting for the server to answer. The button stays disabled until the answer (or the failure) comes back.

What to do:
1. Give it up to about a minute. On a weak datacenter signal the round-trip can be slow.
2. If it never resolves, close and reopen the app, then try again. (You can't double-submit while it's spinning — the button is disabled — but avoid many rapid retries: sign-in attempts are throttled per account, and once you exceed the limit you'll see the error "rate_limited" and need to wait a moment before trying again.)
3. If it hangs again, treat it as "server unreachable": check that you have working internet, and ask your administrator whether the RackTrack server is up. There is no client-side timeout on sign-in, so a dead connection will spin indefinitely rather than showing an error.

Also check the obvious: if you left the username or password box empty, RackTrack does not send anything at all and instead shows "Enter your username and password." straight away. The Organization box is optional and can be left blank.
symptoms: Sign in button spinner never stops
No error message appears at all
entries.rootCause: LoginPage disables the submit button on the `loading` flag, which AuthContext.login only clears in a finally block after the fetch settles; a stalled connection leaves the promise pending indefinitely (no client-side timeout is set on the login fetch). Empty fields short-circuit before any request is made.
entries.short:
A spinning Sign in button means the request went out and RackTrack is still waiting for RackTrack to answer.
1. Give it up to about a minute. On a weak datacenter signal the round-trip can be slow.
2. If it never resolves, close and reopen the app, then try again.

entries.question: How do I get a report of my rack scan?
entries.answer:
Open the scan result (Results screen) and tap the **View** chip in the row at the bottom of the page (the row with View, Share, Change Device, New Scan). A window titled **Scan Report · <your rack ID>** opens inside the app. It briefly says **Preparing report…** while it authorises, then shows the full report.

The report contains, in this order:
1. A header banner reading "Rack Scan Report" with the rack ID and the date/time it was scanned, plus a **Download PDF** button.
2. Two figures: **Units** (the U range detected) and **Devices** (how many devices were found).
3. A **Port Identifications** section — one card per port you have identified on this rack, each showing the port number, the device label, its class and U position, the full-rack photo and the close-up device photo, plus any switch console commands you ran on that port with their output. If you haven't located any ports yet it says "No ports have been identified yet."

To save or send a copy, tap **Download PDF** inside the report (it renders a real PDF you can save or share), or use the **Share** chip on the Results screen to send it by email/Slack/Teams/Outlook.

The report is rebuilt fresh each time you tap View, so it always reflects your latest corrections.
symptoms: I can't find where to download my scan
how do I get a report
entries.rootCause: GET /api/scan/:rackId/report?format=html calls buildScanReport(rackId), which regenerates the self-contained HTML and writes it to outputs/<rackId>/report.html. The client opens it in an iframe inside a modal.

Preparing report…

Units
${htmlEscape(d.units_range || `${d.units_detected.length}`)}

Open the scan result (Results screen) and tap the **View** chip in the row at the bottom of the page (the row with View, Share, Change Device, New Scan).
1. A header banner reading "Rack Scan Report" with the rack ID and the date/time it was scanned, plus a **Download PDF** button.
2. Two figures: **Units** (the U range detected) and **Devices** (how many devices were found).

entries.question: How do I save the report as a PDF?
entries.answer:
Open the report with **View**, then tap the **Download PDF** button in the bar at the top of the report itself. RackTrack renders a real PDF on the server and opens it in your phone's browser or PDF viewer, where you can save or share it.

The PDF is A4 with 14 mm top/bottom and 12 mm left/right margins and backgrounds printed. The file is named `rack-report-<your rack ID>.pdf`.

One thing to expect: the PDF opens in a **new tab**, not inside RackTrack. That is deliberate — an Android WebView cannot display or save a PDF on its own. If nothing happens when you tap Download PDF, your browser has blocked the pop-up; allow pop-ups for RackTrack and tap it again.
symptoms: nothing happens when I tap Download PDF
PDF opens in a different app
entries.rootCause: The report HTML embeds a button that rewrites its own URL from format=html to format=pdf and calls window.open(url, '_blank'). The server renders it via headless Chromium (puppeteer) and serves it inline.
entries.short: Open the report with **View**, then tap the **Download PDF** button in the bar at the top of the report itself. RackTrack renders a real PDF in RackTrack and opens it in your phone's browser or PDF viewer, where you can save or share it.

entries.question: My report says "No ports have been identified yet" — where is my data?
entries.answer:
That message means the scan itself worked, but you never asked RackTrack to locate a specific port on this rack. The **Port Identifications** section of the report is built only from port lookups you have run on this rack.

To fill it in: go back to the scan result, pick a device, enter or tap the port you want, and let RackTrack find it. Then reopen the report with **View** — the port card, the photos and any console output will now be there.

Note that this section shows only your most recent port lookup for the rack, not a list of every port you have ever checked. Looking up a different port replaces what the report displays.

The Units and Devices figures at the top of the report come from the scan and will be filled in even when this section is empty.
symptoms: No ports have been identified yet.
entries.rootCause: buildScanReportData reads outputs/<rackId>/port_identifications.jsonl. If that file does not exist (no port was ever located for this rack), port_identifications is an empty array and renderHTMLReport emits the empty-state paragraph.

evidence.snippet:
Port Identifications
${d.port_identifications.length ? portIdsHtml : `

No ports have been identified yet.

`}

entries.short: That message means the scan itself worked, but you never asked RackTrack to locate a specific port on this rack. The **Port Identifications** section of the report is built only from port lookups you have run on this rack.

entries.question: I looked up five ports but the report only shows one of them
entries.answer:
Right now the scan report shows only the most recent port you located on that rack, not all of them. Every port lookup is recorded, but the report is currently built from just the newest entry — so earlier lookups do not appear.

Workaround: generate the report after each lookup. Tap **View** on the results screen, then **Download PDF** in the report window (or use **Share** to send it to Outlook, Slack or Teams). Each copy captures the port that was current at that moment, so one copy per port gives you the full set.

This affects every format — the on-screen report, the PDF, the CSV and the JSON — because they are all built from the same data.

If you need all ports in a single report, let us know: the underlying record does contain every port you inspected, so this is something support can raise with the product team rather than a permanent limitation.
symptoms: only my last port lookup appears
entries.rootCause: buildScanReportData walks port_identifications.jsonl newest-first and `break`s after the first successfully parsed line, so exactly one entry ever reaches the renderers.
entries.short: Right now the scan report shows only the most recent port you located on that rack, not all of them. Every port lookup is recorded, but the report is currently built from just the newest entry — so earlier lookups do not appear. Workaround: generate the report after each lookup.

entries.question: What formats can a scan report be exported in, and what does each one contain?
entries.answer:
There are four export formats, all built from the same underlying scan data:

| Format | How to get it | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| **On-screen report (HTML)** | The **View** button in the app | Rack ID, scan time, Units and Devices count tiles, and the Port Identifications section — one card per identified port with the rack and device photos and the console transcript. Self-contained: images are embedded in the file, so a saved copy still works offline. |
| **PDF** | The **Download PDF** button inside the report | The same report rendered to A4 by headless Chromium on the server. This is also the file attached when you Share to Slack, Teams or Outlook. |
| **CSV** | A download link from the report summary | Rack ID, timestamp and unit range as header lines, then Port Identifications, Port Command Transcripts (one row per command), and Feedback totals plus every feedback entry. No device inventory table. Sections only appear when there is data for them. |
| **JSON** | A download link from the report summary | Everything: rack ID, timestamp, quality note, units detected and unit range, the full devices array (label, class, U position, port count, console/SFP/other/connected port counts, PDU power outlet counts), port identifications with their console transcripts, feedback totals and every feedback entry, and the list of report images. |

The report's default summary view shows a small overview (rack ID, timestamp, device count, unit range, feedback total and accuracy) plus links to the HTML, JSON and CSV forms and to the saved report file.
entries.rootCause: Single source of truth (buildScanReportData) with four renderers: renderHTMLReport, buildScanReportPDF, renderJSONReport, renderCSVReport.

return {
    rackId,
    timestamp: meta.timestamp || null,
    quality_note: meta.quality?.note || null,
    units_detected: unitsDetected,
    units_range: formatUnitsRangeSrv(unitsDetected),
    devices,

entries.short: Scan reports export as HTML (View), PDF (Download PDF/Share), CSV and JSON — each covering more of the same scan data, from summary tiles to full detail.

entries.question: The report window says "Could not open report" — what do I do?
entries.answer:
The report opens with a short-lived pass that RackTrack fetches in the background. That message means fetching the pass failed.

Do this, in order:
1. **Close the window and tap View again.** A fresh pass is requested every time, so a one-off network blip clears itself.
2. If the message ends in **HTTP 401**, your session was not accepted. In most cases RackTrack detects this itself and returns you to the sign-in screen — sign back in and reopen the scan. If you are left on the report window, sign out and back in manually.
3. If the message ends in **HTTP 404**, RackTrack cannot find that rack for your account. Either the scan does not exist (a mistyped or deleted rack ID), or it belongs to a different Site from yours — for example someone sent you a rack ID from another Site. Check the rack ID, and if it is someone else's rack, ask its owner to share the report with you instead.
4. If you have no signal or you are off the datacenter network, reconnect and retry — the report is generated on the server, not on your phone.
entries.rootCause: fetchReportToken() calls GET /api/scan/:rackId/report-token via authFetch; any non-OK response sets reportTokenErr, which the modal renders as "Could not open report: <message>". A 401 is an expired/absent session; a 404 comes from the app.param('rackId') tenant guard rejecting a rack outside the caller's tenant/org.

evidence.snippet:
