Could not open report: {reportTokenErr}

entries.short:
The report opens with a short-lived pass that RackTrack fetches in the background. That message means fetching the pass failed.
1. ** A fresh pass is requested every time, so a one-off network blip clears itself.
2. If the message ends in **an error**, your session was not accepted.
3. If the message ends in **an error**, RackTrack cannot find that rack for your account.

entries.question: I left the report open, and now Download PDF does nothing / shows an error
entries.answer:
The pass that authorises the report expires after **5 minutes**. If you open the report, get distracted, and come back later, the **Download PDF** button inside the report fails — it reuses the same pass, which has by then expired, so the PDF opens to an authorisation error instead of your report.

The fix takes two taps: close the report (the **X** in the top-right of the report panel), tap **View** again — this mints a brand-new pass — then tap **Download PDF** straight away.

Same advice if the PDF tab has been sitting open in the background for a while: go back to the scan results and reopen the report fresh rather than reusing the old tab.
symptoms: Download PDF does nothing after a while
report worked earlier but not now
PDF tab shows an error or blank page
Rack not found when opening the PDF
entries.rootCause: REPORT_TOKEN_TTL_SEC = 300. openPdf() rewrites the current URL (which carries ?t=<token>) from format=html to format=pdf, so it reuses the token minted when the modal was first opened. Once it expires, app.param('rackId') falls through to the auth path; the new tab has no Authorization header, so it 401/404s.
entries.short: The pass that authorises the report expires after **5 minutes**. If you open the report, get distracted, and come back later, the **Download PDF** button inside the report fails — it reuses the same pass, which has by then expired, so the PDF opens to an authorisation error instead of your report.

entries.question: How do I email or send my scan report to a colleague?
entries.answer:
On the scan result, find the report row (View, Share, Change Device, New Scan) and tap **Share**. Choose **Teams**, **Outlook** or **Slack**. A dialog titled "Send report via <channel>" opens:

- **Recipient email** (required) — RackTrack remembers the last address you used for each channel on that device and pre-fills it next time.
- A free-text box marked *(optional)*, labelled **Subject** for Outlook and **Message** for Teams and Slack. Leave it blank and RackTrack uses "Rack scan report for <rack ID>".

Tap **Send report**. The Share button changes to **Sending to <channel>**, then **Sent**, and a green bar at the bottom reads "Sent to <address> via <channel>". RackTrack renders a fresh PDF of the report and attaches it — the recipient gets the PDF, not a link.

If you leave the address blank you get **"Recipient email is required."**; if it is malformed you get **"Enter a valid email address."**
symptoms: how do I email the report
entries.rootCause: confirmShareSend POSTs to /api/scan/:scanId/{slack,teams,outlook}; runShareSender builds the PDF via buildScanReportPDF and spawns the matching Python sender with --email and --file.
entries.short: On the scan result, find the report row (View, Share, Change Device, New Scan) and tap **Share**. Choose **Teams**, **Outlook** or **Slack**.

entries.question: Sharing failed with "Could not generate the report. Please try again."
entries.answer:
This means the email/message was never attempted — RackTrack could not build the PDF of your report in the first place.

What to try:
1. Tap **View** first and check the report opens on screen. View and Share read the same scan files, so if View also fails the scan's files are the problem, not the sharing.
2. If View works, tap **Share** again. The server reuses a background browser to render the PDF and will restart it if it has dropped, so a retry clears transient failures.
3. If it keeps failing on this one scan, rescan the rack. A scan whose files were partly written (for example the app was killed mid-scan) cannot produce a report.
4. If it fails on every scan, contact your administrator — the server-side PDF renderer may not be installed or reachable.
symptoms: Could not generate the report. Please try again.
entries.rootCause: buildScanReportPDF threw inside runShareSender. The route maps 'not found'/ENOENT to 404 and anything else to 500, and always returns the same generic user-facing message. Underlying causes are a missing/corrupt outputs/<rackId> folder, a missing scan_meta.json (readMeta returns null → 'Scan <id> not found'), or a puppeteer launch/navigation failure (page.goto has a 60 s timeout).

evidence.snippet:
await page.goto(fileUrl, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60_000 });
    await page.evaluate(() => document.body.classList.add('pdfMode'));

entries.short:
This means the email/message was never attempted — RackTrack could not build the PDF of your report in the first place.
1. Tap **View** first and check the report opens on screen.
2. If View works, tap **Share** again.
3. If it keeps failing on this one scan, rescan the rack.

entries.question: Sharing to Slack fails — the error mentions "users.lookupByEmail failed"
entries.answer:
Slack sharing works by finding the person in your Slack workspace **by their email address** and sending them a direct message with the PDF attached. The error means Slack could not match that address.

Check these:
1. **Use the exact address the person has in Slack.** A personal alias or a forwarding address will not match, even if mail reaches them.
2. **The person must be a member of the same Slack workspace** RackTrack is connected to. External or guest contacts will not be found.
3. If the error text mentions `not_authed`, `invalid_auth` or reads **"SLACK_TOKEN is not set"**, RackTrack's Slack connection is not configured on the server — that is an administrator fix, not something you can change.

Workaround in the meantime: tap **View**, then **Download PDF**, and attach the file to a Slack message yourself.
symptoms: SLACK_TOKEN is not set (env var or DEFAULT_TOKEN)
entries.rootCause: pipeline/slack_email.py resolves the recipient with Slack's users.lookupByEmail, opens a DM via conversations.open, then does the getUploadURLExternal → binary upload → completeUploadExternal dance. Any non-ok Slack response is raised verbatim and forwarded to the client by runShareSender as a 502.

evidence.snippet:
send(502, {
      ok: false,
      channel,
      error: parsed?.error || stderr || `${channel} sender exited with code ${code}`,

entries.short:
Slack sharing works by finding the person in your Slack workspace **by their email address** and sending them a direct message with the PDF attached.
1. ** A personal alias or a forwarding address will not match, even if mail reaches them.
2. **The person must be a member of the same Slack workspace** RackTrack is connected to.

entries.question: The Share button spins for ages and then fails — how long should it take?
entries.answer:
A share happens in two steps, each with its own limit.

First RackTrack renders the report as a PDF using a headless browser. Loading the report page is allowed up to **60 seconds**, and the PDF render takes a little longer on top of that. If this step fails you get "Could not generate the report. Please try again."

Then the message is sent to Teams, Outlook or Slack. That sending step gets **two minutes**; if it hasn't finished, RackTrack stops it and the share fails. The two minutes are for the send only, so a slow share can exceed two minutes overall.

A scan with several large photos genuinely takes longer to share than a small one, and the very first share after the server has been restarted is the slowest because the headless browser has to start up (about a second).

If you hit a timeout: wait a moment and tap **Share** again — the second attempt is usually faster because the browser is now warm. If it times out repeatedly, use **View → Download PDF** and send the file yourself.
symptoms: Sending to teams stays for a long time
entries.rootCause: SHARE_PDF_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000 SIGKILLs the Python sender. Separately, buildScanReportPDF's page.goto uses a 60 s timeout, and getBrowser() keeps one Chromium instance warm across requests because launching it costs ~1 s.

evidence.snippet:
const SHARE_PDF_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
const EMAIL_RE = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
await page.goto(fileUrl, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60_000 });

entries.short: A share happens in two steps, each with its own limit. First RackTrack renders the report as a PDF using a headless browser. Loading the report page is allowed up to **60 seconds**, and the PDF render takes a little longer on top of that. If this step fails you get "Could not generate the report. Please try again."

entries.question: The photos in my report look lower quality than in the app
entries.answer:
That is intentional. Before the report is built, RackTrack makes a smaller copy of every scan image that is 500 KB or larger: resized to 1400 pixels wide (never enlarged) and saved as JPEG at quality 76. The report embeds those copies.

The reason: the report is a single self-contained file with the images baked in, so you can save it, email it and open it offline. At full resolution a rack render is several megabytes, and a report that heavy black-screens inside a phone's viewer.

If you need the full-resolution image, use the photo shown on the scan result screen rather than the one in the report. Images already below 500 KB are embedded untouched, and if the resizing step cannot run for a particular image the original is embedded unchanged.
symptoms: images in the PDF are lower resolution
entries.rootCause: shrinkImagesForReport creates <name>.rpt.jpg copies with sharp (resize width 1400, withoutEnlargement, jpeg quality 76) for any source file ≥ 500 KB, cached by mtime; imageToDataUri prefers the shrunk copy when present.
entries.short: That is intentional. Before the report is built, RackTrack makes a smaller copy of every scan image that is 500 KB or larger: resized to 1400 pixels wide (never enlarged) and saved as JPEG at quality 76. The report embeds those copies.

entries.question: Are reports generated automatically or on a schedule? Can I schedule a weekly rack report?
entries.answer:
No — every report in RackTrack is generated **on demand**, at the moment you ask for it. There is no scheduling, no nightly batch, and no email digest.

What happens automatically is different: after a scan (and after certain updates to it) RackTrack refreshes an internal `scan_result.json` snapshot of that rack, so the data is ready when you next tap **View**. That snapshot is not delivered anywhere; nothing is sent to you.

If you want a report on a cadence, you have to open the scan and share it each time.
entries.rootCause: The only report entry points are the GET/POST /api/scan/:rackId/report routes, GET /api/rack-group/:groupId/report and the three share POSTs — all request-driven. No cron/scheduler exists for report generation; writeCanonicalScanResult is the only automatic post-scan write and produces a local JSON file only.
entries.short: No — every report in RackTrack is generated **on demand**, at the moment you ask for it. There is no scheduling, no nightly batch, and no email digest.

entries.question: Who is allowed to open or share a rack report?
entries.answer:
Access to a report follows access to the rack it belongs to. There is no admin-only report and no separate permission you can be granted for reports on their own.

- **Members and site managers** can open, download and share reports for racks scanned by **their own Site**. A rack belonging to another Site reads as "not found".
- **Organization admins** can reach any rack owned by any Site inside their own organization.
- **The platform owner** can reach any rack on the platform.
- Not signed in at all gives "Authentication required" rather than not-found.

So if a colleague sends you a raw rack ID and you get a not-found error, it is almost certainly a rack in a different Site — your account is fine, the rack just is not yours.

Two ways your colleague can get it to you: ask them to share the report by Teams, Outlook or Slack (the PDF travels fine across Sites), or have them send you the report link itself. A shared report link carries a short-lived, single-rack access token, so it opens for you even across Sites — but only for that one rack, and only until the token expires. It does not give you access to anything else in their Site.
symptoms: I can't open my colleague's report
do I need admin rights for reports
entries.rootCause: app.param('rackId') runs before every :rackId route (including all report routes). Owner passes unconditionally; org_admin passes if tenant.rackInOrg matches; everyone else must satisfy tenant.tenantOwnsRack, otherwise 404 'Rack not found'. Unauthenticated callers get 401.
entries.short: Access to a report follows access to the rack it belongs to. There is no admin-only report and no separate permission you can be granted for reports on their own. - **Members and site managers** can open, download and share reports for racks scanned by **their own Site**.

entries.question: Where do generated reports actually land on the server?
entries.answer:
Reports are written into the rack's own output folder on the server.

• buildScanReport(rackId) renders report.html into outputs/<rackId>/ and refreshes that rack's canonical scan result alongside it (server/app.js:1354-1361).
• buildScanReportPDF(rackId) builds the HTML first, then writes report.pdf into the same folder (server/app.js:1695-1697).
• The API hands clients the path directly as `htmlFileUrl: "/outputs/<rackId>/report.html"` (server/app.js:5008 and 5023).

Two things to be careful about.

Access: outputsDir is mounted with a plain `express.static` at /outputs (server/app.js:272-273), with no authentication. The tenant check that protects /api/scan/:rackId/report is an app.param('rackId') authorisation hook, not requireAuth on the route — the route deliberately has no requireAuth so the in-app iframe can pass ?t=<report token> instead of an Authorization header. The static mount bypasses that hook entirely, so anyone who knows a rack id can fetch its report file.

Retention: orphan_gc deletes outputs/RK-* folders that have NO row in rack_owners AND are older than retentionDays, default 14 (server/lib/orphan_gc.js:53-67). A rack that is still owned is never pruned by age, so "report files missing after two weeks" only ever applies to orphaned or unclaimed scans.
symptoms: report files missing after two weeks
entries.rootCause: buildScanReport writes report.html into data._rackDir; buildScanReportPDF writes report.pdf alongside; express.static mounts outputsDir at /outputs with no auth; orphan_gc.findOrphans defaults to a 14-day retention cutoff.

evidence.snippet:
app.use('/uploads', express.static(uploadsDir));
app.use('/outputs', express.static(outputsDir));
htmlFileUrl: `/outputs/${rackId}/report.html`,

*  retention threshold. */
...
  retentionDays = 14,
...
  const cutoffMs = Date.now() - retentionDays * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

entries.short: Reports are written into the rack's own output folder: outputs/<rackId>/report.html, with outputs/<rackId>/report.pdf alongside it when a PDF is built. That whole directory is served by an unauthenticated express.static mount at /outputs.

entries.question: What is the Incident Report I see when working from a ServiceNow ticket?
entries.answer:
When you scan while working a ServiceNow incident (ticket mode), the **View** button opens a purpose-built panel titled **Incident Report** with the incident number underneath, instead of the normal scan report.

It shows five blocks:
- **Incident** — the short description, priority, and when it was opened.
- **Image** — the rack or result photo, or "not available".
- **Port Located** — the device and interface alias (or "port N"), plus rack name, model and management IP from the CMDB.
- **Output** — a live sample from the switch: link active/idle, LLDP neighbour and its remote port and management IP, MAC count, the lookup method, and the time it was taken. If the sample failed you get "Live sample failed: <reason>"; before the first sample it reads "no live sample yet".
- **Suggestions** — a plain-English recommendation that depends on what the live sample found:
  - port confirmed active after being down: "Port is active now — cable was attached at <time>. Incident likely resolved; verify with monitoring, then close the ticket."
  - port currently up: "Port is currently active. Issue may be intermittent — watch for re-flaps over the next few minutes."
  - port down: "No traffic on this port right now. Verify the cable is plugged in on both ends, check the far-end device power/NIC status, then re-monitor."
  - SSH failed: "Cannot reach the switch over SSH to verify. Check mgmt connectivity to <mgmt IP>."
  - before any sample: "Waiting for first live sample."

The panel itself is view-only — there is no download or export button inside it. To get something shareable, use the **Share** chip on the results page (it works the same in ticket mode) or post a work note back to the incident.
symptoms: View shows the incident instead of the scan report
entries.rootCause: In ResultsPage the View chip is conditional: `onClick={ticketMode ? () => setTicketReportOpen(true) : viewReport}`. The ticket report is an inline React modal, not a generated document, and has no export path.

evidence.snippet:
<button className={`${styles.reportChip} ${styles.reportChipView}`}
              onClick={ticketMode ? () => setTicketReportOpen(true) : viewReport}
              title="View report">

Incident Report
{ticket.incident_number}

entries.short: When you scan while working a ServiceNow incident (ticket mode), the **View** button opens a purpose-built panel titled **Incident Report** with the incident number underneath, instead of the normal scan report. It shows five blocks: - **Incident** — the short description, priority, and when it was opened.

entries.question: Where is everything? I can't find my way around the app.
entries.answer:
On a phone the menu is a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen. Normally it holds three tabs: HOME, SCAN and PROFILE. That is the whole top-level menu.

Once you open a rack, that same bottom bar switches to the rack's own tabs: Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology, and a More button that opens Network and Drift. So HOME/SCAN/PROFILE is not visible while you are looking at a rack — press the phone's back gesture or the back arrow to leave the rack and the three tabs come back.

On a bigger screen (a laptop, a desktop browser, or an iPad in either orientation — anything from about 768px wide) there is no bottom bar for the main menu. Instead a sidebar runs down the left with: Home, Scan, Two racks, Profile — plus Console and Lab if you are the platform owner, and Data Sources and Marketplace if you are an organization admin or the owner.

Once you have opened a rack, the sidebar grows a second section headed "Rack · <the rack's ID>" containing Overview, Ports, Topology, Network, Switches and Drift.
symptoms: where did the rack links go
entries.rootCause: Two different navigation shells: BottomNav (3 tabs) below the sidebar breakpoint, DesktopShell (sidebar + rack-context links) at/above it. Rack sub-pages are a separate ScanTabBar with a More overflow.

evidence.snippet:

entries.question: How do I scan a rack?
entries.answer:
1. Tap SCAN in the bottom bar (or Scan in the sidebar).
2. At the top of the page pick either Upload (use a photo already on your device) or Camera (take one now).
3. If you chose Upload, a second row of buttons appears: SINGLE, MULTI and VIDEO. Leave it on SINGLE for one photo of one rack, then pick your file.
4. If you chose Camera, frame the rack until the line of text under the picture reads "Looks great — tap the shutter below", then tap the round shutter button. Tapping the middle SCAN tab at the bottom also fires the shutter while the camera is live.
5. Tap Analyze Rack.
6. When it finishes you land on that rack's Overview.

Limits: one file can be up to 340 MB, and you can start up to 20 scans a minute.
symptoms: How do I use RackTrack to scan a rack?
entries.rootCause: Scan flow is ScanPage: a primary Upload/Camera tab pair, then an upload-mode row (SINGLE/MULTI/VIDEO), then the Analyze Rack CTA. Server caps uploads at 340 MB and 20/min.

entries.question: I'm pointing the camera at the rack but the shutter won't take the picture. How do I make it fire?
entries.answer:
The shutter is switched off until three checks all pass: the rack has to fill the frame, the light has to be good enough, and the camera has to be steady. The single line of text under the guide box tells you which one is failing:

- "Move closer so the rack fills the frame" — step towards the rack.
- "Move to better lighting" — change your position or angle away from the light behind the rack.
- "Hold steady — keep still for focus" — brace your elbows and wait a moment.
- "Starting camera…" — the camera has not finished opening yet, just wait.

Once it says "Looks great — tap the shutter below", the shutter works.

This only applies to photos. In Video mode the shutter is available as soon as the camera is ready.
symptoms: Move closer so the rack fills the frame
Hold steady — keep still for focus
entries.rootCause: CameraCapture computes canShoot = ready && quality.sharp && quality.framed && quality.lit for photo mode and disables the shutter button on that flag; photoHint names the first failing check.

evidence.snippet:
const allGood = quality.sharp && quality.framed && quality.lit;
  const canShoot = mode === 'video' ? ready : ready && allGood;

const photoHint = !ready
    ? 'Starting camera…'
    : allGood
      ? 'Looks great — tap the shutter below'
      : !quality.framed ? 'Move closer so the rack fills the frame'
      : !quality.lit    ? 'Move to better lighting'
      : !quality.sharp  ? 'Hold steady — keep still for focus'
      : 'Align full rack within the frame';
disabled={!canShoot && !recording}

The single line of text under the guide box tells you which one is failing: - "Move closer so the rack fills the frame" — step towards the rack.

entries.question: How do I scan two racks and see the cabling that runs between them?

entries.question: The app says my photo isn't good enough. What are Retake and Proceed anyway?
entries.answer:
When a photo or video fails a quality check you get a warning with the reason and two buttons.

- Retake clears the file so you can take or choose another. This is almost always the right choice.
- Proceed anyway runs the analysis on the file regardless, with the quality checks turned off (on your device and on the server). A genuinely poor photo then comes back with devices missing, or with an empty rack.

Messages that give you these two buttons:
- "Image resolution is low (W×H). Results may be inaccurate." — the shorter side of the picture is under 480 pixels.
- "The image looks blurry. Results may be inaccurate."
- On a video: "Video resolution is low", "Video is too short" (must be at least 1 second) or "Video is too long" (keep it under 120 seconds).

One message looks similar but does NOT offer Proceed anyway: "Please upload a clearer photo of the rack — keep the camera steady and make sure the full rack fits in the frame." That appears as a plain error with no buttons, and means the app could not open the image file at all. Take a fresh photo or pick a different file.

Note: HEIC/HEIF photos (the iPhone default format) skip the on-device checks entirely — the server validates those after upload.
symptoms: Please upload a clearer photo of the rack
entries.rootCause: qualityChoice state renders the Retake / Proceed anyway pair; Proceed anyway re-calls analyze({override:true}) which bypasses the pre-shot checks. Client-side thresholds: MIN_DIM 480, BLUR_THRESHOLD 100.

entries.question: How do I find a specific port on a device after a scan?
entries.answer:
From the rack Overview:

1. Pick the device. Either tap its box in the photo, or use the Device dropdown further down — it opens on "— Pick a device (or tap one in the image) —" and lists each device with its type and port breakdown.
2. A Port number card appears. Above the input is a row of port-type buttons — RJ45, SFP, Console, USB — showing how many of each that device has. Only the types the device actually has are offered. Tap the one you want.
3. Type the port number in the box (it hints the valid range, e.g. 1–48).
4. Tap Find Port, or just press Enter.

The photo zooms to that port. Underneath, Find lets you jump straight to another port on the same device without starting over.

If the device is a power strip (PDU) you get a Power card summarising outlets instead of a port search.
entries.rootCause: ResultsPage device picker + PORT_CATEGORIES type buttons + numeric port input driving findPort().

entries.question: How do I zoom into a device in the rack photo, and how do I get back out?
entries.answer:
Tap a coloured box in the photo to select that device. Tap the selected (blue) box a second time to zoom into just that device — the rest of the rack's boxes are hidden. A "Back to rack" button appears where the zoom controls were; tap it to return to the whole rack.

When you are not zoomed into a single device, you get two magnifier buttons on the picture instead. Tap + to zoom in and – to zoom out (on a computer you can also scroll the mouse wheel over the photo). Once you have zoomed in past normal size, you can drag the photo with your finger to move around it. Pinch-to-zoom is not supported — use the + and – buttons.

To change which device you are working on without leaving the results, scroll to the buttons at the bottom and tap "Change Device". That clears the selection, resets the zoom, and takes you back to the top of the page where the Device dropdown is.
symptoms: stuck zoomed in on one device
entries.rootCause: focusMode in ResultsPage crops to the selected device's box and swaps the zoom controls for a 'Back to rack' button; the Change Device chip resets selection and scrolls to top.

entries.question: The app identified something incorrectly. How do I correct it?
entries.answer:
RackTrack asks you to check its work with plain yes/no questions as you work through a result. Answering No lets you set the correct value, and your correction is saved to the scan.

The questions you may see, once you have a device selected:
- "Detected as <type> — right?" — the device type. Answer No and pick the real one.
- "Detected N RJ45 ports — right?" (or "Detected N total ports (…) — right?" when other port types were found) — appears once you have answered the device-type question. Answer No and pick 8, 12, 16, 24 or 48, or type your own number. This question is not asked for PDUs, which have power outlets rather than RJ45 ports — the Power card covers those.
- "Port N on <device> — right?" — after you have located a port. Answer No and pick the real port number.
- "Cable colour is <colour> — right?" — only when the port is shown as connected and a cable colour was detected. Answer No and pick the real colour.

Each question shows Yes and No buttons. Choosing No replaces them with "What is it actually?" and a dropdown of choices; if your answer is not in the list, choose "Other (type it)" and a box appears for you to type it. Press Submit to save — you will see "Saving…" and then "Thanks for the feedback.", after which the question disappears. If you come back to something you have already corrected, it shows a short confirmation line instead of asking again.
symptoms: how do I correct the app
entries.rootCause: StandardFeedback component rendered four times in ResultsPage with different prompts/option sets, posting corrections to the feedback endpoints.

evidence.snippet: {prompt} ... Yes ... No ... What is it actually?

entries.short: RackTrack asks you to check its work with plain yes/no questions as you work through a result. Answering No lets you set the correct value, and your correction is saved to the scan.

entries.question: How do I share a scan result or open the full report?
entries.answer:
Scroll to the row of buttons near the bottom of the results page. There are four:

- View — opens the full scan report.
- Share — opens a small menu with Teams, Outlook and Slack. Pick one, fill in the recipient email (required) and an optional note, and send. While it sends the button reads "Sending to Slack" (or Teams/Outlook) with a spinner, then changes to "Sent" with a checkmark.
- Change Device — go back to picking a different device in this rack.
- New Scan — start a fresh scan.

entries.question: How do I see which ports are actually in use on the switch right now?
entries.answer:
Open the rack, then open Ports. This screen signs in to the switch over the network and reads it live — it is not built from your photo.

At the top you get three tiles: In use (ports with a live link, out of the total), Available (ports you can plug into today) and Identified (ports where the far-end device announced itself over LLDP/CDP).

Below that are three tabs: Ports, Cables and Ping.

On the Ports tab you get a picture of the switch front, then filter buttons: All, In Use, Available, Linked, and Errors (Errors only appears if there is something to show). Each one shows a count. The list underneath splits into "Ethernet (ETH) Modules" and "SFP Modules".

A port can show as Reserved rather than Available for either of two reasons:
- it has a description saved on the switch but nothing plugged in — somebody has claimed it; or
- the switch reports it as shut down, admin-down or err-disabled — it is not usable until someone re-enables it.

The Errors filter shows exactly these Reserved ports, so if you want to see them all in one place, tap Errors. Open a port to see its raw status text from the switch (for example "Not connected", "Err-disabled") — that tells you which of the two cases you are looking at.
entries.rootCause: PortsPage live-probe view: three stat tiles, Ports/Cables/Ping tabs, and FilterPill row driven by logicalVerdict() which returns available/used/reserved.

entries.question: How do I check whether the switch can reach a particular device or IP address?
entries.answer:
Open the rack, open Ports, then tap the Ping tab (the third tab, after Ports and Cables).

The card is headed "Reachability check — ping, run from the switch". The test runs from the switch itself, not from your phone or laptop, so it tests the path your equipment actually takes.

1. Type an IP address or hostname in the box (it hints "IP or hostname — e.g. 192.168.1.1").
2. Tap Ping, or press Enter.

Under the box is a "Quick ping:" row of shortcuts so you don't have to type. There is always one for 8.8.8.8 (labelled "8.8.8.8 · internet"). A second chip for the local gateway appears only when the switch's management address is a plain IPv4 address — RackTrack derives the likely gateway by replacing the last part of that address with .1, so it is a best guess rather than a discovered gateway. If the gateway answers and 8.8.8.8 does not, that usually points to a problem upstream of your rack rather than in it.

If you leave the box empty you get "Enter an IP address or hostname first." If the switch hasn't finished loading you get "The switch isn't reachable yet — wait for it to load."

Only ping is offered on this screen — there is no traceroute button. That is deliberate: on TP-Link switches the tracert command needs a higher privilege than the read-only account RackTrack uses, whereas ping works at that level.
symptoms: how do I ping from the switch
Enter an IP address or hostname first
entries.rootCause: PortsPage ReachabilityTool posts to /api/switch/trace with kind='ping'. Traceroute is intentionally not exposed because tracert on TP-Link needs privileges above the read-only account used.

entries.question: How do I check a switch's firmware and whether it has security problems?
entries.answer:
Open the rack, then Switches, and pick the switch you want.

If the card shows the tag "Not detected" next to Identification, the app could not read the label from your photo. Tap Enter make / model and type them in — the lookups need both. (If only one is missing the link says Add model or Add vendor instead; once you have typed something it says Edit.)

Then use the tab strip on the card: Specifications, Firmware, SFP Advisor. Open Firmware. If it says "No firmware version recorded.", tap Enter version and type the version you are running.

If you see "Latest version unknown", that does NOT mean you are up to date — it means RackTrack could not confirm the newest version. Follow the "Check site ↗" link to the vendor's own download page and look yourself.

Important: anything you type here is saved in this browser only. It does not reach the server, your CMDB, or your colleagues, and it is lost if you clear your browsing data or switch device.
entries.rootCause: SwitchInformationPage stores manual make/model/version overrides in localStorage keyed per rack+switch; the Firmware tab drives the vendor/CVE lookup and falls back to a 'Check site' vendor link when no verified latest exists.

entries.question: How do I see the rack as a diagram or in 3D?
entries.answer:
Open the rack's results, then the Topology tab (on a laptop or iPad landscape it's "Topology" in the left sidebar).

At the top there is a 2D / 3D toggle. 2D draws the rack as a flat elevation — a numbered column of U slots (U01, U02, …) with empty slots marked, like the drawing on the cabinet door. 3D puts the same rack in space; drag to orbit and scroll to zoom.

Click any device and the panel at the bottom fills in with its details (type, U position, model, management IP), the peers it is connected to, and a table of its ports showing how many are connected and how many are free. You can also click a cable or a link to inspect it.

If you see "Topology is being prepared", the drawing is still being built in the background after your scan. Wait a moment and tap Retry. The message itself explains it should appear on its own, and that rescanning regenerates it.
entries.rootCause: TopologyPage renders a lazy-loaded TopologyScene3D behind a 2D/3D mode toggle; when no snapshot exists it renders the 'Topology is being prepared' state with a Retry that bumps reloadKey.

entries.question: How do I find out what changed on a port, and when?
entries.answer:
Open the rack and go to Drift (on a phone it is behind the More button in the rack tab strip). There is also a standalone Port history & drift page.

1. The monitored switch appears at the top, tagged Streaming when it is being watched, or Paused when it is not.
2. Below it is the Interface inventory — a grid of every port, colour-coded: link up, link down, unknown. Click the port you care about.
3. The panel that opens has three tabs: Specs, Timeline and History (History shows a count of changes).
4. On Timeline, use the Window dropdown to widen the view — the choices are Last 1 Hour, Last 3 Hours, Last 12 Hours, Last 1 Day and Last 1 Week. This is how you tell a one-off outage from a port that has been flapping for a fortnight.
5. The circular arrows button next to the switch name is Poll now — it checks the switch immediately instead of waiting for the next scheduled pass. You can press it at most 5 times a minute; beyond that you get "rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute".

If it says "Waiting for first poll…" and never changes, no switch is being monitored — ask an administrator to set one up. Note the background poller runs on a long interval (hourly by default), so use Poll now if you need fresh data immediately.
symptoms: rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute
entries.rootCause: PortHistoryPage + port_poller. DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS is 3_600_000 (hourly) — deliberately not 60s, because these switches allow one SSH session. Manual poll is capped at 5/min server-side.

entries.question: How do I reopen a scan I did earlier?
entries.answer:
Open PROFILE and scroll to Recent Scans.

Every rack you have scanned is listed newest first, with a thumbnail, its rack ID, how many devices, units and ports it found, and how long ago it was. Tap any row to reopen the full result. (As a regular member you see your own scans; site and org admins see more.)

Only the five most recent are shown at first. If you have more, a button underneath reads "Show all N scans" — tap it to reveal the rest, and "Show less" to collapse them again.

If you have never scanned anything, you get "No scans yet." with a "Start your first scan" button.

Recent Scans is the dependable way back to an older rack. On a laptop, desktop browser or iPad in landscape, the rack links in the left sidebar (Overview, Ports, Topology, Network, Switches, Drift) only ever point at the rack you are currently working on — they are cleared the moment you open the Scan page to start a new one, and a page refresh clears them too. On a phone there are no rack links in the bottom bar at all. (The old /history address redirects to Profile.)
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage lists /api/scans, slicing to 5 unless showAllScans. DesktopShell clears the remembered rackId on navigation to /scan, and holds it in module memory only (a refresh wipes it). /history redirects to /profile.

entries.question: How do I change my profile picture, and how do I sign out?
entries.answer:
Both are on the PROFILE tab.

Profile picture: tap your avatar at the top of the page (it has a small blue pencil badge on it). A sheet slides up titled "Choose your picture" with the available images. Tap the one you want — it saves straight away and the sheet closes by itself. While it is saving the images dim and the bottom button reads "Saving…". If you change your mind and want to leave your picture as it is, tap Close.

Sign out: tap the exit icon in the top-right corner of the Profile header. A box appears asking "Sign out?" with the note "You'll need to sign in again to scan racks." Confirm with the Sign out button, or tap Cancel to stay signed in (tapping outside the box does nothing). After signing out you are taken back to the home screen.

The page also shows your username, email, your site name and the month you joined (for example "Sprintpark · Since Jul 2026"), along with your recent scans.
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage: topbar logout icon opens a confirm modal calling logout() then navigating to '/'; the avatar button opens the AVATARS picker which PATCHes the choice.

entries.question: How do I register a rack in the CMDB after a scan?
entries.answer:
After a scan, if RackTrack finds equipment your configuration database has no record of, it raises the registration ticket for you and shows you a box asking you to approve it. You only need to approve.

1. Finish a scan and stay on the results screen. Within about half a minute a box headed "Ticket submitted" appears, showing a Reference number and the note "Submitted for approval. Approve below to register the discovered inventory in the configuration database now."
2. Tap Approve. (Close dismisses the box — your scan is unaffected, but the rack stays unregistered, and it will not reappear for that rack until you scan again in a new session.)
3. It shows "Synchronizing…", then "Successfully registered", listing the devices, ports, cables and rack size that were written to your records.
4. Tap Done.

Notes:
- The box only appears on a freshly completed scan. Reopening an old rack from your history will not show it.
- If nothing appears, either the rack is already registered, nothing was missing from your records, or no configuration database is connected for your organization.
- If approval fails you are returned to the same screen with a message such as "Request to ServiceNow timed out — try again"; tap Approve again.

entries.rootCause: CmdbApprovalModal state machine: unregistered -> Raise Ticket -> pending -> Approve -> syncing -> registered.

entries.question: How do I add someone to my team?
entries.answer:
Admin only. Open the Organizations console (Profile > Organization Dashboard, or go to /organizations).

An Organization is your company, it contains Sites (your buildings), and each Site contains members. Find the Site row you want. It has two buttons.

Invite (the normal route — nobody shares a password):
1. Tap Invite.
2. Enter their Email and choose a Role — Member or Site Manager.

4. The link appears with a Copy button. The screen tells you: "Send this link to <email>. It works once and expires in 7 days."

2. Fill in Username, Email, Password (at least 8 characters with upper case, lower case, a digit and a symbol) and a Role.
3. Tap Add member, then hand them the details.

entries.question: How do I use the Operations Console, and how do I clear the log?
entries.answer:
Platform owner only. Open Console in the sidebar, or go to /dashboard. (The old /logs address redirects here.)

The page is titled Operations Console and has two tabs:
- Operations — "Everything happening across RackTrack — who's scanning, what's working, what's failing."
- Logs — "Live application log — email delivery, errors, and requests as the server records them."

In the header there are two controls that apply to whichever tab you are on: a Live toggle (auto-refresh on / auto-refresh paused) and a Refresh button for a one-off reload.

To start the log fresh, open the Logs tab and press Clear log. It asks you to confirm first — "Delete all N stored log entries and start fresh? This cannot be undone." The button reads Clearing… while it works. This cannot be undone.

entries.question: How do I sign up, sign in, or reset my password?
entries.answer:
Sign up (creates a new organization, and you become its administrator):
1. On the welcome screen tap Create account (top right).
2. Fill in Email, Username, Organization, Password and Confirm password. All five are required.
3. Watch the meter under the password. It names the one thing still missing, e.g. "Need a digit". It needs all five: 8 characters, an uppercase, a lowercase, a digit and a special char. Continue turns on once the meter reads "✓ Strong password", the second box reads "✓ matches", and Email and Username are filled in.
4. Tap Continue, type the six-digit code from your email into the boxes, and tap Verify. Resend gets you a new code.

Sign in:
1. Tap Sign in on the welcome screen.
2. Fill in Username or email and Password. Leave Organization empty — it is marked (optional), and usernames are unique across RackTrack, so a blank field finds your account. Only fill it in if your administrator has told you to; it accepts your organization's or your Site's name. RackTrack staff (owner accounts) must always leave it blank.
3. Tap Sign in. If you type an organization RackTrack doesn't recognise, you get "Invalid organization or credentials" — clear the field and try again.

Forgotten password:
1. On the sign-in screen tap Forgot password?, enter your Email, tap Send reset code.
2. Enter the six-digit code (it expires in 1 minute) and tap Verify code. Resend is there if you need another.
3. RackTrack then asks whether you want to change your password — you are signed in either way. Choose Yes, change password to set a new one (same five password rules as signup), or No, take me to the app to go straight in and leave your old password unchanged.
entries.rootCause: HomeLight welcome buttons route to /signup and /login; SignupPage enforces five password rules and a six-digit verify step; ForgotPasswordPage is a three-step email -> code -> optional-change flow.

entries.question: How do I choose the right SFP module for an empty slot?
entries.answer:
Open the rack, then Switches, pick the switch, and open the SFP Advisor tab on its card.

Using the switch make and model read from your photo, it works out what kind of SFP slot the switch has and recommends transceivers that fit. The recommended one appears as a large card marked ★ TOP PICK, with its specs, a price where we have one, and a link to buy. Up to three alternatives sit underneath behind a "N more compatible modules" row — tap the + to expand it. If the switch has free SFP slots, the card also shows a total cost for filling them.

It also suggests direct-attach cables (DAC/AOC), which replace the transceiver-and-fibre pair for short runs inside a rack.

Check any recommendation against your switch's own compatibility list before buying. If you see "No exact listings for <model> — showing nearest-match modules", RackTrack could not find listings for your exact switch and is showing generic modules for that slot type, which may not be the right brand for your switch.

entries.question: The app counted the wrong number of ports on my switch. How do I fix it?
entries.answer:
Open the scan result, pick the device from the Device list, and look for the question **"Detected N RJ45 ports — right?"** (if the device has more than just RJ45 jacks it reads "Detected N total ports (…) — right?"). Tap **No**, then either choose 8, 12, 16, 24 or 48 from the dropdown, or pick **Other (type it)** and type the real number. Tap Submit.

RackTrack does not just record your number — it re-runs port detection on that device using your count as the target: if the model had found more ports than you say exist it trims to your count, and if it found fewer it lays out an exact grid of your count (keeping the connected/empty status of the ports it did find) and redraws the port picture with the corrected numbering. The device then shows **"Port count corrected — you set this"**.

Two things to know:

- This question only appears **after** you have answered the device-type question above it ("Detected as <type> — right?"). RackTrack deliberately asks one thing at a time. If you don't see the port-count question, answer the device-type question first.
- The question is **not shown for PDUs**. A PDU has power outlets rather than RJ45 ports, so RackTrack skips it there — the Power card summarises the outlets instead.

Port count corrected — you set this
entries.rootCause: The typed-port YOLO model (Models/ports_9.pt) runs at ports_conf 0.23; dark, dusty, angled or partially-occluded jacks fall below that confidence and are never detected, so device.port_count under-reports. The correction path POSTs /api/feedback/port-count, which calls runRelabelPortCount → worker.handle_relabel_port_count, synthesising an exact grid of target_count ports and setting port_count_source='user_relabeled'.

entries.question: There is no "Detected N ports" question on my device — why can't I correct the port count?
entries.answer:
Two reasons, both intentional:

1. **You haven't answered the device-type question yet.** RackTrack shows one question at a time. Answer **"Detected as <type> — right?"** first (Yes, or No plus the correct type), and the port-count question appears underneath it. If you already corrected this device's type on an earlier visit, the port-count question is shown straight away.

2. **The device is a PDU.** A PDU has power outlets, not network ports, so the port-count question is skipped entirely for PDUs. The **Power** card on the device already summarises its outlets (total and how many are in use) — read that instead.

If the device really is a switch and RackTrack called it a PDU, correct the device type first: answer **No** to "Detected as PDU — right?" and choose **Switch**. The port-count question then becomes available.

Note on wording: the port-count question reads **"Detected N RJ45 ports — right?"** when only RJ45 ports were found, or **"Detected N total ports (…breakdown…) — right?"** when fibre/SFP ports were detected as well.

entries.question: RackTrack called my firewall a switch (or my switch a patch panel). How do I correct the device type?
entries.answer:
Select the device, then answer **No** to **"Detected as <type> — right?"**. You get a dropdown with fourteen choices: Switch, Patch Panel, Firewall, Router, Server, Load Balancer, Modem, Controller, Recorder, Amplifier, Gateway, PDU, PSU, UPS — plus **Other (type it)** if yours isn't listed.

Submit and the device relabels across the result. It then shows **"Device: <type> — you set this"**.

Why it happens: firewalls, routers and 1U servers look very similar head-on, and the detector accepts anything above a fairly low confidence bar. A device that is partly hidden behind cables, in shadow, or shot at an angle is the most likely to be mislabelled. Correcting it also teaches RackTrack — future scans of the same or a visually similar device within your organization pick up your label automatically.
entries.rootCause: Device detection uses Models/devices_seg.pt at devices_conf 0.20 (server_conf 0.25). At that threshold visually similar 1U chassis classes are frequently confused. /api/feedback/device logs the correction, overlays it into scan_result.json, and calls fireMemoryCorrection('devices', …) so the pHash+ResNet18 memory auto-applies it on future scans within the same organization.

entries.question: The cable colour is wrong — it says Blue but the cable is grey.
entries.answer:
On the port view, answer **No** to **"Cable colour is <colour> — right?"** and pick the real colour. Twelve swatches are offered: Black, Blue, Brown, Green, Grey, Orange, Pink, Red, White, Yellow, Violet, Aqua — plus a free-text box if yours isn't one of them. The colour repaints straight away and the port shows **"Cable colour: <colour> — you set this"**.

Why it gets it wrong: colour is judged from a small crop of your photo, so lighting, shadow and camera white balance can push one colour towards another. RackTrack also only knows a fixed list of colour/connector combinations it was trained on, so a colour outside that list is forced into the nearest one it does know.

Note that cable colour is only worked out for ports RackTrack believes have a cable in them. If the port isn't shown as connected, there is no colour to correct and the question won't appear.
symptoms: cable shows as blue but is grey
entries.rootCause: pipeline/cable.py classifies a ~4x-enlarged port crop with the cable_eff_best EfficientNet into a fixed 14-class argmax (LC_Aqua, RJ-45 Violet, RJ_45 Black/Blue/Brown/Green/Grey/Orange/Pink/Red/White/Yellow, SC_Orange, SC_Yellow). Any real-world colour outside those classes is forced to the nearest. Enrichment only runs on ports whose status is 'connected'.

entries.question: What does "Not fully sure about this cable (42% confidence)" mean? Should I trust it?
entries.answer:
No — treat it as a guess and check with your own eyes.

RackTrack shows this warning whenever its confidence in reading the cable drops below 50%. The exact wording is: *"Not fully sure about this cable (N% confidence) — the photo resolution may be too low to read it clearly. Please check the cable and its colour, and correct them below if they're wrong."*

It almost always means the photo was too low-resolution, too dark, or too far away for that particular port. What to do:

- Look at the actual cable and use the **"Cable colour is <colour> — right?"** question just below the warning to set the correct value.
- If several ports on the same device are hedging, the photo itself is the problem — retake it closer, straight-on, with more light, and rescan.

A confidence figure is shown for a reason: the app is telling you it may be wrong. Above 50% you get no warning, but that is not a guarantee of correctness either.

the photo resolution may be too low to read it clearly

entries.question: I rescanned a rack after changing equipment, but RackTrack showed me the old result.
entries.answer:
Yes — this is expected behaviour, and there are two separate reasons it can happen.

**1. You uploaded the identical photo.** RackTrack identifies a scan by the content of the image, so re-uploading the exact same file returns the earlier result instantly (with your corrections still applied), rather than re-analysing it. The time in Recent Scans is refreshed so it shows as scanned now.

**2. You confirmed the rack's layout previously.** Once a rack layout has been confirmed, RackTrack fingerprints that rack photo. A later photo of the same rack that looks near-identical serves the confirmed result instead of re-detecting. This is deliberately strict — a re-shoot from a noticeably different angle falls through to a fresh detection rather than risking showing you another rack's data.

If you have physically changed the rack, take a **noticeably different photo** — a different distance or angle, or a shot that shows the new equipment clearly. That produces a new fingerprint and forces a fresh analysis.

There is currently no button in the app to force a fresh re-analysis of an unchanged photo. If a user is stuck on a stale result and cannot get a different-enough photo, escalate.
symptoms: changed the rack but results are the same
entries.rootCause: Two bypasses in POST /api/analyze: (a) content-hash cache — computeRackId(tmpPath) hits an existing device_unit_map.json and returns cached; (b) confirmed-rack bypass — find_confirmed_rack matches on pHash (HAMMING_TOL 6) then a strict embedding threshold _RACK_SIM_THRESH = 0.96. The server honours a forceFresh flag, but grep shows no client code sends it, so there is no UI escape hatch.

entries.question: I scanned my rack and got "This doesn't look like a server rack" — but it is a rack.
entries.answer:
RackTrack runs a quick rack-presence check before the full analysis and refuses the photo if it finds no rack equipment at all. The exact message is: *"This doesn't look like a server rack. Point the camera at the front of a rack so its devices and ports are visible."*

It is not a rejection of your rack — it means nothing rack-shaped was detected in that particular frame. Usual causes:

- The photo is of the **back or side** of the rack rather than the front faces.
- The rack door is **closed**, or the front is completely covered by cable bundles.
- The shot is too far away for individual device faces to be made out.
- The rack is largely empty, so there are no device faces to find.

(Photos that are too dark, blurry or tilted usually fail the earlier photo-quality check instead, which gives a different message naming the specific problem.)

Retake from the front, close enough that individual devices and their ports are visible, with the full rack in frame and the camera level with the middle of the rack.

This check is skipped if you used **Proceed anyway** on an earlier quality warning — in that case the photo goes through and you may get an empty or badly incomplete result instead of this message. On a MULTI stitch the wording differs: "No devices were detected on the stitched rack — make sure each photo shows the front of the rack and the shots overlap."
symptoms: This doesn't look like a server rack
Point the camera at the front of a rack
entries.rootCause: A detect_only pass runs before the full pipeline; if it returns zero devices the request is rejected with kind:'not_a_rack'. The gate is skipped entirely when skipQualityCheck is set by 'Proceed anyway'.

evidence.snippet: if (override) body.append('skipQualityCheck', '1');

The exact message is: *"This doesn't look like a server rack. Point the camera at the front of a rack so its devices and ports are visible."* It is not a rejection of your rack — it means nothing rack-shaped was detected in that particular frame.

entries.question: A colleague corrected this scan but I still see the old value — or my correction isn't visible to my team.
entries.answer:
Corrections behave differently depending on what was corrected.

**Corrections to a specific scan** — device type, port number, port count, port type, cable colour — are stored against that scan and are visible to anyone who can open that scan. They are baked into the scan result, the report, and anything exported to your CMDB. If a colleague's correction isn't showing, reload the page; the corrected view is rebuilt after each correction is saved.

**The learned memory that re-applies corrections to future scans** is shared across every Site in your organization — so a correction made by a technician at one site does improve scans at another site in the same organization. It is never shared with a different organization.

If you genuinely cannot see a scan a colleague corrected, that is an access question, not a correction question. Scans belong to a Site: as a member or site manager you can only open scans from your own Site, while an organization admin can open any scan in their organization. Ask your administrator to check your Site membership.
symptoms: my correction not shared with team
other site doesn't see the fix
entries.rootCause: Scan-level corrections live in server/feedback.jsonl keyed by scanId and are overlaid into scan_result.json by writeCanonicalScanResult (triggered via scheduleCanonicalRefresh after each feedback POST) — visible to anyone who can access the rack. Rack access is tenant/Site-scoped via canAccessRack. The active-learning memory store is partitioned per organization by store.set_org().

evidence.snippet:
# Active learning is scoped at the ORGANIZATION level: each org keeps its own
# corrections + retraining snapshots, so all Sites/tenants within one org share
# a single model memory while different orgs stay isolated.

# Active learning is organization-scoped: an optional org_id on the
# request routes all store reads/writes to that org's partition, so
# corrections are shared across an org's Sites but isolated between orgs.

entries.short: Corrections behave differently depending on what was corrected. **Corrections to a specific scan** — device type, port number, port count, port type, cable colour — are stored against that scan and are visible to anyone who can open that scan.

entries.question: Why does RackTrack keep asking me "right?" questions — and what happens if I just answer Yes to everything?
entries.answer:
The questions are RackTrack asking you to check its work, because it is reading a photograph and can be wrong. Each one is a plain Yes/No. You may see more than one at a time — on a selected port you can get separate questions for the port number, the port type and the cable colour — though the port-count question only appears once you have answered the device-type question.

Answering **Yes** confirms the detection and the question collapses to a tick line for the rest of your visit. Answering **No** opens a dropdown (with an "Other" option you can type into) and a Submit button, then you see "Thanks for the feedback."

If you answer Yes to something that was actually wrong, two things happen: your scan result keeps the wrong value (and so does the report and anything you send to your CMDB), and although RackTrack logs that you confirmed it, it saves no correction and no training example — so it will make the same mistake next time. Confirming a wrong value is worse than skipping the question.

Corrections stick when you come back to the scan; a plain Yes does not, so a confirmed-only item may ask again next time you open the result.

If you're not sure, you can simply not answer — nothing forces you to. RackTrack shows a confidence percentage next to the detected device and cable, and warns you outright when a cable read is uncertain; those are the ones worth checking with your own eyes first.

Values you corrected yourself are called out so you can tell them apart from the model's guesses: a "Your correction" badge next to the device type and cable colour in the port detail panel, and a "— you set this" line under the question itself for everything else.

entries.question: I get "Camera access denied. Allow camera permission or use Upload."
entries.answer:
RackTrack asked your phone or browser for the camera and was refused, so the camera view is replaced by that message with a crossed-out camera icon. (The same message also appears if the device has no usable camera at all.)

Fix it in one of these ways:

• **On iPhone/iPad**: Settings → RackTrack → turn **Camera** on, then reopen the app.
• **On Android**: Settings → Apps → RackTrack → Permissions → **Camera** → Allow.
• **In a desktop browser**: click the padlock/camera icon in the address bar, allow the camera for this site, then reload.

If you tapped "Don't allow", the prompt will not reappear on its own — you have to change it in settings.

**You do not need the camera at all to scan.** On the Scan screen there are two tabs, **Upload** and **Camera**. Tap **Upload** and you get three mode buttons just below it: **SINGLE** (one photo), **MULTI** (2-8 photos stitched together for a tall rack) and **VIDEO** (a 1-120 second clip, useful for a whole row of racks). Each one opens your photo/file picker. This path produces exactly the same results as the camera and is the normal route on an iPad or a computer.

entries.question: I picked a photo and got "The image looks blurry. Results may be inaccurate." — should I press Proceed anyway?
entries.answer:
RackTrack checked the photo before uploading it and found it isn't sharp enough. You get two buttons:

• **Retake** — clears the photo so you can take or pick a better one. **This is almost always the right choice.**
• **Proceed anyway** — sends the blurry photo through regardless.

Why Retake matters: pressing **Proceed anyway** doesn't just skip this warning, it switches off *every* later safety check too. So a genuinely unusable photo comes back as an empty or badly wrong rack instead of an honest error. If your rack "came back empty", this is usually why.

To get a sharp photo: hold the phone still for a second before shooting, tap the screen to focus, and make sure there's enough light — phones drop the shutter speed in dim aisles, which is what causes most of this blur.

entries.question: "The image appears tilted. Please hold the phone straight and retake."
entries.answer:
RackTrack looks at the rack's vertical rails in your photo. If the whole picture is rotated by more than **6 degrees**, or if the lines on the left side of the frame and the lines on the right side disagree by more than **5 degrees** (which means you were standing off to one side), it stops and asks you to retake.

**How to fix it:**
1. Stand square in front of the rack, not off to one side.
2. Hold the phone upright, not rolled left or right — the rack rails should run straight up and down the screen, parallel to the edges of the frame.
3. Step back far enough that the rails run the full height of the frame; RackTrack needs to see several full-length vertical lines to judge the angle.

Retake rather than proceeding — a tilted photo mis-assigns devices to the wrong U positions, which is worse than no result.

Note: shooting up or down at the rack is a different problem. That produces the separate message "The image appears to be taken from a side angle. Results may not be accurate." — a warning rather than a stop. If you see that one instead, move to about the middle height of the rack and retake.
symptoms: "The image appears tilted. Please hold the phone straight and retake."
Devices assigned to the wrong U numbers

entries.question: After the scan finished I got an "Image quality warning" pop-up saying it was taken from a side angle. Is my result wrong?
entries.answer:
Not necessarily wrong, but treat it with suspicion. RackTrack noticed the horizontal lines in your photo (the tops and bottoms of each device) are sloping or fanning out, which is what happens when you shoot a rack from off to one side rather than straight on.

It let the scan through rather than blocking it, then showed you the **Image quality warning** box over the Overview tab of your results, with the message "The image appears to be taken from a side angle. Results may not be accurate." and these tips:
• Stand directly in front of the rack — not at an angle.
• Keep the camera level with the middle of the rack.
• Make sure the full rack fits inside the frame.

At an angle, devices near the far edge of the rack are the ones most likely to be missed or misidentified. You have two buttons:
• **Retake** — takes you back to the scan screen so you can shoot it square-on. Use this if the unit map looks wrong at one end.
• **Proceed anyway** — dismisses the warning and keeps the result you already have. Use this if the unit map looks right; the scan itself is complete either way.

(The same warning box is also used for other image-quality problems, such as a rack whose front is buried in cabling — the message line at the top tells you which one fired.)

"The image appears to be taken from a side angle. Results may not be accurate."

entries.question: "This rack is heavily covered by cables" — it won't scan my patched-up rack.
entries.answer:
RackTrack looked at your photo and worked out that cables, not equipment faces, dominate the view — either because cable edges outnumber device edges, or because a large share of the picture is brightly-coloured patch cable. It tells you which, e.g. "cable edges dominate (2.4x device edges)" or "41% of view is colored cables".

The message asks you to **take additional photos from the left and right sides of the rack so we can see behind the cable bundles, or proceed with this image (results may miss devices)**.

What to do, in order:
1. If you can, **dress or lift the cable bundle** aside briefly and reshoot square-on. This gives by far the best result.
2. Otherwise shoot from slightly left and slightly right of centre so the gaps between bundles reveal different devices, and use the **MULTI** mode to submit them together.
3. Only as a last resort press **Proceed anyway** — the scan will run, but devices hidden behind cable bundles will simply be missing from the unit map.

A milder version of this appears as a warning after the scan: "Cables cover much of the rack — some devices behind cable bundles may not be detected. Side-angle photos would improve accuracy." That one lets the scan through but tells you to expect gaps.

"Cables cover much of the rack — some devices behind cable bundles may not be detected."

entries.question: "Please take the photo from the front of the rack — we need to see the devices and ports face-on."
entries.answer:
The analysis ran all the way through but found **zero devices** in the finished result, so RackTrack discarded the scan rather than showing you an empty rack.

Usual causes:
• You shot the **rear** of the rack (cable spaghetti and power leads, no faceplates).
• You were side-on rather than square to the rack, or it was too dark.
• The rack door was shut, or glass/mesh was between you and the equipment.
• You were too far away for any faceplate to be readable.

**Fix:** open the front door, stand square-on far enough back that the whole rack fits inside the guide box, and reshoot. If the shutter will not fire, the hint line under the guide box names the one quality check still failing.

Related messages:

• **"This doesn't look like a server rack. Point the camera at the front of a rack so its devices and ports are visible."** — same underlying problem, but caught immediately instead of after a long wait, because a quick pre-check found no devices before the full analysis started.

• **"Please upload a clearer photo of the rack — keep the camera steady and make sure the full rack fits in the frame."** — most often means devices were found but fewer than three rack units were mapped, i.e. only a sliver of the rack is in shot, so step back until the whole cabinet is in frame. Note that RackTrack also falls back to this same message if the analysis fails for an unrelated reason, so if reshooting a clearly-framed full-rack photo keeps producing it, it is not your photo — escalate.

"Please upload a clearer photo of the rack — keep the camera steady and make sure the full rack fits in the frame."

entries.rootCause: Post-pipeline gates in POST /api/analyze: deviceCount === 0 → front-of-rack error; unitCount < 3 → clearer-photo error. Both are skipped when skipQualityCheck is set.

entries.question: The MULTI (tall rack) stitch failed or produced a mangled panorama.
entries.answer:
MULTI takes **2 to 8 overlapping photos** of a rack too tall for one frame and joins them into one tall image before analysing. The screen tells you: "Take 2-8 overlapping photos of the rack. Any order — we'll arrange them automatically." You do not need to add them in order; RackTrack works out the top-to-bottom sequence itself.

The errors you may see:
• **"Please upload at least 2 images to stitch (top-to-bottom)."** — you only added one. The button reads "Add 1 more photo" until you do.
• **"Could not stitch and analyze the rack. Make sure each photo shows the rack front and adjacent shots overlap by ~20–40%."** — this is the key one. **Adjacent photos must overlap by roughly 20–40%** (about a fifth to two-fifths of the frame). If you shot the top half and the bottom half with no common band, there is nothing for RackTrack to match on.
• **"No devices were detected on the stitched rack — make sure each photo shows the front of the rack and the shots overlap."** — the join worked but no equipment was found; usually the rear of the rack or a closed door.

**How to shoot it:** start at the top, and for each next photo include roughly the bottom third of what you just captured. Keep the same distance and the same left-right position for every shot — moving sideways between shots is the most common cause of a bad join. If RackTrack cannot confidently match a pair it butts them flush instead, which shows up as a visible step in the middle of the rack.
symptoms: "Please upload at least 2 images to stitch (top-to-bottom)."

entries.question: My upload is rejected — "Unsupported file type" or it fails on a large video.
entries.answer:
Two separate limits apply.

**File type.** RackTrack accepts JPG/JPEG, JFIF, PNG, GIF, WebP, TIFF, AVIF, BMP and HEIC/HEIF for photos, and MP4, MOV, WEBM, M4V and AVI for video.

There are two checks. In the app, anything that isn't recognised as an image or a video at all — a PDF, a ZIP, a document — is refused immediately with **"Unsupported file type. Upload an image or video."** A file that *is* an image or video but isn't in the list above (for example a .mkv recording or an unusual image format) gets past that first check and is then refused by the server, which shows a generic upload error rather than the message above. Either way, converting the file to a standard format — JPG or PNG for photos, MP4 or MOV for video — fixes it.

HEIC photos from an iPhone are fine — the browser can't read them, so RackTrack skips its own checks and lets the server convert them.

**File size.** The hard cap per file is **340 MB**. Long 4K videos are the only realistic way to hit it. If you do, record a shorter clip (the video limit is 120 seconds anyway) or drop the recording quality.
symptoms: "Unsupported file type. Upload an image or video."
Large video upload fails with a generic error
entries.rootCause: Client validateMedia rejects any MIME that is not image/* or video/*. Server multer applies a 340 MB fileSize limit and a fileFilter driven by _safeExt's extension whitelist.

entries.question: I'm scanning a row of racks quickly and got "Too many uploads — retry in 34s" / rate_limited.
entries.answer:
Scan uploads are capped at **20 per minute per signed-in user** (a token bucket, refilling continuously). The cap is shared across every scan-type upload: single photo, MULTI stitch, video, rack-label OCR, the ticket/incident verification routes — **and the live camera overlay**. Going over it returns HTTP 429 with **"Too many uploads — retry in Ns"**, where N is the seconds until a token is available. The request is rejected before the file is stored, so nothing is lost and nothing was half-processed.

If you hit it:

• Wait the number of seconds shown and scan again.

• **If you hit it while barely scanning, an open Camera tab is almost certainly the cause.** The viewfinder posts a frame every 0.4 seconds to draw the live device labels — roughly 150 requests a minute against a 20-a-minute budget. Those background frames fail silently, but they drain the allowance, so the shutter press is what surfaces the error. Close the camera view (the X in the top corner) whenever you aren't actively shooting, or use the **Upload** tab to pick photos from the camera roll instead.

The limit is keyed to your account, not your network, so colleagues on the same site don't consume each other's allowance. Administrators can raise it on the server via the RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_MIN setting; note the limit is tracked per server process, so it isn't shared if the server is ever run as multiple instances.
entries.rootCause: lib/rate_limit.js uploadLimiter token bucket, DEFAULT_RATE 20/min keyed by user id (falling back to IP), applied as scanLimit to /api/detect, /api/analyze, /api/stitch, /api/analyze-video, /api/ocr/labels and the ticket routes. The camera's live overlay posts to /api/detect every DETECT_INTERVAL_MS = 400.

const DEFAULT_BURST = Number(process.env.RATE_LIMIT_BURST) || DEFAULT_RATE;

const DETECT_INTERVAL_MS = 400;

entries.question: I switched apps while a scan was running and came back to the upload screen — is my scan lost?
entries.answer:
No. The scan keeps running on the server even though your phone lost the connection.

When you start a scan RackTrack quietly notes a ticket for it. When you come back to the app it checks that ticket and, if the scan finished, takes you straight to the results — you don't need to rescan.

Two things to know:

• The ticket lasts **15 minutes from the moment the scan started** (not from when you left the app). If more than 15 minutes have passed since you hit SCAN, the ticket expires and you'll land on the upload screen. The scan itself may well have completed — check **Profile**, which lists your past scans, before rescanning.

• If you come back while the scan is still running, RackTrack waits about 45 seconds for it. If it hasn't finished by then you'll see the upload screen, but the ticket is still held — reopen or re-foreground the app and it will try again and drop you on the results.

• Rescanning the exact same photo costs you nothing anyway — an identical image is recognised and returns instantly.

**Tip:** the progress bar deliberately stops at 88% and waits. That's normal — the bar is an estimate, not a real measurement. Don't background the app just because it looks stuck.

While it checks, the app shows a full-screen message — "Bringing your scan back…" with "We're finishing the analysis you started. This takes a moment." — and it polls about every 1.5 seconds.

entries.question: "Your organization is awaiting owner approval before you can scan."
entries.answer:
Your account is fine — the organisation it belongs to isn't in an "active" state, and RackTrack blocks scanning until it is. Nothing you can change in the app will lift this.

Check the message on your Waiting-for-approval screen, because there are three different situations behind the same scan error:

- **"Waiting for approval"** — your organisation has been submitted and is sitting in the platform owner's approval queue. It appears there automatically; you don't need to do anything to put it in front of them. The screen re-checks every few seconds and will let you straight in the moment it's approved, so in most cases waiting is the right move. There's no automatic email to the owner, so if it's been sitting unusually long, a direct nudge is reasonable.
- **"Request not approved"** — the owner declined the request. Waiting will not change this; contact the platform owner if you think it's a mistake.
- **"Organization deactivated"** — the owner has switched your organisation off. It will come back on its own if they reactivate it.

Once the organisation is active, scanning works immediately with no further action from you.
symptoms: "Your organization is awaiting owner approval before you can scan."
Held on the Waiting for approval screen
Scan button works but every scan is refused
entries.rootCause: POST /api/analyze calls auth.isOrgActive(organizationId) and returns 403 for any non-active organization before touching the pipeline.
entries.short: Scanning is blocked because your organization isn't active — awaiting approval, request declined, or deactivated; only the owner can change it.

entries.question: The live ports screen says "The switch didn't respond. Check you're on the same network as the switch, then Retry."
entries.answer:
RackTrack tried to log into the switch over the network and got no answer at all within the time allowed.

By far the most common cause is being on the **wrong network** — guest Wi-Fi, a mobile hotspot, or a different VLAN from the switch's management address. From those networks the switch simply isn't reachable.

Check, in this order:
1. **Are you on the right network?** Get off guest Wi-Fi and onto the network that can reach the switch's management address.
2. **Is the switch's management address still the same?** RackTrack already retries a short list of known addresses automatically, so a DHCP change usually recovers on its own — but if the switch moved to an address RackTrack has never seen, every attempt times out.
3. **Is a firewall or ACL blocking SSH (port 22)** between you and the switch's management address? A silently dropped connection looks identical to "not responding".

Then tap **Retry**.

A related wording — "The switch didn't respond in time. Check you're on the same network as it, then tap Retry." — means the whole attempt was abandoned after about 38 seconds rather than a single address timing out.

None of this affects your rack photo scan; the unit map, devices and ports read from the photo are unaffected.

entries.question: "Lost the SSH session to the switch — it may limit simultaneous connections. Tap Retry."
entries.answer:
The connection to the switch was established and then dropped. Small managed switches typically allow only **one** SSH session at a time, so this normally means something else already has it — a colleague on the switch, a terminal window someone left open, or RackTrack's own background check.

**What to do:** wait a moment and tap **Retry** once. Usually the slot frees and the second attempt works.

**What not to do:** don't hammer Retry. On these switches every failed attempt can leave another stuck session behind, which makes the problem worse rather than better.

If retrying keeps failing, you may see the more specific message: *"The switch accepted the login but refused a CLI session — its concurrent-session limit is saturated by stuck sessions. Do NOT keep retrying (each attempt adds another session). Clear it out-of-band: log into the switch web UI and disable/enable SSH, or reboot the switch; then a single probe will succeed."* Follow exactly that — clear it from the switch's own web interface, then try once.
symptoms: "Lost the SSH session to the switch — it may limit simultaneous connections. Tap Retry."
"The switch accepted the login but refused a CLI session — its concurrent-session limit is saturated by stuck sessions."
Not connected / Unable to open shell in logs

Server-side, when auth succeeded but the shell channel closed, the close handler emits the saturation message. Retries are deliberately capped at one attempt (attempts = 1) because reconnecting adds stuck sessions.
