entries.question: The live switch read returns nothing useful, or garbled columns, on our Juniper/Arista/HPE/Aruba switch.
entries.answer:
RackTrack's live switch reading only understands the command sets for three switch types: Cisco IOS, D-Link and TP-Link. If your switch is a different make, RackTrack quietly falls back to one of those command sets rather than telling you the vendor isn't supported — the live read and console features fall back to Cisco IOS, and port-locate falls back to TP-Link. Because there's no "unsupported vendor" message, it looks like a bug rather than a limitation.

So on a Juniper, Arista, HPE or Aruba switch, RackTrack ends up sending commands the switch doesn't understand. The switch either rejects them or returns output in a shape RackTrack can't read, so you get empty tables, missing speed/VLAN columns, or a probe that ends with "Probe returned no port rows." (One partial exception: the general-purpose neighbour reader can understand Aruba/Juniper-style LLDP/CDP output, so the odd neighbour row may still come through — but only when the Cisco command happens to be accepted by the switch.)

What to do: for these switches, use the rack photo scan to capture the port layout, and use your own tools or the Network View for live state. Adding support for a new switch vendor is a product change, so please raise it with RackTrack rather than retrying.

Separately, on Cisco IOL virtual lab devices, speed, duplex and PoE correctly show "—". IOL never negotiates a real link, so the dash is the truth, not a reading failure.
symptoms: Empty port table from a non-Cisco/D-Link/TP-Link switch
entries.rootCause: The VENDORS table defines only 'cisco-ios', 'dlink' and 'tplink'; every switch route resolves vendorKey = VENDORS[vendor] ? vendor : 'cisco-ios', so unsupported vendors silently receive Cisco IOS commands. parseIfStatusFor documents that Cisco IOL returns null speed/duplex by design.

evidence.snippet: const vendorKey = VENDORS[vendor] ? vendor : 'cisco-ios';
if (parsed.length === 0) throw new Error('Probe returned no port rows.');

entries.short: Live switch reads only support Cisco IOS, D-Link and TP-Link; other vendors fall back and misread — use the photo scan and Network View for those.

entries.question: The Network View shows "Network View offline" and no discovery data.
entries.answer:
The Network View is powered by a separate **Netdisco** discovery server, and RackTrack cannot reach it. The badge at the top reads **Network View offline**.

This is a setup issue, not something you can fix from the phone. The badge comes from a quick reachability probe of the Netdisco server, so "offline" means one of exactly two things:

• The Netdisco server isn't running (or is running but not accepting connections).
• RackTrack is pointed at the wrong address for it. By default it looks for Netdisco at `http://localhost:5000`, overridden with the `NETDISCO_URL` setting.

The probe gives up after about 4 seconds, so a very slow or unreachable host also lands here.

RackTrack deliberately hides the raw technical text (connection-refused messages, Python tracebacks, bare status codes) behind the friendly offline banner, so "offline" is all you'll see even though the underlying cause is more specific — an administrator will need to check the server logs.

**A different symptom: the badge says "Network View online" but no devices appear.** That is not a reachability problem. Two likely causes:

• Netdisco rejected the login RackTrack used (`NETDISCO_USER` / `NETDISCO_PASSWORD`, defaulting to admin/admin). Credentials do not affect the online/offline badge — only the data. Requests for the device data time out after 15 seconds.
• Netdisco is reachable and authenticated but simply hasn't discovered those devices. Netdisco finds devices by SNMP, and its shipped configuration reads with SNMP **v2 community `public`**, read-only. Devices with a different community or SNMP version won't be seen. That is configured in Netdisco, not RackTrack.

**Everything else keeps working.** The Network View is the only screen that needs Netdisco; your rack scans, unit map, ports, topology and live switch screens are unaffected.
symptoms: Network view empty with no error text
No devices listed for a rack in Network View
Devices missing from Netdisco but page loads
entries.rootCause: netdisco_proxy.js fetches NETDISCO_URL (default http://localhost:5000) with a 15 s AbortSignal timeout and an api_key login using NETDISCO_USER/NETDISCO_PASSWORD (default admin/admin); failures raise 'Netdisco unreachable' 502. NetdiscoPage's looksLikeNetdiscoNoise suppresses ECONNREFUSED/traceback/bare-status text and renders the offline state. Netdisco's own device_auth ships as SNMP v2 community 'public', read-only.

entries.question: The scan hangs for a long time and then fails with a timeout or "Internal server error".
entries.answer:
There is a hard ceiling on how long a single image analysis may take: **two minutes**. If the analysis worker is still busy after that, RackTrack gives up on it, restarts that worker, and the scan fails with a timeout.

On the phone you'll see the progress overlay sit at 88% (which is normal on its own) and then an error appear on the scan screen.

What causes it:
- A very large or very high-resolution image on a busy or under-powered server.
- Several people scanning at once — by default the server runs a single analysis worker, so scans queue behind each other.
- The worker crashed and is being restarted. If a worker keeps dying within seconds of starting, RackTrack waits longer between restart attempts each time, from 2 seconds up to a maximum of 30 seconds.

**What you can do:** wait a moment and submit the scan again — tap **Analyze Rack** for a single photo, or **Stitch & Analyze** if you are combining several photos of a tall rack. A retry usually succeeds once the queue clears. If every scan times out, the server needs attention: the worker count is sized to the host's memory (each worker holds all the models), and the timeout itself is adjustable.
entries.rootCause: WorkerPool per-request wall-clock cap defaults to RACKTRACK_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS || 120000; on timeout the worker is killed and respawned with 2s→30s exponential backoff on fast crash loops. Pool size defaults to 1 (RACKTRACK_WORKERS). Uncaught errors fall through to o11y.errorHandler which returns 'Internal server error' in production.

evidence.snippet: const WORKER_COUNT = Math.max(1, parseInt(process.env.RACKTRACK_WORKERS, 10) || 1);

entries.short: There is a hard ceiling on how long a single image analysis may take: **two minutes**. If the analysis worker is still busy after that, RackTrack gives up on it, restarts that worker, and the scan fails with a timeout.

entries.question: On an iPad or a computer there's no way to take a photo — where is the scan button?
entries.answer:
On a large screen, use the **Upload** tab rather than the camera — it is already the tab you land on.

The scan screen has two tabs, **Upload** and **Camera**, and under Upload three modes: **SINGLE** (one photo), **MULTI** (2–8 photos of a tall rack) and **VIDEO**. Drag a file onto the drop zone or tap it to browse. SINGLE and MULTI accept JPG, PNG, HEIC and MP4; VIDEO accepts MP4, MOV and WEBM.

The Camera tab does work in a desktop browser if a webcam is available, but a webcam pointed at a rack rarely passes the sharpness, framing and lighting checks, so the shutter tends to stay disabled. Upload is the intended path on iPad and desktop.

Once the file is selected, tap **Analyze Rack**. In MULTI mode the button reads **Add N more photo** until you have at least two photos, then becomes **Stitch & Analyze (N)**. Everything after that is identical to a phone scan.

entries.question: The Switch Information screen is empty and mentions a missing ServiceNow connection. Why?
entries.answer:
The Switch Information screen builds its list from your CMDB (ServiceNow), so it needs a saved ServiceNow connection. Without one the server stops before it queries the CMDB and returns: "No active ServiceNow connection. Add one under Profile → Connections."

If you are a technician (member or site manager): you cannot fix this yourself. Connections are an administrator-only screen, and it will not appear on your Profile. Despite what the message says, contact your organisation admin and ask them to add a ServiceNow connection for the organisation. Everything else in the app — scanning, the unit map, live switch ports, cables, topology, firmware — keeps working without it; only Switch Information and other CMDB-backed views are affected.

If you are an organisation admin or the platform owner: open Profile → Connections (or the Connections panel in the Org Console), tap "Add connection", choose "ServiceNow / CMDB", and fill in Instance ID (just the part before .service-now.com, for example dev266363), Username and Password. It becomes the active connection as soon as you save. Then reopen Switch Information.

Note on precedence: the organisation-wide ServiceNow connection is used first, and only if there is none does the app fall back to the admin's own personal connection. Seeing this message means neither is saved.
symptoms: No active ServiceNow connection. Add one under Profile → Connections.
Serial numbers show as an em dash
entries.rootCause: GET /api/cmdb/rack/:rackId/switches resolves ServiceNow credentials from the org profile then the personal profile, with no env/file fallback; with no active 'servicenow' profile it returns 400 before spawning list_rack_switches.py.

Add one under Profile → Connections.', rack: null, switches: [] }); }

Without one the server stops before it queries the CMDB and returns: "No active ServiceNow connection. Add one under Profile → Connections." If you are a member or site manager you cannot fix this yourself — Connections is an administrator-only screen.

entries.question: I updated a switch in ServiceNow but RackTrack still shows the old details.
entries.answer:
RackTrack keeps the CMDB answer for a rack for up to one minute so the screen loads fast. If you change a switch in ServiceNow, wait about a minute, then leave the Switch Information screen and open it again — the new model, serial or IP appears.

If it still shows the old details after a couple of minutes, ask your administrator to open Connections, select the ServiceNow source and press "Refresh data from this source". A successful refresh (it reports how many incidents were pulled) also drops the stored copy so the next load is fresh; if the refresh reports an error, the old copy stays until the minute is up. The Connections screen is only available to organization administrators and the platform owner.
symptoms: Switch Information shows the previous model, serial or IP
Edit made in ServiceNow not visible immediately
entries.rootCause: _cmdbCache in app.js serves any cached payload younger than 60000 ms; the cache is only cleared explicitly after a successful incident refresh poll.

evidence.snippet:
const _cmdbCache = new Map(); // rackId -> { at, payload }
app.get('/api/cmdb/rack/:rackId/switches', auth.requireAuth, (req, res) => { const cached = _cmdbCache.get(rackId); if (cached && Date.now() - cached.at < 60_000) { return res.json(cached.payload); }
try { _cmdbCache.clear(); } catch (_) {}

entries.short: RackTrack keeps the CMDB answer for a rack for up to one minute so the screen loads fast. If you change a switch in ServiceNow, wait about a minute, then leave the Switch Information screen and open it again — the new model, serial or IP appears.

entries.question: Where do the specifications on a switch come from, and what am I looking at?
entries.answer:
Open the scan result and tap the Switches tab, then pick the switch — the card opens on the Specifications tab, under the heading "Hardware."

What you see is the manufacturer's datasheet for the make and model RackTrack read off the chassis in your photo. Nothing is queried from the switch itself — RackTrack doesn't SSH or SNMP the device for this tab, so it works even when you're not on the switch's network. (It does need to reach the RackTrack server: the app sends the vendor and model, and for a model it hasn't seen before RackTrack may fetch the vendor's datasheet live from the web. Once loaded, the result is cached for that rack, vendor and model.)

The rows are a mix of two things:
1. A fixed set of labelled fields when RackTrack has them: Family, SKU, Ports, Port config, Uplinks, Max port speed (Gbps), Switching capacity (Gbps), Forwarding rate (Mpps), Buffer (MB), Latency (ns), MAC table, PoE, PoE budget (W), Power typical (W), Power max (W), Layer, Features, Rack units, Network OS, Status, Typical use.
2. Everything else RackTrack pulled off the vendor's datasheet, keyed by whatever wording the vendor used (these never overwrite a labelled field above) — which is why one switch shows a handful of rows and another shows dozens.

If a field is blank for that model it's left out rather than shown empty. If RackTrack has no vendor/model yet you'll see "Add vendor and model to see specs." Tap "View full details ↗" at the top right of the Hardware section to open the vendor's own product page and confirm anything that matters before you order or install.

Are these specs read from the switch
One switch shows lots of specs and another shows only a few

entries.question: The switch card says "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo" and there are no specs. What do I do?
entries.answer:
Type the make and model in yourself — the card has a built-in editor and the specs reload as soon as you save.

1. On the Switches tab, expand the device. Its title will be the switch's name if RackTrack has one, otherwise "Unidentified device".
2. Under the heading "Identification" you will see a "Not detected" chip and the line "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo."
3. Tap "Enter make / model" on the right of that heading.
4. Fill in "Make / Vendor" (placeholder: e.g. MikroTik) and "Model" (placeholder: e.g. CRS328-24P-4S+RM). Both are required — Save stays greyed out until you have filled in both. Enter saves, Esc cancels.
5. Tap Save. RackTrack re-runs the spec lookup with your values and the chip changes to "Manual entry". The firmware check also re-runs, but only if RackTrack already knows the device's OS version — if it doesn't, add the version with the firmware section's own editor and the check will run then.

Type the model exactly as printed on the chassis, including hyphens and any + signs. If you get it wrong, tap "Edit" and correct it, or tap "Clear" to remove what you entered and go back to whatever the photo produced.

Why it happens: RackTrack reads the make and model off the label in your photo. A device shot at an angle, in shadow, with the label hidden behind cables, or with no printed model on the front will come back blank. (If only one of the two fields came back blank you will see "Vendor not detected" or "Model not detected" instead, and the button reads "Add vendor" / "Add model" — the same editor.)

entries.question: It got the brand right but the model is missing — "We identified "Cisco" but couldn't read the model. Specs and firmware checks need both."
entries.answer:
Add the missing half by hand. Specs and the firmware check will not run on a brand alone.

1. On the Switches tab, expand the device.
2. Under "Identification" you will see a chip reading either "Model not detected" or "Vendor not detected".
3. Tap the action on the right — it reads "Add model" when the vendor is known, or "Add vendor" when only a model was read.
4. Both boxes ("Make / Vendor" and "Model") appear, prefilled with whatever was detected. Fill in the blank one and leave the other as it is. Save stays greyed out until both boxes have text, then tap Save (or press Enter).

Saving re-runs the lookup immediately — the Specifications tab switches from "Add vendor and model to see specs." to the real spec table, and the firmware check runs too (if an OS version is known). You do not need to close and reopen the card.

Afterwards the chip reads "Manual entry" and the link becomes "Edit", so you can correct the values later or clear them to fall back on what the scan read.

This half-detected case is common: the brand name is usually a big silkscreen logo that survives a bad photo, while the model number is small printed text on a sticker. If you can, get closer to the label and re-shoot the rack; otherwise just type the model in.

entries.question: I typed in the make and model on the Switches tab, but my colleague still sees "Unidentified device" — and it vanished when I used a different phone.
entries.answer:
That is expected. A make/model you type on the Switches tab is saved only in the browser or app you typed it in. It is not sent to the server, so it does not travel to your teammates, to another phone, or to a browser where you cleared site data.

What it does do: it sticks on that device for you across reloads. The saved value is keyed to the device's serial number, MAC address or U position — deliberately not to the make/model you can change — so it survives a re-scan that reads different text off the label. (If the device has no serial, MAC or position at all, the value is pinned to the detected device name instead, and a re-scan that names it differently will lose it.)

If the whole team needs the corrected identity:
- Correct the device on the scan result itself instead. Open the device from the Device list and answer "No" to "Detected as <type> — right?" for the device type; that correction is posted to the server and merged into the scan, so your organisation sees it.
- For the make and model specifically there is no shared correction: everyone who needs the specs has to type it once on their own device, or you re-shoot the rack with the label readable so the photo picks it up for everyone.

To remove your typed value, expand the device, tap "Edit" under Identification, and tap "Clear". (Before you have entered anything, that button reads "Enter make / model", "Add model" or "Add vendor" instead of "Edit".)
symptoms: My make/model correction isn't visible to my team
Manual entry disappeared on another device
Typed model didn't save for everyone
Manual entry chip only shows for me
entries.rootCause: saveOverride writes to localStorage under racktrack:<field>:<rackId>::<stableId>; there is no server round-trip, so the override is per browser profile.
entries.short: That is expected. A make/model you type on the Switches tab is saved only in the browser or app you typed it in. It is not saved to RackTrack, so it does not travel to your teammates, to another phone, or to a browser where you cleared site data. What it does do: it sticks on that device for you across reloads.

entries.question: [Internal] How does the OCR model auto-correction work, and does the UI tell the user it happened?
entries.answer:
Internal only — do not describe this mechanism to customers beyond "RackTrack may correct a misread model number".

POST /api/specs and POST /api/firmware both take an optional `fromOcr` flag (server/app.js:7009 and 7190).

Who sets it:
- client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:309 — direct fetches set it to `!!sw._fromOcr && !modelIsUserSupplied`, i.e. OCR-derived AND the user has not manually overridden the model.
- client/src/utils/scanPrefetch.js:172 and :184 — the background prefetcher always sends `fromOcr: true` for every OCR device it walks. So a prefetched, client-cached spec/firmware result may already contain a substitution even for a device the technician later edits.

When fromOcr is true, resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection (server/app.js:7071-7090) runs:
1. A DB-only probe (`--no-live`) on "<vendor> <model>". On a hit it returns with matchedFrom/matchedTo null.
2. Otherwise it takes probe.response.suggestions and scores each against the queried model with _modelSimilarity (server/app.js:7032-7050) = 0.6 * (shared-prefix chars / shorter string length) + 0.4 * (in-order common chars / longer string length), alphanumeric-normalised and case-insensitive. _bestSuggestion (7052-7065) returns the top scorer only if its score is >= 0.5. If that suggestion differs from the query, it retries live with "<vendor> <suggestion>"; a successful retry returns matchedFrom = original model, matchedTo = suggestion.
3. If the retry fails or no suggestion qualifies, it falls back to a live lookup of the original query and reports no substitution.

When a substitution happened the response carries matchedFrom (what OCR read) and matchedTo (what was actually looked up) — /api/specs at 7021-7024, /api/firmware at 7211-7214. A grep of client/src shows nothing reads either field, so the swap is invisible in the UI. That is the root cause of "the specs are for a different model" tickets.

/api/firmware runs the same probe purely for its matchedTo (the probe's spec result is discarded) and sets firmwareModel = matchedTo || model before calling the agent's --firmware mode (7199-7207), so a bad substitution also skews the firmware verdict. Note the response's `model` field still echoes the model the client sent, not matchedTo.
symptoms: User reports specs for a sibling model
matchedFrom / matchedTo in the API response
Why did the lookup use a different model number
entries.rootCause: resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection substitutes a similar model above a 0.5 similarity threshold and the client never renders matchedFrom/matchedTo, so the swap is invisible.
entries.short:
Internal only — do not describe this mechanism to customers beyond "RackTrack may correct a misread model number".
1. A DB-only probe (`--no-live`) on "<vendor> <model>". On a hit it returns with matchedFrom/matchedTo null.
2. 4 * (in-order common chars / longer string length), alphanumeric-normalised and case-insensitive. 5.

entries.question: How does RackTrack work out the make and model from a photo — and what can I do to help it?
entries.answer:
It reads the printed label on the front of each device. For the devices worth OCRing — switches, servers, routers, firewalls, aggregation/core gear, and anything the scan couldn't classify — RackTrack crops that device out of your rack photo, enlarges the crop if it's less than about 120 pixels tall, and runs text recognition on it three times (plain, contrast-boosted and sharpened) so faint text on dark plastic still comes out. Patch panels, PDUs, UPS units and blank panels are deliberately skipped: they rarely carry model text and OCRing them just adds noise.

It then works through the recognised text in this order:

1. Model-number patterns first. If the text contains something shaped like a known SKU — for example WS-C…/C9300-48P (Cisco), TL-SG… (TP-Link), DGS-/DXS- (D-Link), EX/QFX/MX/SRX (Juniper), CRS/CCR/CSS/RB (MikroTik), USW-/UDM-/ES- (Ubiquiti UniFi and EdgeSwitch), GS/JGS/XS (NETGEAR) and others — that both gives the model and fixes the brand.
2. If no model pattern matches, it looks for a manufacturer name from RackTrack's vendor list.
3. If that fails, it looks for brand words like Catalyst, Nexus, Meraki, JetStream, Omada, ProCurve, PowerEdge, ProSafe, UniFi, RouterOS, FortiGate and DiskStation, and tolerates common misreads (Csco, Unfi, Mikrorik) via a fuzzy match.

What helps, in order of impact:
- Shoot the rack straight on, not from the side — the label has to be square to the lens.
- Get light on the front panel; the label is usually small dark text.
- Move cables off the label if you can.
- Fill the frame with the rack so each device gets more pixels.

If it still misses, open the device on the Switches tab and use the "Identification" section — "Enter make / model" — to type them in. Saving clears the cached results and re-runs the specs and firmware lookups straight away. (Both fields are needed: with only a vendor, specs and firmware checks can't run.)

entries.question: The Switches tab just says "Scanning…" / "Run a rack scan to detect switches." and never fills in.
entries.answer:
Reading the chassis labels (per-device OCR) is a separate, slower step that the server kicks off in the background once your scan finishes — on CPU it takes roughly 1-2 minutes for a full rack. Until it writes its result, the Switches tab has nothing to list and shows the misleading "Scanning…" empty state.

What to do:
1. Wait a minute or two, then leave the Switches tab and come back. The tab only checks once, when it opens — it does not keep retrying — so re-opening it (or reloading the page) is what triggers a fresh check.
2. If it is still empty after several minutes, confirm the scan actually found devices: the rack Overview should show a unit map with devices in it. No detected devices means there is nothing to read labels from.
3. If devices were detected but no switch appears, the rack may contain no device classified as a switch. This tab lists switches only — routers and patch panels are deliberately excluded even when detected.

Older scans taken before label-reading existed will also stay empty; re-scan the rack to get identification for it.

Switches tab empty after a scan
entries.rootCause: GET /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices returns 404 until ocr_devices.json exists; the prefetcher gives up after 8 consecutive 404s until the page is reloaded, and the empty state renders when the switch list is empty.

entries.question: [Internal] A rack keeps showing the same wrong make/model after re-processing. How is device identification re-run?
entries.answer:
Internal only.

Per-device label OCR is written once per rack to outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json. scheduleOcrDevices() (server/app.js:1577) is a fire-and-forget spawn of `python -m pipeline.ocr_devices <rackId> --json` and returns immediately if that file already exists, or if device_unit_map.json is missing (server/app.js:1583). It is only called from scheduleCanonicalRefresh() (server/app.js:1478), so a canonical refresh, a Netdisco resync, or re-opening the rack all keep serving the original identification.

To force a re-identification: POST /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices (server/app.js:7356). It runs pipeline.ocr_devices synchronously with a 5-minute timeout (OCR_DEVICES_TIMEOUT_MS, server/app.js:7355; EasyOCR on CPU is the slow path, 1-2 min for a full rack), 404s if outputs/<rackId> does not exist, 504s on timeout, and returns the parsed JSON. pipeline/ocr_devices.py always rewrites outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json (line 588), so the cached result is overwritten. GET on the same path only reads that cached file (404 if OCR has never run).

Important caveat: only the background run re-syncs downstream — after a successful spawn, scheduleOcrDevices rewrites the canonical scan result and reschedules the Netdisco sync (server/app.js:1600-1608). The POST endpoint does NOT do this. After forcing a re-run via POST you must also trigger a canonical refresh / CMDB rebuild, or downstream consumers (synth.py, Netdisco, CMDB) keep serving the old synthesized make/model.

Customer-facing wording: tell the user to re-scan the rack (new rack id, therefore a fresh OCR run). Do not give customers the endpoint.
symptoms: Same wrong model after reprocessing a rack
entries.rootCause: scheduleOcrDevices short-circuits when outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json exists, so identification is computed exactly once per rack id.
entries.short: Internal only. Per-device label OCR is written once per rack to outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json, and scheduleOcrDevices() returns immediately if that file already exists — so a canonical refresh, a Netdisco resync or re-opening the rack all keep serving the original identification. To force a re-run, POST /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices.

entries.question: How do I look up the datasheet for a device that isn't in a scan?
entries.answer:
Use the Specifications screen at /specifications — it is a standalone lookup and is not linked from the sidebar or bottom nav today, so navigate to the URL directly (you must be signed in). On a desktop or tablet the top bar then reads "Specifications / Vendor & model lookup"; the page heading is "Find datasheet specs for a device."

1. Type the maker into "Make / Vendor" (placeholder: e.g. Cisco, Juniper, Aruba). Up to six matching vendor suggestions appear as you type — tap one to fill the box.
2. Type the model into "Model" (placeholder: e.g. C9300-48P, EX4400-24T).
3. Tap "Get specifications". The button reads "Searching…" while it works. Leaving either box empty gives "Both vendor and model are required."

You get a summary card with the vendor and model, a line reading "We pulled N specs from the vendor's product page — here are the most useful ones at a glance", and up to five headline rows picked from Ports, Throughput, Layer, Form factor, Power, PoE, Uplinks, MAC table and Stacking. If the product page is found but no spec table can be extracted, it says so instead.

Underneath:
- "Open product page ↗" — opens the vendor's own page in a new tab (shown only when a product URL was found).
- "Show all specs (N)" — expands the full spec table; it then reads "Hide all specs".

This screen is a pure lookup: it does not touch your rack, your scans or your CMDB, and nothing you type here is saved to a scan.

entries.question: The vendor box doesn't suggest my manufacturer, or it says "Vendor list unavailable". Can I still search?
entries.answer:
Yes — type the vendor name in anyway and tap "Get specifications". The suggestion list is only a convenience; the lookup itself does not require the name to be on it.

Things to know about that list:
- It comes from RackTrack's vendor sheet on the server, loaded once when the screen opens.
- It only shows suggestions once you start typing, and never more than six at a time — keep typing to narrow it down.
- If the server could not supply it you get "Vendor list unavailable: …" under the box. The search still works.

You do always need both fields filled in — leaving "Make / Vendor" or "Model" empty gives "Both vendor and model are required."

If the lookup then comes back with no match, the vendor spelling is usually not the problem — re-check the Model field instead and enter the exact SKU as printed on the device, hyphens included (e.g. C9300-48P). Very short or generic model strings are the most common cause of a miss; if it still misses, confirm the full part number on the maker's own site.
symptoms: My vendor isn't in the dropdown
No suggestions when typing a vendor
entries.rootCause: The type-ahead is populated from GET /api/specs/vendors (the vendor Excel sheet) and sliced to 6; POST /api/specs passes the typed vendor string straight through without validating it against that list.
entries.short: Yes — type the vendor name in anyway and tap "Get specifications". The suggestion list is only a convenience; the lookup itself does not require the name to be on it. Things to know about that list: - It comes from RackTrack's vendor sheet in RackTrack, loaded once when the screen opens.

entries.question: The Specifications screen shows "Both vendor and model are required." or an error about the backend / port 3001.
entries.answer:
Three different messages, three different causes:

"Both vendor and model are required." — you left one of the two boxes empty. Fill in both Make / Vendor and Model, then tap "Get specifications" again. Nothing was sent to the server.

"Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP …). Is the server running?" — the request reached something, but it did not answer with a result. Usually a server-side problem, not yours.

"Request failed: … Is the backend running on port 3001?" — the request never completed at all: no signal, no network, a VPN that just dropped, or RackTrack's server unreachable from where you are standing.

For the last two: check you have a working data or Wi-Fi connection, then retry once. If it keeps failing while the rest of the app works, report it to your administrator with the exact message and the make/model you typed — it is a server-side fault, not something you can fix on the phone.
symptoms: Both vendor and model are required
Is the backend running on port 3001
Request failed on the Specifications screen
entries.rootCause: SpecificationsPage validates both fields client-side, then distinguishes an unparsable response body from a thrown fetch error and shows a different banner for each.

"Both vendor and model are required." means you left one of the two boxes empty — fill in both Make / Vendor and Model, then tap "Get specifications" again; nothing was sent to the server. The other two, "Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP …). Is the server running?" and "Request failed: … Is the backend running on port 3001?", are server-side or connection faults, not something you can fix on the phone.

entries.question: It says "We found the product page but couldn't extract a spec table" — where are the specs?
entries.answer:
RackTrack located the manufacturer's page for your model but could not turn it into a table — some vendors publish specs as a PDF, an image, or behind a tab that has to be clicked. The lookup itself succeeded; the extractor just returned zero fields.

Use the link instead:
- On the Specifications screen, tap "Open product page ↗" in the summary card and read the specs on the vendor's own page.
- If the lookup failed outright but a candidate page was still found, you get "Found a candidate page but couldn't extract specs:" followed by the URL — tap it.
- On a switch card's Specifications/Hardware tab, the same link is "View full details ↗" at the top right of the Hardware section. With zero specs the table below it will be empty — that is expected, not a loading state.

If no link appears either, the vendor page had no datasheet or image URL to fall back on; search the vendor's site for the model directly.

There is nothing to retry here — re-running the same vendor/model gives the same result. A different model from the same vendor will often extract fine. If you need the numbers recorded against the rack, note them from the vendor page.

entries.question: What is the "Login portal" / "Vendor site" chip next to the switch name?
entries.answer:
It is a shortcut to the manufacturer's own website for the brand RackTrack identified. It appears on the small grey line directly beneath the device name on the switch card, alongside the U position and IP address.

- "Login portal" means RackTrack has that maker's actual customer/support sign-in page on file — tap it to sign in to the vendor and look up entitlement, downloads or case history. For brands that were absorbed by another company, the link goes to the parent brand's portal (for example an Aerohive switch opens the Extreme Networks sign-in).
- "Vendor site" means RackTrack only has a general support or landing page for that maker.
- No chip at all means the make is blank, or the make RackTrack read didn't match anything in its vendor list — usually an unusual spelling.

To make the chip appear when the make is missing or misread:
1. Tap the switch card to expand it.
2. Under "Identification", tap "Enter make / model" (or "Add vendor" / "Edit").
3. Fill in BOTH "Make / Vendor" and "Model" — Save stays greyed out until both boxes have text.
4. Tap Save. The card re-checks specs and firmware, and the chip appears if the make matches a known vendor.

The chip opens in your phone's browser, in a new tab, not inside RackTrack. RackTrack does not have your vendor account — you sign in with your own company's credentials on the vendor's site. Tapping the chip does not expand or collapse the switch card.
symptoms: What is the Login portal link
Vendor site chip on the switch card
No vendor link shown for my switch
Where do I sign in to the manufacturer
entries.rootCause: SwitchCard calls findVendorLogin(effectiveMake) against a generated vendor→portal map; source 'login' renders the "Login portal" chip, 'fallback' renders "Vendor site", null renders nothing.
entries.short:
It is a shortcut to the manufacturer's own website for the brand RackTrack identified.
1. Tap the switch card to expand it.
2. Under "Identification", tap "Enter make / model" (or "Add vendor" / "Edit").
3. Fill in BOTH "Make / Vendor" and "Model" — Save stays greyed out until both boxes have text.

entries.question: In the port view, some downstream devices show a maker name and others say "Unknown". Where does that name come from?
symptoms: Downstream device shows Unknown instead of a maker
Where does the vendor name next to a MAC come from

entries.rootCause: The client extracts the first 3 octets of each MAC and asks /api/oui/lookup, which reads the IEEE OUI table; prefixes registered as 'Private' are omitted when the table is built, so those resolve to null and render as unknown.

The first three pairs of a MAC (the OUI) are a block the IEEE assigns to one company, so RackTrack can name who built a device it has never seen — that is how a MAC hanging off a port gets labelled Dell, Realtek, Apple and so on.

entries.question: What do the words on the Firmware tab mean — "Up to date", "Upgrade available", "Latest version unknown"?
entries.answer:
The pill next to the word Firmware on the Firmware tab is the whole verdict. Once the check finishes, it says exactly one of six things:

1. "Up to date" — the version we have on file for this model is character-for-character the same as the version you are running. (We compare the two strings exactly; we do not do clever version maths.)
2. "Upgrade available" — the version we have on file is different from yours. Read it as "different", not automatically "newer" — check the release notes before you act.
3. "Recommended min: <version>" — we could not confirm a latest version, but we do have a minimum safe version to aim for.
4. "Check vendor portal" — this vendor keeps its release notes behind a login, so all we can do is point you at their portal.
5. "Couldn't read latest — check vendor" — we have a release-notes link but could not pull a version number out of it.
6. "Latest version unknown" — we have nothing on file. This is NOT the same as being up to date.

Underneath the pill you get up to four cells:
- Current — the version on the switch.
- Latest — the version we have on file. If we don't have one, this cell shows a dash; if we don't have one but we do recognise the vendor, it turns into a tappable "Check site ↗" that opens that vendor's official download page.
- Min safe — only shown when there is a recommended minimum version and it differs from Latest.
- A "Release notes ↗" link, or "Vendor portal ↗" if there is no release-notes link.

Whenever Latest is unknown, a short plain-English line appears below the cells explaining why (or saying we couldn't find a verified latest firmware for that make/model) — read that line, it is usually the most useful thing on the tab.

entries.question: It says "Upgrade available" — what am I supposed to do about it?
entries.answer:
RackTrack cannot upgrade anything. It only compares two version strings and shows you where to read. Do this:

1. Open the vendor's own notes from the badge. On the switch's firmware card that link is "Release notes ↗" (or "Vendor portal ↗" if no release-notes link was found). On the standalone Firmware page the same link is labelled "source ↗". Read what changed before you touch the switch.
2. Compare the Current and Latest numbers yourself. "Upgrade available" only means the two strings are not identical — we do not order versions, so it does not prove the version we show is newer than yours.
3. If the change matters, raise it through your normal change process and upgrade from the vendor's own download page. Nothing you do on this screen is pushed to the switch.
4. If the switch card shows a "Min safe" number, that is the lowest version worth aiming for. It only appears when it differs from Latest, and it is not shown on the standalone Firmware page.

Nothing on either screen writes to the switch, to your CMDB, or to a ticket.

2. Compare the Current and Latest numbers yourself.

entries.question: It says "Latest version unknown" — does that mean my switch is fine?
entries.answer:
No. It means RackTrack found nothing to compare against. Treat it as "not checked", not as "safe".

On a switch card (Firmware tab), what you see depends on what the lookup came back with:

- "Latest version unknown" with the Latest cell showing "Check site ↗" — tap it; it opens that vendor's official download page. This link only appears for vendors RackTrack knows a download URL for (Cisco, Juniper, Arista, HPE/Aruba, Dell, Fortinet, Extreme, Netgear, TP-Link, D-Link, Ubiquiti, Huawei, Ruijie, Zyxel and similar).
- Latest showing just a dash ("—") — same meaning, but RackTrack has no download URL on file for this vendor, so there is nothing to tap. Search the vendor's own support site yourself.
- "Check vendor portal" — the lookup returned a vendor portal link (often because release notes sit behind a login). Use the "Vendor portal ↗" link; you may need your vendor account.
- "Couldn't read latest — check vendor" — there is a release-notes URL but no readable version in it. Open "Release notes ↗" and read the version yourself.
- "Recommended min: X" — no confirmed latest, but RackTrack knows a minimum safe version. Being at or above X is still not the same as being current.

Below the cells you get either the agent's own explanation or "Couldn't find a verified latest firmware for <vendor> <model> in our database."

On the Firmware Check screen the wording is "We couldn't confirm the latest version." with the body "The vendor's site didn't show a clear latest version. Check the vendor's site yourself — this is not the same as being up to date." Under "Find latest firmware:" you get a "Google search ↗" link, plus a "Vendor support ↗" link when RackTrack has a vendor site on record. (If a version was found but couldn't be compared to yours, the body instead reads "The newest version we saw was X, but we couldn't compare it to Y.")

In every one of these cases the correct assumption is "unverified", not "up to date".

entries.question: Where do I find the racks I scanned earlier? I can't find a History screen.
entries.answer:
Past scans live on your Profile screen, not on a separate History screen.

1. Tap PROFILE in the bottom bar (the person icon, third tab).
2. Scroll to the "Recent Scans" section.
3. Tap any row to reopen that scan's results.

Only your 5 most recent scans are listed at first. If you have more, tap "Show all N scans" at the bottom of the section to reveal your full history ("Show less" collapses it again).

On a desktop or iPad, click "Profile" in the left sidebar — its subtitle is "Account & history".

If you saved an old /history bookmark, it still works: RackTrack now sends it straight to the Profile screen.

entries.question: My Recent Scans list only shows 5 scans — where are the rest?
entries.answer:
Nothing is missing. Recent Scans shows the 5 newest by default and hides the rest behind a button.

1. Open PROFILE and scroll down to the "Recent Scans" section.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the list.
3. Tap "Show all N scans" (N is your real total).
4. The full list appears; tap "Show less" to collapse it back to 5.

The button only appears once you have more than 5 scans, and only after the list has finished loading. There is no page-by-page paging — when expanded, every scan you are allowed to see is on screen at once, newest first.

Note that "allowed to see" depends on your role: a regular member sees only the racks they claimed, an org admin sees every rack in their organization's Sites, and the platform owner sees everything. So if a scan a colleague did is still missing after expanding, that is a permissions boundary, not a truncated list.
symptoms: Where is the rest of my history
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage slices the /api/scans response to 5 unless showAllScans is toggled; the server route returns the complete list with no limit or offset parameter.

evidence.snippet:
// Show the 5 most recent by default; "Show all" reveals the full history.
const recent  = useMemo(() => (showAllScans ? scans : scans.slice(0, 5)), [scans, showAllScans]);

Nothing is missing. Recent Scans shows the 5 newest by default and hides the rest behind a button.
1. Open PROFILE and scroll down to the "Recent Scans" section.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the list.
3. Tap "Show all N scans" (N is your real total).

entries.question: What do the numbers on each row of Recent Scans mean?
entries.answer:
Each row on the Profile page's "Recent Scans" list summarises one scan:

• The picture on the left is the original photo taken of that rack. If no photo was kept, you get a terminal icon instead.
• The bold mono code (for example RK-4F2A9C1B — always "RK-" plus 8 characters) is the rack ID, the scan's permanent address. It is derived from the photo itself, so re-scanning the same image gives the same ID.
• The line under it reads "N dev · N units · N ports":
  – dev = how many devices RackTrack found in the rack.
  – units = how many rack units it mapped.
  – ports = how many port identifications have been recorded for that rack so far. This one grows every time you identify another port, so an older scan can show more ports than a newer one. A single one reads "1 port".
• On the right is how long ago the scan was taken — "just now", "12m ago", "5h ago", "3d ago", "2w ago", "4mo ago". If the scan has no timestamp you'll see a dash.

There is no search box and no sort control: the list is always newest scan first. Only the 5 most recent are shown; tap "Show all N scans" to see the rest.
symptoms: What does 3 dev 12 units 8 ports mean
Port count on history row keeps changing
Can I search my scan history
How is the history list sorted
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage renders rackId, deviceCount, unitCount, portCount and a relative timestamp from /api/scans; portCount is the line count of port_identifications.jsonl, and the server sorts by timestamp descending. No search or sort UI exists.

{s.image ? : terminal}

{s.rackId}

{s.deviceCount} dev · {s.unitCount} units · {s.portCount} port{s.portCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}

entries.question: How do I reopen a scan I did last week and get back to its results?
entries.answer:
Tap it — that is all.

1. PROFILE tab → "Recent Scans".
2. Tap the row for the rack you want. Only the 5 most recent are listed; tap "Show all N scans" to reveal the rest of your history.
3. RackTrack reloads that scan and drops you on its results screen with the same tabs as when you first scanned it: Overview, Switches, Ports and Topology in the tab bar, with Network and Drift under "More".

The address it opens is /results/<rack ID> — rack IDs look like RK- followed by 8 characters, e.g. /results/RK-4F2A9C1B — so you can also bookmark or type that directly and land straight on the scan without going through Profile. Reopening a scan does not re-run the analysis and does not use your camera. If the rack no longer exists on the server, the deep link sends you back to the Scan screen and removes the stale entry from your local history.
symptoms: How do I open an old scan
Get back to last week's rack
entries.rootCause: openScan() fetches /api/scan/<rackId>/report?format=json and navigates to /results/<rackId> with the result preloaded in router state; the /results/:rackId route is deep-linkable and re-fetches via /api/scan/:rackId when opened cold.
entries.short:
Tap it — that is all.
1. PROFILE tab → "Recent Scans".
2. Tap the row for the rack you want.
3. RackTrack reloads that scan and drops you on its results screen with the same tabs as when you first scanned it: Overview, Switches, Ports and Topology in the tab bar, with Network and Drift under "More".

entries.question: I tapped an old scan and a red message appeared saying the scan was not found.
entries.answer:
That scan's data is no longer on the server, so RackTrack cannot rebuild the results screen. The message is "Scan <rack ID> not found" and it appears as a red banner just under the Recent Scans heading on Profile — you stay on Profile, the app does not navigate anywhere.

What to do:
1. Stay on Profile and tap a different row in Recent Scans. If the others open, only that one rack's data is gone.
2. Take a fresh photo of that rack from the SCAN tab. You will get results again (a new rack ID if the photo is new).
3. If several old scans fail the same way, tell your organization admin — something removed rack folders on the server (specifically the scan's scan_meta.json).

Two related cases that look similar but are not the same thing:
- A rack that belongs to a different Site gives "Rack not found" (an access boundary), not "Scan ... not found".
- If you open a /results/<rack ID> link directly and the rack no longer exists, RackTrack shows no error at all: it quietly drops that entry from the app's local history and sends you to the Scan screen.
symptoms: Red banner on Profile when opening a scan
Tapping a history row does nothing / bounces to Scan
entries.rootCause: buildScanReportData throws 'Scan <rackId> not found' when scan_meta.json is missing, and the report route converts any throw into a 404; ProfilePage surfaces the message in scansError. ResultsPage handles a cold-link 404 by pruning the local cache and redirecting to /scan.
entries.short: That scan's data is no longer on the server, so RackTrack cannot rebuild the results screen. The message is "Scan <rack ID> not found" and it appears as a red banner just under the Recent Scans heading on Profile — you stay on Profile, the app does not navigate anywhere.

entries.question: My Recent Scans says "No scans yet." but I have definitely scanned racks.
entries.answer:
"No scans yet." plus a "Start your first scan" button means the server returned an empty list for the account you are signed in as. Work through these in order:

1. Check who you are signed in as — your username and email are shown under your avatar at the top of the same Profile screen. A second account (or a re-signup) starts with an empty history.
2. Check whether you were moved to a different Site. Your history is the racks you claimed while in your current Site; if an admin moved you, the older scans stay with the old Site.
3. Remember that you only see scans you ran yourself. A colleague's scan of the same rack does not appear in your list.
4. If none of that fits, ask your organization admin — they can see every scan from every Site in the organization and can confirm the scan still exists.

A red error banner instead of "No scans yet." means the history failed to load, not that it is empty. The list is only fetched when the Profile screen opens, so navigate away and back to Profile (or reload the app) to retry it.
symptoms: Start your first scan button but I already scanned
entries.rootCause: For a member, /api/scans intersects the outputs folders with tenantUserRackIds(tenant_id, user_id) — racks claimed in the CURRENT Site by THIS user. A different account, a Site move, or a colleague's claim all yield an empty set. The empty state renders only when there is no error.

entries.short: "No scans yet." plus a "Start your first scan" button means the server returned an empty list for the account you are signed in as. Check who you are signed in as (your username and email are shown under your avatar on the same Profile screen), check whether an admin moved you to a different Site, and remember you only see scans you ran yourself.

entries.question: I was moved to a different site and now my old scans are gone from Recent Scans.
entries.answer:
That is expected. Your scan history follows the Site you are in, not just your login.

RackTrack records each scan as "this Site claimed this rack, and this person did it" (rack_owners: tenant_id + created_by). When an admin changes your Site, Recent Scans is rebuilt immediately from the racks claimed in your NEW Site, so scans you ran under the old Site stop showing for you. Nothing was deleted — the old records are still on the server under the old Site.

What to do:
1. Ask your organization admin to look the rack up — an org admin sees every scan from every Site in the organization, including your old ones.
2. If you know the rack ID (RK-…), you may still be able to open it directly for a while: rack access is checked against the Site baked into your login token, and that token is not refreshed when the admin moves you. Once you log out and back in (or the session expires), opening a rack from your old Site returns "Rack not found".
3. To get the rack into your new Site's history permanently, simply scan it again from your new Site.
symptoms: History emptied after being moved to another site
Scans vanished after admin changed my site
Rack not found after site change
Lost my history but colleague still sees it
entries.rootCause: PATCH /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId can set users.tenant_id. /api/scans for a member queries rack_owners by (tenant_id, created_by), and the :rackId guard denies members any rack their current tenant does not own — so a Site move detaches the member from previously claimed racks.

entries.question: Do my past scans expire? How long can I go back and open one?
entries.answer:
No — scans do not expire. Nothing in RackTrack deletes a scan because it got old. A scan you ran stays in Recent Scans and stays openable indefinitely: there is no 30-day, 90-day or 1-year cut-off, and no cap on how many scans you can have. (Recent Scans shows your latest 5 by default; tap "Show all N scans" to see the rest.)

Two things can make a scan drop off your list, and neither is a timer on your history:

• You are looking at it from a different place. As a technician you see the scans you yourself ran inside your current Site — not every scan the Site owns, and not scans you ran under a previous Site or a different account. The scan still exists; it just is not listed for you any more. (Site managers see their org's Sites; the platform owner sees everything.)

• The rack is no longer owned by any Site at all — for example after the organization or Site it belonged to was deleted on the server. Only then does the scan folder become a candidate for the server's orphan clean-up, and even then it is not immediate: the folder must also be older than the retention window (14 days by default), and the nightly job runs in report-only mode unless an operator has explicitly switched deletion on. An admin can also run it on demand.

Separately, live port drift history has its own retention (port events ~30 days, snapshots ~90 days, latest state per port always kept). That is the port timeline, not your scan — the scan, its unit map and its report stay put.

If an old scan matters for an audit, export it: open the scan and download the report (HTML, PDF, CSV or JSON). That gives you a copy that does not depend on the server at all.
symptoms: How long is scan history kept
Do scans get deleted after 30 days
entries.rootCause: Nothing prunes scans by age while a rack_owners row exists; the only scheduled deletion is orphan GC, which targets outputs/RK-* folders with NO rack_owners row and is dry-run unless ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1.

...

entries.short: No — scans do not expire. Nothing in RackTrack deletes a scan because it got old. A scan you ran stays in Recent Scans and stays openable indefinitely: there is no 30-day, 90-day or 1-year cut-off, and no cap on how many scans you can have.

entries.question: Can I put two past scans of the same rack side by side to see what changed?
entries.answer:
There is no built-in "compare two scans" view — RackTrack has no scan-to-scan diff. Each scan stays reachable at its own URL, so compare them by opening both:

• On a laptop or desktop: open /results/<rack ID> for the first scan in one browser tab and the second rack ID in another tab, then flip between them. A rack ID opens cold — you don't need the original scan session.
• On the phone: open one from Profile → Recent Scans, note what you need, use Back, then open the other.

The side-by-side racks you may have seen are a different feature: they belong to a two-rack scan group ("Scan two racks"). On desktop, the Overview tab of such a group shows both racks of that group side by side; the other tabs (Ports, Network, Switches, Drift) and the phone show one rack at a time with a pill toggle, so live port probes don't run twice at once. Either way it compares the two racks of one scan group, not two scans taken at different times.

If what you actually want is what changed on a switch over time, use Port history & drift ("Continuous SSH telemetry") instead — it is built for before/after and has a Change log listing each recorded change.

Note: if a scan has been removed on the server, its /results/<rack ID> link 404s and sends you back to the scan screen.
symptoms: Diff between old and new scan
entries.rootCause: No scan-to-scan diff exists. RackToggle only renders one rack of a multi-rack group at a time; each scan is addressable at /results/:rackId, so the practical workaround is two deep links. Temporal change is covered by the port history/drift view.

entries.question: On a port's History tab, how far back does the "Value at" table and the change log go?
entries.answer:
Open Port history & drift. The page targets your monitored switch automatically — there is no switch picker. Under "Interface inventory" tap a port tile, then in the panel that slides up tap the History tab (it reads "History · N" when that port has changes).

The History tab has two blocks:

• "Value at" — the port's state as it was 1h, 3h, 12h, 1d and 1w ago. Five fixed points, nothing longer than a week. Columns are Ago / Oper / Admin / Speed / Recorded. If consecutive points land on the same recorded state you get one row labelled "1h+" instead of repeated identical rows — that just means the port did not change across that span. (Snapshots are only written on change, so this is normal for a stable port.) On a port with no snapshots yet this block is hidden entirely.

• "Change log (N)" — the most recent changes for that port, newest first, capped at 200. N is how many are being shown, so N = 200 means you are seeing the newest 200 and older ones exist but are not displayed here.

The Timeline tab has its own Window picker: Last 1 Hour, Last 3 Hours, Last 12 Hours, Last 1 Day, Last 1 Week. One week is again the longest view.

If you need to prove a change older than a week, capture the evidence while it is still on screen.
symptoms: Port history only goes back a week
What does 1h+ mean in Value at
entries.rootCause: The /history route computes exactly five offsets (1h/3h/12h/1d/1w) and requests eventsForPort with a limit of 200; the client's WINDOW_OPTIONS top out at 1 week and dedupedOffsets collapses identical snapshots into a '<first>+' row.

  { key: '3h',  label: 'Last 3 Hours', sec: 3  * 3600 },
  { key: '12h', label: 'Last 12 Hours',sec: 12 * 3600 },
  { key: '1d',  label: 'Last 1 Day',   sec: 24 * 3600 },
  { key: '1w',  label: 'Last 1 Week',  sec: 7  * 24 * 3600 },
];

entries.short: Open Port history & drift. The page targets your monitored switch automatically — there is no switch picker. Under "Interface inventory" tap a port tile, then in the panel that slides up tap the History tab (it reads "History · N" when that port has changes).

entries.question: A port's change log says "No changes recorded yet." even though the port has been monitored for days.
entries.answer:
That is a healthy port, not a broken history.

RackTrack only writes a history row when something about the port actually changes. The tracked fields are: operational state (link up/down), admin state, speed, duplex, flow control, active medium, description, and the three LLDP neighbour fields (chassis, port, system). Every poll is compared against the last stored snapshot; if nothing differs, neither a snapshot nor an event is written. A port that has stayed exactly the same since monitoring began therefore has nothing to log, so the History tab shows "Change log (0)" and "No changes recorded yet."

How to confirm the port really is being watched:
1. Switch to the port's Specs tab and look at "Last poll" — it should show a recent time. That timestamp is stamped on every successful poll of the device whether or not anything changed, so a recent value proves monitoring is alive.
2. "Last change" on the same tab tells you when the current state was first recorded — for a never-changed port that is effectively when monitoring began.
3. If you need to prove logging works, shut/no-shut or unplug/replug the port; the change appears on the next poll.

If "Last poll" is blank or very old, the problem is polling (SSH failure or backoff), not history.

One caveat for admins: description tracking can be switched off with the server env var PORT_DRIFT_TRACK_DESCR=0. If that is set, a changed port description will not produce a change-log entry.
symptoms: Port history empty but port is monitored
entries.rootCause: port_events rows are written only on a detected diff (writePollTxn compares against the previous snapshot), and snapshots are likewise written only on change — so a stable port legitimately has zero events.

entries.question: Admin: how many scans does the Organizations console show me, and can I search or filter them?
entries.answer:
The organization dashboard shows the 40 most recent scans across every Site in your organization, newest first — a fixed cap, not page 1 of N. (The platform owner sees no scan grid on the platform-level Organizations list at all — only the totals tiles, pending approvals and org cards; the owner gets the same 40-scan grid once they open a specific organization.)

Filtering is by click, not by typing — there is no search box:
• Click a person's card to narrow the grid to their scans; the heading changes to "Scans · by <username>".
• Click a Site row to narrow to that Site; the heading becomes "Scans · <site name>".
• Click "Show all", or the same card/row again, to clear the filter.

Because the filter is applied in the browser to the 40 rows already loaded, filtering by someone who has not scanned recently can legitimately show "No scans for this selection yet." even though they have older scans. To reach anything older than the last 40, open it by rack ID at /results/<rack ID>.

Note the Scans totals tile counts every scan ever claimed by your Sites, so it will normally be much larger than 40.
symptoms: No scans for this selection yet but the user has scanned
Can I search scans in the organization console
Scan count doesn't match the grid

entries.question: Admin: if I remove a member, or the owner removes an organization, what happens to their scan history?
entries.answer:
Two very different outcomes.

Removing a member:
• The scans survive. In a single step, the person's name is cleared from anything they created or invited, and only their user account is deleted.
• The scan records stay attached to the Site, so the Site and the organization keep seeing them. In the console's scan grid the attribution falls back to "—" instead of "by <username>."
• Caveat: a plain member's own personal history only shows racks they created, so once their name is cleared those scans no longer appear in any member's personal history — only organization admins and the platform owner still see them.
• Guardrails: you cannot remove yourself ("You cannot remove your own account"), an owner account, or — unless you are the platform owner — an organization admin. A site manager can only remove plain members of their own Site.

Removing an organization (platform owner only):
• For each Site in the organization, every rack-ownership and rack-group record is deleted and audit-log entries have their organization link cleared; then the invites, users, Sites and the organization itself are deleted.
• The scan folders on disk are NOT deleted by that action — they simply become unowned. Organization admins and members can no longer list or open them, but the RackTrack platform owner still can, and continues to see every folder on disk.
• Unowned folders older than 14 days then become eligible for the orphan cleanup sweep. That sweep is dry-run by default: the daily scheduled job only logs counts unless it is explicitly switched to apply, and the manual run also defaults to a dry run. So files aren't auto-deleted out of the box, but they are eligible.
• Export anything you need before deleting an organization; there's no in-app undo — only a platform owner can still reach the leftover folders.
symptoms: What happens to scans when I remove a user
Scans show by — instead of a name
Deleting an organization removes scan history
Can I recover scans after removing an org
entries.rootCause: member.remove nulls rack_owners.created_by and deletes only the user; org.remove deletes rack_owners/rack_groups/users/tenants for the org, leaving outputs/<rackId>/ folders unreferenced and therefore orphan-GC eligible.

evidence.snippet: {s.by_user ? `by ${s.by_user}` : '—'}{s.site ? ` · ${s.site}` : ''}

entries.short: Removing a member keeps their scans (attribution shows '—'); deleting an org leaves the scan folders unowned, reachable only by the platform owner.

entries.question: Internal: a scan is counted in the organization totals but never appears in Recent Scans — why?
entries.answer:
Same diagnosis as the entry, with corrected anchors and two additions.

Accurate line references (the cited ones have drifted ~20-27 lines):
- server/app.js:4923-4928 — /api/scans: `fs.readdirSync(outputsDir).filter(name => name.startsWith('RK-')).map(rackId => { if (allowedRacks && !allowedRacks.has(rackId)) return null; const meta = readMeta(rackId); if (!meta) return null; ...`
- server/app.js:679-690 — readMeta: returns null if scan_meta.json is absent, and swallows a JSON.parse error to return null on a truncated/corrupt file.
- server/auth.js:1472 — org dashboard total: `SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM rack_owners WHERE tenant_id IN (${inList})`; server/auth.js:1443 — owner platform total: `SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM rack_owners`.
- server/app.js:3230-3234 — /api/select's comment explaining that it reconstructs and heals a missing meta instead of 404-ing.
- server/app.js:4933 and 4944 — the per-rack device_unit_map.json and port_identifications.jsonl reads that make the endpoint scale with the size of outputs/.

Two causes the entry omits:
1. rack_owners holds one row per (tenant_id, rack_id) claim, and a rack id is a hash of the source image — so if two Sites in the same org scan the same rack, the org total counts it twice while the history list shows it once. Duplicate claims alone can explain a totals/list gap with nothing wrong on disk.
2. Scope mismatch: for a member, /api/scans uses allowedRacks = tenant.tenantUserRackIds(tenantId, userId) (only racks THEY claimed), while the org dashboard total spans every Site in the org. A member's Profile list is expected to be smaller than the org total.

Also note the owner dashboard's own "Recent Scans" table (server/auth.js:1451-1459) is a pure SQL query over rack_owners joined to tenants/organizations/users — it will still show a rack whose files are missing. Only the Profile history list (/api/scans) and /api/racks are filesystem-driven and can silently drop it.

The diagnosis order is otherwise correct: check that outputs/<rackId>/ exists, check scan_meta.json is present and valid JSON, then compare against rack_owners rows for that rack_id.

Scan missing from Profile but present in DB

entries.question: Internal: a user says a "Clear" button wiped their scan history — where is that button?
entries.answer:
It is not reachable. HistoryPage.jsx still exists and is still imported by App.jsx (line 18), but no <Route> renders it — App.jsx:312 makes /history a redirect: <Route path="/history" element={<Navigate to="/profile" replace />} />. Nobody can reach its "Scan history" header, its "Clear" button, or its "No past scans yet." empty state through the app. Treat any report about them as a stale build, a screenshot from an old version, or a URL typed by hand into a dev bundle.

What does still exist is the localStorage key rackTrackHistory:
- ResultsPage appends the current result to it and truncates with history.slice(0, 12) — so at most 12 entries, per browser/device, per WebView, never synced to the server.
- The only live readers/writers left are in ResultsPage: it writes on every new result (~line 1736) and prunes the entry when a cold /results/<rackId> link 404s (~line 1127).
- It is NOT cleared on sign-out. AuthContext logout() only drops the stored token and user keys, so rackTrackHistory persists across sign-out and across users on the same device. Only clearing site data (or the unreachable Clear button) removes it.
- It has no effect on Recent Scans, which ProfilePage serves entirely from GET /api/scans (server/app.js:4904, auth-scoped).

So: the authoritative history is server-side; rackTrackHistory is a vestigial, device-local 12-item cache. Clearing browser storage never deletes a scan.
symptoms: Scan history page with a Clear button
History differs between phone and laptop
entries.rootCause: HistoryPage is dead code (imported, never routed); the local rackTrackHistory cache is capped at 12 entries and is device-local, while the real history comes from GET /api/scans.

entries.question: How do I add a third rack to a multi-rack view I already built?
entries.answer:
You can't add a rack to a view that already exists — there is no "add rack" control in the app, and no API call that appends a rack to an existing group. Build a new view instead.

On the "Scan two racks" screen there are exactly two ways in:
1. Two photos — only two picture slots, "Rack 1" and "Rack 2". Hard limit of that mode: two racks, no more. When you tap "Build combined view" RackTrack analyzes both photos and links them into one group.
2. One video — tap "Tap to add a video panning across both racks" and pan across every rack you want included. However many racks RackTrack detects in that pan go into the one view (at least 2 are required, or it asks you to re-pan), so this is the only way in the app to get three or more racks together.

If you need three or more racks in one view, use the video mode: pan slowly across all of them and hold each rack fully in frame for a moment. A group can hold at most 8 racks.

entries.question: My video of both racks came back with "Only 1 rack detected — pan across both racks so each is clearly visible."
entries.answer:
The video only produced one usable rack, so RackTrack won't build a two-rack view from it.

Re-record the pan:
1. Start with the first rack completely in frame — top to bottom, both side rails visible.
2. Hold still on it for a couple of seconds before you start moving.
3. Pan sideways slowly and evenly to the next rack. Don't tilt or walk while panning.
4. Hold still on the second rack for a couple of seconds at the end.
5. Back on the Scan two racks screen, choose One video again, tap the video box, pick the new clip and tap Build combined view.

If you instead get "No racks detected in the video. Try a clearer pan.", the video gave nothing usable at all — more light, steadier hands, and a full-height view of each rack are what fix it. If the pan keeps failing, switch to Two photos and take one clear picture of each rack.

entries.question: I reopened my two-rack scan from Profile and only one rack shows up. Where did the second rack go?
entries.answer:
Nothing is lost — you're just looking at one rack's own report. The side-by-side/two-rack view only appears while the web address still carries the pair's id (a `?group=…` on the end), so opening a scan from your scan history on Profile opens that single rack and the Rack 1 / Rack 2 pills don't appear.

To get the pair back:
1. While you are in a two-rack view, bookmark or copy the address bar — it looks like /results/RK-XXXXXXXX?group=GRP-XXXXXXXXXXXX. Opening that link later brings the pair back. The combined 3D scene at /multi-rack/GRP-XXXXXXXXXXXX/topology works as a bookmark too.
2. Otherwise rebuild the pair: Scan → "Scanning two racks?" → Two photos → the same two photos → Build combined view. Re-using photos you've already scanned is quick — RackTrack recognises the identical image and returns the cached analysis instead of redoing it. Note this creates a fresh pair id, so bookmark the new address.

One related trap: inside the combined 3D scene, tapping a rack chip under the canvas opens that rack's Ports tab on its own — no pills, no side-by-side. Use the back arrow to return to the pair rather than the chip.

Only one rack after reopening from history

entries.question: How do I actually compare the two racks against each other?
entries.answer:
It depends on the screen size, and that is deliberate.

On a laptop or wide screen (1024px and up), the Overview of a two-rack scan draws both racks as two columns side by side. Each column has a sticky header with a "#1" / "#2" position chip, the rack's name, and its RK- id next to the name, and below that the full report for that rack — photo, device boxes and all. Read straight across to compare. (The Drift view is the one exception: even on a wide screen it switches between racks rather than showing them side by side.)

On a phone, or anywhere narrower than 1024px, side by side is too cramped, so you get a row of pills at the top instead — "#1 Rack 1" and "#2 Rack 2" (your own rack names if you set them) — and you tap between them. Whatever page you're on stays the same when you switch, so if you're on Ports for Rack 1 and tap Rack 2 you land on Ports for Rack 2 and can flick back and forth. That same pill strip is also what you use on Ports, Topology and Drift on a desktop — only the Overview goes two-column.

For the racks as diagrams, open Topology and use the 2D button: it draws both rack elevations in two columns with any cross-rack cables listed underneath, so you can line up U positions between them. That view is not desktop-only — on a screen narrower than 780px the two columns simply stack one above the other. The 3D button puts both racks in one shared scene.
symptoms: Side by side view not showing on my phone
Only see one rack at a time
entries.rootCause: RackResultsRoute renders the two-column layout only when useIsDesktop() (>=1024px) and the group signal is present; otherwise it falls back to the single ResultsPage with the RackTabs pill switcher. The 2D topology columns collapse to one column under 780px via CSS.

entries.question: Why do Ports, Switches and Network only show one rack at a time, when Overview shows both?
entries.answer:
That's on purpose. Ports, Switches and Network are the three pages built around a single rack's live equipment data — the Ports page in particular opens a live SSH session to the switch as soon as you open it, and the switch only allows about one session at a time. Rendering two racks at once would fire two of those checks together, which is slower and can come back with readings that disagree.

So on those three pages you get a pill toggle at the top instead — one pill per rack, showing its position (#1, #2) and its label — and only the selected rack is shown. Tapping the other pill fully remounts that rack's page, so its state and its probe start clean and the readings you see belong to that rack alone.

Overview and the 2D topology don't open live sessions to the switches, so they're allowed to draw both racks together — but only on a wide screen (roughly laptop-width and up). On a phone, Overview also shows one rack at a time with its own rack switcher, and the Drift view uses the same one-at-a-time pill toggle as the other pages.

entries.question: How do I open the combined 3D view of both racks, and what am I looking at?
entries.answer:
There are two ways in:
- From any page of a two-rack scan, tap the small "3D" button at the right-hand end of the rack pill strip ("Open all racks in one 3D scene"). This opens the standalone combined view.
- Or open the Topology tab of the scan and tap 3D in the header — the header reads "Topology · 2 racks" with a 2D / 3D toggle next to it. This embeds the same scene inside the Topology page.

What you see, top to bottom:
1. A header. On the standalone route it reads "Combined topology" with a tag showing how many racks are in the scene ("2 racks"). If you came in via the Topology tab's 3D toggle, the page keeps that tab's own "Topology · 2 racks" header and the 2D/3D toggle instead — the "Combined topology" title is hidden in that case.
2. One shared 3D space with the racks standing side by side on the same floor — same lights, same camera. Devices sit at their real U heights.
3. The few cables that actually cross from one rack to the other, drawn as sagging patch cables with connector plugs on each end. Amber = fibre, blue = DAC. Cabling that stays inside a rack is not drawn here.
4. Under the scene, a strip of rack chips — "#1 <name>" plus the RK- id. Tapping one leaves the 3D scene and opens that rack's Ports page on its own.
5. Below that, an "Inter-rack connections" panel listing each crossing cable (role, both endpoints with device and port, and the cable type). It only appears if there is at least one cross-rack cable.

Clicking a device highlights it in its own rack only — selection is tracked per rack, so clicking something in rack 2 doesn't dim rack 1. Tap empty space to clear all selections.

entries.question: How do I move around the 3D rack view on a phone? It keeps spinning when I want to slide it across.
entries.answer:
On a phone, the normal rules are:
- One finger dragging = spin the rack around.
- Two fingers = pinch to zoom, and drag with both fingers to slide the view across.
- Tap a device to select it; tap empty space to deselect (this works in both the single-rack and the two-rack view).

On a single rack there's an extra behaviour: once you zoom right in (camera closer than the pan threshold), the gestures flip automatically — one finger now slides the view and two fingers become pinch-zoom plus spin. So when you're zoomed in, use one finger to pan, not two. Zoom back out and it flips back to one finger spinning / two fingers panning. On a desktop the cursor turns into a grab hand at the same moment. This flip only happens on a single rack's 3D view — in the combined multi-rack scene one finger always spins and two fingers always pinch/slide, at every zoom level, so use two fingers to slide across from one rack to the other.

On a laptop: drag with the left mouse button to spin, right button to slide, scroll wheel to zoom. When you're zoomed right in on a single rack, left and right swap over so left drags (pans) the view and right spins it.

In both views you can't tip the camera completely flat from directly above or directly underneath — the tilt stops just short of both extremes, which keeps the rack readable. Zoom range also differs: a single rack zooms between roughly 4 and 28 units, while the multi-rack scene allows pulling much further back so both racks fit.

Can't slide across to the second rack

Polar angle is clamped at both extremes.
