entries.question: The combined topology says "No topology data yet for any rack in this scan." What now?
entries.answer:
The rack diagrams are built in the background after a scan, and none of the racks in this group had a diagram ready when this screen loaded. The combined view asks the server once per rack — it does not keep checking on its own.

Do this:
1. Wait about a minute.
2. Reload the page, or go back and tap 3D again. That re-asks the server for every rack in the scan. (Your first visit already told the server to start building the missing diagrams, so a reload is usually enough.)
3. If it's still empty, open one rack on its own: back out to the scan, open the Topology tab and stay on it. The single-rack Topology screen keeps retrying by itself (15 tries, 4 seconds apart — about a minute), and asking for a rack's diagram is what kicks off building it.
4. Once you can see a rack's diagram on its own, go back to the combined view and reload — it will have data. Racks that still have no diagram simply won't appear in the combined scene.

If a rack never produces a diagram (the single-rack view ends with "Topology could not be prepared. Try rescanning this rack."), rescan that rack — that regenerates it from scratch.

entries.question: Only one of my two racks appears in the combined 3D scene. The other one is just gone.
entries.answer:
The missing rack is still in your scan — it just has no topology diagram yet, and the combined 3D scene silently drops any rack whose diagram it couldn't fetch. That's why the rack strip under the scene shows only one chip and the header counts only one rack.

Why it happens: the diagram for each rack is generated in the background after the scan. Until it's ready the server answers "pending" for that rack, and the combined view leaves that rack out instead of telling you.

To bring it back:
1. Confirm which rack is the problem: from the scan, open the Topology tab and switch to 2D. The rack that isn't ready shows "Topology still generating — refresh shortly." in its own column instead of vanishing.
2. Wait about a minute — the first request already kicked off generation in the background — then reload that Topology screen (pull to refresh / reload the page, or toggle 3D → 2D → 3D). Neither the 2D nor the 3D group view retries on its own, so nothing changes until you reload.
3. Once the second rack draws in 2D, open the combined 3D view again. Both racks will be there, along with the inter-rack cables.

If the rack still has no diagram after a few reloads, rescan that rack.

(Note: leaving the group Topology screen open does not help — the automatic ~1 minute retry only runs on a single-rack topology view, not on the two-rack group view.)

Combined topology only shows one rack
Rack chip strip shows one rack instead of two
entries.rootCause: MultiRackTopologyPage stores per-rack fetch failures in an errors map that is never surfaced, and the layout memo filters members down to those with a loaded topo, so a rack with a 404 topology is dropped from placed (and therefore from the chip strip and the rack count).

entries.question: What is the "Inter-rack connections" list under the topology, and why are there only a handful of cables between the racks?
entries.answer:
That panel lists only the cables that run from one rack to the other. Almost all cabling stays inside a single rack — you see that cabling on each rack's own topology — so only the few uplinks that cross racks appear here.

Each row reads left to right:
- A coloured dot and, at the far right, the cable type in capitals: FIBER or DAC. Amber/yellow = fibre, blue = DAC.
- The cable's job: "Primary uplink", "Redundant uplink", "Cross-connect" or "Backup link".
- The two ends, separated by ⇄: rack name, then the device, then the port on that device.

The heading also tells you the total, for example "3 cross-rack cables".

In 3D these same cables are drawn between the racks, leaving the actual port on the front of the switch at its real U height and sagging across the gap, with a connector plug modelled at each end — amber for fibre, blue for DAC. In 2D they appear as a rail of coloured wires down the gap between the two rack columns (hidden on a narrow phone, where the racks stack instead — the list below still shows them all).

entries.question: What are the hard limits on a multi-rack group, and why would pairing two racks fail with a server error? (admin reference)
entries.answer:
Grouping rules for the two-photo pairing:
- Minimum 2 racks: fewer is rejected with a message that you must provide at least two racks to group.
- Maximum 8 racks: more is rejected with "A group can hold at most 8 racks." The app's photo flow only ever pairs 2 at a time, so you'd only reach this ceiling outside the normal app.
- The video flow doesn't apply either limit — it groups however many racks it split out.
- Duplicate rack IDs are removed before the count is checked, so submitting the same rack twice fails the minimum-of-two rule. From the app you never hit this: the two-rack flow stops with "Both photos resolved to the same rack — use two different racks." before it submits.
- Every remaining rack must have a valid rack ID and already have a completed analysis saved. Otherwise you get "Rack <id> not found — analyze it first." — the app shows that message (or "Could not link the racks.") right after the "Linking the two racks…" step, which means one photo's analysis produced no result.
- Groups are scoped to your Site/organization when created, and every read re-checks it — group lookups return "Group not found" on a mismatch rather than a permission error, so a group belonging to another organization is never revealed to exist.
Note: member labels are always generated automatically as "Rack 1", "Rack 2", … in the order the racks were submitted; you can't set your own label.
symptoms: Provide at least two rackIds to group
A group can hold at most 8 racks
Rack RK-... not found — analyze it first
Two-rack pairing fails at Linking the two racks
entries.rootCause: POST /api/rack-groups validates uniq.length (>=2, <=8), the RK- id pattern and the on-disk device_unit_map.json before creating the group; labels are generated server-side and req.body.label is never consumed.
entries.short: Rack groups take 2–8 racks, each already analysed with a valid ID; duplicates or unanalysed racks are rejected and labels are auto-set Rack 1, Rack 2.

entries.question: Are the cables shown between two racks actually discovered, and what should we tell a customer who asks?
entries.answer:
No. Inter-rack links are synthesized server-side, deterministically, from each rack's own topology snapshot. Never describe them to a customer as discovered, measured or verified cabling.

How they are produced (deriveInterRackLinks in server/app.js):
- Members are sorted by capture position and only ADJACENT pairs are chained — position 1↔2, 2↔3. There is never a link between non-adjacent racks. (A group can hold 2–8 racks.)
- Each rack's endpoints come from _uplinkPorts: switches sorted top-of-rack first, preferring in-rack switches that have a u_position, taking at most 2 ports per switch (is_uplink-flagged ports first, otherwise the first 2 ports) and at most 6 endpoints per rack.
- Link count per adjacent pair is min(min(endpointsA, endpointsB) + 1, 5) — so at most 5 cables between any two racks.
- Roles come from a fixed list: Primary uplink, Redundant uplink, Cross-connect, Backup link, then "Uplink N". The extra "+1" run (which reuses switch 0) only exists when the pair count is 4 or fewer; if both racks yield 5+ endpoints you get exactly 5 links and none of them is an extra redundant run — but index 1 is still labelled "Redundant uplink" regardless.
- cable_type is 'fiber' only when an endpoint's role is 'core' (an out-of-rack aggregation switch, used only when a rack has no racked switches at all), otherwise 'dac'.
- Every link carries synthetic: true and a deterministic cable_id of the form IRL-<rackA>-<rackB>-<n> with the RK- prefix stripped from both rack ids (e.g. IRL-A1B2-C3D4-1). Same members always produce the same wiring, which is why the view looks stable across reloads.
- If either rack has no topology.json or no switches, that pair contributes zero links and the panel simply doesn't appear.

Side effect to be aware of: POST /api/rack-groups (the two-image pairing entry point) best-effort spawns servicenow/cmdb_interrack_link.py to write these synthesized links into the customer's CMDB as cmdb_rel_ci "Connects to" relationships. It is a no-op when SN_INSTANCE is unset or the script file is missing, is de-duplicated per group while in flight, and failures are logged (cmdb.interrack_failed) without affecting the view. Groups created by /api/analyze-video do not trigger this push. On a configured instance this does write fabricated relationships into the customer's CMDB — flag that before enabling it.
symptoms: Customer asks if cross-rack cables are real
Where do inter-rack uplinks come from
Why are the same cables shown every time
Unexpected Connects to relationships in ServiceNow
entries.rootCause: deriveInterRackLinks fabricates rack-to-rack uplinks from static topology snapshots (there is no live network path between two independently photographed racks), and scheduleInterRackCmdbLink pushes them to ServiceNow when SN_INSTANCE is configured.
entries.short: No. Inter-rack links are synthesized server-side, deterministically, from each rack's own topology snapshot. Never describe them to a customer as discovered, measured or verified cabling.

entries.question: A customer wants one report covering both racks in a two-rack scan. Is there one?
entries.answer:
There is a combined-report endpoint, but no UI anywhere calls it, so it cannot be reached from the app — do not tell a customer to "click Export" for a two-rack report.

GET /api/rack-group/:groupId/report builds a single HTML document (HTML only — there is no server-rendered PDF): a cover page headed "RackTrack · Combined report" with the hardcoded title "Two-Rack Report" (it says that even if the group holds three or more racks), the rack count and today's date, then a pill per member reading "#<position> <label> <rackId>". Each rack's standard scan report follows, spliced in under a black "Rack #<n> — <label>" band with a page break before it, so browser Print → Save as PDF gives a clean multi-rack PDF. It reuses buildScanReport per member and substitutes a red "Report unavailable for <rackId>: <reason>" paragraph for any rack whose report fails, so one bad rack doesn't kill the document.

Two constraints before you promise it to anyone:
- requireAuth accepts an Authorization: Bearer token only — no cookie, and no signed-link fallback (the report-token trick works only for single-rack /api/scan/:rackId/report) — so pasting the URL into a browser tab returns 401 "Authentication required".
- It is tenant-scoped (404 "Group not found" for another tenant or an unknown group) and returns 404 "Group has no racks" for an empty group.

Until a UI entry point exists, the supported answer to the customer is: open each rack's own report, or have someone run the endpoint for them.
entries.rootCause: GET /api/rack-group/:groupId/report exists and works but has no client caller (no reference to /api/rack-group/.../report anywhere in client/src), and requireAuth only accepts an Authorization: Bearer header, so it is not openable as a plain URL.

entries.short: There is a combined-report endpoint, but no UI anywhere calls it, so it cannot be reached from the app — do not tell a customer to "click Export" for a two-rack report.

entries.question: I just opened RackTrack for the first time. What am I looking at, and where do I start?
entries.answer:
You are on the welcome screen. It is not a dashboard — it is the front door, and it has exactly one button that moves you forward.

On a phone (viewport under 768px, HomeLight):
1. You see the RackTrack logo and name at the top, a photo of a datacenter aisle, the headline "Manage your datacenter. From anywhere." and the line "Track racks, ports, and assets in real time."
2. If you are not signed in there is a Create account button in the top-right corner, and the big button reads Sign in. Once you are signed in the Create account button disappears.
3. If you are already signed in, that same big button reads Start a scan and takes you straight to the Scan screen. That is the intended first move: tap Start a scan, then scan a rack.

On an iPad or a computer (768px and wider, HomeStudio) the same screen is laid out side by side: a small kicker line ("AI rack intelligence", or "Welcome back, <your name>" once you are signed in), the headline "See every port. Know every rack.", a paragraph explaining what RackTrack does, three figures (30+ device classes, 0.3s per rack, 98% accuracy), and a datacenter photo on the right marked LIVE SCAN with a sample status strip (CHENNAI-DC1 - 24 racks - 1,048 ports mapped; that strip is illustrative, not your data). The main button reads Sign in when signed out and Start a scan once you are signed in; a Create an organization button sits beside it when signed out. When you are signed in a second button, Past scans, appears next to it — it opens your Profile page, where your scan history lives. The top-right button is Create account when signed out and Sign out when signed in.

There is nothing actionable beyond that on this screen. The rest of the app opens up once you tap through to Scan.

entries.question: A four-step introduction popped up the first time I signed in. Can I get it back?
entries.answer:
No — the walkthrough is shown once per device and there is no button anywhere in the app to replay it. Signing out and back in will not bring it back either.

What it said, so you do not need it again:
1. "Welcome to RackTrack" — turn a photo of a server rack into a full, labelled map of what's inside, in seconds.
2. "1 · Scan a rack" — point your camera at the rack (or upload a photo or short video) and tap Scan.
3. "2 · Review the results" — see each device, where it sits in the rack, and its details. Tap any item to dig deeper or fix a label.
4. "3 · Check the ports" — open the Ports tab to see the switch live: which ports are free, which are connected, and what's plugged in.

The controls are Skip in the top-right corner, Next to move forward (Back appears from the second card onwards), and on the last card Start scanning, which drops you on the Scan screen. Skipping counts as finishing — it will not come back either way.

It only appears when you are signed in, so if you sign in on a second phone or tablet you will see it again there. Reinstalling the app, or otherwise clearing the app's local storage on a device, would also make it reappear, but there is no supported in-app way to reset it.
symptoms: How do I see the tutorial again
I skipped the walkthrough by accident
entries.rootCause: OnboardingTour records completion in localStorage under the key 'racktrack:onboarded' and returns null forever after; it also renders only when isAuthed. No UI resets the flag.

No — the walkthrough is shown once per device and there is no button anywhere in the app to replay it.
1. "Welcome to RackTrack" — turn a photo of a server rack into a full, labelled map of what's inside, in seconds.
2. "1 · Scan a rack" — point your camera at the rack (or upload a photo or short video) and tap Scan.
3. "2 · Review the results" — see each device, where it sits in the rack, and its details.

entries.question: I tapped HOME at the bottom and the menu bar vanished. Now I can't get anywhere.
entries.answer:
That is how the home screen is built — it deliberately has no bottom bar and no sidebar. It is the welcome screen, not a hub.

To get moving again:
1. On a phone, tap the big button in the middle — it reads Sign in when signed out and Start a scan once you are signed in. Since you are signed in it takes you straight to the Scan screen, where the bottom bar with HOME, SCAN and PROFILE comes back.
2. On an iPad or computer (768px wide and up) the welcome screen shows Start a scan and, next to it, Past scans. Start a scan goes to Scan; Past scans goes to Profile. Both bring the left sidebar back.
3. Do not rely on the back gesture on the Android app: on the home screen the hardware/gesture back is wired to exit RackTrack, not to go back a page. (In a browser, back does return you to the previous screen.)

Practical advice: on a phone, treat SCAN and PROFILE as your two real destinations — HOME only returns you to the welcome screen. On an iPad or computer the sidebar is present on the normal app screens (Scan, Profile, Results, Ports, Topology and so on), and clicking Home in that sidebar drops it again until you navigate on. A few full-page screens — sign in, sign up, the pending-approval wait screen and the Organizations console — also have no sidebar by design.
symptoms: Nav bar missing on home screen
No menu on the welcome page
entries.rootCause: In App.jsx the '/' route renders <HomePage /> bare — it is not wrapped in ResponsiveLayout, so neither BottomNav (phone) nor DesktopShell (>=768px) is mounted. Only routes passed withBottomNav render the bottom bar.

    useIsDesktop, so DesktopShell is bypassed for "/" —
    otherwise we'd double-render the chrome. */}
<Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />

<Route path="/scan" element={
  <ProtectedRoute><ResponsiveLayout withBottomNav><ScanPage /></ResponsiveLayout></ProtectedRoute>
} />

1. On a phone, tap the big button in the middle — it reads Sign in when signed out and Start a scan once you are signed in.
2. On an iPad or computer (768px wide and up) the welcome screen shows Start a scan and, next to it, Past scans.

entries.question: The app looks totally different on my phone, my iPad and my laptop. Which one is right?
entries.answer:
All three are right — RackTrack has three layouts and switches between them purely on how wide the screen is. Nothing is broken and there is no setting to change it.

- Narrower than 768 pixels (any phone, and an iPad app window that has been split small): the phone layout, with no sidebar. Most pages pin a bar to the bottom with HOME, SCAN and PROFILE. A few do not: the rack result pages show their own tab strip along the bottom instead (Overview / Ports / Topology / Network / Switches / Drift), and Two racks, Console and Data Sources show no bottom bar at all.
- 768 pixels and wider (iPad in portrait or landscape, small laptop windows): the sidebar appears down the left with Home, Scan, Two racks and Profile — plus Console and Lab for the platform owner, and Data Sources and Marketplace for organization admins. The bottom bar disappears completely, and once you have scanned a rack the sidebar also lists that rack's Overview / Ports / Topology / Network / Switches / Drift.
- 1024 pixels and wider (laptops, desktop browsers, iPad landscape): the same sidebar, but pages that have a wide layout switch to it — most visibly, the rack tab strip is dropped from the page because the sidebar already carries the same links.

So an iPad in portrait sits between the two: it gets the sidebar but still uses the phone-width page layouts, which is why on a portrait iPad you can briefly see the rack tabs in both the sidebar and the page. If you rotate the iPad or resize the browser window, the layout changes live — you do not need to reload.

One exception at every size: the welcome screen at Home has neither the bottom bar nor the sidebar. It does change appearance at 768 pixels — a simpler welcome on phones, a richer one on tablets and laptops — but that is a different page design, not different navigation.
symptoms: Different layout on iPad vs phone
Sidebar on laptop but not on phone
Layout changed when I rotated the tablet
entries.rootCause: Two breakpoints drive everything: SIDEBAR_BREAKPOINT = 768 (useHasSidebar -> DesktopShell vs bare mobile + BottomNav) and DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT = 1024 (useIsDesktop -> wide content layouts, e.g. suppressing ScanTabBar). Both are matchMedia hooks so they re-evaluate on resize/rotation.

Nothing is broken and there is no setting to change it. - Narrower than 768 pixels (any phone, and an iPad app window that has been split small): the phone layout, with no sidebar.

entries.question: The welcome screen on my iPad has different buttons from the one on my phone. Why?
entries.answer:
There are two different welcome screens and the app picks one purely by browser/screen width — 768 pixels is the cut-off (HomePage renders HomeStudio at 768px and above, HomeLight below). Rotating an iPad or resizing a browser window switches you between them live.

Phone welcome screen (under 768px): logo and the RackTrack name, a Sign in button top-right that appears only when you are signed out, a datacenter photo, the headline "Manage your datacenter. From anywhere." with the line "Track racks, ports, and assets in real time.", and one big button that reads Sign in when signed out and Start a scan once you are signed in. Creating a new organization is the Create account button in the top-right corner.

iPad / computer welcome screen (768px and up): a two-column layout. On the left a small line reading "AI rack intelligence" — which becomes "Welcome back, <your username>" once you are signed in — the headline "See every port. Know every rack.", a short description, then the buttons. The buttons depend on whether you are signed in: signed out you get a Sign in button plus Create an organization; signed in the first becomes Start a scan and a second Past scans button appears next to it. Below that are three figures: 30+ device classes, 0.3s per rack, 98% accuracy. On the right is a photo tagged LIVE SCAN with a scanning overlay and a strip reading CHENNAI-DC1 · 24 racks · 1,048 ports mapped.

Those three figures and the CHENNAI-DC1 strip are fixed illustration text written into the welcome screen itself. They are not your organization's numbers, they are not fetched from the server, and they never change — so nothing is wrong if 24 racks or 1,048 ports does not match your site.

The top-right button also differs between the two screens: on the phone screen it offers Sign in and is hidden entirely once you are signed in. On the iPad/computer screen it is always visible and switches to Sign out once you are signed in.
symptoms: Where did Get Started go on my iPad
Home page shows numbers I don't recognise
Welcome back message only on desktop
entries.rootCause: HomePage branches on useIsTabletOrUp (TABLET_BREAKPOINT = 768): HomeStudio above, HomeLight below. HomeStudio's stats and HUD strip are hard-coded literals in the component, not fetched data.

entries.short: There are two different welcome screens and the app picks one purely by browser/screen width — 768 pixels is the cut-off (HomePage renders HomeStudio at 768px and above, HomeLight below). Rotating an iPad or resizing a browser window switches you between them live.

entries.question: I clicked the button in the top-right of the home screen on my laptop and it signed me straight out with no warning.
entries.answer:
That button is Sign out, and on the home screen it takes effect immediately — there is no "are you sure?" step there.

What happened: on an iPad or computer, the home screen's top-right button shows Sign in with an arrow icon when you are signed out, and swaps to Sign out once you are signed in. Pressing it signs you out and returns you to the home screen straight away.

To get back in, press Sign in in that same corner and enter your credentials. Nothing is lost — your scans stay on the server and your Recent Scans list is intact when you sign back in.

If you want the safer version, sign out from Profile instead: the exit icon in the Profile header asks "Sign out?" with the note "You'll need to sign in again to scan racks." and gives you a Cancel button. The phone home screen never shows a Sign out button at all — it only offers Sign in, and only when you are signed out.
symptoms: Clicked top right and lost my session
Sign out button on the home page
entries.rootCause: HomeStudio's header button calls auth.logout() then navigate('/') directly with no confirmation dialog, unlike ProfilePage which gates sign-out behind a confirm modal.

evidence.snippet:
<button
  type="button"
  className={styles.signBtn}
  onClick={authed ? () => { auth.logout(); navigate('/'); } : () => navigate('/login')}
>
  <SignIcon out={authed} width="15" height="15" />
  {authed ? 'Sign out' : 'Sign in'}
</button>

entries.short: That button is Sign out, and on the home screen it takes effect immediately — there is no "are you sure?" step there. On an iPad or computer the home screen's top-right button shows Sign in when you are signed out and swaps to Sign out once you are signed in. Nothing is lost: press Sign in in that same corner to get back in.

entries.question: I pressed the back arrow on my scan result and it threw me out to the Scan screen. How do I get the result back?
entries.answer:
The back arrow on a rack result means "go back one tab", and on the Overview tab it means "leave this rack" — which lands you on the Scan screen. That is deliberate, not a bug.

Exactly what the arrow does:
- On the Overview tab: leaves the rack entirely and goes to Scan.
- On any other tab (Switches, Ports, Topology, Network, Drift): steps back through the tabs you opened, in the order you opened them. When there are none left, it returns you to Overview. Press it again from Overview and you leave the rack.

To get the result back:
1. Open PROFILE and find the rack under Recent Scans — tap it to reopen. (On an iPad or computer the sidebar also keeps a "Rack · <rack ID>" section pointing at the rack you were on.)
2. Or, if you still have the rack's web address, open it again — a /results/<rack ID> link reopens the rack from the server.

Tip: the rack ID is printed under the title at the top of the result screen, so note it down if you are moving between racks a lot.
symptoms: Back button leaves the scan result
Lost my results after pressing back
Back arrow goes to the upload screen
How do I return to my scan
entries.rootCause: ResultsPage.handleHeaderBack navigates to /scan whenever tab === 'overview'; on other tabs it pops tabHistoryRef (the in-page tab stack) and otherwise falls back to the overview tab.

{rackId || scanId}

entries.short:
The back arrow on a rack result means "go back one tab", and on the Overview tab it means "leave this rack" — which lands you on the Scan screen.
1. Open PROFILE and find the rack under Recent Scans — tap it to reopen.
2. Or, if you still have the rack's web address, open it again — a /results/<rack ID> link reopens the rack from RackTrack.

entries.question: The phone's back gesture doesn't step back through the rack tabs — it jumps out of the result completely.
entries.answer:
Use the back arrow inside the app (top-left of the result screen) or the bottom tab strip, not the phone's back gesture, to move between a rack's tabs.

Why: switching between Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology, Network and Drift on a phone does not change the web address — the whole rack lives at one address and the tabs swap the content in place. Your phone's back gesture only knows about address changes, so it skips the tabs entirely and takes you to the screen you were on before you opened the rack.

What to use instead:
- The back arrow in the result's own header steps back through the tabs you visited, in order — but only while you are on a tab other than Overview. Overview is treated as the root of the rack: pressing back there always leaves the rack and returns you to the scan screen, and it also clears the remembered tab history. If you are on another tab and there is no history to step back through, back returns you to Overview.
- The tab strip fixed at the bottom of the result (Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology, and More for Network and Drift) jumps anywhere directly, and is the most reliable way to move around. Note this strip is mobile-only; on desktop the same links live in the left sidebar.

On Android specifically, the hardware back button walks the app's page history (the previous screen, not the previous tab) and, on the home screen or the sign-in screen, closes RackTrack.
symptoms: Android back button skips the tabs
Browser back loses my place in the result
entries.rootCause: The rack tab strip changes React state via handleTabChange (setTab + tabHistoryRef) without touching the URL, so browser/OS history has no entry per tab. AndroidBackHandler maps the hardware back button to navigate(-1), i.e. the previous route, or exitApp on '/' and '/login'.
entries.short: Use the back arrow inside the app (top-left of the result screen) or the bottom tab strip, not the phone's back gesture, to move between a rack's tabs.

entries.question: On my iPad the rack tabs appear twice — once in the left sidebar and once as a strip in the page. Is that a display fault?
entries.answer:
It is not a fault, and both sets do the same thing — it is a side-effect of the iPad's width.

RackTrack shows the left sidebar from 768 pixels wide, but only hides the rack tab bar from 1024 pixels wide. An iPad in portrait is roughly 768–834 pixels, so it lands between the two and gets both.

What to do: use either. The sidebar section is headed "Rack · <rack ID>" and holds Overview, Ports, Topology, Network, Switches and Drift. The other set is a tab bar pinned along the bottom of the screen (not a strip in the page body); it holds Overview, Switches, Ports, Topology and a More button that opens Network and Drift. There is one small difference worth knowing — the bottom bar also shows small count badges: on Ports, the combined port count of all switches found in the rack, and on Switches, how many switches were found.

If you would rather see only one set, turn the iPad to landscape: past 1024 pixels the bottom tab bar is hidden and the sidebar becomes the only rack navigation.
symptoms: Two sets of tabs on iPad
Tab strip and sidebar both visible
entries.rootCause: DesktopShell mounts at useHasSidebar() >= 768px, while ResultsPage suppresses ScanTabBar only when useIsDesktop() >= 1024px. Viewports in the 768-1023px band therefore render both navigations.

RackTrack shows the left sidebar from 768 pixels wide, but only hides the rack tab bar from 1024 pixels wide. An iPad in portrait is roughly 768–834 pixels, so it lands between the two and gets both. What to do: use either.

entries.question: I typed an address (or followed an old link) and RackTrack dumped me on the welcome screen.
entries.answer:
The welcome screen is where RackTrack sends anything it cannot open. Three different things land you there:

1. The address does not exist. Any unrecognised address — a typo, a link to a page that was removed — is redirected to the home screen rather than showing a "page not found" error. Check the spelling and try again. Two old addresses are deliberate exceptions and still work: an old /logs bookmark opens the Operations Console, and an old /history bookmark opens Profile.
2. The page is restricted and you do not have the role for it. Data Sources, Marketplace and the Operations Console are limited to organization admins and the platform owner; if you are a member or a site manager, opening those addresses directly bounces you to home instead of showing an error. Ask your organization admin.
3. You are in the Organizations console and pressed App — that button is a deliberate exit back to the main app.

Different symptom, different cause: if you land on the Scan screen rather than the welcome screen, the address was a valid rack link but that scan no longer exists on the server. If you land on the Sign in screen, your session ended. And if you land on the "waiting for approval" screen, your organization has not been approved yet.
symptoms: Typed a URL and got the welcome screen
Bounced back to home when opening a page
entries.rootCause: App.jsx has a catch-all <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} /> so unknown paths redirect home, and AdminRoute redirects non-(org_admin|owner) users to '/'. There is no 404 page in the route table.

evidence.snippet: <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />

entries.short:
The welcome screen is where RackTrack sends anything it cannot open. Three different things land you there:
1. The address does not exist.
2. The page is restricted and you do not have the role for it.
3. You are in the Organizations console and pressed App — that button is a deliberate exit back to the main app.

entries.question: I scanned two racks together — how do I get from one rack to the other, and why did the switcher disappear?
entries.answer:
A multi-rack scan puts a small sticky strip across the top of the result. It holds one pill per rack, numbered — #1, #2 — with each rack's label, plus a small "3D" button on the right that opens all the racks in one combined scene.

How to use it:
1. Tap the other rack's pill. You stay on the same sub-page — if you were on Ports for rack 1, you land on Ports for rack 2. (The strip appears on the Overview, Ports and Topology pages; it is not shown on Netdisco.)
2. The rack you are currently viewing is the pill that is filled in solid/highlighted — it cannot be tapped. The other racks are the outlined, grey pills you can tap. That is how you tell which rack you are on.
3. Tap 3D to open all the racks in one scene with the cabling that runs between them.

If the strip has disappeared, the link you followed lost the group marker that tells RackTrack these racks belong together. RackTrack only shows the strip when the address carries a ?group=<group ID> marker that matches the rack's real group and the group has at least two racks. Opening a plain /results/<rack ID> address — which is what your Recent Scans list links to — or hand-editing the address drops that marker. The rack itself opens fine, just on its own. To get the group back, follow the link you were given for the multi-rack scan, or re-open the combined view. A single-rack scan never shows the strip at all — and re-uploading a photo that was once part of a multi-rack scan still gives you a single-rack report, by design.
symptoms: Can't switch between the two racks
Two-rack scan only shows one rack
entries.rootCause: RackTabs renders only when useGroupView reports isGroup, which depends on the ?group query parameter being present on the URL. Navigating to a bare /results/<rackId> (e.g. from Recent Scans) drops that signal, so the group strip is not rendered.

entries.short:
A multi-rack scan puts a small sticky strip across the top of the result.
1. Tap the other rack's pill.
2. The rack you are currently viewing is the pill that is filled in solid/highlighted — it cannot be tapped.
3. Tap 3D to open all the racks in one scene with the cabling that runs between them.

entries.question: The title bar on my laptop says "Live Network Switch" but I clicked Ports. Am I on the wrong page?
entries.answer:
You are on the right page. On a laptop, desktop browser or iPad, the strip above the page content is a location label, and a few of them are worded differently from the menu item you clicked.

The ones that catch people out:
- Ports (rack) shows as "Live Network Switch — Available ports".
- Network (rack) shows as "Network view — Live device + port table".
- Topology (rack) shows as "Topology — 3D rack & cabling".
- Switches (rack) shows as "Switch info — CMDB-driven".
- Scan shows as "New scan — Upload, camera, or video".
- Two racks shows as "Scan two racks — Detect both + the cabling between them".

A few screens do not show that strip at all — the Operations Console (Console), Profile, Data Sources and every Marketplace page draw their own heading instead, so there is no second title stacked on top. That is why clicking Console gives you no strip: the page's own "Operations Console" header is the only title there.

If the strip ever just says "RackTrack" with nothing under it, you are on a page that has no label of its own; the left sidebar still shows which item is highlighted.

On the rack's Ports page there is also a small back arrow to the left of the title — that walks you back one step.
symptoms: Page title doesn't match the menu item
No title bar on the Profile page
entries.rootCause: DesktopShell derives the topbar crumb from a PAGE_TITLE map plus deriveTitle() suffix rules; SELF_HEADED paths (/dashboard, /profile, /connections) and every /marketplace* path suppress the crumb because those pages render their own header.

On a laptop, desktop browser or iPad, the strip above the page content is a location label, and a few of them are worded differently from the menu item you clicked. entries.question: INTERNAL: which home component actually renders, and is HomeDesktop still in use?
entries.answer:
HomeDesktop.jsx is dead code. Nothing imports it — the only remaining references are its own file/CSS module, a passing mention in index.css (line ~205), and a stale comment in App.jsx above the '/' route claiming "HomePage has its own desktop branch (HomeDesktop) via useIsDesktop". That is no longer true.

What actually runs for '/':
- App.jsx (line 229) renders <HomePage /> bare (no ResponsiveLayout), so '/' has no DesktopShell and no BottomNav at any width.
- HomePage.jsx contains no markup of its own any more: the component ends with `const isTabletOrUp = useIsTabletOrUp(); if (isTabletOrUp) return <HomeStudio />; return <HomeLight />;`. Its local state, RACKS, SCREENS, the Rack3D helper and the drag-to-rotate handlers still execute as plain code on each render but nothing they feed is ever rendered.
- Breakpoint is useIsTabletOrUp (768px, iPad portrait), not useIsDesktop (1024px) — so desktop widths also land on HomeStudio, which is why HomeDesktop can never appear.
- HomeStudio portals to document.body to escape #root's 540px max-width column cap; DesktopShell does the same.

Support implications: never tell a customer about HomeDesktop's copy ("Scan the rack. Know everything.", the four "How it works" step cards, the RACK-U42-DEMO hero visual) — that page cannot be reached from the running app. The tablet/desktop welcome copy is HomeStudio's ("See every port. / Know every rack."). Do not quote HomePage's demo racks either: R-101 and R-102 (Chennai-DC1), R-103 (Hyderabad-DC2), incidents INC0042/INC0058, or its 3D rack views — all dead data inside HomePage.jsx.
symptoms: Which home screen does the user see
HomeDesktop copy doesn't match the app
R-101 rack not in my account
entries.rootCause: HomePage.jsx short-circuits to HomeStudio/HomeLight before rendering any of its own markup, and HomeDesktop.jsx has no importers; the App.jsx comment referencing it was not updated.

    useIsDesktop, so DesktopShell is bypassed for "/" —
    otherwise we'd double-render the chrome. */}
<Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />

Nothing imports it — the only remaining references are its own file/CSS module, a passing mention in index.css (line ~205), and a stale comment in App.jsx above the '/' route claiming "HomePage has its own desktop branch (HomeDesktop) via useIsDesktop". That is no longer true.

entries.question: INTERNAL: full navigation reference — which route renders which chrome, and who can reach it?
entries.answer:
Navigation chrome is decided per route, by whether the page element is wrapped in ResponsiveLayout and whether withBottomNav is passed; who can reach a route is decided by the ProtectedRoute / AdminRoute / PendingRoute wrappers plus DesktopShell's conditional link array.

Chrome:
• At >=768px, ResponsiveLayout renders the page inside DesktopShell — sidebar plus a breadcrumb topbar, portalled to document.body. The gate is useHasSidebar() at SIDEBAR_BREAKPOINT = 768. The "≥1024px" comments in App.jsx and DesktopShell are stale; useIsDesktop()'s 1024 breakpoint only drives content layouts such as side-by-side racks.
• The breadcrumb topbar is suppressed on pages that draw their own header. SELF_HEADED = ['/dashboard', '/profile', '/connections'], plus '/marketplace' and every '/marketplace/*' path (those render MarketplaceShell). On those routes you get the sidebar and a full-width canvas but no breadcrumb bar.

• ProtectedRoute requires a session; PendingRoute is the inverse gate for organizations that are not active yet (it bounces an active user to /scan and a signed-out one to /login); AdminRoute gates the admin-only client routes. Client gating is an affordance — /api/lab/* is separately enforced server-side with requireRole('owner').

Remembered rack id: DesktopShell keeps _liveRackId at module level and never in session or localStorage. It is set from the URL (/results/<id> or /switch-info/<id>) or from an rt:rack-id-changed event — dispatched with a rack id by ResultsPage after an upload finishes, and with null by AuthContext on login and logout and by ScanPage when a new scan starts. So it clears on refresh, on login/logout, on starting a new scan, and on landing on /scan.

entries.question: I asked for port 7 and the app highlighted the wrong physical port. How do I fix the numbering?
entries.answer:
Tap **No** under **"Port 7 on <device> — right?"**. The prompt changes to **"What is it actually?"** — choose the real number from the **Port 1 … Port N** dropdown, or choose **Other (type it)** and type it, then tap **Submit**.

Here is the part that surprises people: **the number you asked for does not change**. You were looking for port 7 and you still want port 7. RackTrack learns the offset between its numbering and the real numbering, then immediately re-highlights the port that is genuinely port 7. So if you tell it "the port you highlighted is really port 5", the highlight jumps two positions to land on the true port 7.

The correction is remembered for that device on that scan and collapses to **"Port number corrected — you set this"**. Repeated corrections don't stack up — only your most recent one counts, so you can correct it again if the first attempt was off.

Note: the automatic re-highlight applies to the device's main (RJ45) port row. On the **SFP** or **Console** tabs your correction is still recorded, but the highlight won't move on its own — re-select the port you want from that tab.
symptoms: port numbering is off by one
Port number corrected — you set this
entries.rootCause: Port ordering comes from the geometric layout in pipeline/port_pattern.py (column-major for two rows, left-to-right for one). A missed or extra detection at the start of a row shifts every subsequent index. /api/feedback records an absolute offset (predicted_port is normalised back to RAW model space) and _latestPortShift uses only the newest correction so shifts cannot compound.

evidence.snippet: > **NOTE** — Correcting a port number does not change the number you asked for. Say “port 7 is really port 5”, and RackTrack learns the offset then shows you where **port 7** truly lives.

entries.short: Tap **No** under **"Port 7 on <device> — right?"**. The prompt changes to **"What is it actually?"** — choose the real number from the **Port 1 … Port N** dropdown, or choose **Other (type it)** and type it, then tap **Submit**.

entries.question: The app says this port is RJ45 but it's actually an SFP slot. Can I change the port type?
entries.answer:
Yes. On the port view, answer the question **"Port type: <type> — right?"**. Tap **No** and choose the correct one from the list. Nine types are available, and the app displays them in sentence case: **Rj45, Sfp, Qsfp, Console, Aux, Management Port, Usb A, Usb B, Usb C** (so an RJ45 port reads "Port type: Rj45 — right?"). There is no free-text "Other" option here — the list is the full set the model understands.

When it saves you'll see **"Saved — thanks, this trains the model."** and afterwards the port reads **"Port type: <type> — you set this"**.

This correction does more than fix the current scan: as long as RackTrack has a location box for that port, it saves a crop of the port and stores a fingerprint of it in your organization's learned memory, so a future scan of the same port re-applies your corrected type automatically. That memory is shared across every Site in your organization and never with another organization.

RJ45 and SFP are the pair most often confused, because an empty SFP cage and an empty RJ45 jack are close to the same dark rectangle at photo resolution.
symptoms: Saved — thanks, this trains the model.
Port type: SFP — you set this
entries.rootCause: Typed port detection uses Models/ports_9.pt at ports_conf 0.23; the visual difference between an unpopulated SFP cage and an RJ45 jack is small at typical photo resolution. /api/feedback/port-type validates against a fixed nine-value PORT_TYPE_OPTIONS list, crops the port, and calls fireMemoryCorrection('port_type', …) for auto-apply on rescan.
entries.short: Yes. On the port view, answer the question **"Port type: <type> — right?"**. Tap **No** and choose the correct one from the list. Nine types are available, and the app displays them in sentence case: **Rj45, Sfp, Qsfp, Console, Aux, Management Port, Usb A, Usb B, Usb C**. There is no free-text "Other" option here — the list is the full set the model understands.

entries.question: My patch panel has 12 ports but RackTrack insists it has 24. Why won't it show the real number?
entries.answer:
This is deliberate, not a bug. For devices classified as **Patch Panel**, RackTrack recognises only two sizes: **24 and 48**. The combined connected+empty detection count is snapped to one of those two.

The snap is deliberately asymmetric, not simple "nearest". Patch-panel jacks are missed far more often than invented — dark, dust-capped or cable-obscured jacks don't get detected — so synthesising a missing slot costs 1 while discarding a real detection costs 3, and a tie keeps the larger size. In practice: anything under 30 snaps to 24, 30 and above snaps to 48. So a panel reading 18 becomes 24 with six slots filled in, and a panel reading 32 goes UP to 48 rather than down to 24.

The side effect is that genuinely non-standard panels (12-port, 16-port) are always reported as 24. To correct one:

1. Answer the device-class question first (the port-count question only appears after it) — if the unit isn't really a patch panel, fix the type there.
2. Then answer the port-count question with the true number: it offers 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, or type your own.

Your typed number wins from then on, the ports are laid out to match, and the selected-device image is redrawn. (For a Patch Panel, SFP and console ports are also force-cleared, since a panel is pure RJ-45 jacks.)

Note: if no ports are detected at all, the device is demoted to "Unidentified" instead — set the class first, then the count.
symptoms: patch panel port count too high
entries.rootCause: pipeline/port_pattern.py::_pp_closest_standard snaps the combined connected+empty count to PATCHPANEL_STANDARD_COUNTS = (24, 48) using an asymmetric cost — synthesising a slot costs 1, discarding a real detection costs DROP_PENALTY = 3.0, and ties resolve to the larger standard. There is deliberately no 12 option.

evidence.snippet:
# Patch panels are always a standard size. The status model can over- or
# under-detect, so we snap the COMBINED (connected + empty) count to the
# nearest standard...
PATCHPANEL_STANDARD_COUNTS = (24, 48)

"""Snap a detected port count to the nearest standard patch-panel size.
We only support 24 and 48 (there is deliberately no 12 option), so any
small count rounds up to 24.
...
overshoot (n <= c, synthesise) costs 1 per slot,
undershoot (n > c, discard a real detection) costs 3 per slot.
...
DROP_PENALTY = 3.0

entries.short:
This is deliberate, not a bug. For devices classified as **Patch Panel**, RackTrack recognises only two sizes: **24 and 48**.
1. Answer the device-class question first (the port-count question only appears after it) — if the unit isn't really a patch panel, fix the type there.
2. Then answer the port-count question with the true number: it offers 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, or type your own.

entries.question: A device that is definitely in the rack is missing from my results. How do I add it?
entries.answer:
You cannot add a missing device by hand — RackTrack has no "add device" control. The correction questions only let you re-label, re-count or re-number things it already found; every feedback endpoint needs an existing device to attach to. So the fix is to get RackTrack to see it, which means a better photo.

Most likely causes, in order:

- **Cables blocking the front of the equipment.** A heavily-patched rack hides the very faces the detector needs.
- **Shot from an angle, or too far away.** Stand directly in front, camera level with the middle of the rack.
- **Low light or glare** on that part of the rack.
- **You tapped "Proceed anyway"** past a quality warning. That switches the safety checks off, and a genuinely bad photo comes back with devices missing — sometimes an empty rack. Retake is nearly always faster.
- **The rack is taller than one frame.** Use the MULTI mode (2 to 8 overlapping photos) instead of trying to fit it all into one.

One thing to know before you retake: a retake is a **new scan**, and most of your corrections do not follow it. Port corrections, port-number corrections and port-count corrections are saved against the scan you made them on and stay there. The one exception is device-type corrections — if you told RackTrack "this is a firewall, not a switch", that is remembered for your whole organization and will usually be re-applied on later scans of the same equipment. So if you have a lot of port work invested in the current scan, finish and export it before retaking.
symptoms: switch not shown in rack map
fewer devices than actually in rack
entries.rootCause: Devices below devices_conf 0.20 are never emitted. Unclaimed rack rows become synthetic 'Unidentified' placeholders with confidence 0.0, which are hidden from the device picker. No API or UI path exists to insert a device — all feedback endpoints require an existing device_index.

evidence.snippet:
synthetic.append({
    "class_id": -1,
    "class_name": "Unidentified",
    "confidence": 0.0,
    ...
    "source": "synthetic_unidentified",
})

• Stand directly in front of the rack — not at an angle.
  • Keep the camera level with the middle of the rack.
  • Make sure the full rack fits inside the frame.

> **IMPORTANT** — **Proceed anyway** switches the safety checks **off** and analyses the photo regardless. A genuinely bad photo then comes back with devices missing — or an empty rack. **Retake** is nearly always the faster route to a correct answer.

entries.short: You cannot add a missing device by hand — RackTrack has no "add device" control. The correction questions only let you re-label, re-count or re-number things it already found; every correction needs an existing device to attach to. So the fix is to get RackTrack to see it, which means a better photo.

entries.question: The same device appears twice in my results, or there are phantom empty rows.
entries.answer:
RackTrack already tries hard to prevent this, so a genuine duplicate is unusual.

What RackTrack does automatically: when two device boxes overlap by more than about 30% of the smaller box, it keeps the higher-confidence one and drops the other; it then forces every device to the same width, snaps neighbouring devices so they share an edge (closing small overlaps and small gaps under about 40% of the median device height), and removes half-height grid rows that a device already covers so they don't appear as phantom "Empty" rows. Genuinely empty slots and larger real gaps are always preserved — a real blank U in your rack is not treated as an error.

A duplicate that survives is therefore one where the two boxes overlapped only slightly (roughly 30% or less). That usually means a photo shot at an angle — perspective makes one chassis appear in two places — or a MULTI stitch where RackTrack could not line the seam up. On a MULTI scan an undetected seam either fails the scan with a message asking you to retake those shots with more overlap, or the photos are joined flush, so anything in the overlapping band (including a whole device) is printed twice.

Fix: for a stitch, retake the photos with a clear overlapping band between them. For a single photo, stand square to the rack and retake.

You can correct a device's type from the results screen, but there is no way to delete a duplicate row by hand.
symptoms: device appears twice after MULTI stitch
entries.rootCause: remove_overlapping_devices drops any device whose overlap ratio with a kept device exceeds max_overlap_ratio=0.01; normalize_device_stack snaps small gaps/overlaps (gap_close_factor=0.4); cleanup_duplicate_units removes over-detected grid units that overlap a device but weren't claimed. Residual duplicates come from perspective distortion or an unaccepted stitch seam.

evidence.snippet:
"""Drop grid units that overlap a device but weren't picked by any
device in the top-N pass. These are the half-height duplicates that
the YOLO grid over-detected — keeping them around would show as
phantom "Empty" rows in the unit report.

Truly empty units (no overlap with any device) are preserved — they
represent real rack gaps."""

(2) vertically adjacent devices share an edge (bottom of the upper =
    top of the lower) with ZERO overlap.

Real empty slots are preserved: only a SMALL overlap or gap — one under
`gap_close_factor` × the median device height — is snapped shut.

entries.short: RackTrack already tries hard to prevent this, so a genuine duplicate is unusual.

entries.question: Do my corrections actually train the model, or do they only fix my own scan?
entries.answer:
Both — but they take effect at different speeds, and it's worth knowing which is which.

**Immediately (guaranteed):** your correction is overlaid onto your scan result. The rack map, the port view, the report and anything exported to your CMDB all show your corrected value. The original prediction is kept underneath as an audit trail, and corrected values are marked with a **"Your correction"** badge so nobody mistakes your value for the model's own guess.

**On your next scan (usually):** RackTrack saves a visual fingerprint of what you corrected — an image hash plus a deep-feature embedding. When a later scan sees a device, cable or port type that looks the same, it re-applies your label automatically. This memory is shared across every Site in your organization, but is never shared with other organizations.

**Into the trained model itself (slowly, and never silently):** corrections are queued, and once enough have piled up for a given model a retraining run starts on its own. But a retrained model is never trusted just because it was trained. It has to beat the current production model on a held-out test set the trainer never saw — by at least +0.5 percentage points for the device and cable models, +1.0 for port count — and even then a person has to deliberately promote it from the command line. If it doesn't clear the bar, the production model is left alone and your corrections stay queued for the next attempt. (The only exception is the very first model of its kind, where there's no prior score to beat.)

So: the correction you make today fixes today's result for certain, tends to fix tomorrow's scan of the same kit, and contributes to a model improvement on a much longer timescale.
symptoms: will it get it right next time
Saved — thanks, this trains the model.
entries.rootCause: Three layers: (1) applyFeedbackOverrides overlays feedback.jsonl onto scan_result.json with a _correction audit trail; (2) fireMemoryCorrection writes a pHash + ResNet18 embedding into the org-scoped active_learning_Cache store for auto-apply; (3) triggerActiveLearning spawns retraining_learning.run_loop --once, which registers candidates gated by PROMOTION_MIN_DELTA (0.005 for devices/cable, 0.010 for port_count) and requires a manual `cli promote`.

evidence.snippet:
# Promotion gate: a candidate must beat the production model's primary
# metric by at least this much (absolute) to be promoted. Stops noisy
# tiny improvements from churning the production model.
PROMOTION_MIN_DELTA = {
    "devices":    0.005,   # ≥ +0.5pp accuracy on holdout
    "cable":      0.005,
    "port_count": 0.010,
}

c. On success + gate pass → register as a CANDIDATE (kept under
   Models/candidates/<model>-<run_id>.pt). DOES NOT change the
   production model — promotion is a deliberate operator action
   via `python -m retraining_learning.cli promote ...`.

# Active learning is scoped at the ORGANIZATION level: each org keeps its own
# corrections + retraining snapshots, so all Sites/tenants within one org share
# a single model memory while different orgs stay isolated.

entries.short: Both — but they take effect at different speeds, and it's worth knowing which is which. **Immediately (guaranteed):** your correction is overlaid onto your scan result. The rack map, the port view, the report and anything exported to your CMDB all show your corrected value.

entries.question: I corrected a device last week, but a new scan of the same rack got it wrong again.
entries.answer:
RackTrack does try to re-apply your past corrections to new scans, but the match has to be close enough visually to be safe.

How it works: when you correct something, RackTrack stores a fingerprint of that device's or port's picture. On a later scan it crops each device and looks for a stored correction that matches — first by a fast image hash, then by a deeper visual comparison. Only a confident match re-applies your label. A photo shot from a noticeably different angle, distance or light level may not match, and RackTrack will fall back to detecting it fresh rather than risk applying the wrong label.

Things that stop a correction re-applying:

- The new photo is framed very differently (much closer, from the side, much darker).
- You are in a different organization from the one where the correction was made — corrections are shared across all Sites in your organization, but never between organizations.
- It was a one-off port-number nudge or a port-count fix. Those are recorded against that specific scan and are not stored as a visual fingerprint. Device type, port type and cable colour are the ones with visual memory.

The exception worth knowing on ports: if you use "verify port layout" on the Ports page rather than nudging a single port number, RackTrack saves that whole layout against the photo's fingerprint. A later upload of the same (or a visually similar) rack photo then reuses your verified layout and skips port detection entirely — that is what the VERIFIED badge means. So if port numbering keeps coming back wrong on rescans, verify the layout once instead of correcting ports one at a time.

Otherwise the fix is simply to correct it again on the new scan. That strengthens the memory.
symptoms: had to correct the same device again
entries.rootCause: pipeline/active_learning/memory.py two-tier matching: pHash Hamming distance <= HAMMING_TOL (6) on a 16x16 hash, else ResNet18 cosine similarity >= SIM_THRESH (0.88). Below both, find_match returns None and detection proceeds normally. Stores are partitioned per organization via store.set_org(). Port-number shifts and port-count relabels are keyed to scanId in feedback.jsonl, not to a visual fingerprint.

evidence.snippet:
"""Image fingerprint + nearest-correction lookup.

Two-tier matching identical to Active Learning CDP/*.py:
  1. Perceptual hash (Hamming distance <= HAMMING_TOL) — fast/exact path
  2. ResNet18 deep-feature cosine similarity (>= SIM_THRESH) — robust path

HASH_SIZE = 16
HAMMING_TOL = 6
SIM_THRESH = 0.88

def set_org(org_id) -> None:
    """Scope all subsequent store reads/writes to one organization."""

entries.short: RackTrack does try to re-apply your past corrections to new scans, but the match has to be close enough visually to be safe. How it works: when you correct something, RackTrack stores a fingerprint of that device's or port's picture.

entries.question: I scanned a video of a row of racks and the devices ended up assigned to the wrong rack.
entries.answer:
When you record one video panning across several racks, RackTrack has to guess where one rack ends and the next begins. It samples 30 frames spread evenly across the whole clip, runs the device detector on each, and declares a new rack whenever either signal trips between two neighbouring samples:

- the equipment's average horizontal position shifts by more than a quarter of the frame width, or
- the overall colour/scene fingerprint changes by more than about a third.

A frame where the detector finds no equipment at all — motion blur from a fast pan, a gap between racks, a wall, someone walking through — is treated as a pan transition and also ends the current rack.

That guesswork is where it goes wrong. The common failures:

- **One rack split into two.** A blurred or empty frame in the middle of a rack ends the segment. Because a segment only needs a single sampled frame to be emitted as a rack, even one bad frame can produce a spurious extra rack.
- **A long video splits everywhere.** Only 30 frames are sampled no matter how long the clip is, so the longer the video, the more real-world time passes between neighbouring samples, and the more likely a normal pan looks like a scene change. Keep the clip short.
- **Racks merged into one.** Nearly identical racks standing tight together give no colour break and no big sideways jump, so there is nothing to split on.
- **Re-framing mid-rack.** Drifting back and forth, stepping closer or further away, or swinging the phone to recompose can trip either signal inside a single rack. Simply holding still on a rack does *not* cause a split — a steady pause is safe and helpful.

How to get a clean result: pan slowly and steadily in one direction, hold steady for a moment squarely on each rack, keep a consistent distance, and keep the whole clip short.

If a row keeps splitting badly, use one photo per rack instead — this is the most reliable path, and it is not a downgrade. On the same **Scan two racks** screen, switch from Video to Photos: RackTrack analyzes each photo separately and links them into the same grouped multi-rack result, with no boundary guessing at all. (Grouping supports up to 8 racks.)

One limitation to know: there is no way to move a device from one rack to another after a scan, and no way to merge or split racks after the fact. If the grouping came out wrong, re-capture using the per-rack photo mode.
entries.rootCause: pipeline/multi_rack_split.py samples at most 30 frames and declares a rack transition when adjacent samples' mean device X differs by more than TRANSITION_X_SHIFT_RATIO (0.25 of frame width) or the HSV-histogram correlation change exceeds VISUAL_CHANGE_THRESHOLD (0.35). Frames with fewer than MIN_DEVICES_FOR_RACK (1) detections at DETECTOR_CONF_THRESHOLD 0.20 are treated as pan-transitions. A rack needs only MIN_FRAMES_PER_RACK (1) sample to be emitted.

evidence.snippet:
MAX_SAMPLED_FRAMES        = 30     # cap on how many frames we score
MIN_DEVICES_FOR_RACK      = 1      # frames with 0 devices are pan-transitions
TRANSITION_X_SHIFT_RATIO  = 0.25   # adjacent samples whose mean-X differs
                                   # by > 25% of frame width = new rack
VISUAL_CHANGE_THRESHOLD   = 0.35   # 1 - HSV-histogram correlation between
                                   # adjacent samples. > 0.35 = scene changed
                                   # (different rack), even if X stayed put.
MIN_FRAMES_PER_RACK       = 1      # a "rack" must hold the camera for ≥ N samples
DETECTOR_CONF_THRESHOLD   = 0.20   # mirrors config.json's devices_conf

4. Detect rack-transition points: split the frame sequence wherever
...
     + 0.35 * mean_detection_confidence

entries.short: When you record one video panning across several racks, RackTrack has to guess where one rack ends and the next begins.

entries.question: How do I see the model's actual confidence numbers for a scan?
entries.answer:
Internal / support use only — do not walk an end user through this unless they are technical and you have a reason.

First check whether you actually need the flag: the normal scan result page already shows a rounded percentage next to the **Device** row (device-class confidence) and next to the **Cable** row (cable classifier confidence). If those are the numbers you want, no flag is needed.

For the full set, a Diagnostics panel on the scan result page shows a **Confidences** section with **device class**, **port detection**, **cable color** and **port type** (the last three only once a device and port are selected, and each only if the pipeline returned it), each as a rounded percentage — alongside pipeline timings (normalize, quality_check, pipeline, total, plus a cache HIT marker, and a separate device+port timing block).

There is no button to open it. It is controlled purely by a browser storage flag: set `rt_devOpen` to `"1"` in localStorage for the app's origin and reload. Once open, the panel has an X in its header that closes it and writes the flag back to `"0"`; you can also set `"0"` by hand. The setting persists per browser.

Reading the numbers: they are raw model confidences, not calibrated probabilities. Reference points enforced in code — devices are detected at 0.20, ports at 0.23, PDU ports at 0.40 (rack units and servers at 0.25); a port whose status confidence is below 0.35 is reported as "Unknown" rather than connected/empty, and the downstream cable and port-type classifiers do not run on it at all; a cable below 0.50 triggers the visible "Not fully sure about this cable" warning.
symptoms: where do I see confidence scores
entries.rootCause: The Diagnostics panel renders behind `devOpen`, whose only source is localStorage key 'rt_devOpen'; no toggle control references setDevOpen(true) anywhere in the client.

device class{fmtPct(selectedDevice.confidence)}
...
port detection...
cable color...
port type...

"units_conf":   0.25,
"devices_conf": 0.20,
"server_conf":  0.25,
"iou_dedup":    0.5,
"ports_conf":   0.23,
"pdu_conf":     0.40

entries.question: Is the automatic retraining loop actually running in this deployment?
entries.answer:
Internal / admin only — do not promise users that corrections are training the model on a schedule.

The retraining pipeline is wired but **cannot complete a cycle in the repository's current state**.

1. **The `active_learning_Cache` Python package is missing.** Only its `data/` directory exists — there is no `__init__.py`, `config.py`, `store.py` or `cli.py`. Every code path that imports it fails:
   - `retraining_learning/config.py:9` does `from active_learning_Cache import config as cache_config` and uses it at lines 62-63 (`MODELS`, `RETRAIN_THRESHOLDS`). Because `run_loop.py:39` does `from . import config`, **the entire cycle dies at process start** — the `python -m active_learning_Cache.cli ingest` subprocess at `run_loop.py:57` is never even reached, so you will not see the "ingest failed (exit N)" warning either. The child is spawned detached with `stdio: 'ignore'` (`server/app.js:7856-7862`), so the traceback goes nowhere and the only trace is `[active_learning] cycle done (exit 1)`.
   - `pipeline/worker.py:440-460` imports `active_learning_Cache.config` and `.store` inside a try; `worker.py:511-514` swallows it with `AL uncertainty hook failed (non-fatal)`. No low-confidence samples are queued.

2. **Even when working, promotion is never automatic.** A retrained model is registered only as a *candidate* under `Models/candidates/`; it must beat production's primary metric on a frozen holdout by at least `PROMOTION_MIN_DELTA` (`retraining_learning/config.py:47-51` — 0.005 devices, 0.005 cable, 0.010 port_count) and a human must run `python -m retraining_learning.cli promote <model> <version> --yes`. Note `ports_typed`/`ports_status` in the registry have no gate configured at all. `retraining_learning/registry.json` confirms nothing has ever been promoted — every model is `"version": "baseline"` with `"metrics": {}` and `"promoted_ts": null`, and empty `candidates`/`history`.

What **does** work today, and is safe to tell users: corrections are written to `server/feedback.jsonl`, overlaid onto their scan result, and stored as pHash+ResNet18 fingerprints in the org-scoped active-learning memory (via `pipeline.active_learning.cli`, a package that does exist) so future scans auto-apply them. That layer is independent of the retrain loop.

Auto-triggering can be disabled entirely with `ACTIVE_LEARNING_AUTOTRAIN=0` (`server/app.js:7845`).
entries.rootCause: `active_learning_Cache` contains only `data/` — no Python module. retraining_learning/config.py does `from active_learning_Cache import config as cache_config` at import time; run_loop's ingest runs `python -m active_learning_Cache.cli ingest`; worker.py's _queue_low_confidence_samples imports `active_learning_Cache.config` and `.store` inside a try that logs and swallows on failure.

try:

    from active_learning_Cache.store import Store

except Exception as e:
    # Anything goes wrong → swallow. Active learning is a side-channel,
    # never a hard dependency of the analyze response.

entries.question: The rack is too tall to fit in one photo. How do I scan it?
entries.answer:
Use MULTI mode, which joins several overlapping photos into one tall image before analysing it.

1. Tap SCAN, then the Upload tab, then MULTI (the middle of the three mode buttons: SINGLE, MULTI, VIDEO).
2. Tap Select photos and pick between 2 and 8 overlapping photos of the rack. The screen tells you "Take 2-8 overlapping photos of the rack. Any order — we'll arrange them automatically."
3. The button at the bottom counts down what is still missing — "Add 2 more photo" with nothing selected, "Add 1 more photo" with one — and once you have at least two it becomes Stitch & Analyze with the photo count in brackets. Tap it.

Once photos are in the list, the header shows "N photos · auto-arranged" and a N/8 counter. You can add more with Add more (hidden once you hit 8), reorder with the up/down arrows on each row, or remove one with the X — but you do not need to: the top-to-bottom order is worked out for you from the overlaps. The server also enforces the same limits, so fewer than 2 or more than 8 photos will not be accepted.
entries.rootCause: MultiUploadZone caps the file list at 8 (slice(0,8)) and the CTA requires >= 2 files before it becomes Stitch & Analyze.

entries.question: How do I see what's on the other end of a cable?
entries.answer:
Open the rack, open Ports, then tap the Cables tab. The number on the tab is how many ports currently see a neighbour on the far end; the list itself is headed with the exact count (for example "6 LINKS").

Each row is one cable: your port number and interface on the left, the far-end device on the right, plus a tag saying whether it is a Device, an Uplink or a Switch link. Tap a row to expand it into a trace showing both ends. Where the port feeds a whole downstream network (an uplink, a switch-to-switch link, or any port with more than one device behind it), the trace lists the devices found behind it with their makers — long lists are shortened, so use "show all" to see the rest.

One thing that is not a fault: a patch panel or wall socket in the middle of a run is passive, with no electronics, so the switch cannot see it. The trace will look like the cable runs straight from the switch to the far-end device. If you keep a cable schedule, record the panel in the port label.

If the tab is empty it just means RackTrack is still reading the switch — only live ports with an LLDP neighbour or a known MAC appear here.
symptoms: what's on the end of this cable
patch panel missing from the trace
entries.rootCause: PortsPage CablesView derives cable rows from live port data + LLDP neighbours; expanding a row mounts CableTrace.

entries.question: How do I connect our CMDB or other data source?
entries.answer:
This is an admin-only area (org admin or owner). Open Data Sources — from Profile it is the row under the Data Sources heading, or use Data Sources in the sidebar.

1. Tap Add connection.
2. Give it a Name (for example "My ServiceNow Dev").
3. Choose the Type. The fields below change to match it:
   - ServiceNow / CMDB — Instance ID (just the part before .service-now.com), Username, Password.
   - NetBox — Base URL, API Token (from your NetBox user profile).
   - SolarWinds Orion — Host, Username, Password.
   - CA / DX Spectrum — Base URL, Username, Password.
   - My own database (SQL) — a PostgreSQL or MySQL connection string.
   - My own database (REST) — Base URL, and an API token if it needs one.
4. Tap Save & use.

Only one connection is active at a time, and every screen reads from that one — switching it switches the source of all your data. To switch, tap Use on any other saved connection. The three-dot menu gives Edit and Delete. Connections are saved per signed-in admin account, not shared across the org.

When you Edit an existing connection the credential boxes open empty on purpose — the page says "Leave the credential fields blank to keep what's already saved." The Type is locked once a connection exists ("Type can't change after a connection is created"); to change type, create a new connection.

There is no test button, and saving is not a test: Save only checks that the required boxes are filled and then stores the credentials encrypted — it never contacts your system, so wrong credentials will save without complaint. To actually prove a ServiceNow connection works, tap Use on it (or, if it is already active, use "Refresh data from this source"). That runs a real poll and shows either "Pulled N incidents from <instance>" or "Refresh failed: …". The poll can take a few minutes on a cold developer instance.
symptoms: credentials are blank when I edit
entries.rootCause: ConnectionsPage (/connections) behind AdminRoute; TYPE_INFO defines the per-type field schema; secrets are never preloaded into the edit form.

entries.question: How do I approve a new organization that has signed up?
entries.answer:
Platform owner only. Open the Organizations console (/organizations). Self-signups appear at the top under "Pending approvals" — the section only shows when at least one request is waiting — each tagged Pending with "Requested by <username> · <email>". Until you act they are locked out of everything: the server rejects every request from a pending org (403 "Your organization is awaiting approval"), not just the UI.

Three buttons on each pending row:
- Approve — sets the org active. Their waiting screen polls every 12 seconds and drops them into the app on its own (they can also hit "Check now").
- Reject — sets the org to "rejected"; they see "Request not approved" instead of the spinner. The org and all its accounts survive, so it is reversible: the org stays in "All organizations" below, and its three-dot menu offers Reactivate to let them in later.
- Remove — permanently deletes the organization (with a confirm modal). Use Reject unless you are certain.

On the All organizations cards below, the three-dot menu gives Edit (rename), Deactivate (or Reactivate), and Remove.

Important: nobody is emailed when a company signs up — the only email the system sends is the signup verification code. You find out about new requests only by opening this console, so check it.
entries.rootCause: OrgConsolePage owner branch renders the pending list with approveOrg/rejectOrg and a removeOrg confirm modal; per-org kebab menu offers Edit / Deactivate / Remove.

entries.question: How do I run an audit on a lab switch?
entries.answer:
Platform owner only. Open Lab in the sidebar (it only appears for owners), or go to /lab. Anyone else sees "Restricted to platform owners."

1. The lab devices are shown as a grid of buttons, each tagged with its state: Live, Offline, No data, Disabled, or Connecting…
2. Click a device. If it is enabled and the poller is reaching it, the audit runs automatically the first time you select it — you do not need to press anything. If the device is Disabled or Offline the auto-run is deliberately skipped (the SSH attempt would just hang), and a banner explains why; press the button to force an attempt.
3. Read the result using the tab strip: Identity, Ports, VLANs, LLDP, MAC.
4. To re-run it later press Refresh audit (the button reads Run full audit if there is no result yet, and Connecting… while one is in flight). It is greyed out while polling is disabled for that device. Disable polling / Enable polling turns the background polling of that device on and off.

Two things that look wrong but are not. Results are kept per device, so flipping between devices shows you what was last seen with a note of how old it is — a stamp like "Audit as of 4m ago · live SSH pass, not polled". And the virtual Cisco switches genuinely report "—" for speed, duplex and PoE, because they have no physical link or PoE hardware.
symptoms: speed and PoE show a dash
entries.rootCause: LabPage is owner-gated (server requireRole('owner') on /api/lab/*). Audits auto-run on first selection, are cached per device in auditsRef, and one SSH pass runs at a time. Cisco IOL has no link negotiation or PoE hardware.

entries.question: How do I list surplus equipment for sale, and how do I search what's already listed?
entries.answer:
Admin only (organization admin or platform owner), and the Marketplace link lives in the desktop/landscape-iPad sidebar — it is not on the phone bottom bar. Open Marketplace.

The section headings across the top are Browse, My listings, Orders, Alerts, Dashboard and Partners.

To search and filter what is listed (this toolbar only appears on the Browse tab):
- Type in the box marked "Search by title, vendor or model…". The X inside it clears your text.
- Use the category dropdown next to it — it opens on "All categories".
- Use the For sale / Wanted pair to switch between things people are selling and things people are looking for.
- When any filter is on, a "Clear filters" link appears next to the results heading (and again in the empty-results panel).

To list something:
1. Tap List an item (top right of the Marketplace header).
2. Choose For sale, or Wanted if you are looking for something rather than selling it.
3. Fill in Title (required, up to 140 characters), Vendor, Model and Category. Category is a dropdown that already has a value selected, so you only change it if the default is wrong.
4. Set Condition (New (sealed) / Refurbished / Used — working / For parts — also pre-selected) and a Price. Leave the price blank and buyers see "Make an offer". You can also set Currency (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, INR) and Quantity.
5. Add a Location and Description (up to 2000 characters) if useful. Both optional.
6. Add a photo — optional, JPG / PNG / WebP / HEIC, up to 8 MB. Wait for it to say Photo ready (it shows Uploading… first, or Upload failed if something went wrong). A wrong file type gives "Only image files are accepted (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC)."; too large gives "Image must be 8 MB or smaller."
7. Tap Publish listing (or Post request if you chose Wanted). The button reads Publishing… while it saves.

If RackTrack recognises the vendor/model as one of its partners, an "Or send buyers to a partner" box appears above the buttons — that is an alternative to publishing, not a required step.

entries.rootCause: MarketplacePage toolbar (search + category + kind segmented control) plus MarketplaceShell's default 'List an item' action into MarketplaceNewPage, which caps images at 8 MB.
