entries.question: My rack was scanned but nothing at all appeared in ServiceNow, and I was never shown a ticket.
entries.answer:
After a scan, RackTrack automatically tries to raise a CMDB ticket in the background (a few seconds after the post-scan topology rebuild finishes). That automatic attempt runs without a signed-in user attached, so it can't pick up the ServiceNow connection you or your admin set up under Data Sources — it can only reach ServiceNow if the server itself has been given ServiceNow credentials. On a normal install it hasn't, so the attempt quietly fails and nothing is shown to you.

What this means for you: use the "Raise Ticket" button on the results screen. That request is sent as you, so it uses your organisation's ServiceNow connection (or your personal one) and creates the request normally. Nothing is lost by the failed background attempt. If "Raise Ticket" also reports that ServiceNow isn't configured, then no active ServiceNow connection exists yet — ask your admin to add one under Data Sources / Connections.

Note: if the scan matches the CMDB exactly, no ticket is created at all, by design — the automatic run reports "scan matches CMDB; no ticket needed," and that's not an error.

Admins: for the automatic post-scan ticket and the 5-minute approval poller to work unattended, the ServiceNow instance, username and password must be set in the server's own environment, because those scheduled attempts run with no user or organisation attached and so can't resolve a saved connection profile.
symptoms: No ServiceNow request created after a scan
Server log: [cmdb-ticket] <rackId> create failed: SN_INSTANCE/SN_USER/SN_PASSWORD not configured
Ticket only appears after pressing Raise Ticket
entries.rootCause: scheduleCmdbTicket() and runPollCycle() call runTicketCmd without userId/orgId, so no credentials are injected into the Python child; _sn() then returns None and the create/poll fails.

evidence.snippet: function scheduleCmdbTicket(rackId, delayMs = 4000) { ... const r = await runTicketCmd(['create', '--rack-id', rackId], { timeoutMs: 120_000 }); ... logger.warn(`[cmdb-ticket] ${rackId} create failed: ${r.error}`);
async function runPollCycle() { const r = await runTicketCmd(['poll'], { timeoutMs: 300_000 });

entries.short: The automatic post-scan ServiceNow ticket runs with no user and often fails silently; use the 'Raise Ticket' button, which files under your connection.

entries.question: My device is not showing up in ServiceNow even though the scan found it.
entries.answer:
RackTrack finds your rack in ServiceNow by a single field on the rack record: the RackTrack scan ID. It looks for a rack record in cmdb_ci_rack whose "u_racktrack_scan_id" field equals the rack ID shown in RackTrack (the RK-... code). If that field is blank or holds a different value, ServiceNow looks empty to RackTrack even though the rack exists - the reconciliation then reports everything in the scan as brand new, and Switch Information shows no serials.

What to do (this needs someone who can edit records in ServiceNow):
1. Open the rack record in ServiceNow.
2. Set the RackTrack scan ID field to the exact RK-... code shown on the RackTrack results screen.
3. Make sure each device is a child of that rack in a CI relationship - RackTrack reads the rack's children from cmdb_rel_ci where parent = the rack, and takes the first 100. (RackTrack itself creates these as "Contains / Contained by".)
4. Re-open the rack in RackTrack.

If the rack ID is set correctly and a single device still does not appear, check two more things on that device's CI:
- Its class must be one RackTrack recognises: IP Switch (cmdb_ci_ip_switch), Netgear/patch panel (cmdb_ci_netgear), Server, Firewall (cmdb_ci_firewall_network) or Router. Any other class is skipped silently. The Switch Information panel is narrower still - it only lists cmdb_ci_ip_switch children.
- Its CI name must match the device name in the scan exactly; devices are paired by name, so a renamed CI shows up as one removal plus one addition.

Devices attached to no rack, or to a rack without that ID set, will never appear.
symptoms: Device present in ServiceNow but RackTrack reports it as "added"
Switch Information empty even though the CMDB has the switch
Everything in the scan is listed as new / missing from CMDB
entries.rootCause: fetch_cmdb_state queries cmdb_ci_rack with sysparm_query u_racktrack_scan_id=<rackId>; no rows means it returns an empty device map. Children are read via cmdb_rel_ci parent=<rack sys_id>.

evidence.snippet: rack_resp = sn._get("/table/cmdb_ci_rack", { "sysparm_query": f"u_racktrack_scan_id={rack_id}", "sysparm_limit": 1, }) ... if not rack_rows: # Not in CMDB yet — treat as "no current state". return {"rack": None, "devices": {}, "reachable": True}
def get_rack_children(self, rack_sys_id: str) -> list[dict]: ... {"sysparm_query": f"parent={rack_sys_id}", "sysparm_limit": 100,}

2. Set the RackTrack scan ID field to the exact RK-... code shown on the RackTrack results screen.
3. Make sure each device is a child of that rack in a CI relationship - RackTrack reads the rack's children from cmdb_rel_ci where parent = the rack, and takes the first 100.

entries.question: I moved a switch to a different rack unit and now the CMDB has two records for it.
entries.answer:
This is expected behaviour, and worth understanding before you move equipment.

RackTrack names devices after the rack unit they sit in: a switch in U10 becomes SW-U10, a patch panel in U06 becomes PP-U06, a server in U01 becomes SRV-U01. The name is derived from the U position in the scan and nothing else, and the CMDB match is done purely on that name — every write is "find by name, patch it if it exists, otherwise create it".

So if you physically move a switch from U10 to U11 and rescan, RackTrack sees SW-U10 as gone and SW-U11 as brand new. Nothing in the push path ever deletes or retires a CI, so the old SW-U10 record stays exactly where it was and you end up with two records for one switch.

What to do after moving equipment:
1. Rescan the rack. RackTrack computes the difference against the CMDB and opens (or updates) a ServiceNow request for that rack.
2. Read the ticket before anyone approves it. The summary line reads as "+1 / -1 / ~0 devices" and the body lists the device names — you should see SW-U10 under removed and SW-U11 under added. That is your signal it is a move, not a real install.
3. Have whoever owns the CMDB rename the old CI to the new name (or retire it) rather than letting the approval create a second one. The push only happens once the ticket is approved and closed-complete, so there is time to act.

The same applies if a device is detected one unit off because of the photo angle: retake the photo squarely and rescan before the ticket is approved.
symptoms: Two CMDB records for the same physical switch
A device shows as removed and a near-identical one as added
Names like SW-U10 and SW-U11 both present
entries.rootCause: Device CMDB names are derived from the U position (SW-U{u:02d} / PP-U{u:02d} / SRV-U{u:02d}) in synth.py, and compute_diff keys added/removed/changed purely on set differences of those names.

    if cls == "Patch Panel":  return f"PP-U{u:02d}", u

entries.question: My incident does not appear in RackTrack's ticket list.
entries.answer:
RackTrack only pulls in tickets it can actually act on, and it applies four filters:

1. The incident must still be active.
2. Its state must be New or In Progress. Closed, resolved or on-hold tickets are ignored.
3. It must resolve to a device name in RackTrack's naming style — SW-U10, SRV-U01, PP-U12 (the U number is one or two digits).
4. Its text must contain a port number, written like "port 12", "Port #12" or "port:12".

For filter 3 there is an important ordering rule: if the incident has a Configuration item (cmdb_ci) set, that name is used and the text is NOT consulted. The name must also START with the RackTrack pattern. So an incident linked to a CI called "Cisco Catalyst 3560" is skipped even if the short description says "SW-U10 port 12" — the CI value wins. For filter 4, the port may appear in either the short description or the full description; RackTrack searches both together.

If either the device name or the port number is missing, the ticket is skipped on purpose because RackTrack would not know what to go and verify. RackTrack also reads a maximum of 200 open incidents per refresh, so on a busy instance an older ticket can fall outside that window.

The fix:
- If the incident has no Configuration item, edit the short description to include both the device name and the port — for example "SW-U10 port 12 link down".
- If the incident IS linked to a Configuration item, point it at the CI whose name is the RackTrack device name (SW-U10), or clear the CI link so RackTrack falls back to parsing the text.

Then have an organization administrator or the platform owner open Connections, select the ServiceNow source and press "Refresh data from this source". The Connections screen is admin-only, so a technician cannot trigger the refresh themselves.
symptoms: Incident missing from the active ticket list
Refresh reports fewer incidents than expected
entries.rootCause: poll.py queries incident with active=true^stateIN1,2 and sysparm_limit 200, then is_racktrack_actionable() requires both a parsed port number and a device matching (SW|SRV|PP)-U\d{1,2}.

RackTrack only pulls in tickets it can actually act on, and it applies four filters:
1. The incident must still be active.
2. Its state must be New or In Progress. Closed, resolved or on-hold tickets are ignored.
3. It must resolve to a device name in RackTrack's naming style — SW-U10, SRV-U01, PP-U12 (the U number is one or two digits).

entries.question: I pressed "Refresh data from this source" and it sat there, then failed.
entries.answer:
That button (shown only for ServiceNow connections) pulls your open incidents and CMDB records out of ServiceNow. It runs in the background — the server accepts the job and returns straight away, so you can keep using the app while it works.

Timings you can rely on:
- The server gives the poll up to 5 minutes, then kills it.
- The screen waits 1.5 seconds, then checks progress every 3 seconds, and gives up watching after 6 minutes with "Stopped waiting after 6 minutes — check the server log for poll progress." The job may still be running server-side at that point.
- If the poll hits the server's 5-minute cap you get a message naming your instance and telling you to open <instance>.service-now.com in a browser, sign in to confirm it is awake, then try again. That is exactly the right thing to do — developer instances hibernate.

One more thing that can look like a hang: pressing Refresh again, or switching to a different active connection while a pull is in flight, cancels the running poll and starts a new one. Let a pull finish before starting another.

When it works you get a green line: "✓ Pulled N incidents from <instance>". A failure shows as "Refresh failed: …".
symptoms: Stopped waiting after 6 minutes — check the server log for poll progress.
Poll timed out after 300s talking to <instance>.service-now.com.
Pulling fresh data from … spinner never finishes
entries.rootCause: POST /api/incidents/refresh spawns servicenow_inbox/poll.py with a 300000 ms kill timer; the client polls /api/incidents/refresh/status every 3s and abandons after 360000 ms.

evidence.snippet: const TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000; const killer = setTimeout(() => { ... error: `Poll timed out after ${TIMEOUT_MS / 1000}s talking to ${creds.instance}.service-now.com. Open ${creds.instance}.service-now.com in a browser, sign in to confirm it's awake, then try again.`,

entries.short: That button (shown only for ServiceNow connections) pulls your open incidents and CMDB records out of ServiceNow. It runs in the background — RackTrack accepts the job and returns straight away, so you can keep using the app while it works.

entries.question: I switched to a different ServiceNow connection but I am still seeing the old account's incidents.
entries.answer:
The incident list is a stored copy from the last successful pull, so switching connections does not change it by itself. RackTrack normally kicks off a fresh pull as soon as someone taps "Use" on a ServiceNow connection — and if a pull for the previous account is still running, it is stopped so the old instance's results cannot overwrite the new ones.

First, note who can do this: the data-source screen is organization-admin only. If you are a member or a site manager, you will not see a "Data Sources" row on your Profile, and typing the /connections address sends you back to the home screen. Ask your organization admin to run the steps below — the connection and its incident list are shared for the whole organization, so they only have to do it once.

If you are an organization admin or the platform owner and the list still looks wrong:
1. Open Profile → Data Sources (on a desktop or landscape iPad it is also "Data Sources" in the left sidebar). The screen is titled "Data Sources".
2. Under "Active", confirm the connection you want is the one shown with the "Active" badge. If not, find it under "Other saved" and tap "Use".
3. Tap "Refresh data from this source".
4. While it runs you will see "Pulling fresh data from <name>…". Wait for the outcome line "✓ Pulled N incidents from <instance>" and check the instance name in it matches the account you expect. A cold ServiceNow instance can take several minutes; the app gives up after about 6 minutes and tells you to check the server log.

Two things to know:
- The incident list is shared across everyone on this server rather than kept per person, so it always reflects whoever refreshed last.
- Only one refresh runs at a time. If a colleague switches sources or hits refresh while your pull is in progress, yours is cancelled in favour of theirs — re-run the refresh if your banner never arrives.

Ticket list shows another account's incidents

entries.question: Is the Network View live data from my network, or from my photo?
entries.answer:
In this deployment the Network View is built from your scan, not from a live SNMP sweep. After each scan RackTrack pushes the rack's devices, ports and links into the discovery server's (Netdisco's) Postgres database, and the Network View then reads them back. Every record created this way carries the rack ID at the end of its description, e.g. "Cisco C9300-48P running IOS-XE 17.9 [racktrack:RK-101]".

What that means in practice:
- Device names and models come from the scan result plus any CMDB/override data, not from anything queried on the wire.
- Management IPs and MAC addresses are used when the scan or CMDB supplies them; when they are missing (patch panels, unmanaged gear) RackTrack synthesises a deterministic placeholder IP/MAC so the device can exist in Netdisco. So an address shown there is not proof the device is reachable.
- "Learned MAC" counts can legitimately be 0 on every port, because the MAC-sightings feed has nothing observed for synthesised devices.
- The push runs automatically about 1.5 s after a scan completes (debounced per rack), and can also be triggered manually.

If you need genuinely live switch state — port up/down, speeds, VLANs, neighbours — use the live switch ports screen instead, which logs into the switch over SSH.
symptoms: Network View shows devices that were never SNMP-discovered
entries.rootCause: push_rack_to_netdisco.py builds device rows from synth.build_inventory over the scan result and inserts them into Netdisco's Postgres, tagging each description with [racktrack:<rack_id>]; scheduleNetdiscoSync fires 1500 ms after a scan.

# Tag stays at the END so it doesn't dominate Netdisco's UI but is still easy to grep on for cleanup — `description LIKE '%[racktrack:%'`.
    desc_parts.append(f"[racktrack:{rack_id}]")

//   /nodes (active MAC sightings) is fetched separately and joined by port.
//   It legitimately may return [] for synthesised RackTrack devices.

After each scan RackTrack pushes the rack's devices, ports and links into the discovery server's (Netdisco's) Postgres database, and the Network View then reads them back. Every record created this way carries the rack ID at the end of its description, e.g. "Cisco C9300-48P running IOS-XE 17.9 [racktrack:RK-101]".

entries.question: Syncing a rack to the Network View fails with "Network View sync is temporarily unavailable."
entries.answer:
The push of your scan into the discovery server (Network View) didn't complete. From your side there's nothing to correct — retry once, and if it fails again, report it with the rack ID. Nothing else is affected: your scan, unit map, ports and topology are all unchanged.

Admins: the sync runs a helper that writes the rack straight into the Network View's PostgreSQL database rather than going through its web interface. Any failure, whatever the cause, is deliberately shown to the user as the single generic message "Network View sync is temporarily unavailable." — the specific reason only ever appears in the server log.

Common causes, most to least likely:
- The Network View's PostgreSQL database can't be reached at the configured host and port (it defaults to the local machine on port 5432, with the default database name, user and password).
- The PostgreSQL Python driver isn't installed in the Python the server uses to run the helper.
- There's no completed scan result for that rack yet, so there's nothing to push.
- The helper script isn't where the server expects to find it.
- The push took longer than 60 seconds and was stopped.
- A database error part-way through: the whole write is rolled back, so nothing is left half-written.

To tell which path failed, check the server log: the manual sync button and the automatic post-scan sync (which runs a moment after every scan) each log their own success or failure line, including the rack ID and, on success, the number of devices, ports and edges written.
symptoms: Network View sync is temporarily unavailable.
Log: [netdisco] <rackId> sync failed — cannot connect to Netdisco Postgres
Missing dependency. Run:  pip install psycopg2-binary
entries.rootCause: runPushScript spawns the push script with a 60s SIGKILL timer and any non-ok result is mapped to a generic 502; the script exits 2 when psycopg2 cannot open the Netdisco database.

evidence.snippet: const r = await runPushScript(rackId); if (!r.ok) { logger.warn(`[netdisco] sync ${rackId} failed:`, r.error); return res.status(502).json({ ok: false, error: 'Network View sync is temporarily unavailable.' }); }
const timer = setTimeout(() => { try { child.kill('SIGKILL'); } catch (_) {} resolve({ ok: false, error: 'push script timed out (60s)' }); }, 60_000);
except psycopg2.OperationalError as e: print(f"ERROR: cannot connect to Netdisco Postgres at {DB_CONFIG['host']}:{DB_CONFIG['port']} — {e}") sys.exit(2)

entries.short: The scan couldn't be pushed to Network View; retry once and report with the rack ID if it fails again — your scan and topology are unaffected.

entries.question: Admin: what exactly do I configure for Netdisco, and what are the common misconfigurations?
entries.answer:
Internal note. The server talks to Netdisco two different ways and both must be configured:

1. Read path (Network View pages) — HTTP against the Netdisco web API. Settings: NETDISCO_URL (code default http://localhost:5000), NETDISCO_USER and NETDISCO_PASSWORD (both default to admin). The proxy POSTs to /login (JSON first, form-encoded fallback), caches the returned api_key in memory, and on a 401 forces one fresh login and retries the request exactly once. Normal proxied requests use a 15-second timeout; the one exception is GET /api/netdisco/health, which uses its own 4-second abort — so the "Network View offline" badge can appear after 4 seconds even though data requests would wait 15.
2. Write path (pushing scans in) — direct PostgreSQL via netdisco-docker/push_rack_to_netdisco.py (psycopg2, requires psycopg2-binary; killed after 60 s). Settings: NETDISCO_DB_HOST, NETDISCO_DB_PORT, NETDISCO_DB_NAME, NETDISCO_DB_USER, NETDISCO_DB_PASS (defaults localhost / 5432 / netdisco / netdisco / netdisco).

Two traps worth checking first:
- Port mismatch. The bundled compose file publishes the Netdisco web container on host port 5005 (5005:5000) and Postgres on 5432:5432. If the RackTrack server runs on the host rather than inside the compose network, NETDISCO_URL must point at http://localhost:5005, not 5000. server/.env.example ships NETDISCO_URL=http://netdisco:5000, which is the in-network form.
- Default credentials. If NODE_ENV is production and user/password are still admin/admin, the server logs a warning at boot (event netdisco.default_creds) but keeps running. Note .env.example ships NETDISCO_USER/NETDISCO_PASSWORD=changeme, so an unedited .env fails login rather than tripping that warning.
symptoms: Network View offline despite the containers running
netdisco.default_creds warning in the boot log
Reads work but sync fails, or vice versa
entries.rootCause: Two independent transports with independent settings: HTTP api-key auth for reads, direct psycopg2 for writes; compose publishes the web UI on host 5005 while the proxy default is 5000.

evidence.snippet: const NETDISCO_URL  = process.env.NETDISCO_URL || 'http://localhost:5000'; ... const TIMEOUT_MS = 15000; if ((process.env.NODE_ENV || 'development') === 'production' && ND_USER === 'admin' && ND_PASSWORD === 'admin') { logger.warn({ event: 'netdisco.default_creds' }, 'Netdisco using default admin/admin credentials — set NETDISCO_USER and NETDISCO_PASSWORD');
NETDISCO_DB_HOST: process.env.NETDISCO_DB_HOST || 'localhost', NETDISCO_DB_PORT: process.env.NETDISCO_DB_PORT || '5432', NETDISCO_DB_NAME: process.env.NETDISCO_DB_NAME || 'netdisco',

NETDISCO_URL=http://netdisco:5000
NETDISCO_USER=changeme
NETDISCO_PASSWORD=changeme

entries.short: Internal note. The server talks to Netdisco two different ways and both must be configured: a read path for the Network View pages, over HTTP against the Netdisco web API (NETDISCO_URL, NETDISCO_USER, NETDISCO_PASSWORD), and a write path that pushes scans straight into PostgreSQL via netdisco-docker/push_rack_to_netdisco.py (NETDISCO_DB_HOST, NETDISCO_DB_PORT and the rest).

entries.question: RackTrack analysed the ticket but never posted a work note back to ServiceNow.
entries.answer:
Posting back is guarded on purpose, and there are three reasons it is skipped:

1. Low confidence — if RackTrack's confidence in its own reading is below 0.5 it stays quiet rather than posting a guess.
2. Nothing changed — if the analysis is identical to the one already posted for that incident, it will not post a duplicate.
3. Too soon — it will not post to the same incident twice within 24 hours.

If you need it posted anyway, the post action supports a force option. Force clears RackTrack's "already posted" record for that incident, which skips the no-change and rate-limit guards only — it cannot override the 0.5 confidence floor, so a low-confidence analysis still will not post.

Two things will refuse the post outright rather than skip it: if the incident is missing its internal record id (sys_id) in RackTrack's copy, and if RackTrack has not analysed the ticket yet (run the analysis first, then post). For the missing record id, refresh your incidents from the Connections screen so the ticket is re-read against your active ServiceNow connection.
symptoms: inbox ticket is missing sys_id — cannot post
No work note appears on the incident
entries.rootCause: auto_post_analysis enforces POST_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR 0.5, an analysis-hash equality check, and POST_RATE_LIMIT_HOURS 24 before calling add_work_note.

evidence.snippet:

POST_RATE_LIMIT_HOURS = 24

if confidence < POST_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR: return {"status": "skipped_low_confidence", ...} ... if prev.get("hash") == cur_hash: return {"status": "skipped_no_change", ...} ... if datetime.now(timezone.utc) - last_dt < timedelta(hours=POST_RATE_LIMIT_HOURS): return {"status": "skipped_rate_limit", ...}

if (!sn_creds) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'No active ServiceNow connection. Add one under Profile → Connections.' }); ... if (!ticket.sys_id) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'inbox ticket is missing sys_id — cannot post' });

entries.short: Posting back is guarded on purpose, and there are three reasons it is skipped: RackTrack's confidence in its own reading is below 0.5, the analysis is identical to the one already posted for that incident, or it already posted to that incident within the last 24 hours.

entries.question: Internal: the CMDB and incident data looks like demo data and does not match our real ServiceNow.
entries.answer:
Internal note. The server can serve fixture data in place of the real external systems. server/mock_routes.js simulates ServiceNow, NetBox, SolarWinds Orion, CA/DX Spectrum and a generic REST source from JSON files under server/data/mock, with its own hardcoded ServiceNow accounts (sn_admin, sn_netops, sn_dcops, sn_secops).

Two things to check when the data looks wrong:
1. These mock routes are mounted whenever MOCK_SERVER_URL is set OR NODE_ENV is anything other than production (server/app.js:358-368). A staging box left on the default NODE_ENV therefore exposes them; the boot log line is "mock data-source routes loaded" (and "mock data-source routes disabled (production, MOCK_SERVER_URL unset)" when they are off).
2. When MOCK_SERVER_URL is set, POST /api/incidents/refresh redirects the poller wholesale: it injects SN_BASE_URL=<MOCK_SERVER_URL>/api/now into poll.py's environment (server/app.js:4161-4173), and servicenow_inbox/poll.py:259 prefers SN_BASE_URL over https://<instance>.service-now.com/api/now. The user's selected instance is still passed as SN_INSTANCE and shown in the UI, so the Connections screen can report a green "Pulled N incidents from <instance>" while the content came from fixtures.

Note on credentials: the mock ServiceNow endpoints do validate Basic auth against the four hardcoded accounts (mock_routes.js checkSnAuth, lines 74-93) and return 401 otherwise — so it is the instance name, not the password, that is effectively ignored.

Fix: unset MOCK_SERVER_URL and run with NODE_ENV=production for any deployment that must reach a real instance.

Boot log: mock data-source routes loaded

entries.question: How do I know if the app on my phone is the current version, and what happens if it isn't?
entries.answer:
RackTrack has no in-app version check. There's no "a new version is available" prompt and no version number shown anywhere in the app, so the app itself will never tell you that you're behind. (The server can report its own version for operators, but nothing in the app reads it.)

You're not entirely on your own, though — new builds are announced out-of-band:
- iPhone/iPad: builds go out through TestFlight, and Apple emails you when one is released. Open TestFlight and tap RackTrack — if an "Update" button is showing, you're behind. Best fix: open TestFlight, tap RackTrack, and switch on Automatic Updates once; new builds then install themselves. Each build also has "What to Test" notes worth ten seconds of your time.
- Android: builds are distributed through Firebase App Distribution, which notifies testers when a new release goes out. Install it from the notification or email link you receive.

Why staying current matters: the server's address is baked into each build when it's made. If the server moves (for example, a restarted Cloudflare tunnel hands out a new random address), an old build keeps calling an address that no longer exists and every screen fails — with no "please update" message, just failures. So if your app has suddenly stopped working, installing the newest build is the first thing to try. Separately, on iOS, TestFlight builds expire 90 days after upload and the app simply stops opening; that's Apple's rule and is also fixed by installing the current build.
symptoms: how do I know I'm on the latest version
old app keeps working then suddenly doesn't
entries.rootCause: There is no client-side version check: nothing in client/src consumes the server's /api/version endpoint, which exists only for operators. API_BASE is frozen into the bundle at build time, so a stale client fails hard rather than degrading.

evidence.snippet: let API_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE || '';
Open TestFlight → tap RackTrack → switch on Automatic Updates. ... If a new build is waiting, RackTrack shows an Update button

entries.short: RackTrack has no in-app version check; watch for TestFlight (iOS) or Firebase (Android) notices and reinstall the latest build if the app stops working.

entries.question: The APK/IPA built fine but points at the wrong server. How is the backend URL set?
entries.answer:
Admin/internal. The backend URL is baked into the app when the build is made, from a build-time setting. There is no runtime setting and no in-app way to change it — a wrong URL means you have to rebuild.

Android, two paths:
- Tunnel path: start the tunnel first (a script records the tunnel's address), then run a second script that writes that address into the app's production configuration and rebuilds. Build the APK in Android Studio afterwards. This path builds without the safety check, so it's the unguarded one.
- Guarded path: a shipping script takes the backend address from an environment variable (falling back to a hardcoded host if none is set) and builds through the guarded build command.

iOS: the packaging script takes the backend URL as its second argument, falling back to a saved tunnel-URL file if you don't pass one; it never reads it from the configuration file.

Two traps:
1. The production configuration file is intentionally empty (so the app talks to the same origin it's served from), but a local override configuration file contains a localhost address, and the local override wins. That's the known misbuild recorded as the top blocker in the TestFlight-readiness notes. It only bites the plain build: the shipping and packaging scripts set the backend address as a real environment variable, which beats any configuration file, so the guarded build's checker (which rejects empty, localhost and non-HTTPS addresses, and warns on temporary quick-tunnel addresses) sees the right value.
2. The app has a self-heal that only works for the browser version: if the configured address is a localhost one but the page isn't actually running on localhost, it drops back to the same origin it's served from. A packaged mobile app runs from an internal local address, so that self-heal deliberately doesn't fire — and every call just fails with "Load failed".
symptoms: Load failed on every call in the packaged app
entries.rootCause: VITE_API_BASE is an import.meta.env value inlined at build time. .env.production.local (localhost:3001) overrides .env.production in a plain vite build.

$content = $content -replace "VITE_API_BASE=.*", "VITE_API_BASE=$url"
...

// Self-heal a common misbuild: the web dist gets built with a LOCALHOST API base ... If we detect a localhost base but the page is actually served from a real host, drop to same-origin
API points at localhost .env.production.local → VITE_API_BASE=http://localhost:3001 — Vite's .local file overrides .env.production. In a packaged app, localhost is the phone itself

entries.question: Sharing to Teams or Outlook fails with a message about "No valid token"
entries.answer:
This is a server-side Microsoft sign-in that has lapsed — nothing is wrong with your phone or your account. RackTrack sends Teams messages and Outlook emails using a Microsoft login cached on the server (a shared MSAL token cache). When that cache is missing or its refresh token has expired, the server tries a silent refresh, fails, and cannot prompt for an interactive login, so every Teams/Outlook share fails until an administrator re-authorises it on a desktop.

The exact wording you will see is:
- Teams: "No valid Teams token. Run `python -m pipeline.teams_send --email X --file Y --interactive` once on a desktop to complete device-flow login and cache a refresh token."
- Outlook: "No valid Outlook token in the shared cache. Run `python -m pipeline.outlook_send --email X --file Y --interactive` once on a desktop to complete device-flow login."
You may also just see "teams send failed" / "outlook send failed", or a message starting "login failed:".

What to do: report it to your RackTrack administrator and quote the message — only they can re-run the one-off device-flow login on the server.

Meanwhile: Teams and Outlook share the same cached login, so if one is broken the other usually is too, but Slack sharing uses a separate sender and normally still works. To get the report out yourself, tap View on the report row, then use the "Download PDF" button at the top of the report — it opens the PDF in your device's browser/viewer where you can save it and attach it to an email or Teams chat manually.
symptoms: No valid Outlook token in the shared cache
entries.rootCause: pipeline/teams_send.py and pipeline/outlook_send.py acquire tokens with MSAL from a SerializableTokenCache on disk (pipeline/shankar_teams_cache.json). Silent refresh is attempted first; with --interactive absent (the server never passes it) a missing/expired cache raises immediately.

entries.question: Is there a single report covering both racks in a two-rack scan?
entries.answer:
Yes — there is a combined report that covers all the racks in a group, though the app doesn't currently have a button that links to it.

It comes as a single HTML document: a cover page reading "RackTrack · Combined report" under the heading "Two-Rack Report" (that heading is fixed text — it still says "Two-Rack Report" even if the group holds more than two racks), followed by the rack count and today's date, plus one pill per rack showing its position, label and rack ID. Each rack's standard scan report then follows, each preceded by a dark "Rack #<n> — <label>" banner that starts on a new page, so your browser's Print → Save as PDF produces a clean multi-rack PDF. There's no ready-made PDF for this one — it's HTML only.

A few things to know:
- You'll need to be signed in, and the group must belong to your Site — otherwise you'll see "Group not found". Any signed-in member of the Site can open it; it isn't restricted to admins.
- A group with no racks in it shows "Group has no racks".
- If one rack's report can't be built, that rack's slot shows "Report unavailable for <rackId>: <reason>" in red and the rest of the document still renders.
entries.rootCause: GET /api/rack-group/:groupId/report loops members, calls buildScanReport per rack, splices each <body> into a shared shell with the first rack's <head>, and returns text/html only. Tenant-checked against data.group.tenant_id.

evidence.snippet:

Two-Rack Report

${members.length} racks · ${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}

entries.short: A combined all-racks report exists (HTML only), though the app doesn't link to it; use Print to PDF for a clean multi-rack file.

entries.question: RackTrack was supposed to post an analysis note to my ServiceNow incident but nothing appeared
entries.answer:
The automated ServiceNow work note ("RackTrack Agent Analysis — auto-generated") is deliberately held back in three situations, all of which happen silently:

1. Low confidence. If the agent isn't confident enough in its analysis (below 0.5), nothing is posted.
2. Nothing changed. RackTrack keeps track of its last conclusion (failure mode, affected device, affected port, confidence, and whether it detected drift). If the new conclusion matches what was already posted for that incident, it won't repeat itself.
3. Rate limited. Even when the conclusion has changed, a new note is held for 24 hours after the last post for that incident.

A ticket that isn't properly linked to a ServiceNow record will report an error rather than silently skipping.

The note itself contains: the one-line incident summary, the confidence figure, the signals used, a numbered reasoning trail with per-step evidence and confidence, a "Suggested action:" block, and "Related incidents in same rack:" — note that this last line only appears on automated batch runs that pass a related-incident list, so a manually forced post never shows it.

An administrator can force a post past the "nothing changed" and rate-limit guards, which clears both the duplicate check and the 24-hour clock for that incident. The confidence threshold still applies. Other things you might see: "No active ServiceNow connection. Add one under Profile → Connections.", "Ticket <INC> not in inbox", a note that the ticket is missing its ServiceNow link and can't be posted, and a message that the analysis couldn't be rebuilt and should be re-run first.
symptoms: no work note on the incident
inbox ticket is missing sys_id — cannot post

POST_RATE_LIMIT_HOURS = 24

...

entries.question: Is there a size limit on the report I email out?
entries.answer:
Yes — only for **Outlook**.

RackTrack renders the rack report to PDF and, for Outlook, base64-encodes that PDF straight into a Microsoft Graph `/me/sendMail` request. Graph caps that whole request at about **4 MB**, and base64 inflates the file by roughly a third, so in practice a report PDF over about **3 MB** will fail to send. The failure surfaces as a `sendMail failed (413 / RequestEntityTooLarge)` style error from the share action.

**Slack and Teams have no such limit.** Slack uploads the file separately via `files.getUploadURLExternal`, and Teams PUTs the file to OneDrive, automatically switching to a chunked upload session for anything over 4 MB. If an Outlook share fails on a photo-heavy scan, re-send it through Slack or Teams.

One caveat about report size: RackTrack does create downscaled copies of scan images (anything over 500 KB is re-encoded to 1400 px wide JPEG), but that only runs when the **HTML** report is generated, not on the share/PDF path. The PDF reuses those shrunk copies only if they already exist — i.e. if the HTML report for that rack has been opened at least once. So a workaround for an oversized Outlook send is to open the rack's HTML report first, then retry the Outlook share.

entries.question: Is the marketplace report a report I can generate from the app?
entries.answer:
No. `docs/features/marketplace-report.md` is an internal design document about the Marketplace feature — its three sell paths, its database tables and its endpoint list — not a report the product generates. It is dated 2026-07-16 and notes that Stripe, eBay and Amazon are env-gated stubs awaiting credentials.

There is no export feature in the Marketplace: `server/marketplace_routes.js` has no CSV, download, XLSX or PDF route anywhere in its ~37 endpoints. So there is no order export, no listing CSV and no downloadable seller statement.

What does exist, and is usually what the customer actually wants, is the **Seller Dashboard** at `/marketplace/dashboard` (`GET /api/marketplace/dashboard`). It shows, for the signed-in user: listing counts (total / active / sold / closed), sales stats (total orders, completed orders, pending orders, and revenue from completed orders), purchase stats (total purchases and amount spent), and the 10 most recent listings. It is on-screen only — there is no download button.

Full route coverage, for reference: listing CRUD, orders and checkout, per-order messaging, saved searches, alerts, partner accounts (eBay/Amazon/Discord), image uploads, partner-search redirect links, listing flag/moderate, the seller dashboard, and env-gated Stripe/eBay/Amazon integration endpoints.

So if a customer asks for "the marketplace report": they either mean this internal document (share the feature notes instead), or they want the Seller Dashboard (point them there), or they want a downloadable order/listing export, which does not exist yet.
entries.rootCause: marketplace-report.md is a Markdown design write-up. Grepping marketplace_routes.js for csv/export/download/xlsx returns only the trailing `module.exports = router;` — there is no export route.

entries.question: What exactly is a connection / data source in RackTrack, and what does "Active" mean?
entries.answer:
A connection — the UI calls them Data Sources — is one saved set of credentials for an external system RackTrack pulls device and ticket data from: ServiceNow/CMDB, NetBox, SolarWinds Orion, CA/DX Spectrum, or your own SQL or REST endpoint.

Where: "Data Sources" in the desktop sidebar (admin only) or Profile → Data Sources. The page explains: "Saved databases this app can pull data from. The active connection is what every screen uses while you're signed in. Switch any time — the data refreshes from the new source."

Two sections: Active (one card with an "Active" badge) and Other saved (each with a "Use" button).

Rules:
1. At most one connection is active at a time — pressing "Use" switches every screen to it and deactivates the previous one without deleting it. The database enforces this with a unique partial index (one is_active=1 row per user). You can also end up with none active.
2. No merging across sources: the active connection is the single source of truth for the session.
3. Saved connections belong to the account that created them; the server scopes every read and write to your user id.

Org-wide credentials are separate — see the "Organization integrations" panel in the Organization Console.
symptoms: What is a data source / connection profile
What does the Active badge mean
Which connection is the app using
Can I use two data sources at once
entries.rootCause: Connection profiles are per-user rows in connection_profiles with a unique partial index allowing one is_active=1 row per user; the Data Sources page renders an Active card and an 'Other saved' list with a Use button that calls the activate route.

A connection — the UI calls them Data Sources — is one saved set of credentials for an external system RackTrack pulls device and ticket data from: ServiceNow/CMDB, NetBox, SolarWinds Orion, CA/DX Spectrum, or your own SQL or REST endpoint.
1. At most one connection is active at a time — pressing "Use" switches every screen to it and deactivates the previous one without deleting it.

entries.question: Which data sources can I connect, and exactly what do I have to type in for each one?
entries.answer:
Six connection types are supported. Picking one in the Type dropdown swaps the form to that type's fields:

• ServiceNow / CMDB — Instance ID (e.g. dev266363), Username, Password. All required. Type only the instance ID, not the full https://…service-now.com URL; the server appends .service-now.com itself.
• NetBox — Base URL (e.g. https://netbox.example.com) and API Token (from your NetBox user profile). Both required.
• SolarWinds Orion — Host (e.g. orion.example.com), Username, Password. All required. NPM / NCM server.
• CA / DX Spectrum — Base URL (e.g. https://spectrum.example.com:8443), Username, Password. All required. OneClick / REST endpoint.
• My own database (SQL) — one Connection string, required. PostgreSQL or MySQL, e.g. postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/dbname.
• My own database (REST) — Base URL (e.g. https://cmdb.example.com/api), required; API Token optional. Must return device / interface JSON.

Anything else is rejected by the server with "unsupported profile type: <type>".
symptoms: What systems can RackTrack connect to
What do I put in the Instance ID field
Do I need an API token for NetBox
Which fields are required for Orion / Spectrum
entries.rootCause: TYPE_INFO in connectionsApi.js defines the label, field schema and hint per type; SUPPORTED_TYPES in connection_profiles.js is the server-side allow-list and validateType rejects anything else.

  'orion',         // SolarWinds Orion / NPM / NCM
  'spectrum',      // CA / DX Spectrum

  'generic_rest',  // user's own DB via REST endpoint

entries.short: Six connection types are supported. Picking one in the Type dropdown swaps the form to that type's fields. ServiceNow / CMDB takes Instance ID, Username and Password, all required — type only the instance ID, not the full https://…service-now.com URL, because the server appends .service-now.com itself.

entries.question: Saving a connection failed with a message like "servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password}" or "name, type, secret are required". What is wrong?
entries.answer:
A required field was left empty, so the server rejected the save. Fill in every field marked * for the type you picked and save again.

What each message means:
- "name, type, secret are required" — the Name box was empty (or nothing was sent at all).
- "servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password}" — Instance ID, Username or Password is blank.
- "netbox profile requires {base_url, token}" — Base URL or API Token is blank.
- "orion profile requires {host, user, password}" — Host, Username or Password is blank.
- "spectrum profile requires {base_url, user, password}" — Base URL, Username or Password is blank.
- "generic_sql profile requires {connection_string}" — Connection string is blank.
- "generic_rest profile requires {base_url}" — Base URL is blank. (Its API Token really is optional.)
- "unsupported profile type: …" — the type isn't one of those six; only happens outside the Data Sources form.

In the Organization Console the check runs in the browser first and reads "Fill in: <field labels>"; spaces alone don't count as filled. On the Data Sources form the browser blocks submit on a new connection while a required field is empty.
entries.rootCause: validateSecret in connection_profiles.js throws a per-type message when a required key is missing; the create route returns 400 'name, type, secret are required' before that; safeAsync maps messages starting with 'unsupported' to 400. OrgConnectionsPanel pre-validates client-side with a 'Fill in:' message.

    if (missing.length) { setFormError(`Fill in: ${missing.map(f => f.label).join(', ')}`); return; }

entries.short: A required field was left empty, so the server rejected the save. Fill in every field marked * for the type you picked and save again. What each message means: - "name, type, secret are required" — the Name box was empty (or nothing was sent at all).

entries.question: I only wanted to change the password on an existing connection, but saving fails with "servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password}". Why?
entries.answer:
The edit form never pre-loads your saved credentials, and as soon as you type in any one credential field it sends all of them — the ones you left blank go up as empty strings. The server merges them over the stored secret, sees a blank Instance ID and Username, and rejects the save. Nothing is lost: validation runs before anything is written, so your saved credentials are still intact.

So an edit has to be one of two things:
- Rename only — leave every credential field blank (the form says "Leave the credential fields blank to keep what's already saved") and change just the Name.
- Replace credentials in full — fill in every starred field. For ServiceNow that is Instance ID, Username and Password together.

Steps: Data Sources → three-dot menu on the connection → Edit → fill in all starred fields → Save changes.
symptoms: Changing just the password fails to save
servicenow profile requires {instance, user, password} when editing
Edit connection error after typing a new password
Save changes rejected on an existing connection
entries.rootCause: ConnectionsPage sends the entire secret object when any field is non-empty (hasSecret check), so untouched fields go up as empty strings; the server's update() merges {...existing.secret, ...secret}, so the empty strings overwrite the stored values and validateSecret then throws the per-type 'requires' error.

entries.short: The edit form never pre-loads your saved credentials, and as soon as you type in any one credential field it sends all of them — the ones you left blank go up as empty strings. The server merges them over the stored secret, sees a blank Instance ID and Username, and rejects the save.

entries.question: Where can I see the password I saved for a connection, and why is the Type dropdown greyed out when I edit?
entries.answer:
Saved credentials can never be read back — not in the UI and not via the API. The connections API returns metadata only (id, name, type, active flag, timestamps); the secret stays encrypted in the database. That's why the credential boxes are blank every time you open "Edit connection" — the code deliberately never pre-loads them ("never preload secrets").

If you've lost a password, RackTrack can't tell you what it was: get it from the source system and type it in again. On edit you only need to fill the field(s) you're actually changing — the new values are merged over the stored ones. Leave every credential box empty and the existing credentials are kept untouched (only the name is updated).

The Type dropdown is disabled while editing ("Type can't change after a connection is created."). To point at a different kind of system, create a new connection of that type — it becomes the active one on save — then delete the old one.
symptoms: Credential fields are empty when editing
Type can't change after a connection is created
How do I recover the credentials I entered
entries.rootCause: The API returns metadata only (rowToMeta has no secret field), openEditForm resets the secret state with the comment 'never preload secrets', and the Type <select> is disabled whenever editingId is set.

evidence.snippet: Credentials for your CMDB/ITSM database, live network sources, etc. Set them once here for the whole organization. They're stored encrypted and are never shown again — not even to you. To change one, just re-enter it.

entries.short: Saved credentials can never be read back — not in the UI and not via the API. The connections API returns metadata only (id, name, type, active flag, timestamps); the secret stays encrypted in the database.

entries.question: How do I test that a connection actually works? I can't find a "Test connection" button.
entries.answer:
There is no Test button — RackTrack has no test endpoint for connection profiles. Saving proves only that the required fields were filled in, never that the host, username or password are correct.

ServiceNow / CMDB is the one type with live verification. When it is the active connection, a "Refresh data from this source" button appears under the Active card. Pressing it runs a real poll against the instance you entered:
• While it runs: "Pulling fresh data from <name>…"
• Success: "✓ Pulled N incidents from <instance>"
• Failure: "Refresh failed: <error from the poller>"
Pressing "Use" on a saved ServiceNow connection starts the same poll automatically. Note that saving a brand-new one with "Save & use" does NOT — it is made active, but nothing is contacted until you press the refresh button.

Every other type (NetBox, SolarWinds Orion, CA/DX Spectrum, own SQL, own REST): no refresh button, nothing contacted at save time — the credentials are just stored encrypted. Confirm them by opening a screen that reads from that source and seeing whether data appears.
symptoms: How do I know the credentials are right
Connection saved but no data appears
entries.rootCause: There is no test route in connection_profiles_routes.js; the only live verification is the ServiceNow poll, and ConnectionsPage renders the 'Refresh data from this source' button only when active.type === 'servicenow'. lastRefresh drives the success/failure banners.

evidence.snippet:
* Routes:
 *   GET    /api/connections              → list metadata for this user
 *   GET    /api/connections/active       → metadata for the active profile
 *   POST   /api/connections              → create {name, type, secret, make_active?}
 *   GET    /api/connections/:id          → metadata for one profile
 *   PATCH  /api/connections/:id          → update {name?, secret?}
 *   POST   /api/connections/:id/activate → make this profile active
 *   POST   /api/connections/deactivate   → clear active (no source for this user)
 *   DELETE /api/connections/:id          → delete one profile

entries.short: There is no Test button — RackTrack has no test endpoint for connection profiles. Saving proves only that the required fields were filled in, never that the host, username or password are correct. ServiceNow / CMDB is the one type with live verification.

entries.question: What is the "Organization integrations" panel, and how is it different from my personal Data Sources?
entries.answer:
"Organization integrations" is where an org admin sets the credentials the WHOLE organization uses, so every member's scans read from the same CMDB without anyone entering credentials on their own account.

Where: Organization Console → "Organization integrations" section. Org admins only — the platform owner does not see it (an owner account has no organization context).

To add one: press "+ Add integration", choose the Integration type (the same six types as personal Data Sources), optionally type a Label (blank = the type's name), fill the fields marked *, then press "Save (encrypted)".

Each one then shows as a row reading "● Configured · encrypted" with a "Remove" button. Secrets are never displayed again and there is no edit — to change a credential you re-add it.

Precedence: for ServiceNow the organization's credential wins; the server falls back to the signed-in user's personal connection only if the org has none. Personal Data Sources stay private to the account that created them.
symptoms: Where do I set credentials for the whole organization
entries.rootCause: OrgConnectionsPanel is rendered in OrgConsolePage only when the viewer is not the platform owner; it posts to /api/org-connections, which is gated to org_admin/owner and requires an organization_id. getSnCreds prefers resolveCredsForOrg over the personal profile.

entries.question: I re-entered our CMDB credentials in Organization integrations and now the same integration is listed twice. Which one is being used?
entries.answer:
The newest one is being used. Nothing was overwritten: pressing "+ Add integration" for a type you already have marks the previous credential of that type inactive and inserts a new active one, and the panel lists every stored row — each showing "● Configured · encrypted" whether or not it is live.

Which row is which: the list is sorted active-first, so within a type the top row is the one in use.

Fix: press "Remove" on the lower, stale row and confirm ("Remove the <type> integration for this organization?"). That deletes only that row and does not affect the active one.

Two rows of *different* types is normal — an organization can hold one active credential per type at once, for example a live ServiceNow and a live SQL source together.

entries.question: Saving an organization integration returns "organization admin only" or "no organization is associated with your account". What now?
entries.answer:
These are two different refusals, and they apply no matter which device or app you're using.

• "organization admin only" — your role isn't organization admin (or owner). Members and site managers can't set organization-wide credentials. Ask your organization admin; they set it once and every member's scans use it.

• "no organization is associated with your account" — your role was fine, but your account isn't tied to any organization. This is the platform-owner case: an owner sits above organizations and belongs to none. Use an organization-admin account inside the organization you want to configure. It's also why the "Organization integrations" panel is hidden for the owner.
symptoms: no organization is associated with your account
entries.rootCause: requireOrgAdmin in connection_profiles_routes.js returns 403 for roles outside org_admin/owner and 400 when req.user.organization_id is missing, which is the platform owner's case; OrgConsolePage hides the panel for owners.
entries.short: Two refusals: you're not an organization admin, or your account isn't tied to any organization (the platform-owner case).

entries.question: How do I stop using a data source, or delete one? Is there an off switch?
entries.answer:
No off switch — the Data Sources screen only offers switch or delete.

Switch: press "Use" on another saved connection. The previous one stops being active immediately and stays saved.

Delete: tap the ⋯ menu on the card → "Delete" → confirm `Delete connection "<name>"?`. This is permanent; the stored credentials live in the same row and are destroyed with it, so you would have to re-enter them.

If you delete the active connection and have no other, the screen shows "No active connection." with the hint "Add a connection below to start pulling data from your CMDB", and CMDB-backed screens return nothing until you add one.

(Organization-wide credentials use the "Remove" button in Organization integrations instead.)
symptoms: How do I disconnect a data source
How do I turn off a connection without deleting it
entries.rootCause: ConnectionsPage exposes only Edit and Delete in the card menu plus the Use button; the /api/connections/deactivate route exists but no control on the page calls it, and remove() deletes the row (secret blob included).

evidence.snippet:

entries.question: INTERNAL: how are connection-profile credentials stored, and what may I say about it to a customer?
entries.answer:
INTERNAL — storage model (do not paste to customers):
• Connection-profile credentials (personal and org-wide) are serialised to JSON and sealed with AES-256-GCM before they reach the database. The row stores base64(iv|tag|ciphertext) in connection_profiles.secret_blob. Only user_id, name, type, is_active, organization_id and timestamps are in cleartext.
• Key: 32 bytes as 64 hex chars, from SSH_CREDS_KEY if set, else server/.env.key (generated 0600 on first run). Same key as the SSH credential store — one rotation surface.
• Decryption happens only inside the server process, in resolveCredsForOrg / resolveCredsForType, at the moment an outbound call is made. Nothing decrypts on the client.
• No route returns plaintext. Create, update, list, get and activate all reply through rowToMeta/orgRowToMeta — metadata only, including for the admin who set an org credential.

Handling rules:
• Never read out, copy, screenshot, relay or "confirm" a stored secret — to anyone, including the account owner or an org admin. There is no supported way to retrieve one; do not invent one.
• Never ask a customer to send a password, token or connection string in a ticket. If a credential must change, they re-enter it themselves in the app.
• Do not discuss key file paths, env var names or database column names with customers.

Safe customer-facing phrasing: "Your credentials are encrypted before they're stored and are never shown again — not even to you. To change one, just re-enter it."
symptoms: Customer asks us to retrieve their stored password
entries.rootCause: connection_profiles.js encrypts the secret JSON with the shared AES-256-GCM helper from ssh-creds.js and persists only the blob; all HTTP responses go through rowToMeta/orgRowToMeta, which omit secret_blob.

evidence.snippet:
* One row per saved connection. The actual credentials (instance URL,
 * username, password, API tokens, optional vendor-specific extras) live
 * in an AES-256-GCM blob; only metadata (name, type, created_at, etc.)
 * is queryable in cleartext.
...
 * Encryption key is shared with the SSH creds store — same AES key file
 * (server/.env.key) or SSH_CREDS_KEY env var. One key, one rotation
 * surface.

entries.short: INTERNAL — storage model (do not paste to customers): • Connection-profile credentials (personal and org-wide) are serialised to JSON and sealed with AES-256-GCM before they reach the database. secret_blob. Only user_id, name, type, is_active, organization_id and timestamps are in cleartext.

entries.question: INTERNAL: every connection suddenly stopped working after a server change and the log shows decrypt failures. What happened?
entries.answer:
The AES key no longer matches the stored blobs. Both stores (connection profiles and SSH creds) share one key: SSH_CREDS_KEY env var, else server/.env.key.

What you see:
• "[connection_profiles] decrypt failed for profile <id>" or "[connection_profiles] org decrypt failed for profile <id>" — the profile resolves to null, so CMDB endpoints act as if nothing is configured.
• "[ssh-creds] decrypt failed — ignoring env creds" — credentials become {}, so polls are skipped and audits return the no-credentials error.
• Profiles still LIST fine (name, type, Active badge are cleartext) — only the blob fails, so it looks like "the app forgot our password", not an outage.

Causes:
1. .env.key not carried across a redeploy. On next start connection_profiles.loadKey writes a brand-new key and logs "[connection_profiles] generated new encryption key at .env.key" — grep the log for that line, it dates the breakage exactly.
2. SSH_CREDS_KEY set to a different key — the env var wins over the file, so an intact .env.key on disk will not save you.
3. Key file truncated/reformatted — must be exactly 64 hex chars, else the loader throws "<path> must contain a 32-byte hex key (64 chars)".

Recovery: restore the original key (file or env var) from backup BEFORE restarting again, then restart. The blobs are intact; nothing else is needed. If the key is truly lost the secrets are unrecoverable by design — profiles must be re-entered by their owners/org admins in the app, switch credentials re-entered on the server via encrypt-creds.js. Never collect credentials over a support channel.
symptoms: must contain a 32-byte hex key (64 chars)
All connections stopped working after redeploy
Connections still listed but no data pulled
entries.rootCause: Both stores decrypt with a key resolved from SSH_CREDS_KEY or server/.env.key; a missing/replaced key makes decrypt throw, and the code logs and degrades to null/empty credentials rather than failing loudly. connection_profiles.loadKey auto-generates a fresh key when the file is absent, permanently orphaning existing blobs.
entries.short: The AES key no longer matches the stored blobs. Both stores — connection profiles and SSH credentials — share one key: the SSH_CREDS_KEY environment variable, else server/.env.key. The usual causes are a key that was not carried across a redeploy, or a key file that was truncated or reformatted; it must be exactly 64 hex characters.

entries.question: INTERNAL: is "only admins can manage connections" a real security boundary?
entries.answer:
Partly — and the distinction matters on a security questionnaire.

• Server-enforced: organization-wide credentials. `/api/org-connections/*` is mounted with `requireAuth, requireOrgAdmin` (server/connection_profiles_routes.js:123). requireOrgAdmin 403s anything outside org_admin/owner, 400s if the user has no organization_id, and pins req._orgId; every org query is scoped `WHERE organization_id = ?`.

• NOT server-enforced: the "admins only" part of personal profiles. `/api/connections/*` is mounted with `requireAuth` alone (line 37) — no role check. Any authenticated user, member included, can create/list/update/activate/delete their own profiles via the API. The admin gate is purely client-side: AdminRoute on the /connections route (App.jsx:77-90, 269) plus isAdmin conditionals on the sidebar link (DesktopShell.jsx:197,210) and the Profile page row. UI affordance, not authorization.

• Cross-tenant exposure is real-enforced either way: every personal query filters `WHERE user_id = ?`, so no user can read another's profile or secret.

• No fallback: resolveCredsForType / resolveCredsForOrg return null when there is no matching active profile (connection_profiles.js:347-360, 467-471) — no env or file fallback, so a missing profile degrades to "no data", never to someone else's credentials.

Short version: cross-tenant credential isolation is server-enforced; "only admins can manage connections" is a screen, not a control. A technician can't reach the UI, but nothing in the API stops them storing their own profile.
symptoms: Security review question about connection permissions
Can a member create a connection profile
entries.rootCause: router.use('/api/connections', requireAuth) has no role check and all queries filter by user_id, while /api/org-connections adds requireOrgAdmin; the admin gate on the /connections page comes from AdminRoute and DesktopShell's isAdmin conditional.
entries.short: Partly — and the distinction matters on a security questionnaire. Organization-wide credentials are server-enforced: `/api/org-connections/*` is mounted with `requireAuth, requireOrgAdmin`. The "admins only" part of personal profiles is not: `/api/connections/*` is mounted with `requireAuth` alone, so the admin gate there is a UI affordance, not authorization.

entries.question: Does RackTrack show me CVEs or security advisories for my switch?
entries.answer:
No. RackTrack shows no CVEs, severity badges or vulnerability counts anywhere — CVE reporting was removed from the product, and the server deliberately ignores the advisory rows the lookup agent still carries.

The closest thing: on the Firmware screen, after a check, tap "Show details" and read "Release notes excerpts". If the vendor's notes for the newer release mentioned security fixes, they appear as a "Security fixes in <version>" block, next to Bug fixes, New features, Known issues and Deprecations.

For a real vulnerability assessment use your vendor's advisory page or your own security tooling. RackTrack answers "is there newer firmware and what changed", not "am I vulnerable".
entries.rootCause: server/app.js maps the agent's FirmwareAdvice onto the /api/firmware contract and explicitly skips advice.advisories; the only security-flavoured output is the target release's security_fixes list rendered as a changelog section.
entries.short: No. RackTrack shows no CVEs, severity badges or vulnerability counts anywhere — CVE reporting was removed from the product, and RackTrack deliberately ignores the advisory rows the lookup agent still carries.

entries.question: Where is the "Firmware Check" screen? I can't find it in the menu.
entries.answer:
There is no menu entry for it — /firmware is a URL-only route. The sidebar has Home, Scan, Two racks, Profile (plus Console/Lab for the platform owner and Data Sources/Marketplace for admins), and the phone bottom bar only has HOME, SCAN, PROFILE.

Use the switch card instead: open the rack, click Switches in the sidebar, pick your switch, and open its Firmware tab (next to Specifications and SFP Advisor). The version is filled in for you from the scan or the CMDB.

If you want the standalone page anyway, type /firmware onto the end of the app address. You will have to type Make / Vendor, Model and Current version by hand — it knows nothing about your rack. Either way you must be signed in.

entries.question: The Firmware tab says "No firmware version recorded" or "Add a model to check for updates" — why won't it check?
entries.answer:
The check needs all three of vendor, model and version. It never calls the server until it has them (the endpoint itself rejects a missing one with "vendor, model, and currentVersion are required").

1. "Add a model to check for updates." — use "Enter make / model" (or "Add model" / "Add vendor") at the top of the card.
2. "No firmware version recorded." — tap "Enter version", type what the switch is running (e.g. 1.0.6 Build 20210323), Save. The check starts straight away: "Checking for updates…".
3. If you save a version and nothing happens, the vendor is what's missing, not the version. Fill the vendor in at the top of the card and it will run.

Use "Edit version" next to the Firmware heading to change it later. Anything you type here is stored in this browser only.
symptoms: Add a model to check for updates
entries.rootCause: loadDetails() sets firmwareStatus='skipped' unless displayVendor and lookupModel resolve, and again unless a cleaned version exists; POST /api/firmware itself 400s with 'vendor, model, and currentVersion are required'.

evidence.snippet:
<StatusLine color={statusColor}>No firmware version recorded.</StatusLine>
...
        >Enter version</button>

entries.short: The check needs all three of vendor, model and version. It never calls the server until it has them (the endpoint itself rejects a missing one with "vendor, model, and currentVersion are required").

entries.question: The check worked but "Release notes excerpts" shows 0 and says it couldn't extract anything. Is that a bug?
entries.answer:
No, that's expected. We got a version number for your device but no written-out release notes to break into sections, which is normal for most vendors — the long-tail lookup only returns a version pointer and never invents bullet points.

Under "Show details", the number next to "Release notes excerpts" is how many blocks we found. "Couldn't fetch release notes: …" means the vendor page couldn't be read at all; "Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page." means we had nothing to split up. Either way, use "Search release notes ↗" or "Open page ↗" just below to read the vendor's page yourself.

When excerpts do exist they appear as Security fixes, Bug fixes, New features, Known issues and Deprecations, each labelled with the newer version.
symptoms: Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page
entries.rootCause: changelog[] is synthesized only from the target release's security_fixes/bug_fixes/new_features/known_issues/deprecations arrays; when those are empty (the usual case for the live 'pointer tier' lookup, which never synthesizes bullets) the section falls back to the empty state plus search links.

evidence.snippet: Release notes excerpts {result.changelog?.length || 0} ... {result.releaseNotesError ? `Couldn't fetch release notes: ${result.releaseNotesError}` : "Couldn't extract any changelog sections from the page."}

Search release notes ↗
...
                              Open page ↗

Returns a *version pointer* (version, optional release_date, notes_url).
Bullet-level diff (security/features/bugs) is **not** synthesized — that
requires either a hand-built per-vendor fetcher (Cumulus / MikroTik) or
an LLM, and we have neither for the long tail. Honest by design.

entries.short: No, that's expected. We got a version number for your device but no written-out release notes to break into sections, which is normal for most vendors — the long-tail lookup only returns a version pointer and never invents bullet points.

entries.question: The Firmware Check screen says "Vendor list unavailable: …" under the Make / Vendor box.
entries.answer:
Only the vendor type-ahead failed to load. The firmware check itself is unaffected — the vendor you type is sent as-is and never checked against that list.

1. Type the vendor as the manufacturer writes it (Cisco, Juniper, Aruba).
2. Fill in Model and Current version — all three fields are required — and tap "Check firmware".
3. To get the list back, reload the screen; it is fetched once on open.
4. If it fails for everyone it is server-side, not your phone. "Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment." means the vendor-sheet lookup on the server hit its 90-second limit. Report the exact text after "Vendor list unavailable:".
symptoms: Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment.
entries.rootCause: FirmwarePage fetches /api/specs/vendors once on mount; that endpoint shells out to pipeline.all_vendor --list-vendors, which reads Switch_Vendors_Websites.xlsx and is killed after PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS (90s). Failure only disables the suggestion list.
entries.short:
Only the vendor type-ahead failed to load.
1. Type the vendor as the manufacturer writes it (Cisco, Juniper, Aruba).
2. Fill in Model and Current version — all three fields are required — and tap "Check firmware".
3. To get the list back, reload the screen; it is fetched once on open.

entries.question: The Switch Info pop-up has its own "Firmware Update" card — is that different from the Firmware tab on the switch card?
entries.answer:
Same lookup, different source for the current version.

The "Firmware Update" card in the Switch Info pop-up (header: "Switch Info · live · <host> · <vendor>") reads the version live off the switch over SSH — it pulls "Firmware Version" / "Software Version" out of the device's system output, trims it ("5.0.2 Build 20220909 Rel.75392" → "5.0.2") and then runs the same vendor check as the switch card.

Only the wording differs: "Up to date", "Upgrade available", or "Could not determine latest version", with Current version / Latest version rows and a "Release notes" link. While it runs: "Checking vendor site for newer firmware…". If the SSH read gave no model or version: "Need both model and firmware version to check for updates." If the lookup failed: "Could not check: …".

The Firmware tab on the switch card uses whatever the scan/CMDB recorded or what you typed — it never talks to the switch. So if the two disagree, the pop-up is the one showing what's actually running.
symptoms: Checking vendor site for newer firmware
Need both model and firmware version to check for updates
entries.rootCause: ResultsPage's SwitchInfoModal parses firmware from the live SSH system-info output, runs cleanFirmwareVersion() on it and calls the same POST /api/firmware; it renders its own headline set independent of SwitchInformationPage's fwHeadline.

Firmware Update

...

Checking vendor site for newer firmware…

... firmware.upToDate === true ? 'Up to date' : firmware.upToDate === false ? 'Upgrade available' : 'Could not determine latest version'; ...

Need both model and firmware version to check for updates.

hwVersion:  get(/Hardware Version\s*[-:]\s*(.+)/i),
    fwVersion:  get(/(?:Firmware|Software) Version\s*[-:]\s*(.+)/i),

entries.short: Same lookup, different source for the current version. The "Firmware Update" card in the Switch Info pop-up reads the version live off the switch over SSH, trims it, and then runs the same vendor check as the switch card. Only the wording differs: "Up to date", "Upgrade available", or "Could not determine latest version".

entries.question: How current is the firmware data, and how often does it refresh?
entries.answer:
There's no automatic refresh — nothing on our side is scheduled to update firmware data.

• The "Latest version" we show comes from a local cache that's only filled when someone runs the firmware fetcher by hand. There's no scheduled job, timer or startup task that runs it automatically.
• We have dedicated public fetchers for exactly three vendors: MikroTik (RouterOS), Ubiquiti (UniFi OS) and NVIDIA (Cumulus Linux). Every other vendor falls back to a best-effort live web lookup with about an 8.5-second deadline, and that result is saved into the same cache.
• In the app, each firmware result is kept in memory for the session (by rack, vendor, model and version) with no expiry. Reload the tab to force a fresh check.

So a firmware answer is only as current as the last manual fetcher run — or, for vendors without a dedicated fetcher, the last live lookup that succeeded.
symptoms: how old is the firmware data
entries.rootCause: Firmware/advisory ingestion is a manually-invoked script (Agent_scrap/scripts/fetch_firmware.py); server/app.js has no scheduler for it, and the client cache in scanPrefetch.js is a module-level Map with no TTL.

evidence.snippet:
python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py                 # all public vendors
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py mikrotik        # one vendor
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py mikrotik -v     # verbose
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py nvd             # CVE data from NIST NVD
    python3 scripts/fetch_firmware.py kev             # CISA actively-exploited overlay

entries.short: Firmware data never auto-refreshes; it's only as current as the last manual fetcher run, or a successful live lookup for other vendors.

entries.question: A switch shows "Upgrade available" but the Latest version we display is the same age or older than what the customer is running. Why?
entries.answer:
The badge means "different from our cached value", not "you're behind" — there's no version comparison anywhere in the process.

We work it out by an exact text match: if our cached "latest" version isn't character-for-character identical to what the customer is running, we show "Upgrade available". Anything not byte-identical — 16.12.1 vs 16.12.01, a trailing build suffix, or different capitalization — counts as different, and the badge appears.

It can also show up when our cached "latest" is actually older than the customer's version. When there's no changelog difference to report, the system falls back to the cached vendor-level latest version and still flags it, so a stale or wrong cached value can surface as a false "Upgrade available".

Handling: read the two version strings back to the customer, explain the badge is a cache mismatch, and point them at the release notes / vendor link. Don't tell them they're behind.
symptoms: says upgrade but we are newer
entries.rootCause: firmwarePayloadFromAgent computes upToDate by exact trimmed string equality; the agent's _synthetic_diff_from_latest returns the cached vendor-level latest unconditionally with releases_behind=0.

evidence.snippet:
def _synthetic_diff_from_latest(latest_rec: FirmwareRecord) -> Optional[FirmwareDiff]:
        # Surface the cached latest unconditionally — the advisor's job is
        # to tell the user what we know, not to silently drop data when
        # their current is newer than our cached pointer. If current ≥
        # latest, releases_behind stays 0 ...
            releases_behind=0,

entries.short: 'Upgrade available' just means our cached latest version differs from yours by exact text — it isn't a real behind-check.

entries.question: Which vendors do we actually have firmware data for, and what does a customer see for the rest?
entries.answer:
Three tiers, and it's about whether we can reach a vendor's data, not a supported-device list.

1. Real changelogs — only MikroTik (RouterOS), Ubiquiti (UniFi OS) and NVIDIA (Cumulus Linux). These are the only vendors with a working public fetcher.

2. Login-gated — Cisco, Juniper, Arista, HPE Aruba, Dell, Fortinet, plus a further gated list (Huawei, H3C, Lenovo, Tejas, ZTE, NEC, Fujitsu, ALE, RUCKUS, Extreme, Ciena, Nokia). Full release notes need a vendor login, but we still return NVD CVE data and a portal link. The card shows "Recommended min: X" if we know a fix version, otherwise "Check vendor portal" with a "Vendor portal ↗" link.

3. Everything else — a best-effort live web lookup (about an 8.5-second deadline) that gives a latest-version pointer only, never a changelog. If it comes up empty, you'll see "No firmware data available for <vendor>" (or "No NOS specified and no default known for <vendor>") and the card reads "Latest version unknown".
symptoms: No NOS specified and no default known for
which vendors are supported for firmware
