entries.short: Full changelogs only for MikroTik, Ubiquiti and NVIDIA; login-gated vendors get CVE data plus a portal link; everything else is best-effort.

entries.question: How much can we trust the "Latest version" values the shipped agent database returns?
entries.answer:
Very little — treat the shipped cache as demo-grade, not authoritative. Never quote it to a customer as a firmware recommendation.

The `firmware_versions` table in `Agent/Agent_scrap/data/switches.db` holds 16 rows, all written by the generic `firmware_fetchers` scrape, and several are plainly mis-scraped: HPE Aruba is stored as version "802.3af" (a PoE standard) with a picclick.com listing as its release-notes link; Cisco as "16.2" pointing at a Nexus 9336C-FX2 model page; MikroTik as "25.6196C16"; Netgear as "36.75ZM17". Every row also has `nos` set to the vendor name rather than a real network OS, and `release_date` is null on all but one.

Why: the fetcher regex-matches any version-like token on a search-result page and upserts it with no validation against the real vendor NOS (`live_firmware.py:29`).

Consequence: lookup is by vendor alone (`firmware.py:192 vendor_latest_any`), so any customer on one of those 16 vendors gets a bogus "Latest", a false "Upgrade available" (`server/app.js:7265` — plain string comparison), and a junk "Release notes" link. Fix is to re-run the fetchers or curate the rows; there is no in-app override.
symptoms: release notes link goes to picclick
entries.rootCause: The generic live/pointer fetcher regex-matches any 'version-like' token on a search-result page and upserts it into firmware_versions with source='firmware_fetchers'; nothing validates the match against the real vendor NOS, and the shipped DB was populated from those runs.

HPE Aruba Networking|HPE Aruba Networking|802.3af|https://picclick.com/Computers-Tablets-Networking/...
Cisco|Cisco|16.2|https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/nexus-9336c-fx2-switch/model.html
MikroTik|MikroTik|25.6196C16|https://mikrotik.com/product/CRS326-24G-2SplusRM

# "v1.2.3" / "Version 5.10.1" / "Firmware: 7.18.2" / "Release 22.4R3"
_VERSION_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:version|firmware|release|build|software|nos|os|v)\s*[:\-]?\s*"
    r"v?(\d+(?:\.\d+){1,3}[A-Za-z0-9\-]*)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

entries.short: Very little — treat the shipped cache as demo-grade, not authoritative, and never quote it to a customer as a firmware recommendation. The fetcher regex-matches any version-like token on a search-result page and upserts it with no validation against the real vendor NOS.

entries.question: "Couldn't check for updates right now" — what actually failed on the server?
entries.answer:
POST /api/firmware shells out to the Python agent CLI (Agent/Agent_scrap/cli.py) and collapses every failure into {ok:false, error} served with HTTP 404 (server/app.js:7230-7237). The switch card shows one generic line for all of them (SwitchInformationPage.jsx:786); the Firmware Check page prints the raw string in its red banner (FirmwarePage.jsx:108). Read that string:

- "agent not installed at Agent/Agent_scrap" — cli.py missing; the agent is cloned separately, not part of this checkout (app.js:7326, 7339).
- "Agent lookup took too long." — exceeded AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 and was SIGKILLed (app.js:7334, 7348).
- "Agent failed to start." — spawn error: wrong pythonCmd / missing interpreter (app.js:7355).
- "Agent returned no parsable JSON." — last stdout line wasn't JSON; last 500 chars of stderr attach as _stderr for the server log only (app.js:7363).
- "Agent failed to return a firmware response." — agent replied but with no usable advice object (app.js:7258).

Not agent failures: HTTP 400 "vendor, model, and currentVersion are required" is a missing-field pre-flight; "Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP …)" and "Request failed: … Is the backend running on port 3001?" are client-side network errors (FirmwarePage.jsx:104, 114).
symptoms: Couldn't check for updates right now
Is the backend running on port 3001
entries.rootCause: runAgentCli() resolves a small set of fixed error strings; firmwarePayloadFromAgent passes them through as payload.error and the route replies 404 when ok is false. SwitchInformationPage collapses all of them to one generic status line; FirmwarePage prints the raw string.

entries.question: Is pipeline/firmware_overrides.json still used for the "latest known firmware" values?
entries.answer:
No — it is dead data. Nothing in the repo reads it.

Its own header (pipeline/firmware_overrides.json:2) claims it is "consulted before web scraping in pipeline.firmware_check" and is "the authoritative source for the 'latest known firmware' badge", but no pipeline/firmware_check.py exists and a repo-wide grep for `firmware_overrides` returns only the file itself.

The real path is server/app.js:7204 (POST /api/firmware) → runAgentCli(['--firmware', '<vendor> <model>', currentVersion]) at app.js:7229, which hits the Agent_scrap SQLite DB (app.js:7322).

So editing rows there — e.g. the Cisco C9300 "17.15.3" / lastChecked 2026-05-08 entry — changes nothing a customer sees. To fix a wrong "Latest" value, update the agent's DB; this file should be wired in or deleted.
symptoms: I updated firmware_overrides.json and nothing changed
where do the latest firmware numbers come from
entries.rootCause: pipeline/firmware_overrides.json documents an integration with pipeline.firmware_check that does not exist in this repo; the live firmware path is server/app.js → runAgentCli('--firmware') → Agent/Agent_scrap.

Vendor sites block our scraper (Cisco/Aruba/Arista return 403, Dell pages are PDFs/JS-rendered) so this file is the authoritative source for the 'latest known firmware' badge."

    ['--firmware', `${vendor} ${firmwareModel}`, currentVersion]);

entries.question: Are the firmware and vendor lookup endpoints authenticated?
entries.answer:
No. In server/app.js, GET /api/specs/vendors (7012), POST /api/specs (7023) and POST /api/firmware (7204) are all registered with no auth.requireAuth — unlike neighbouring routes such as GET /api/cmdb/rack/:rackId/switches (5114). The client sends a token via authFetch, but the server never checks it.

Each call also spawns a Python child process: /api/firmware goes through runAgentCli (AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000, line 7334), /api/specs/vendors through runPipelineModule (PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000, line 6964). The only rate limiter in the file, uploadLimiter (line 38), is applied to scan/detect/auth only (474, 481, 492) — never to these routes. So an unauthenticated caller can hold open long-lived Python processes and drive outbound web scraping from our host.

Internal only — do not mention to customers. Hardening item: add requireAuth plus a rate limit before any public exposure of the API host.
entries.rootCause: The spec/firmware routes were added without the auth.requireAuth middleware used elsewhere in app.js, while each handler shells out to a Python child process with a 60-90 second wall-clock budget and no throttling.

const PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000;

function runPipelineModule(moduleName, extraArgs) {

entries.question: What can the help assistant answer, and what will it not answer?
entries.answer:
Ask in your own words about using RackTrack — signing in, scanning, reports, sync. Messages are capped at 1000 characters.

Three kinds of question it declines outright, before it even searches:
• Future releases, ETAs or roadmap — it only knows RackTrack as it works today, and points you to your administrator to raise a feature request.
• Pricing, licensing or billing — it points you to your administrator or account manager.
• Comparisons with other products — it says it has no reliable information about them and offers to answer RackTrack questions instead.

These are not gaps that will be filled later: the knowledge base is built from the product's source code, so it can only describe how RackTrack behaves now.
symptoms: Can I ask the assistant when a feature is coming?
The assistant says it only covers how to use RackTrack
Asked about price and got redirected to my administrator
entries.rootCause: detectOutOfScope() matches roadmap, commercial and comparison intents before retrieval runs and returns a fixed reply on route 'out-of-scope', because the knowledge base is mined from source code and can only describe current behaviour.

evidence.snippet:
function detectOutOfScope(text) {
...
      kind: 'roadmap',
      reply:
        "I can only tell you how RackTrack works today - I don't have anything about future plans or release timing. " +
        'Your RackTrack administrator can raise a feature request with the product team.',

kind: 'commercial',
      reply:
        "I only cover how to use RackTrack, so I don't have anything on pricing or billing. " +
        'Your RackTrack administrator or account manager can help with that.',
...
      kind: 'comparison',
      reply:
        "I can explain what RackTrack does, but I can't compare it to other products - I don't have reliable information about them. "
What are you stuck on? Ask in your own words. If I don't know something for certain, I'll say so rather than guess.

if (message.length > MAX_QUESTION_CHARS) {
      return res.status(413).json({ error: `message must be under ${MAX_QUESTION_CHARS} characters` });

entries.short: Ask in your own words about using RackTrack — signing in, scanning, reports, sync. Messages are capped at 1000 characters.

entries.question: The assistant said "I don't have reliable information about that." Is it broken?
entries.answer:
No — that is deliberate. When nothing in the verified knowledge base clears the bot's matching thresholds, it declines instead of guessing and sending you the wrong way. Declines are styled differently so you never mistake one for advice.

1. Re-ask using the exact on-screen error text or screen name — unfamiliar words are what trigger the decline.
2. If it still declines, tap "Reach a person" under the reply for how to escalate.
symptoms: I don't have reliable information about that. I'd rather not guess and send you the wrong way.
The assistant refuses to answer my question
The bot says it doesn't know
entries.rootCause: ask() applies four independent gates (confidence, coverage, absolute score, and the fraction of query words absent from the whole corpus). If any gate fails it returns route 'refusal' with a fixed message rather than the best weak match.

evidence.snippet:
*   verbatim  — search is confident; return the verified answer word for word.
 *               Generates nothing, so it cannot hallucinate.
...
 *   refusal   — nothing relevant matched. Say so. Never guess.

1. Re-ask using the exact on-screen error text or screen name — unfamiliar words are what trigger the decline.
2. If it still declines, tap "Reach a person" under the reply for how to escalate.

entries.question: The assistant can't help me. How do I reach a real person?
entries.answer:
Email the RackTrack support team at support@racktrack.ai. Include what you were doing when it happened and the exact error text (or a screenshot) so they can help without going back and forth.

You can also tap "Reach a person" next to "Still stuck?" under any assistant reply that declines — it points you to the same support inbox.

entries.question: I pasted my password into the help chat by mistake — what now?
entries.answer:
Change that secret now. The assistant stops and warns instead of answering, because the message was already sent and may be stored in the conversation.

1. Change the password, key or token immediately.
2. Re-describe the problem without it and the assistant will help.

Never paste passwords, API keys, session tokens or SNMP community strings into the help chat — it never needs them. (Just mentioning a password, e.g. "my password is wrong", is fine and answers normally.)
symptoms: Before anything else: it looks like you included your password in that message.
The assistant refused to answer and told me to change my password
I shared an API key in the support chat
entries.rootCause: detectCredential() runs before anything else in ask() and matches volunteered secrets (password/passphrase, API key or token, SNMP community string, and unambiguous token shapes), returning route 'credential-guard' instead of an answer.

Change that secret now.

2. Re-describe the problem without it and the assistant will help.

entries.question: INTERNAL: What is the support assistant's API surface?
entries.answer:
Two routes, both behind auth.requireAuth (mounted at root, so paths are literal):
• POST /api/support/ask — body {message, history}; returns {answer, detail, sources, route, ms}. `matches`/`warnings` stay server-side (entry ids, internal state). History is trimmed to the last 6 well-formed turns of 1000 chars.
• GET /api/support/status — {ok, tier, entries, mode} where mode is 'search+model' or 'search-only'.

Errors: 400 missing message, 413 over 1000 chars, 429 rate-limited (ask only — token bucket rate 1/min, burst 10, per user id), 503 KB unavailable (both routes). Tier comes from bot.tierForRole(req.user.role), never the body.
symptoms: Which endpoints does the support bot expose?
Can a client request a higher knowledge tier?
entries.rootCause: support_routes.js mounts both routes under a requireAuth guard, resolves the knowledge tier with bot.tierForRole(req.user?.role), sanitises history to at most 6 well-formed turns of 1000 chars each, and rate-limits ask with uploadLimiter({ rate: 1, burst: 10 }) keyed per user.

• GET /api/support/status — {ok, tier, entries, mode} where mode is 'search+model' or 'search-only'.

Errors: 400 missing message, 413 over 1000 chars, 429 rate-limited (ask only — token bucket rate 1/min, burst 10, per user id), 503 KB unavailable (both routes). Tier comes from bot.tierForRole(req.user.role), never the body.

entries.question: INTERNAL: The help launcher has disappeared for everyone, or /api/support returns 503.
entries.answer:
The knowledge base failed to load at boot. Every /api/support route then returns 503 with a `reason` field explaining what failed, and since the client only mounts the launcher when GET /api/support/status returns ok, no help button appears. The rest of RackTrack keeps serving.

1. Check the boot log for "[support] disabled" (or read `reason` from any 503).
2. Restore a valid JSON KB at SUPPORT_KB_PATH (default server/data/support-kb.json) — a missing file and malformed JSON both fail the same way.
3. Restart the server; the KB is loaded once at module load, so it will not recover on its own.
symptoms: Support assistant is unavailable right now. Please contact your administrator.
No help button appears for any user
entries.rootCause: bot.warmup() runs once at module load; if the KB file is missing or malformed the error is captured into kbError, kbReady stays false, and a guard middleware short-circuits every /api/support request with 503. The client only mounts its launcher when GET /api/support/status returns ok.

evidence.snippet: const KB_PATH = process.env.SUPPORT_KB_PATH || path.join(__dirname, '..', 'data', 'support-kb.json');
if (!available) return null;

entries.short: The knowledge base failed to load at boot. Every /api/support route then returns 503 with a `reason` field explaining what failed, and since the client only mounts the launcher when GET /api/support/status returns ok, no help button appears. The rest of RackTrack keeps serving.

entries.question: How do I find a specific part in the Marketplace? My search isn't finding anything.
entries.answer:
Marketplace search only looks at three fields — listing title, vendor and model — and only shows listings that are still active. If a part number returns nothing, search less, not more.

1. Open Browse and type into "Search by title, vendor or model…". It waits ~a third of a second after you stop typing, so give it a beat.
2. Narrow with the "All categories" dropdown (Switches, Optics / SFPs, and so on).
3. Check the For sale / Wanted toggle. These are two separate lists — something missing from For sale will not turn up under Wanted, and vice versa.
4. On "Nothing matches those filters", press "Clear filters" and try fewer words. Matching is on a plain fragment of text, so "WS-C3850" works, but a typo or a stray space will not.

Results are 24 to a page; Next only lights up when a further page actually exists.

Still nothing: scroll past the results to "Can't find it here?" and type the part number into that box — the eBay, Amazon, FS.com and Curvature buttons stay greyed out until you do, then each opens that search in a new tab. They are plain links out; RackTrack has no part in anything you buy there.
entries.rootCause: GET /api/marketplace/listings hard-filters status='active' and matches q with LIKE %q% against title, vendor and model only; the client debounces the query 300ms, requests PAGE_SIZE+1 rows to decide hasMore, and renders distinct empty states for mine / filtered / want / none.

2. Narrow with the "All categories" dropdown (Switches, Optics / SFPs, and so on).
3. Check the For sale / Wanted toggle.

entries.question: How do I put a piece of gear up for sale?
entries.answer:
Tap "List an item" — top right of Marketplace Browse, My listings and the Marketplace dashboard. The form opens titled "New listing".

1. Leave the toggle on "For sale" (switch to "Wanted" to ask for gear instead — the screen retitles to "Post a request").
2. Item: Title is required (up to 140 characters). Vendor and Model are optional; fill them in first and RackTrack pre-fills the title for you, which you can edit. Category defaults to Switches.
3. Condition & pricing: pick New (sealed), Refurbished, Used — working, or For parts / not working. Enter a Price, or leave it blank — the listing then shows "Make an offer" instead of a figure. Set Currency and Quantity if you have more than one.
4. Optional: a Photo (JPG/PNG/WebP/HEIC, up to 8 MB), Location, and a Description of up to 2000 characters.
5. Tap "Publish listing" (or "Post request").

You land on My listings with the new item at the top. It is live immediately — there is no approval queue and nobody reviews it before it appears.

How do I make an offer listing
How do I post a Wanted request

entries.question: My listing won't publish — it says "title is required" / "bad category" / "bad price".
entries.answer:
Those are validation checks, not a rejection. Nothing was saved, so fixing the named field and pressing Publish listing again will not create a duplicate.

• "Title is required." — the Title box is empty or only spaces. Type a real title (vendor plus model is enough).
• "bad price" — the Price box holds something that isn't a plain non-negative number, usually a negative value. Enter 0 or more, or clear the box entirely to list it as "Make an offer".
• "bad category" / "bad condition" / "bad kind" — the value sent isn't one RackTrack accepts. Reselect Category and Condition from the dropdowns and submit again; if it repeats, reload the page, as a stale tab can send an old value.
• "Please wait for the image to finish uploading." — your photo is still going up. Wait for the caption to change from "Uploading…" to "Photo ready", then press Publish again.

Nobody reviews listings before they appear: one that passes these checks goes live the moment you publish it.
symptoms: Please wait for the image to finish uploading.
entries.rootCause: POST /api/marketplace/listings validates kind/category/condition against fixed sets and requires a non-empty trimmed title and a finite non-negative price, returning 400 with a terse machine string that MarketplaceNewPage renders verbatim in its error banner.
entries.short: Those are validation checks, not a rejection. Nothing was saved, so fixing the named field and pressing Publish listing again will not create a duplicate.

entries.question: The photo on my listing won't upload — "Only image files are accepted" or "Image must be 8 MB or smaller".
entries.answer:
Listing photos must be a real image file (JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC) and 8 MB or smaller — the Photo box on the New listing screen says so.

1. "Image must be 8 MB or smaller." — re-shoot at lower resolution, or use your phone's resize/share-as-smaller option, then pick the file again.
2. "Only image files are accepted (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC)" / "Only jpg / png / webp / heic images are accepted" — wrong file type. Camera photos and screenshots are fine; PDFs and GIFs are not. A picture saved without a file extension is also rejected — rename it to end in .jpg or .png and pick it again.
3. "Upload failed" — tap Replace and try again. The photo uploads separately from the listing, so nothing you have typed is lost.
4. The photo is optional — tap Remove to drop it.

Wait for "Uploading…" to finish before you press Publish; the form will otherwise ask you to wait.
symptoms: Only image files are accepted (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC).
Image must be 8 MB or smaller.
Only jpg / png / webp / heic images are accepted
entries.rootCause: The marketplace multer instance limits fileSize to 8 MB and its fileFilter rejects anything whose original filename does not end in jpg/jpeg/png/webp/heic/heif; MarketplaceNewPage repeats both checks client-side before it even calls POST /api/marketplace/uploads.

evidence.snippet: Upload a photo JPG · PNG · WebP · HEIC · up to 8 MB

entries.short: Listing photos must be a real image file (JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC) and 8 MB or smaller — the Photo box on the New listing screen says so. "Image must be 8 MB or smaller." means re-shoot at a lower resolution, or use your phone's resize option, then pick the file again.

entries.question: I pressed Edit on one of my listings and got a blank New listing form — where did my listing go?
entries.answer:
Your listing is safe — nothing was deleted. Edit is broken: it opens the New listing form blank instead of loading your item, and publishing from it creates a second, duplicate listing rather than editing the original.

2. Status changes still work: "Mark sold" takes it off Browse, "Relist" puts a sold or closed one back.
3. To change price, title or description: tap Delete, confirm "Yes, delete", then re-post with "List an item".
4. If you already published from the blank form, delete whichever of the two you don't want.

Nothing on your side causes this — report it to your platform owner so it gets tracked.

entries.question: How do I actually buy something? What happens after I tap "Buy now"?
entries.answer:
"Buy now" opens the Checkout screen — "Review the order and confirm shipping". Nothing is charged until you press the button at the bottom.

1. Tap "Buy now" on a listing card, or the "Buy now — <price>" button inside the listing. It only shows on priced listings that aren't your own.
2. If the seller has more than one, set Quantity — the label says how many are available and you can't go above it.
3. Fill in the Shipping address. Full name, Street address and City are required; State / region, ZIP / postcode and Country are optional (Country is pre-filled with US).
4. Check the Order summary (right-hand column on desktop, below the form on a phone): Unit price, Quantity, Subtotal, Platform fee (3%), Total.
5. Press the button at the bottom. It reads "Pay with Stripe — <total>" if your RackTrack server has card payments configured, or "Complete purchase — <total>" if it doesn't. With Stripe you're handed off to Stripe's payment page; without it the order is recorded straight away.
6. Either way you land on the order screen, where you can message the seller and follow the status.

Leave a required field blank and the page tells you which one — "Name is required.", "Street address is required.", "City is required." — and nothing is submitted.
symptoms: Difference between Pay with Stripe and Complete purchase
entries.rootCause: MarketplaceCheckoutPage validates name/street/city client-side, POSTs to /api/marketplace/orders, and either follows data.stripeSessionUrl or navigates to /marketplace/orders/<id>; the button label is driven by GET /api/marketplace/stripe/status.

1. Tap "Buy now" on a listing card, or the "Buy now — <price>" button inside the listing.
2. If the seller has more than one, set Quantity — the label says how many are available and you can't go above it.

entries.question: There's no "Buy now" button on a listing, or checkout says "listing is not active" / "listing has no price — contact seller".
entries.answer:
Buy now only appears when the listing is active, is a For sale listing (not a Wanted request), and the seller set a price.

• No price — you'll see "Make an offer" and "No set price on this listing — contact @<seller> to make an offer." There's no checkout; message the seller. Forcing checkout returns "listing has no price — contact seller".
• "listing is not active" — it sold, was marked sold, or was withdrawn while your page was open. Go back to Browse and search again; Browse only shows active listings.
• "listing not found" — the seller deleted it. Nothing to recover.
• Grey "sold"/"closed" badge on the card — same thing, no longer purchasable.
• Wanted request — those are people asking for gear; you can't buy one. Post your own For sale listing instead.
• "cannot buy your own listing" — Buy now still shows on your own listings, but checkout blocks it.

If you were mid-checkout, nothing was charged and no order was created.
symptoms: listing has no price — contact seller
No set price on this listing
entries.rootCause: ListingCard/ListingDetailModal gate the Buy control on status==='active' && kind==='sell' && priceCents != null; POST /api/marketplace/orders re-checks the listing exists, is active and has a price, returning 404/400 with those exact strings.
entries.short: Buy now only appears when the listing is active, is a For sale listing (not a Wanted request), and the seller set a price. With no price you see "Make an offer" instead — there is no checkout, so message the seller.

entries.question: What do the order statuses mean, and how do I mark an order shipped or cancel it?
entries.answer:
Open Orders and pick Buying or Selling. Each order shows one status pill:

• Pending — order placed, payment not confirmed yet.
• Paid — payment confirmed; the seller can ship.
• Shipped — sent, usually with carrier and tracking.
• Completed — closed out for both sides.
• Cancelled — called off (red pill).

Actions appear only when they're allowed:

• Mark shipped — seller only, and only while the order is Paid. Fill in Carrier ("UPS, USPS, FedEx…") and Tracking number under "Ship this order", then press Mark shipped. The tracking number then shows on the order for the buyer.
• Mark completed — either side, only while Shipped. Confirm with "Yes, complete"; it closes the order for both sides.
• Cancel order — either side, only while Pending or Paid. Confirm with "Yes, cancel"; it can't be undone.

Errors: "cannot cancel at this stage" means the order already shipped or closed — message the other party instead. "invalid status transition" means the step isn't allowed from the current status (e.g. a buyer trying to mark shipped). "not your order" means you're neither the buyer nor the seller on it.
symptoms: What does Pending mean on an order
entries.rootCause: PATCH /api/marketplace/orders/:id allows cancel only from pending|paid, 'shipped' only when isSeller, 'completed' from either party, and rejects anything else with 'invalid status transition'; the Ship block is rendered only when isSeller && order.status === 'paid'.

{isSeller && order.status === 'paid' && (

Ship this order

... placeholder="UPS, USPS, FedEx…" ... Mark shipped

{confirming === 'complete'
                    ? 'Mark this order completed? This closes it for both sides.'
                    : 'Cancel this order? This cannot be undone.'}
...
                      Mark completed
...
                      Cancel order

entries.short: Open Orders and pick Buying or Selling. Each order shows one status pill: • Pending — order placed, payment not confirmed yet. • Paid — payment confirmed; the seller can ship. • Shipped — sent, usually with carrier and tracking. • Completed — closed out for both sides. • Cancelled — called off (red pill).

entries.question: How do Marketplace alerts work? I saved a search but I'm not getting any matches.
entries.answer:
A saved search is a standing watch: it only fires on listings posted AFTER you saved it. It never looks backwards, so an empty Matches list usually just means nothing new has been posted yet.

To create one: Alerts → "New search" (or "Save a search" if you have none), enter a Label (required — it names each match, e.g. "Cisco switch under $2k"), optionally set Keyword, Category, Max price and For sale / Wanted, then "Save search".

Why a search may never fire:
• Existing listings are never matched retroactively — only new posts.
• Every filter must match. Keyword is a plain substring of title, vendor or model. Category must be exactly the one the seller picked (a switch filed under "Other" won't match a Switches search).
• Kind must match: a "For sale" search never matches a Wanted post.
• Max price excludes anything above it; listings with no price ("Make an offer") still come through.
• You are never alerted about your own listings.

Limits: 20 saved searches max (the 21st gives "max 20 saved searches"); Alerts shows the 50 most recent. "Mark all read" clears the badge, the × on a row dismisses one match, and deleting a search ("Stop alerts and delete?") also removes its matches.
entries.rootCause: matchAlerts() runs only inside the POST /api/marketplace/listings response wrapper, so it evaluates saved searches against newly inserted rows only; it skips the listing's own owner, requires kind and (if set) category equality, a substring hit on title+vendor+model, and max_price_cents >= price. Saved searches are capped at 20 per user; GET /alerts is LIMIT 50; alerts cascade-delete with their saved search.

evidence.snippet:
WHERE a.user_id = ?
    ORDER BY a.created_at DESC LIMIT 50
How this search is named in your alerts.

entries.short: A saved search is a standing watch: it only fires on listings posted AFTER you saved it. It never looks backwards, so an empty Matches list usually just means nothing new has been posted yet.

entries.question: My listing disappeared from Browse and now shows "closed" — I didn't touch it.
entries.answer:
Listings auto-retire at 90 days. Any listing still "active" 90 days after it was posted is flipped to "closed" — it drops out of Browse (Browse only shows active listings) but stays in My listings with a grey "closed" pill.

To bring it back:
1. Open My listings (closed listings are still there — they only vanish from public Browse).
2. Press "Relist" — it goes straight back to active and reappears in Browse.
3. If the gear is gone, press Delete, then "Yes, delete".

Other reasons a listing leaves Browse:
• It shows "sold" — you pressed "Mark sold", or a buyer took the last unit, which marks it sold automatically.
• Your platform owner hid it after it was reported. That also shows as "closed"; relisting without fixing the problem just gets it hidden again, so ask them what was wrong first.

Note: the expiry sweep is lazy (it runs at most once an hour, and only when certain pages are loaded), so a listing may sit past 90 days for a while before it flips.

The Dashboard's "Closed" tile ("Expired or withdrawn") counts both cases.
entries.rootCause: maybeExpireListings() flips any active listing created more than 90 days ago to 'closed'. It is debounced to once an hour and is registered as router.use AFTER most /api/marketplace routes, so in practice it only fires on the later-registered endpoints (dashboard, stripe/status, partner OAuth status) rather than on every request.

evidence.snippet: <Stat label="Closed"   value={d.listings.closed} meta="Expired or withdrawn" />

entries.short:
Listings auto-retire at 90 days.
1. Open My listings (closed listings are still there — they only vanish from public Browse).
2. Press "Relist" — it goes straight back to active and reappears in Browse.
3. If the gear is gone, press Delete, then "Yes, delete".

entries.question: What do the numbers on the Marketplace Dashboard mean, and why is my revenue zero when I've sold things?
entries.answer:
The Marketplace Dashboard ("Seller dashboard — Listings, sales and purchases") is per-user, not per-organization, and Revenue counts completed orders only.

What the numbers are:
• Listings — Total, Active, Sold, Closed ("Expired or withdrawn").
• Sales — Revenue ("From N completed orders"), Orders (all orders where you're the seller), Completed, and Pending ("Awaiting shipment"). Pending counts orders at Paid or Shipped — it's your to-ship / to-close queue, not unpaid orders.
• Purchases — Spent ("Across N orders") and your buyer order count.

Why Revenue reads zero: only orders with status Completed are totalled. An order still at Paid or Shipped sits in Pending and contributes nothing. Close them out: Orders → Selling → open the order → "Mark completed" → "Yes, complete". The button only appears once the order is Shipped, so mark it shipped first.

There is no combined org view — if several admins in your org sell, each sees only their own figures. "Recent listings" shows your last ten; "View all" opens the My listings tab.
symptoms: Dashboard doesn't show my team's sales
entries.rootCause: GET /api/marketplace/dashboard aggregates strictly by req.user.id: revenue_cents sums total_cents only WHERE status='completed', pending_orders counts status IN ('paid','shipped'), and there is no organization-level rollup.

evidence.snippet:
const orderStats = db.prepare(`
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)                                   AS total_orders,
      SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_orders,
      SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN total_cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
      SUM(CASE WHEN status IN ('paid','shipped') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)   AS pending_orders
    FROM marketplace_orders WHERE seller_id = ?
  `).get(uid);

<StatGroup title="Sales">
            <Stat
              lead
              label="Revenue"
              value={formatCurrency(d.sales.revenueCents)}
              meta={`From ${plural(d.sales.completedOrders, 'completed order')}`}
            />
...
            <Stat
              label="Pending"
              value={d.sales.pendingOrders}
              meta={d.sales.pendingOrders > 0 ? 'Awaiting shipment' : undefined}
            />

<MarketplaceShell
      title="Seller dashboard"
      subtitle="Listings, sales and purchases"
      backTo="/marketplace"

entries.short: The Marketplace Dashboard ("Seller dashboard — Listings, sales and purchases") is per-user, not per-organization, and Revenue counts completed orders only. What the numbers are: • Listings — Total, Active, Sold, Closed ("Expired or withdrawn").

entries.question: What do Partner accounts do, and how do I get new listings posted into our Discord channel?
entries.answer:
Partners (/marketplace/partners, admin only) shows three cards — eBay, Amazon, Discord — each with a Connected / Not connected pill. Discord is the only one that does anything today.

Discord (announce new listings in a channel):
1. Discord: Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy webhook URL.
2. RackTrack: Partners → Discord → paste into "Webhook URL" → "Save webhook".
3. Press "Send test". You should see "Test notification sent to Discord." here and a "Webhook Test" message in the channel.
4. After that, every listing anyone creates posts a card with title, category, condition, price, equipment and location. The fan-out is server-wide, not per-user: every connected Discord webhook gets it.

If the test fails:
• "No Discord webhook connected" — it was disconnected; save the URL again.
• "Webhook failed: Discord returned 404" — the webhook was deleted in Discord; create a new one and save it.

entries.question: INTERNAL: A buyer says they paid but the order is still Pending — how does Marketplace payment actually work?
entries.answer:
Marketplace payment is env-gated and the order's initial status depends on whether Stripe is wired up: `const initialStatus = stripe ? 'pending' : 'paid'` (server/marketplace_routes.js:642).

Check GET /api/marketplace/stripe/status ({configured:true|false}) first.

configured:false — no charge is ever taken. POST /api/marketplace/orders writes the order straight in as 'paid' ("offline payment assumed"). The checkout button reads "Complete purchase — …". Treat it as an IOU settled outside RackTrack; never tell a customer RackTrack charged them.

configured:true — the order is written 'pending', a Checkout Session is created with the order id in metadata, and the client redirects to session.url (MarketplaceCheckoutPage.jsx:113-117). The only path to 'paid' is POST /api/marketplace/stripe/webhook receiving checkout.session.completed, matching metadata.orderId, and running an UPDATE guarded by `AND status = 'pending'` (marketplace_routes.js:1310-1330).

Known defect — the webhook currently cannot work. server/app.js:284 mounts express.json() globally before the marketplace router (app.js:434), so the route's express.raw() is skipped and req.body arrives as a parsed object. With STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET set, constructEvent throws; without it, JSON.parse on an object throws. Either way the response is 400 "Webhook verification failed: …". So on any deployment with Stripe enabled, orders never leave Pending. Fix is server-side: mount the webhook with express.raw before express.json.

Other ways an order sits at Pending: the buyer abandoned or failed the Stripe page (cancel_url returns them to /marketplace/orders/<id>?payment=cancelled, but MarketplaceOrdersPage never reads ?payment=, so they see no message and often assume it worked); or session creation itself failed, in which case the API returns { ok:true, order, stripeError } and the client — which only looks for stripeSessionUrl — silently drops them on a pending order page. Grep the log for marketplace.stripe_error.

There is no in-app way to re-drive payment on an existing order (only one create-session call site, at order creation). Cancel the order via PATCH /api/marketplace/orders/:id (allowed from pending) and have the buyer check out again.
symptoms: Buyer paid but status didn't change
No confirmation after returning from Stripe
entries.rootCause: initialStatus = stripe ? 'pending' : 'paid'. Without Stripe the order is fabricated as paid with no charge; with Stripe the only path to 'paid' is the checkout.session.completed webhook, and both a cancelled session and a failed session-creation leave the order pending with no user-visible message because MarketplaceOrdersPage ignores ?payment=.
entries.short: Marketplace payment is env-gated, and the order's initial status depends on whether Stripe is wired up: the handler sets `pending` when Stripe is configured and `paid` when it is not. Check GET /api/marketplace/stripe/status first — with `configured:false` no charge is ever taken.

entries.question: INTERNAL: An admin says "Connect eBay" (or Connect Amazon) just goes to a broken page even though the API keys are set.
entries.answer:
Client bug, not credentials. Verify keys, then set expectations.

1. GET /api/marketplace/partner-accounts/ebay/status (or …/amazon/status). If `configured:false`, the Connect button is disabled with "API keys not configured on this server" — that IS the credentials case: set EBAY_APP_ID / EBAY_CERT_ID / EBAY_REDIRECT_URI (or AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_ID / AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_SECRET / AMAZON_REDIRECT_URI) in .env and restart.
2. If `configured:true`, the button works but the page is broken: …/auth-url returns `{ ok: true, url }` while the page reads `data.authUrl`, so it navigates to the literal string "undefined" — blank / not-found page, consent screen never reached (MarketplacePartnerAccountsPage.jsx:128 vs marketplace_routes.js:1349 and :1397).
3. No in-app workaround. POSTing /api/marketplace/partner-accounts with {platform:'ebay'} only creates a stub row — it grants no eBay access.
4. The callbacks redirect with ?error=ebay_auth_failed / ?error=amazon_auth_failed (and ?connected=ebay), but the page never reads query params, so a failed — or successful — exchange also shows nothing.

Even once connected, nothing cross-posts: no code publishes a RackTrack listing to eBay or Amazon. Never promise cross-posting.
symptoms: Connect eBay goes to a blank page
entries.rootCause: MarketplacePartnerAccountsPage reads data.authUrl from the /auth-url response, but the server returns the field as `url`, so window.location.href is assigned undefined. Separately, the ?error=…/?connected=… params the OAuth callbacks redirect with are never read by the page.

evidence.snippet: return res.redirect(`${STRIPE_BASE_URL}/marketplace/partners?error=ebay_auth_failed`);

entries.short: Client bug, not credentials. Verify the keys first: GET /api/marketplace/partner-accounts/ebay/status (or …/amazon/status). If it reports `configured:false`, the Connect button is disabled with "API keys not configured on this server" — that IS the credentials case, so set the keys in .env and restart.

entries.question: INTERNAL: A customer reported a listing and nothing happened. How does reporting and moderation work?
entries.answer:
Reporting writes a row and stops there. Handle these tickets manually.

"Report listing" POSTs to /api/marketplace/listings/:id/flag, which only inserts into marketplace_flags (server/marketplace_routes.js:1139-1146). A repeat report from the same account hits the UNIQUE(listing_id,user_id) constraint and shows "already flagged" in the modal. The UI then says "Reported. An admin will review this listing." (client/src/pages/MarketplacePage.jsx:410-413) — that is not true; nobody is queued to see it.

Missing pieces:
- No endpoint or screen lists flags. marketplace_flags appears exactly twice in the codebase (CREATE TABLE + INSERT). The only way to read reports is querying server/data/auth.db directly.
- No notification fires on a flag. The Discord webhook is wired to listing creation only.
- POST /api/marketplace/listings/:id/moderate ('hide' → status closed, 'restore' → active) gates on `user.role === 'admin' || user.id === 1` (marketplace_routes.js:1156-1159). RackTrack never issues an 'admin' role — roles are owner, org_admin, site_manager, member (server/auth.js:211-214) — so only the first user row can moderate. Everyone else, platform owner included, gets 403 "admin only".

Resolution: escalate to whoever holds user id 1 on that deployment, or ask the seller to delete their own listing (DELETE /api/marketplace/listings/:id is owner-only and always works for them). Never promise the customer a review.
symptoms: Where do I review reported listings
Can't hide a listing as owner
entries.rootCause: marketplace_flags is write-only — no list/read endpoint and no notification hook. The moderate endpoint gates on a role string ('admin') that the auth system never issues, falling back to user.id === 1, so owner/org_admin accounts receive 403 'admin only'.

evidence.snippet:
{reported ? (

Reported. An admin will review this listing.

entries.short: Reporting writes a row and stops there, so handle these tickets manually. No endpoint or screen lists flags, and no notification fires on one — the only way to read reports is querying server/data/auth.db directly.

entries.question: I never picked a picture — where did my letter and colour come from?
entries.answer: They're assigned automatically, not picked by anyone. The letter is the first character of your username (or your email if you have no username), upper-cased; the colour gradient is derived from that same first character, so it's the same every time you sign in. To change it, tap your avatar on the Profile tab and pick a gradient from the "Choose your picture" sheet — it saves as soon as you tap.
symptoms: why is my avatar this colour
my avatar changed to a letter
what does the coloured circle mean
entries.rootCause: resolveAvatarIndex falls back to autoAvatarIndex(username||email), a deterministic charCodeAt(0) % AVATARS.length pick, and avatarInitial upper-cases the first character of username||email.
entries.short: They're assigned automatically, not picked by anyone. The letter is the first character of your username (or your email if you have no username), upper-cased; the colour gradient is derived from that same first character, so it's the same every time you sign in.

entries.question: A teammate has exactly the same avatar colour as me — is something wrong?
entries.answer: No. Until you pick one, your gradient is derived from the first character of your username (or email) modulo the 8 available gradients, so collisions are normal and nothing is broken. To stand apart: on Profile, tap your avatar (blue pencil badge), then tap a different gradient in "Choose your picture" — it saves immediately and the sheet closes. There are still only 8, so a colleague could pick the same one.
symptoms: two users look identical in the app
same colour avatar as my colleague
I can't tell who is who
entries.rootCause: autoAvatarIndex maps the first character's char code modulo the 8-entry AVATARS list, so different initials routinely map to the same gradient, and no per-user uniqueness is enforced.
entries.short: No. Until you pick one, your gradient is derived from the first character of your username (or email) modulo the 8 available gradients, so collisions are normal and nothing is broken.

entries.question: How do I know which picture I'm currently using in the picker?
entries.answer: Your current picture is the one with a white ring around it. Tap any other circle to switch; the sheet closes itself once the new picture is saved (if saving fails it stays open so you can retry). On desktop, hovering also shows a tooltip reading "Current" vs "Select" — that tooltip does not appear on a phone, so go by the ring.
symptoms: no tick mark in the picker
can't tell which one is mine
entries.rootCause: ProfilePage passes ring={idx === currentAvatar} and title 'Current'/'Select' to each preview Avatar; Avatar renders `ring` as a white box-shadow halo.
entries.short: Your current picture is the one with a white ring around it. Tap any other circle to switch; the sheet closes itself once the new picture is saved (if saving fails it stays open so you can retry).

entries.question: Is my picture choice remembered, and does it show on my other phone?
entries.answer: Yes to both. Your pick is saved against your account on the server, so it follows you to any device you sign in on and survives signing out or reinstalling — you never have to re-pick it. (The app also keeps a local copy for speed, but the server's copy is the one that counts.)
symptoms: do I have to pick my avatar again
entries.rootCause: The picker POSTs to /api/auth/avatar, which writes the index to the users.avatar column and returns the refreshed user; the client then calls refreshUser(). Nothing is kept in device storage.
entries.short: Yes to both. Your pick is saved against your account in RackTrack, so it follows you to any device you sign in on and survives signing out or reinstalling — you never have to re-pick it. (The app also keeps a local copy for speed, but RackTrack's copy is the one that counts.)

entries.question: I tapped a picture in "Choose your picture" and nothing happened — the sheet stayed open.
entries.answer: The save didn't reach the server, and the sheet stays open on purpose so you can retry — it never shows an error. While a save is in flight the pictures dim and the bottom button reads "Saving…"; on success the sheet closes by itself. Check your signal and tap the picture again. If it still won't close, tap Close and retry once you're back online.
entries.rootCause: chooseAvatar only closes the picker when the POST returns r.ok; a network throw is swallowed by the catch, which intentionally leaves the sheet open with no error message shown.
entries.short: The save didn't reach RackTrack, and the sheet stays open on purpose so you can retry — it never shows an error. While a save is in flight the pictures dim and the bottom button reads "Saving…"; on success the sheet closes by itself. Check your signal and tap the picture again.

entries.question: How do I switch RackTrack to dark mode / where is the appearance setting?
entries.answer: There is no dark mode. RackTrack ships a single light theme (white surface, black accent) — no appearance setting anywhere, and the old theme toggle now renders nothing. The app also forces light rendering, so it stays white even when your phone is in system dark mode.
symptoms: night mode for the cold aisle
theme toggle does nothing / is missing
app stays white in system dark mode
entries.rootCause: ThemeToggle returns null and ThemeContext hard-codes THEME='light', setting data-theme="light" on <html> at mount; setTheme and toggleTheme are no-ops, so no user preference exists.
entries.short: There is no dark mode. RackTrack ships a single light theme (white surface, black accent) — no appearance setting anywhere, and the old theme toggle now renders nothing. The app also forces light rendering, so it stays white even when your phone is in system dark mode.

entries.question: Internal: where does the audit trail live and what is in one row?
entries.answer: Table `audit_log` in server/data/auth.db (SQLite, WAL), created on first require of server/audit.js. One row per sensitive action: id, ts, user_id, username, tenant_id, action, target_type/target_id, status ('ok' or 'fail'), ip, user_agent, payload (JSON, capped at 8 KiB) and error. Username and tenant_id are snapshotted at write time rather than joined from users, so deleting a user or moving them to another tenant leaves the existing trail intact. Note tenant_id is added by auth.js's migration, not the base CREATE TABLE, and audit.query() can filter on it but does not return it in the row.

entries.question: Internal: how do I pull one user's or one action's audit trail while investigating an incident?
entries.answer: GET /api/audit (auth required), newest-first. Filters: action, targetType, targetId, status, since, until, limit, offset — since/until take ISO or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; limit is clamped to 1-1000 (default 100). action supports a wildcard suffix: action=scan.* matches every scan.* event. There is no username filter — scope decides whose events you see. Default is scope=self. scope=tenant and scope=all are gated on the caller's username appearing in the server's AUDIT_ADMINS env allow-list; a non-admin is silently downgraded (all→tenant→self) with no 403, so check the "scope" field the response echoes back alongside ok/count/events to see what you actually got. Page with offset.

scope=all returns only my own events and no error is shown
Need to page through more than 100 audit events
entries.rootCause: The /api/audit route requires auth and gates cross-user visibility on an AUDIT_ADMINS username allow-list, downgrading scope=all to tenant and tenant to self rather than returning 403; audit.query clamps limit and supports an 'action.*' prefix match.

entries.question: Internal: an action definitely happened but there is no audit_log row for it.
entries.answer: Missing audit rows are normal-path, not corruption: audit.log() never throws. Two causes, both visible in the server log. (1) The event was rejected before the INSERT — no action, or status not exactly 'ok'/'fail' — logged as kind:"audit" with drop:true ("[audit] dropped event ..."). (2) The SQLite INSERT failed — logged as kind:"audit", subkind:"persist_failed", message "audit DB write failed". Any event that passes validation is also mirrored to the structured log stream as kind:"audit" (audit.<action> counter included), so the trail is usually still queryable in logs even when the table has no row. Exception: if the observability module isn't loaded (one-off scripts), there is no mirror and drops/failures go to console only.
symptoms: Expected audit event missing from /api/audit results
Log lines reading 'audit DB write failed' or '[audit] dropped event'
Audit gap with no user-visible error at the time
entries.rootCause: audit.log() validates action and status and drops invalid events with a warn, wraps the INSERT in a try/catch that logs instead of throwing, and separately mirrors each event to the observability stream via emitAudit — all deliberately non-fatal to the request path.

entries.question: Internal: how far back does the audit log go, and is it ever pruned or truncated?
entries.answer: Never pruned. audit.js (server/data/auth.db) only inserts and selects — it exports just log/query/_db and contains no DELETE — so audit_log grows for the life of the DB. Retention belongs to the separate application log (lib/log-store.js, logs.db: 7 days / 200,000 rows), and the Logs tab's "Clear log" runs DELETE FROM app_logs only — it never touches audit_log. Individual rows are truncated at write time (payload 8 KB, user-agent 512, error 1024), but rows are never removed. Removing an organization sets tenant_id = NULL on its audit rows: they survive but stop matching scope=tenant.

entries.answer: In-process cache. `GET /api/demo/tenant-mat?source=cmdb` (server/demo_topology.js, note: no `/demo/topology` route exists) memoises the CMDB result in module scope for CMDB_TTL_MS = 30 s; a cached reply carries `_cached: true`. entries.question: Internal: I changed the demo data but /demo/topology still shows the old racks.
entries.answer: Depends on which source toggle is active. CMDB: the response is cached in-process for 30 s (CMDB_TTL_MS), so wait 30 s and reload — a `_cached: true` field marks a cache hit. Local: it reads server/data/demo_tenant.json and re-reads it whenever the file's mtime changes, so edits show on the next request with no restart. Note demo_tenant_bootstrap.py writes to ServiceNow, not to that file — editing demo_tenant.json is the only way to change the Local view.
symptoms: Edited demo_tenant.json, Local view unchanged for a moment
entries.rootCause: demo_topology.js keeps _cmdbCache with CMDB_TTL_MS = 30_000 for source=cmdb, and loadDemo() caches the parsed JSON keyed on the file's stat.mtimeMs for source=json.
entries.short: Depends on which source toggle is active. CMDB: the response is cached in-process for 30 seconds, so wait and reload — a `_cached: true` field marks a cache hit. Local: it re-reads server/data/demo_tenant.json whenever the file's mtime changes, so edits show on the next request with no restart.

entries.question: Internal: on the /demo/topology Floor map, OK, Drift and Orphan racks all look identical. Is the map broken?
entries.answer: Cosmetic gap, not missing data. STATUS_META (TenantMatPage.jsx:20-25) gives ok, drift and scan_only the same colour #1a1c1d; only cmdb_only ("Unscanned") is #cfc4c5. On the map the sole extra cue is fillOpacity/strokeDasharray driven by rack.scanned, so unscanned racks look faded and dashed and everything else looks identical. The legend has the same problem (one dot per status, three sharing a colour). To read status, use the List view and sort by the Status column, or the header counts (racks / ok / drift / unscanned / orphan).

entries.question: Internal: clicking a rack in the /demo/topology tree jumps me into 3D — how do I narrow the Floor map instead?
entries.answer: Select a container, not a rack. In the left "Containers" tree, picking the tenant, a Building, a Floor or a Row just scopes the rack set — Floor map and List narrow to it, and the current view is left alone. Picking a rack additionally opens the detail panel and forces the view to "3D rack". Note the Hierarchy view is never filtered: it always draws the whole tree and only highlights your selection. The sidebar button hides/shows the tree. If a scope has no racks the canvas reads "No racks match the current selection."

Canvas reads 'No racks match the current selection.'

entries.question: Internal: what has to be true before a build containing /demo/topology goes on an internet-facing host?
entries.answer: Treat /demo/topology and its API as public. server/app.js:372 mounts the demo_topology router with a plain app.use, and its routes — /api/demo/tenant-mat and /api/demo/tenant-mat/rack/:rackId — have no requireAuth and no tenant scoping; the UI route in App.jsx sits outside ProtectedRoute. Worse, ?source=cmdb spawns python3 (servicenow/demo_tenant_query.py) per request outside a 30s cache, so anonymous traffic can fork processes. Before exposing a host: block /demo/* and /api/demo/* at the proxy, or stop mounting the router (env-gate it the way mock_routes already is).
symptoms: Demo dataset visible to anonymous visitors
Unauthenticated hits on /api/demo/tenant-mat in the access log
python3 processes spawned by web requests
entries.rootCause: server/app.js mounts require('./demo_topology') unconditionally with app.use and the router declares its routes without any auth middleware; the cmdb branch calls spawn(PYTHON_CMD, [QUERY_SCRIPT]) from the request handler.

evidence.snippet:
const env = { ...process.env, PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8' };
    const child = spawn(PYTHON_CMD, [QUERY_SCRIPT], { cwd: PROJECT_ROOT, env });

entries.short: Treat /demo/topology and its API as public. The demo_topology router is mounted with a plain app.use and its routes carry no requireAuth and no tenant scoping, the UI route sits outside ProtectedRoute, and ?source=cmdb spawns a python3 process per request outside the 30s cache. Before exposing a host, block /demo/* and /api/demo/* at the proxy or env-gate the router the way mock_routes already is.

entries.question: During a scan there's a small spinning 3D rack above "Analyzing rack…" — what is it telling me?
entries.answer: It is decoration, not a picture of your rack. The little rack spins on a timer; only the glowing beam and the lit shelf mean anything, and they just walk top-to-bottom as the percentage climbs. The real information is the step text and the % under it ("Preprocessing image…" through "Locating incident target…", or a different list for a multi-photo upload). It ignores taps by design.
symptoms: Small rotating rack shown above the words "Analyzing rack…"
Wondering whether the animation reflects the rack being scanned
entries.rootCause: MiniRack3D is a decorative WebGL animation driven only by the `progress` number; the scan beam and the lit unit are derived from progress, and the container sets pointerEvents: 'none'.

Analyzing rack…

... {progress}%

// Top → bottom: progress 0% → top unit; progress 100% → bottom unit.

entries.short: It is decoration, not a picture of your rack. The little rack spins on a timer; only the glowing beam and the lit shelf mean anything, and they just walk top-to-bottom as the percentage climbs.

entries.answer:
The spinning 3D rack is decoration only — the step text and percentage are the real status, and your scan and its results are unaffected.

entries.question: Where does the product photo on an SFP Advisor card come from — is it the exact part I'd receive?
entries.answer: It's a real product photo, but not guaranteed to be the exact revision you'll receive. RackTrack takes the image from the retailer/vendor page the recommendation came from — and if that page's image isn't from a trusted host, it falls back to a web image search for "<brand> <part number> SFP transceiver". Either way the file is downloaded and re-served from RackTrack's own cache, which is why it always loads. It appears large on the ★ TOP PICK card and as a thumbnail on the best-price, alternatives and cable tiles. (Modules whose photo can't be fetched are dropped, so everything listed has a picture.) Treat it as a shape/connector sanity check only — confirm the part by part number and the buy link before ordering.
symptoms: Unsure whether the picture is a real photo of the recommended module
Photo shows a slightly different label or revision than expected
Wanting to confirm a module before buying
entries.rootCause: SfpModuleImage renders module.imageUrl, which the SFP recommender populates from the product page (or an image-search fallback) and re-hosts from the server's own image cache.

entries.question: An SFP module card has an empty box where the picture should be.
entries.answer: Expected. RackTrack never draws a stand-in graphic: if a module has no photo, or the photo fails to load, the image slot is just left empty — that's why some rows have thumbnails and others don't, and why there's no broken-image icon. Nothing is wrong with the recommendation; use the part number, the spec chips and the buy link. If it only happens on a restricted site network, reopen the SFP Advisor tab on a better connection.

entries.question: The photo on the ★ TOP PICK card looks cropped or zoomed in, but the small thumbnails don't.
entries.answer: By design, and it means nothing about the part. The large TOP PICK photo is scaled to fill its square slot, so the edges get trimmed; the small thumbnails shrink the whole image to fit instead. Tap the card's "Buy on ..." link to see the vendor's full product shot.

entries.question: INTERNAL: why does the SFP Advisor return fewer modules than the source catalog lists?
entries.answer: Internal. After image enrichment, sfp_recommend.py drops every module that has no locally cached image: `modules = [m for m in modules if m.get("imageUrl")]` (line 1283) — the rule is that a part the user can't see isn't worth recommending. Images are fetched server-side into outputs/sfp_images/; a scraped URL is only tried directly if `_is_trusted_image_host` passes (page's own domain or a known retailer/CDN), otherwise a DDG image-search fallback runs. With outbound fetching blocked, every candidate fails and lists come back short or empty. Two other filters also shrink the list: brandless entries are dropped (line 1244) and a per-brand round-robin cap limits how many SKUs one vendor contributes (line 1285+).
