entries.answer: Yes. Your scan history is stored on the server against your account, so it appears wherever you sign in.

entries.question: How do I reopen an old scan?
entries.answer: Tap its row in Recent Scans. RackTrack loads that rack's saved report and opens it in full — no re-scanning needed.

entries.question: Why do I only see five scans?
entries.answer: Five is just the default view to keep things tidy. If you have more, tap "Show all …" to see them all, and "Show less" to collapse the list again.

entries.question: What do the numbers like "8 dev · 42 units · 3 ports" mean?
entries.answer: They are quick counts from that scan: how many devices were found, how many rack units were detected, and how many ports have been identified so far.

entries.question: Can I change my profile picture?
entries.answer: Yes. Tap your avatar and pick one of the preset gradient avatars — it saves immediately. There is nothing to upload, and they work offline.

entries.question: Can I switch to dark mode?
entries.answer: No. RackTrack uses a single light theme, so there is no theme or dark-mode setting.

entries.question: Why don't I see the Administration or Data Sources shortcuts?
entries.answer: Those appear only for owners and organization admins. If your role is member or site manager, your Profile shows just your identity and your scans.

entries.question: Why does a colleague see more scans than I do?
entries.answer: Visibility depends on your role. Owners see every rack, organization admins see their organization's racks, and members see only the racks they scanned themselves.

entries.question: I tapped a scan and it wouldn't open — what happened?
entries.answer: Most often the rack was removed on the server. RackTrack shows a short error instead of a broken report, and on a direct link to a missing rack it sends you back to the scan screen.

entries.question: Why won't the shutter let me take the photo?
entries.answer: In Camera Photo mode the shutter stays locked until three things pass: the picture is sharp, the rack fills the frame, and the lighting is neither too dark nor too bright. The coaching line tells you which one to fix ("Move closer…", "Hold steady…", "Move to better lighting"). Once all three pass the corner brackets turn green and the shutter unlocks. In Video mode the shutter works as soon as the camera is ready.

entries.question: My photo is fine but it said "please upload a clearer photo" / "take it from the front" — why?
entries.answer: Those come from the server's checks after upload. "Take the photo from the front of the rack" means the pipeline found no devices face‑on; "only N rack units could be made out" means fewer than three units were visible. Both are retryable — move so the whole rack front is in frame, or hit Proceed anyway to accept what was found. A true "couldn't read the image" only appears for a genuinely unreadable file.

entries.question: Can I scan a photo from my gallery instead of taking a new one?
entries.answer: Yes. Use the Upload tab (SINGLE mode) and pick or drag in a file. Uploads skip the live camera coaching but go through the exact same server‑side quality gate and pipeline.

entries.question: It's an iPhone HEIC photo — will that work?
entries.answer: Yes. The app deliberately doesn't try to decode HEIC in the browser; it uploads it and the server converts it to JPEG before analysing. The Upload zone accepts .heic/.heif explicitly.

entries.question: My rack is too tall to fit in one shot. What do I do?
entries.answer: Use MULTI mode. Add 2 to 8 overlapping photos (top to bottom, but the order doesn't have to be right — the server works it out from the overlaps), then tap Stitch & Analyze. RackTrack merges them into one long image and analyses that.

entries.question: Do I have to add the tall‑rack photos in the correct order?
entries.answer: No. The header even says "auto‑arranged". The stitcher infers top‑to‑bottom order by detecting where images overlap. The up / down / remove controls are there if you want to override, but "drop them in and hit Analyze" is the intended flow.

entries.question: What happens with a video — does it analyse the whole clip?
entries.answer: No. In the main Scan flow the server scores the frames and picks the single sharpest, most device‑rich one, then analyses that one frame like a photo. So a short, slightly shaky pan still gives a clean result.

entries.question: The live boxes on the camera look a bit jumpy or briefly wrong. Is that the result?
entries.answer: No — those live labels are a real‑time preview only, drawn from lightweight detection frames and smoothed on the device. A label only appears after two consecutive detections and disappears quickly when the device leaves view. The authoritative result comes from the full analysis after you press the shutter.

entries.question: I scanned the same rack twice — did I create a duplicate?
entries.answer: No. A rack's id is a hash of the image content (scoped to your organisation), so re‑scanning the exact same photo returns the stored result instantly instead of creating a second scan. Its "recent" timestamp is refreshed so it still shows as just‑scanned.

entries.question: My upload failed / the connection dropped mid‑scan. Do I lose the work?
entries.answer: The app retries once automatically after a brief pause, and because the rack id is content‑based, a retry that actually landed the first time just returns the same scan. If your phone suspended the app mid‑analysis, the scan is remembered and can be picked back up when you return.

entries.question: What is "ticket mode" and the "Wrong rack" pop‑up?
entries.answer: If you link an active incident before scanning, the scan targets that incident's specific device and port. When RackTrack knows which physical rack the incident belongs to, it compares the labels read off your photo against the expected rack; if they don't match it stops you with a "Wrong rack" modal showing detected vs. expected labels, so you don't attach the wrong rack to the ticket.

entries.question: Do I need to be signed in to scan?
entries.short: Yes — a normal photo scan needs you signed in with an approved organisation; it happens automatically.
entries.answer: For a normal photo scan, yes — scanning requires you to be signed in, and your organisation must be approved. Your sign-in is applied automatically, so in day-to-day use you won't notice; you just need to be logged in.

entries.question: Where do I find Rack Topology?
entries.answer: Open a rack's results and choose the Topology tab, or go to the rack's …/topology page. For a two-rack scan you'll also see a 3D button in the rack switcher that opens both racks together in one scene.

entries.question: What's the difference between the 2D and 3D views?
entries.answer: They're the same rack, drawn two ways. 2D is a flat, front-on elevation — fast to read, good for scanning shelf positions and port states. 3D is an interactive model you can orbit, tilt and zoom, with the cabling drawn as tubes. Use the 2D / 3D toggle to switch; your choice is remembered for next time.

entries.question: How do I move around in the 3D scene?
entries.answer: Right-click and drag to orbit, scroll to zoom. Once you zoom in past a point, dragging switches to a hand-pan (the cursor turns into a grab hand) so you can slide across a device's front panel. Tapping empty space clears whatever you had selected.

entries.question: Why can I open the rack's side doors?
entries.answer: The 3D rack has clickable glass side panels that swing open when you tap them — a way to "look inside" the rack. It's purely visual; it doesn't change any data.

entries.question: How do I see what a device connects to?
entries.answer: Tap the device (in either view). The panel at the bottom shows its class, shelf and model, a strip of its connected neighbours, and a full ports table listing each port's status, the cable, the connector, the type and length, and the device on the other end.

entries.question: What do the port colours mean?
entries.answer: In the 2D view a legend spells them out: connected copper (RJ45), free RJ45, SFP/fibre, console, and uplink each have their own colour. In 3D the jacks are shaded more simply — connected, empty, uplink and highlighted ports look different — and hovering a device gives you a card with the exact connected-vs-free count.

entries.question: Are the cables real?
entries.answer: The ends are real — a cable is only ever drawn on a port the scan actually saw as plugged in. But which port pairs with which, along with the cable IDs, types and lengths, is a best guess unless your team supplied a curated override. Use it as a plausible starting point, not a verified wiring record.

entries.question: It says "Topology is being prepared" — what should I do?
entries.answer: Nothing, usually. The snapshot builds in the background after a scan and the page keeps re-checking for about a minute, so it normally appears on its own. If it doesn't, tap Retry, or rescan the rack to regenerate it.

entries.question: Can I filter cables by type, see a capacity heat-map, or trace a path between two devices?
entries.answer: Not from a button in the current app. Those capabilities exist in the code's data layer, but the toolbar that would switch them on isn't shown in this build — so today there's no on-screen filter, capacity or trace control. What you can do is tap a device to see its ports and neighbours, and tap a single cable (in 3D) to see its two ends.

entries.question: What's the "UPLINK / EXTERNAL" or "CORE" device I see outside the rack?
entries.answer: That's a stand-in aggregation point where the switch uplinks terminate. It's generated (it lives outside the rack), and it's drawn on a shelf above the rack in 3D or in the right-hand "UPLINK · EXTERNAL" column in 2D so you can see where the uplinks go.

entries.question: Can I see two racks at once?
entries.answer: Yes — a two-rack scan can render both racks in one shared 3D space, side by side on the same floor, with the handful of inter-rack uplink cables drawn between them and a panel listing those cross-rack connections. The …/topology page also offers a 2D version that puts the two elevations next to each other.

entries.question: Why does the scene look different in light and dark theme, and does my view choice stick?
entries.answer: The 3D scene reads the app's theme and swaps its background, floor and cable-jacket colours to match, live, when you toggle themes. And yes — whether you last used 2D or 3D is remembered, so Topology reopens the way you left it.

entries.question: How do I share a scan?
entries.answer: Open the scan's results screen, tap Share in the button row, pick Teams, Outlook or Slack, type the recipient's email, and confirm. RackTrack builds a PDF of the report and sends it to that person.

entries.question: How do I send a report to someone?
entries.answer: Same as sharing: tap Share, choose a channel, enter their email, optionally add a short message or subject, and send. They receive the report as a PDF.

entries.question: How do I email a scan?
entries.answer: Use Share. All three options (Teams, Outlook, Slack) are addressed to an email address and deliver the report PDF to that recipient — so "email a scan" and "share a scan" are the same action here. To email it to yourself, put your own address in the recipient field.

entries.question: Can I export to CSV?
entries.answer: Yes. The report can be produced as a CSV file, which downloads named after the rack. It lists the port identifications, any console-command transcripts, and the feedback entries.
entries.short: Yes — export the report as a CSV, named after the rack, covering port IDs, command transcripts and feedback.

entries.question: Can I export to Excel?
entries.answer: Yes — the CSV is designed to open directly in Excel or any spreadsheet program. There isn't a separate .xlsx format; the CSV is the spreadsheet export.

entries.question: Can I download a PDF?
entries.answer: A PDF absolutely exists — it's the exact file that Share emails to your recipient, and the report engine renders it as a real A4 PDF. The simplest way to get the PDF in the app is to Share the report to an email address (including your own). There is no dedicated "Download PDF" button in the results row; sharing is the in-app path to the PDF.

entries.question: Can I get a JSON of the scan?
entries.answer: Yes. The report is available as JSON, containing the full structured data — devices, ports, live readings and feedback. The app itself uses this format internally when it re-opens a scan from your history.
entries.short: Yes — get the report as JSON with the full data: devices, ports, live readings and feedback.

entries.question: How do I share to Teams?
entries.answer: Tap Share → Teams, enter the recipient's email and an optional message, and send. It goes through your organisation's Microsoft connection.

entries.question: How do I share to Outlook?
entries.answer: Tap Share → Outlook, enter the recipient's email and an optional subject, and send. The report PDF is attached to the email.

entries.question: How do I share to Slack?
entries.answer: Tap Share → Slack, enter the recipient's email and an optional message, and send. As with the others, it delivers the report PDF to that recipient.

entries.question: What's in a report?
entries.answer: The scan's device inventory (type, position, port counts, and make/model where it was read), how many ports are patched, PDU power counts, the latest port findings with cable details, any live switch console readings you captured, accuracy feedback, and the annotated rack image. See section 3 for the full list.

entries.question: How do I view a report?
entries.answer: Tap View in the results button row. The report opens as a web page inside the app.

entries.question: Do report links expire?
entries.answer: Yes. A report is opened with a short-lived token that lasts 5 minutes (300 seconds). It's not a permanent public link, and the token only unlocks the one rack it was minted for.

entries.question: Why did the report ask for a token / why can't I just paste the link to a colleague?
entries.answer: Because report access is deliberately time-limited and rack-scoped for security. To give a colleague the report, use Share (which sends them the PDF) rather than passing a link.

entries.question: Do I need the recipient's email to share?
entries.answer: Yes. Every share — Teams, Outlook or Slack — is addressed to a specific email. The dialog won't send without a valid address.

entries.question: Does RackTrack remember who I shared with last time?
entries.answer: Yes, per channel and per device. When you open the Share dialog for a channel, the recipient field is pre-filled with the last address you used for that same channel.

entries.question: Can I add a message when I share?
entries.answer: Yes, it's optional. For Teams and Slack it's a Message; for Outlook it's the Subject. Leave it blank and a default line is used.

entries.question: Which format does Share actually send?
entries.answer: A PDF. All three channels attach the same PDF of the report.

entries.question: The share failed — what do the error messages mean?
entries.answer: RackTrack translates the common failures into plain English: the connection has expired (reconnect it under Data Sources), the recipient isn't in your organisation, RackTrack lacks permission to post there (an admin needs to approve it), the destination couldn't be reached, or the email address was rejected. The raw technical detail is kept in the server log, not shown to you.

entries.question: Is there a "Download" button on the results screen?
entries.answer: The results button row shows View, Share, Change Device and New Scan. There is no separate labelled download button there. To view, use View; to get a file out (PDF), use Share.

entries.question: Can I export the whole thing as one document for a group of racks?
entries.answer: Yes, for a rack group there's a combined HTML report that stacks every rack in the group into one document.

entries.question: Can I print a report?
entries.answer: Yes — open it with View and use your device's normal print/share sheet on the web page. Separately, the server can render the same report to a real PDF, which is what Share attaches.

entries.question: What do "Change Device" and "New Scan" do (the other two buttons)?
entries.answer: They're not export actions. Change Device takes you back to picking a different device in the same scan; New Scan starts a brand-new scan. They sit in the same button row as View and Share.

entries.question: Is any of a report made up or estimated?
entries.answer: No. Everything in a report comes from your real scan and any live switch readings you captured. If OCR couldn't read a device's printed model, that field is simply left generic rather than guessed.

entries.question: Does scanning touch my switches or network?
entries.answer: No. Drawing the results screen uses only your photo. RackTrack contacts a real switch only when you open a specific port (Find Port) or open the Switches tab — and only for that one lookup.

entries.question: How does it know what each device is?
entries.answer: A single vision model (devices_seg.pt) recognises equipment by shape into 12 base classes. Then OCR reads the faceplate: it can supply the real name, and if it reads a known brand it can correct the type (e.g. a box the model called "UPS" becomes a "Controller").

entries.question: Why do I sometimes see types like "Controller" or "Recorder" that aren't in the 12 classes?
entries.answer: Those come from OCR reading the brand, not from the shape model. The shape model can't tell a Planar controller from a generic chassis, so the brand name on the label is what upgrades it.

entries.question: What do the names like `U12-SW01` mean?
entries.answer: They are generated names: the unit position (U12) plus a type code (SW = Switch) and a sequence number. If RackTrack reads a real label on the rack, it uses that instead — and if it finds a naming pattern, it mints matching names for the rest.

entries.question: Why don't empty slots or "Unidentified" rows show up in the list?
entries.answer: Because there's nothing to inspect or act on there. Empty, Closed Unit and Unidentified rows are hidden from the image overlay and the device picker, but they stay in the rack record so the layout has no gaps.

entries.question: I can see a device on the image but I can't select it. Why?
entries.answer: Only port-bearing types you can drill into are selectable: Switch, Patch Panel, Router, Gateway, Firewall and PDU. Servers, UPSes and load balancers are shown but not offered for selection.

entries.question: It labelled a device wrong. How do I fix it, and does it stay fixed?
entries.answer: Use the "Detected as … — right?" card, tap No, and choose the correct type. It is saved immediately, reused when you reopen the scan, and used to auto-correct visually similar devices later. Your value carries a "Your correction" badge so it's clearly yours.

entries.question: What does "Confirm rack" do?
entries.answer: It marks the whole rack as correct and registers the photo's fingerprint. If you later re-photograph the same rack, RackTrack serves your confirmed result instead of detecting it all over again.

entries.question: If I upload the same photo twice, do I get a duplicate?
entries.answer: No. A rack's ID is derived from the image itself (scoped to your org/tenant), so an identical re-upload lands on the existing record and returns the cached result.

entries.question: The port counts changed after I corrected one. Is that expected?
entries.answer: Yes — correcting a port count can trigger a re-detection at the corrected number, and the screen refetches the saved result so it reflects what's now on disk.

entries.question: How do I get a report out, and in what formats?
entries.answer: Use View to open it in the app, then download it as a PDF, or let the server produce HTML, JSON or CSV. Share sends it to Teams, Outlook or Slack by entering a recipient email.

entries.question: It says "no devices could be read." What should I do?
entries.short: Follow the reason shown (it often names the problem — too tilted, rack occluded by cabling, etc.). Generally: retake the photo straight-on with the whole rack in frame and good light.
entries.answer: Follow the reason shown (it often names the problem — too tilted, rack occluded by cabling, etc.). Generally: retake the photo straight-on with the whole rack in frame and good light.

entries.question: Where does the switch information come from — is it reading the live device?
entries.answer: No. Everything on this screen is built from the rack photo. RackTrack reads each switch's faceplate and then looks specs and firmware up on the vendor's website. It does not log into the switch, and it does not read from your CMDB here.

entries.question: Why is my router not showing up?
entries.answer: By design. Switch Information shows only devices the scan classed as switches. Routers are a different class and are kept out so they are not mislabelled.

entries.question: The maker is right but the model is wrong or missing. What do I do?
entries.answer: Use the Identification editor. If the model was not read, an "Add model" button appears; type the correct model and both the Specifications and Firmware tabs will run against it. Your entry is saved to that switch.

entries.question: The scan read the model but got a character wrong. Do I have to fix it?
entries.answer: Usually not for the specs. The datasheet lookup runs an automatic OCR-correction pass that recovers the real model for garbled reads. The firmware check, however, uses the model as read — so if firmware fails, correcting the model can help.

entries.question: It says "Unidentified device." Is that a bug?
entries.answer: No — it is the honest result when the photo could not be read (a blurry, angled, or obscured faceplate). Type the maker and model into the Identification editor and the card comes to life.

entries.question: How do I get a firmware verdict if no version was detected?
entries.answer: Open the Firmware tab and use the "Enter version" box (for example 16.12.1 or 1.0.6 Build 20210323). RackTrack compares what you type against the latest the vendor ships.

entries.question: What does "Check vendor portal" mean in the firmware tab?
entries.answer: It means RackTrack reached the vendor's page but could not confirm the latest version automatically — often because the page needs a sign-in or blocks automated reading. Rather than guess, it hands you the real link so you can check it yourself.

entries.question: Does the firmware check tell me what changed or whether I am vulnerable?
entries.answer: No. It is a currency check — "are you on the newest version?" — not a changelog and not a security or end-of-life scan. It deliberately does not scrape release notes (they are easy to get wrong); it links you to the vendor's page where the real notes live.

entries.question: Are the SFP prices the total I will pay?
entries.answer: Treat them as per-module guide prices. In this card the advisor is not told how many SFP cages are open, so it shows each module's unit price and a buy link rather than a total to fill the switch. Some picks can also come from a curated backup list, so confirm the part and price on the vendor's page before ordering.

entries.question: Why do some SFP results look "curated" rather than from a live search?
entries.answer: When the live optics search comes back empty, the advisor falls back to a hand-verified catalog (MikroTik optics) so you are not left with a blank screen. It is not visibly marked as a fallback, which is exactly why the guidance is to verify before you buy.

entries.question: Do my typed corrections survive another scan?
entries.answer: Yes. Each entry is saved against a stable key for that switch (serial, then hardware address, then rack position), chosen so it re-attaches even when a new scan returns slightly different text. You only have to fix a bad read once.

entries.question: What is the difference between the "Login portal" and "Vendor site" links in the header?
entries.short: "Login portal" is a curated, maker-specific sign-in URL RackTrack keeps on file. "Vendor site" is a general support/landing page used when there is no curated portal for that maker. Both open in a new tab.
entries.answer:
"Login portal" is a curated, maker-specific sign-in URL RackTrack keeps on file. "Vendor site" is a general support/landing page used when there is no curated portal for that maker. Both open in a new tab.

---

Switch Information — Specs, Firmware & SFP Advisor

entries.question: "It says this doesn't look like a server rack."
entries.answer: RackTrack found nothing rack-shaped in that frame. You are probably shooting the back or side, the door is shut, or you are too far away. Shoot the front, close enough to see device faces, whole rack in frame. Full message: "This doesn't look like a server rack. Point the camera at the front of a rack so its devices and ports are visible."

entries.question: "But it IS a rack — why does it say that?"
entries.answer: The check judges one frame, not your rack. A closed door, a rear/side shot, an empty rack, or too much distance all read as "no rack here". Retake the front, square-on.

entries.question: "My photo isn't good enough."
entries.answer: Depends which message you got. "The image looks blurry" → hold still and refocus. "Image resolution is low" → use the original, not a shrunken copy. "The image appears tilted" → hold the phone level. "…side angle…" → stand square-on. "…heavily covered by cables…" → shoot extra angles or Proceed anyway.

entries.question: "It says the image is blurry but it looks fine to me."
entries.answer: Your phone measures focus, not what looks fine at thumbnail size. If you are sure, tap Proceed anyway — RackTrack will accept it.

entries.question: "Camera access denied."
entries.answer: The phone refused the camera. Allow Camera permission for RackTrack in your phone settings, or use the Upload tab instead. Full message: "Camera access denied. Allow camera permission or use Upload."

entries.question: "I see a black screen."
entries.answer: If the hint says "Starting camera…" and never changes, another app (a video call, another camera app) is probably holding the camera, or the app was backgrounded during the permission prompt. Close other camera apps and reopen; or use Upload.

entries.question: "The camera doesn't work."
entries.answer: Two cases: a red "Camera access denied" card (fix permissions or use Upload), or a black screen stuck on "Starting camera…" (another app has the camera; reopen). Video-only errors like "Video recording is not supported in this browser" mean this phone can't record in-app — record normally and Upload the clip.

entries.question: "The shutter button is greyed out and I can't take the photo."
entries.answer: In Photo mode the shutter unlocks only when the picture is Sharp, Framed and Lit. Read the hint line — it names the one thing to fix (move closer, better lighting, hold steady). When it says "Looks great — tap the shutter below" the button is live and the brackets turn green.

entries.question: "What does 'Move closer so the rack fills the frame' mean?"
entries.answer: You are too far back (or aimed at a blank surface) for the camera to see enough rack detail. Step closer until the rack fills the guide.

entries.question: "It says 'Hold steady — keep still for focus.'"
entries.answer: The live picture is not sharp, usually from hand shake. Brace your arms and hold still for a moment.

entries.question: "It says it couldn't read how many ports."
entries.answer: RackTrack knows it's a switch but never got a port count from the photo, so it won't guess. Enter the real port count with the control below the message, then pick your port. Full message: "We couldn't read how many ports this device has. Set the port count below, then pick a port."

entries.question: "It says this device has N ports, enter a number between 1 and N."
entries.answer: You picked a port number higher than the device has. Choose one within range.

entries.question: "Why are there no ports?"
entries.answer: Either the whole scan found nothing (*"No components detected."* — reshoot the front, square-on), or one device's count could not be read (a dash —; set it by hand).

entries.question: "Why does it say couldn't identify this device?"
entries.answer: RackTrack reads make/model off the label in the photo; an angled, shadowed, cable-hidden or unlabelled front comes back blank. Type the make and model in yourself via Enter make / model on the Switches tab. Full message: "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo."

entries.question: "The switch card says 'Not detected' and there are no specs."
entries.answer: Same as above — no make/model was read, so specs and firmware have nothing to look up. Tap Enter make / model, fill in both fields, Save. The chip changes to "Manual entry" and specs reload.

entries.question: "It found the vendor but not the model" (or vice versa).
entries.answer: You'll see "We identified \"<vendor>\" but couldn't read the model…" with an Add model button, or "We read a model but couldn't identify the vendor." with Add vendor. Both need filling in for specs/firmware to work.

entries.question: "I can't sign in on the app."
entries.answer: If it fails instantly with "Load failed" / "Failed to fetch" (not "invalid password") and the website works fine, your app build points at an old server address and needs rebuilding. Use the current address in a browser meanwhile; ask your admin for a fresh build.

entries.question: "Sign-in works in my browser but not the app."
entries.answer: Exactly the case above — the app has an out-of-date server address baked in. A new build fixes it; reinstalling the old one does not.

entries.question: "I got signed out on my own."
entries.answer: Your session expired or was ended elsewhere, so RackTrack sent you back to login rather than leaving a broken page. Just sign in again. Sessions last about 30 days.

entries.question: "My scan images are broken / blank but the app otherwise works."
entries.answer: The 12-hour image access token expired while your 30-day login stayed valid — classic "next-morning" symptom. Close and reopen the app to re-mint it.

entries.question: "Did I lose my scans when I reinstalled?"
entries.answer: No. Scans live on the server. Reinstall, sign in, and they're all there.

entries.question: "The switch shows offline."
entries.answer: The last poll to it failed — it's stopped, unreachable, or (for lab nodes) came back without its config. RackTrack recovers on its own once the switch answers again. Banner: "Offline — the switch isn't answering…".

entries.question: "A switch says 'No data' but there are no failures."
entries.answer: It's enabled and hasn't failed, but a poll has never succeeded — usually missing credentials. Add the switch's login.

entries.question: "Why are the LINK and SPEED columns empty?"
entries.answer: On a virtual or routed switch that's the honest answer: it has no physical link to negotiate and no PoE hardware, so Speed/Duplex/PoE read —. A real physical switch fills them in. Blank means "nothing to report", not "error".

entries.question: "Why does the switch show no VLANs / no neighbours?"
entries.answer: A routed (Layer-3) switch has no switchports to put in a VLAN, and may not run LLDP at all (Cisco defaults to CDP). Both empty states are expected on that kind of device.

entries.question: "Why did a port report say 'Link is DOWN'?"
entries.answer: Nothing is plugged into that port, or the far end is unplugged. Not an error — just the port's real state.

entries.question: "The app won't update."
entries.answer: It doesn't update through the stores because it isn't on them. iPhone: turn on Automatic Updates in TestFlight, or tap Update there. Android: install the newest APK (uninstall the old one first if you get "App not installed").

entries.question: "RackTrack isn't in the App Store / I can't find it."
entries.answer: It's a beta, delivered through TestFlight on iPhone and as an APK on Android — not the public stores. Install TestFlight first, then open your invite email on the phone.

entries.question: "TestFlight can't find my invitation."
entries.answer: The invite is tied to the Apple ID email it was sent to. If your phone is signed into a different Apple ID, TestFlight won't see it. Ask your administrator to re-issue the invite to the address you actually use.

entries.question: "RackTrack suddenly won't open and TestFlight says the build expired."
entries.answer: TestFlight builds expire after 90 days. Nothing is lost — open TestFlight and install the current build.

entries.question: "Android says 'App not installed' when I try the new APK."
entries.answer: It's a signing mismatch with the old copy. Uninstall the existing RackTrack, then install the new APK.

entries.question: "It told me to take the photo from the front of the rack."
entries.answer: The scan finished but found zero devices — a rear or side shot, a closed door, or too much distance. Open the front, stand square-on, reshoot. Full message: "Please take the photo from the front of the rack — we need to see the devices and ports face-on."

entries.question: "It says only N rack units could be made out."
entries.answer: Only a sliver of the rack was in frame. Step back until the whole cabinet fits inside the guide.

entries.question: "It says that image could not be read."
entries.answer: The file was corrupt or an unsupported format. Use an original JPG or PNG straight from the camera. Full message: "That image could not be read. Try a JPG or PNG taken straight from the camera."

entries.question: "It says something went wrong on your side."
entries.answer: That message is RackTrack owning the failure — a crash or timeout, not your photo. Retaking won't help; just try again, and report it if it persists. Full message: "Something went wrong on our side analysing that photo — it is not a problem with your image. It has been logged; please try again."

entries.question: "My upload keeps failing."
entries.answer: Over a weak connection the send can drop; RackTrack retries once (*"Connection dropped — retrying…"*). If it still fails you'll see "Upload failed — the connection dropped while sending the photo. Check your signal and try again." Move to better signal and retry — no duplicate scan is created.

entries.question: "My iPhone photos are HEIC — will that be a problem?"
entries.answer: No. HEIC/HEIF photos skip your phone's local checks and are validated on the server instead, so they're never wrongly rejected for blur or resolution on the phone.

entries.question: "It said the rack is covered by cables."
entries.answer: Too many cables are hiding the equipment. Shoot extra photos from the left and right of the rack, or tap Proceed anyway knowing some devices may be missed.

entries.question: "It warned about a side angle but still scanned."
entries.answer: The side-angle notice is a soft warning, not a stop — the scan runs anyway. For a cleaner result, stand square-on to the rack.

entries.question: "What's the difference between Retake and Proceed anyway?"
entries.answer: Retake clears the photo so you can shoot a better one. Proceed anyway tells RackTrack to accept the photo as-is and skip the quality gate — it will analyse whatever it can, even if the result ends up thin or empty.

entries.question: I opened /dashboard and it just says "Owner access required to view this dashboard." Why?
entries.answer:
The Operations Console is for the RackTrack platform owner. The app itself will let an Organization Admin open /dashboard, but the server refuses the data with a 403 and the page shows "Owner access required to view this dashboard." On the Logs tab the equivalent message is "Admin access required to view logs." (The old /logs bookmark now redirects to /dashboard, where Logs is a tab.)

There is nothing you can change from inside the app — the role check happens on the server, so no setting in your organization will unlock it. Access is limited to the platform owner, though RackTrack staff can optionally add a specific username to a server-side allow-list if there's a genuine operational need. If you need operational figures for your own organization, contact RackTrack support (the platform owner) to pull them for you or to arrange access.
symptoms: Owner access required to view this dashboard.
Admin access required to view logs.
Console page is blank for an org admin
entries.rootCause: The client route /dashboard uses AdminRoute (org_admin OR owner), but the server endpoints /api/admin/dashboard and /api/logs* require role === 'owner' (or a username listed in the AUDIT_ADMINS env allow-list) and return 403 otherwise. The client turns that 403 into the friendly message.

evidence.snippet: if (res.status === 403) { setError('Owner access required to view this dashboard.'); setLoading(false); return; }
if (logsRes.status === 403) { setError('Admin access required to view logs.'); setLoading(false); return; }

entries.short: The Operations Console is for the RackTrack platform owner. ) There is nothing you can change from inside the app — the role check happens on the server, so no setting in your organization will unlock it.

entries.question: I locked my phone / switched apps while a scan was running, and when I came back I was on the upload screen. Did I lose the scan?
entries.answer: No — the scan almost certainly finished on the server, and RackTrack will bring it back for you. When you start a scan the app saves a small marker on the phone before uploading. When you return to the app it shows a full-screen message — 'Bringing your scan back…' with 'We're finishing the analysis you started. This takes a moment.' — while it asks the server what happened. As soon as the server says the scan is done, it drops you straight on the results. It waits up to 45 seconds, checking about every 1.5 seconds. If those 45 seconds run out before the server answers, don't panic: reopen the app and it will try again, because the marker stays on the phone for 15 minutes. (If the server instead reports that the scan failed or that it has no record of it, the marker is cleared and the app stops retrying automatically.) After 15 minutes the marker expires and automatic recovery stops. If that happens, go to Profile — the finished scan is in your scan list there. As a last resort, upload the exact same photo again: RackTrack recognises the identical image and returns the same result without re-analysing.
symptoms: Back on the Scan screen after switching apps
Progress bar disappeared and nothing happened
Scan looked like it never ran
entries.rootCause: iOS suspends the WebView when backgrounded, killing the in-flight /api/analyze response. ScanPage writes a clientJobId marker to localStorage before awaiting; PendingScanResumer polls GET /api/analyze/result/:jobId on cold start and on the Capacitor 'resume' event. Client marker TTL is 15 min; the resume poll deadline is 45 s with a 1500 ms interval.

evidence.snippet:
const KEY = 'racktrack:pendingScan';
const TTL_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;   // matches the server-side job TTL

Bringing your scan back…
We’re finishing the analysis you started. This takes a moment.

entries.short: No — the scan almost certainly finished, and RackTrack will bring it back for you. When you start a scan the app saves a small marker on the phone before uploading. When you return to the app it shows a full-screen message — 'Bringing your scan back…' with 'We're finishing the analysis you started.

entries.question: I switched to another app mid-scan and came back — is my scan lost?
entries.answer:
No. RackTrack keeps a ticket for the scan that was running. When you come back (or reopen the app), it shows a full-screen "Bringing your scan back…" spinner with the note "We're finishing the analysis you started. This takes a moment.", then drops you straight on the finished results.

It waits up to about 45 seconds for the scan to finish. If it is still not ready by then, the spinner clears and you stay where you are — reopen the app a moment later and it will try again; the analysis keeps running on the server regardless. The ticket is kept for 15 minutes, so if you leave it much longer, open the scan from your history in Profile instead. If the scan failed on the server, the spinner simply clears and you are left on the screen you were on.
symptoms: We're finishing the analysis you started
back to the upload screen after leaving the app
entries.rootCause: PendingScanResumer polls the scan-job endpoint on cold start and on every Capacitor 'resume' event, navigating to /results/:rackId when status is done. It gives up polling after a 45000 ms deadline but keeps the marker.

evidence.snippet:
Bringing your scan back…
We’re finishing the analysis you started. This takes a moment.

entries.short: No. RackTrack keeps a ticket for the scan that was running. When you come back (or reopen the app), it shows a full-screen "Bringing your scan back…" spinner with the note "We're finishing the analysis you started. ", then drops you straight on the finished results.

entries.question: It says "This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator." — how do I get back in?
entries.answer:
Your individual user account was switched off by an administrator. Your password is fine; the server checks your password first, then refuses the sign-in on purpose (HTTP 403).

Important: nothing you do on the phone will fix this. Resetting your password, reinstalling the app, or trying a different device will all produce the same message.

Steps to fix:
1. Contact your organization admin. (A site manager can also do this, but only for regular members in their own Site — if you are a site manager or an admin yourself, you need an organization admin or the platform owner.)
2. Ask them to open the Organizations console, find you in the Members list, open the menu on your row and choose "Reactivate".
3. Then sign in normally — no new password needed. Your past scans and history are still there; deactivation never deletes them.

If your admin says your account looks active, ask them whether the whole ORGANIZATION was deactivated instead. That is a different problem: your sign-in actually succeeds, and you land on a screen titled "Organization deactivated". Only the RackTrack platform owner can reverse that one.
symptoms: This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator.
Correct password is rejected on every device
entries.rootCause: users.active = 0. The login route verifies the password first, then rejects with 403 before issuing a token. The flag is set via PATCH /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId with {active:false}.

evidence.snippet:
// Soft-disable: a deactivated user keeps their data/history but can't sign in.
  _ensureColumn('users', 'active', 'active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1');

entries.short:
Your individual user account was switched off by an administrator.
1. Contact your organization admin.
2. Ask them to open the Organizations console, find you in the Members list, open the menu on your row and choose "Reactivate".
3. Then sign in normally — no new password needed.

entries.question: My colleague sent me an invite link but it says the invite has expired / has already been used.
entries.answer:
Invite links are single-use and last 7 days. Once someone completes the sign-up form on that link it's dead; after a week an untouched link dies too.

What you may see on the invite page:
- "This invite has expired" — more than 7 days have passed since it was created.
- "This invite has already been used" — an account was already created from it.
- "Invite not found" — the link was mistyped or truncated by a chat app, so the code doesn't match any invite. Copy the whole link rather than typing it.
- "An account already exists for this email" — you already have a RackTrack account on that address. Go to Sign in and use "Forgot password?" instead. (Usually your admin will hit this first: RackTrack refuses to issue an invite to an email that already has an account.)
- "That username is taken" — pick a different username; usernames must be unique across all of RackTrack.
- "Could not load this invite." — that's a network problem, not a bad invite. Check your connection and reopen the link.

Steps to fix: ask whoever invited you (your organization admin or site manager) to generate a new invite for your email address. There's no way to revive an old one.

Note: accepting an invite signs you in immediately and drops you on the Scan screen — you set your own username and password, and you do not need approval from the platform owner.
symptoms: This invite has already been used
An account already exists for this email
entries.rootCause: invites.expires_at = Date.now() + 7*24*60*60*1000 and accepted_at is stamped on first use; both GET /api/invites/:code and POST /api/invites/:code/accept return 410 on used/expired and 404 on unknown codes. AcceptInvitePage renders the server's error string, or 'Could not load this invite.' for a fetch rejection.

evidence.snippet:
const code = crypto.randomBytes(18).toString('base64url');
    const expiresAt = Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 7 days

.then(({ ok, d }) => { ... else setErr(d.error || 'This invite is invalid.'); })
      .catch(() => { if (!cancelled) setErr('Could not load this invite.'); })

entries.short: Invite links are single-use and last 7 days. Once someone completes the sign-up form on that link it's dead; after a week an untouched link dies too. What you may see on the invite page: - "This invite has expired" — more than 7 days have passed since it was created.

entries.question: The drift / port history page says "Waiting for first poll…" and never changes.
entries.answer: Same as the entry, with one clarification to the rate-limit sentence: "That is limited to 5 manual polls per minute for each person on each switch (the limit is counted per user and per switch); going over returns 'rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute'." Everything else in the answer stands as written.
symptoms: "rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute"
"poll already in progress for this device"
entries.rootCause: port_poller default interval is DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS 3,600,000 ms; failures enter an exponential backoff from BASE_BACKOFF_MS 60,000 up to MAX_BACKOFF_MS 1,800,000; devices with no stored creds or no VENDOR_RECIPES entry are skipped with only touchPolled; manual probes suppress polling for MANUAL_PROBE_YIELD_MS 60,000. Manual poll route caps at POLL_RATE_MAX 5 per 60 s window and 409s when busy.

evidence.snippet:
const BASE_BACKOFF_MS = Math.max(1000, Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_BACKOFF_BASE_MS) || 60_000);
const MAX_BACKOFF_MS  = Math.max(BASE_BACKOFF_MS, Number(process.env.PORT_POLL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS) || 30 * 60_000);
const MANUAL_PROBE_YIELD_MS = 60_000;

const POLL_RATE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000;
const POLL_RATE_MAX       = 5;
Waiting for first poll…

entries.short: Same as the entry, with one clarification to the rate-limit sentence: "That is limited to 5 manual polls per minute for each person on each switch (the limit is counted per user and per switch); going over returns 'rate limit: max 5 manual polls per minute'." Everything else in the answer stands as written.

entries.question: How do I invite new members to my organization?
entries.answer: As an admin, you can email invitation links to new members. They'll be able to set their own password and join the organization immediately.

entries.question: What does the Live Switch Data feature do?
entries.answer: The Live Switch Data feature opens a live connection to the switch and tells you how many ports are free versus in use, and whether an open port is copper or fiber, so you know instantly whether there is room to plug something in.
symptoms: How many free ports do I have?
What type of ports are available?

entries.question: How do I use the Live Switch Data feature?
entries.answer: To use the Live Switch Data feature, open the Ports view for a rack, and the server will open a session to the switch and request its interface status. You can then use the filter pills to narrow the list of ports.
symptoms: How do I get a list of available ports?

entries.question: How do I use RackTrack to scan a rack?
entries.answer: To scan a rack, open the Scan screen from the central capture button in the bottom navigation. Choose a capture family: Upload (a file you have) or Camera (live capture). For Camera Photo mode, frame the rack until the guide box turns green. Press the primary button to analyze the rack.

entries.question: How do I log in?
entries.answer: Open RackTrack — you land on the Sign in screen, because you cannot use it without an account. Type the username or email you signed up with and your password (and your organization name if the screen asks for one), then tap Sign in. A sign-in lasts 30 days and is tied to that one device, so signing in on your phone does not sign you in on a laptop. If you were invited, tap “Use an invite code” instead; if you have forgotten your password, tap “Forgot password” to reset it by email.
entries.short: Enter your username or email and password on the Sign in screen and tap Sign in; a sign-in lasts 30 days per device.

entries.question: I can't sign in
entries.answer: A few things can block a sign-in. If you see “Invalid username or password”, recheck your details — you can leave the Organization box blank, and use Forgot password to reset by email. If it says “Load failed” or “Failed to fetch”, your device can’t reach the RackTrack server (a connection problem, not your password). If the installed app can’t sign in but the website can, the app was built with an old server address — get the latest tester build. If it says “This account has been deactivated”, ask your administrator to reactivate you. And if your organization is still awaiting approval, you’ll wait on the approval screen until the owner approves it.
entries.short: Check password (Forgot password resets it), your connection, whether the app build is current, or if your account is deactivated / pending approval.

entries.question: My scan came back empty
entries.answer: An empty result almost always comes down to the photo. RackTrack usually names the reason — too tilted, the rack hidden behind cabling, or poor light. Retake the photo straight-on with the whole rack in the frame and good, even lighting, then analyse again. If a clear, straight photo still finds nothing, add the missing gear by correcting a nearby device.
entries.short: Usually the photo — retake it straight-on, whole rack in frame, good light, and analyse again.

entries.question: Where did my earlier scans go?
entries.answer: They aren’t on a separate History screen — your past scans live on your Profile. Tap Profile (the person icon in the bottom bar, or in the sidebar on a larger screen), scroll to “Recent Scans”, and tap any row to reopen that scan’s results.
entries.short: On the Profile screen under “Recent Scans” — tap a row to reopen it.

entries.question: How do I export a report?
entries.answer: Open the scan and tap View to open its report, then tap Download PDF at the top to save a PDF. The same report is also available as CSV (opens in Excel), JSON, and the on-screen HTML. To send it to someone, tap Share and choose Teams, Outlook, or Slack — RackTrack emails them the PDF.
entries.short: View → Download PDF (also CSV / JSON / HTML), or Share to Teams / Outlook / Slack.

entries.question: Why is my device showing the wrong model?
entries.answer: The make and model are read from the text on the device in your photo, so a blurry or partly-hidden label can be misread. To fix it, open the switch card and, under Identification, tap “Enter make / model” to type the correct values. If the whole device TYPE is wrong (say a firewall called a switch), answer “No” to “Detected as X — right?” and pick the correct type.
entries.short: The model is read from the photo’s label — correct it via the switch card’s “Enter make / model”, or fix the type with the “Detected as X — right?” card.

entries.question: Do I need internet to scan?
entries.answer: Yes. Both signing in and analysing a photo need the app to reach the RackTrack server, so a working connection is required. It doesn’t have to be the public internet if the server is on your local network, but the app must be able to reach the server. If the installed app can’t connect, the web version is a fallback.
entries.short: Yes — signing in and analysing a photo both need the app to reach the RackTrack server.
